Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Payogasiddhipāḷi

The Pāḷi Text on the Accomplishment of Practice

1. Saññādikaṇḍa

1. The Chapter on Designations

Siddha-mbatthuṃ sammā vande

May there be success! I rightly pay homage.

Ganthārambhakathā

Introduction to the Text

Siddha+miṭṭhadadaṃ [M 0.0001] buddhaṃ, dhammaṃ maṇiṃva svatthadaṃ;

Saṅghañca sādaraṃ natvā, payogasiddhi vuccate.

Having paid homage with reverence to the Buddha, the giver of success and what is desired; to the Dhamma, like a gem that bestows well-being; and to the Sangha, the Payogasiddhi is now proclaimed.

Pabhāvo moggallānassa, byākaraṇe ca peṭake;

Nisseseva kabbātitto, aho acchariyo vata.

The power of Moggallāna in grammar and the Piṭaka, and his complete mastery of composition—ah, how wonderful indeed!

Vuttañhi pubbasīhaḷācariya+pācariyehi –

For it was said by the ancient Sinhalese masters and the eastern masters:

Yā satti pāṇine yā ca, candra+kātyāyanādisu;

Sā+yaṃ muttimatī maññe, moggallāyanarūpinī-ti.

That skill which is in Pāṇini, and that which is in Candra, Kātyāyana, and others—that very skill, I believe, has become embodied in the form of Moggallāna.

Suttaṃ vutti ca teneva, katā ekena pañcikā;

Tasmā+ssa sattha+maññehi, supasaṭṭhaṃ+tisundaraṃ.

The Sutta (rules), the Vutti (commentary), and the Pañcikā (glossary) were all composed by him alone. Therefore his treatise is more highly praised than others and is exceedingly beautiful.

Tamhi ca dubbidhaṃ ñeyyaṃ, suttaṃ kammatthabhedato;

Tesvā+di mītisaddena, dutiyaṃ tippakārato.

In that treatise, what is to be known is twofold, distinguished as the Sutta (rules) and the subject matter. Of these, the first is indicated by the word 'iti' (thus), and the second by its threefold structure.

Suvisadaṃ pakāsetvā, subodha+mākumārakaṃ;

Byāpikāvaḷiyā kassaṃ, taṃ suṇātha samāhitāti.

Having made it very clear and easy to understand even for a child, I will now compose a comprehensive commentary. Listen to it with concentrated minds.

1. Aādayo titālīsa vaṇṇā

1. The forty-three letters, beginning with 'a'.

Akārādayo [M 0.0002] niggahītantā tecattālīsakkharā vaṇṇā nāma honti. Taṃ yathā a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, ऐ, o, औ, ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra lava sa ha ḷa aṃ. Tena kvattho “e ona+ma vaṇṇe”ti. Titālīsāti vacanaṃ katthaci vaṇṇalopaṃ ñāpeti, tena “paṭisaṅkhā yoniso”tiādi siddhaṃ.

The forty-three characters, beginning with the letter 'a' and ending with the niggahīta, are called 'letters' (vaṇṇā). They are as follows: a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, ai, o, au, ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha, ña, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa, ta, tha, da, dha, na, pa, pha, ba, bha, ma, ya, ra, la, va, sa, ha, ḷa, aṃ. What is the purpose here of the rule 'e o ṇa ma vaṇṇe'? The statement 'forty-three' indicates that in some cases there is elision of a letter; by this, forms such as 'paṭisaṅkhā yoniso' are accounted for.

Akāro ādi mariyādabhūto yesaṃ te aādayo. Tayo ca cattālīsa ceti titālīsa, iminā nipātanena vā catabhāgalopo. Vaṇṇīyati attho etehīti vaṇṇā.

Those for which the letter 'a' is the beginning and boundary are called 'a-ādayo' (beginning with 'a'). 'Titālīsa' (forty-three) is formed from 'tayo ca cattālīsa ca' (three and forty); by this irregular formation (nipātana), there is elision of the syllable 'ca' and part of the following word. They are called 'letters' (vaṇṇā) because meaning is described by them.

Etthā+ha – “kasmā ācariyakaccāyanādīhi viya ekacattālīsakkharāna+makkharasañña+makatvā titālīsakkharānaṃ vaṇṇasaññā katā”ti. Vuccate –

Here it is asked: "Why, unlike the master Kaccāyana and others who gave the designation 'akkhara' to forty-one letters, have you given the designation 'vaṇṇa' to forty-three letters?" It is answered:

Sā māgadhī mūlabhāsā, narā yāyā+dikappikā;

Brahmāno cā-sutālāpā, sambuddhā cāpi bhāsareti –

That Māgadhī is the root language, which was spoken by people at the beginning of the aeon, by Brahmās, by those who have not heard other speech, and which the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones also speak.

Vacanato māgadhikānaṃ ettha, seyyo, oṭṭho, sotthi-tyādīsupi asesabyāpikānaṃ titālīsakkharānaṃva ujukānvatthappakkharaguṇikā, neva pana ‘rukkhā vanaṃ’tyādo viya avayave samudāyavohāro, ‘samuddo mayā diṭṭho’tyādo viya ca samudāye avayavavohāroti dassetuṃ paccekaṃ vaṇṇasaññā katāti.

Therefore, because of that statement, in the Māgadhī language, even in words like 'seyyo,' 'oṭṭho,' and 'sotthi,' the forty-three letters are universally applicable and have a direct etymological correspondence with their meaning. This is not like the figurative use of a collective term for a part, as in 'trees are a forest,' nor like the use of a term for a part for the whole, as in 'I have seen the ocean.' To show this, the designation 'vaṇṇa' was made for each sound individually.

“Sakkaccasavanaṃ buddhasāsanasampattī”ti “sithiladhanitādi akkharavipattiyañhi atthassa dunnayatā hotī”ti ca yasmā vuttaṃ.

Since it has been said: "Careful listening is the treasure of the Buddha's teaching," and, "Indeed, when there is a defect in the letters, such as being lax or aspirated, the meaning becomes difficult to grasp."

Tasmā [M 0.0003] akkharakosallaṃ, sampādeyya vicakkhaṇo;

Upaṭṭhahaṃ garuṃ sammā, uṭṭhānādīhi pañcahi.

Therefore, a discerning person should acquire skill in letters by properly attending upon a teacher with the five methods beginning with rising to greet them.

Tattha akārādīna+manukkamo pane+sa ṭhānādikkamasannissito. Tathā hi ṭhāna+karaṇa+payatanehi vaṇṇā jāyanti. Tattha cha ṭhānāni kaṇṭha+tālu+muddha+danta+oṭṭha+nāsikāvasena.

Now, the sequence of the letters beginning with 'a' is based on the sequence of their place of articulation and so on. For letters are produced by the place of articulation (ṭhāna), the articulator (karaṇa), and effort (payatana). Therein, there are six places of articulation: the throat, the palate, the head (retroflex), the teeth, the lips, and the nose.

Tattha avaṇṇa+kavagga+hānaṃ kaṇṭho ṭhānaṃ, ivaṇṇa+cavagga+yānaṃ tālu, ṭavagga+ra+ḷānaṃ muddhā, tavagga+la+sānaṃ dantā, uvaṇṇa+pavaggānaṃ oṭṭho, e vaṇṇassa kaṇṭhatālū, o vaṇṇassa kaṇṭho+ṭṭhā, vakārassa danto+ṭṭhā, niggahītassa nāsikā, ṅa, ñña, ṇa, na, mānaṃ sakaṭhānaṃ nāsikā ca. Ettha ca –

Therein, the throat is the place of articulation for the a-vowels, the k-group, and 'h'. The palate is for the i-vowels, the c-group, and 'y'. The head is for the ṭ-group, 'r', and 'ḷ'. The teeth are for the t-group, 'l', and 's'. The lips are for the u-vowels and the p-group. For the letter 'e', it is the throat and palate. For the letter 'o', it is the throat and lips. For the letter 'v', it is the teeth and lips. For the niggahīta, it is the nose. For 'ṅ', 'ñ', 'ṇ', 'n', and 'm', it is their own respective place and also the nose. And here it is said:

Hakāro pañcameheva, antaṭṭhāhi ca saṃyuto;

Oraso iti viññeyyo, kaṇṭhajo tadasaṃyuto.

The letter 'h' when conjoined with the fifth letters of the consonant groups (the nasals) and with the semivowels, should be known as thoracic (orasa). When not conjoined with them, it is guttural (kaṇṭhaja).

Yathā avaṅhoti (avaṅa hoti., tañhi, taṇhā, pubbanho, amhe, guyhaṃ, gārayhā, ārulho, bahvakkharanti.

For example: `avaṅhoti` (from `avaṃ hoti`), `tañhi`, `taṇhā`, `pubbanho`, `amhe`, `guyhaṃ`, `gārayhā`, `ārulho`, `bahvakkharanti`.

Karaṇaṃ –

The Articulator:

Jivhāmajjhaṃ tālujānaṃ,

Jivhopaggaṃ muddhajānaṃ,

Jivhaggaṃ dantajānaṃ se-

Sā sakaṭhānakaraṇā.

For the palatal sounds, the articulator is the middle of the tongue; for the retroflex sounds, the blade of the tongue; for the dental sounds, the tip of the tongue. For the remaining sounds, their own place of articulation also serves as the articulator.

Vaṇṇānaṃ uccāraṇussāho payatanaṃ, taṃ kiṃ – saṃvutādikaraṇaviseso, saṃvutatta+makārassa, vivaṭattaṃ sesasarānaṃ sakāra+hakārānañca, phuṭṭhattaṃ vaggānaṃ, īsaṃphuṭṭhattaṃ ya+ra+la+vānaṃ.

The exertion in the utterance of letters is called 'effort' (payatana). What is that? It is the specific manner of articulation, such as closure and so on. For the letter 'a' there is closure; for the remaining vowels and for the letters 's' and 'h' there is openness; for the consonant groups there is full contact; for 'y', 'r', 'l', and 'v' there is slight contact.

Evaṃ ṭhāna+karaṇa+payatana+suti kālabhinnesu akkharesu sarā nissayā, itare nissitā. Tattha –

Thus, among the letters, which are distinguished by place, articulator, effort, sound, and length, the vowels are the support (nissayā), and the others (the consonants) are the supported (nissitā). In this regard:

Nissayā+do [M 0.0004] sarā vuttā, nissitā byañjanā tato;

Vagge+kajā bahuttā+do, tato ṭhāna+lahukkamā.

First the vowels are stated, as they are the support; then the consonants, as they are the supported. The consonants are arranged first in groups, beginning with the k-group, because of their number; then according to the natural progression of their places of articulation.

“Aādayo”ti vattate yāva “bindu niggahīta”nti. Tañca kho “atthavasā vibhattivipariṇāmo”ti sattamyanta+mabhisambandhīyate, “vaṇṇā”ti vattate –

The rule starting 'Beginning with a...' is to be understood as carrying forward until the rule 'The dot is the niggahīta.' And by the principle 'a change of case-ending occurs according to the requirements of the meaning,' this is connected with a word in the seventh case. The word 'letters' also carries forward.

2. Dasā+do sarā

2. Ten are the initial vowels.

Aādīsvā+dimhi niddiṭṭhā odantā dasa vaṇṇā sarā nāma honti. Yathā a ā, i ī, u ū, e ऐ, o औ. Saranti=sappadhānabhāvena pavattanti, byañjane vā sārentīti sarā.

The ten letters indicated at the beginning, commencing with 'a', are called vowels. For example: a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, o. They are called vowels (sarā) because they flow (saranti) with predominance, or because they cause consonants (byañjana) to be sounded (sārenti).

“Dasā+do sarā”ti vattate.

The rule 'Ten are the initial vowels' is carried forward.

3. Dve dve savaṇṇā

3. In pairs, they are of the same class.

Aādīsvā+dimesu dasasu dve dve savaṇṇā nāma honti yathākkamaṃ. Yathā a āiti, i īiti, u ū iti, e eiti, o, oiti. Samānā sadisā vaṇṇā savaṇṇā, samānattañca ṭhānato. “Dve dve”ti vattate vakkhamānesu dvīsu.

Among these ten initial vowels, they are called 'of the same class' (savaṇṇa) in successive pairs. For example: a and ā; i and ī; u and ū; e and e; o and o. Letters that are similar and alike are 'savaṇṇa', and their similarity is based on their place of articulation. The rule 'in pairs' carries forward to the two rules to be stated.

4. Pubbo rasso

4. The first is short.

Tesveva dasasu ye dve dve savaṇṇā, tesu yo yo pubbo, so so rassasañño hoti. Yathā a i u e o. Tesu ‘saṃyogato pubbāva dissanti dve panantimā’ta dassetuṃ tattha sādhuttā tesampi idha saṅgaho, yathā ettha seyyo oṭṭho sotthi. Rassakālayogā tabbantatāya vā [M 0.0005] rassā. Rassakālo nāma accharāsaṅghāto akkhinimmilanasaṅkhāto vā kālo, tena ekamatto rasso, dvimatto dīgho, aḍḍhamatto byañjano. Chandasi diyaḍḍhamattampi rassanti gaṇhanti ācariyā.

Among those very ten which are 'of the same class' in pairs, whichever is the first of each pair has the designation 'short'. For example: a, i, u, e, o. Among these, in order to show that 'the last two are also seen as short before a conjunct consonant,' their inclusion here is also proper for correctness. For example: ettha, seyyo, oṭṭho, sotthi. They are short because of their connection with a short duration or because they possess that nature. A short duration is the time of a finger-snap or the time it takes to blink an eye. By this measure, a short vowel has one mora, a long vowel has two moras, and a consonant has half a mora. In meter, teachers also consider one and a half moras to be short.

5. Paro dīgho

5. The other is long.

Aādīsvā+dibhūtesu dasasu ye dve dve savaṇṇā, tesu yo yo paro, so so dīghasañño hoti. Taṃ yathā ā ī ū e o. Dīghakālayogā tabbantatāya vā dīghā.

Among these ten initial vowels which are 'of the same class' in pairs, whichever is the latter of each pair has the designation 'long'. For example: ā, ī, ū, e, o. They are long because of their connection with a long duration or because they possess that nature.

6. Kādayo byañjanā

6. Those beginning with 'ka' are consonants.

Aādīsu kādayo niggahītapariyantā tettiṃsa byañjanā nāma honti. Yathā ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra lava sa ha ḷa aṃ iti. Byañjīyati attho etehīti byañjanā. Kakārādīsva+kāro uccāraṇattho.

Among the letters, those beginning with 'ka' and ending with the niggahīta, thirty-three in number, are called consonants. For example: ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va sa ha ḷa aṃ. Meaning is made manifest by these, therefore they are called consonants. In 'ka' and so on, the vowel 'a' is for the purpose of pronunciation.

“Kādayo”ti vattate.

The rule 'beginning with ka' continues to apply.

7. Pañcapañcakā vaggā

7. The vaggas are in groups of five.

Aādīsu kakārādayo makārantā pañcapañcakā vaggā nāma honti. Yathā ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma iti. Pañca pañca parimāṇa+mesaṃ pañcapañcakā. Vajjenti yakārādayoti vaggā. Te pana paṭhamakkharavasena [M 0.0006] kavagga+cavaggādivohāraṃ gatā kusalattikādayo viya.

Among the letters, those from 'ka' to 'ma', in groups of five, are called 'vaggas' (groups). For example: ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma. Their measure is five by five, hence they are called 'pañcapañcakā'. Because they exclude 'ya' and the following letters, they are called 'vaggas'. However, according to the initial letter, they have come to be designated as the 'ka-group', 'ca-group', and so on, like the 'kusalattika' and others.

8. Bindu niggahītaṃ

8. The dot is the niggahīta.

Akārādīsva+yaṃ vaṇṇo bindumatto, so niggahītasañño hoti. Rassasaraṃ nissāya gahita+muccāritaṃ niggahītaṃ, karaṇaṃ niggahetvā vā.

Among the letters, that letter which is merely a dot has the designation 'niggahīta'. It is 'niggahīta' because it is uttered in dependence on a short vowel, or by restraining the organ of speech.

Karaṇaṃ niggahetvāna, mukhenā+vivaṭena yaṃ;

Vuccate niggahītanti, vuttaṃ bindu sarānugaṃ.

Having restrained the organ of speech, what is uttered with the mouth not opened is called 'niggahīta'; it is said to be a dot that follows a vowel.

Bahvakkharasaññākaraṇaṃ anvatthasaññatthaṃ, jha+lādayo tu ruḷhīsaññā.

The creation of multi-syllable technical terms is for the purpose of etymological designation, but terms like 'jha', 'la', and so on, are conventional designations.

Vaṇṇā sarā savaṇṇā ca, rassā dīghā ca byañjanā;

Vaggā ca niggahītanti, hoti saññāvidhikkamo.

Letters, vowels, and those of the same class, short and long, and consonants, groups and the niggahīta—such is the procedure for designations.

(Saññāvidhānaṃ.)

(The Chapter on Designations.)

Sandhi vuccate –

Now sandhi is explained:

Loka aggapuggalo, paññā indriyaṃ, tīṇi imāni, no hi etaṃ, bhikkhunī ovādo, mātu upaṭṭhānaṃ, sametu āyasmā, abhibhū āyatanaṃ, dhanaṃ me atthi, sabbe eva, tayo assu dhammā, asanto ettha na dissanti itī+dha sarasaññāyaṃ –

Loka aggapuggalo, paññā indriyaṃ, tīṇi imāni, no hi etaṃ, bhikkhunī ovādo, mātu upaṭṭhānaṃ, sametu āyasmā, abhibhū āyatanaṃ, dhanaṃ me atthi, sabbe eva, tayo assu dhammā, asanto ettha na dissanti—in these cases involving the technical term 'vowel':

26. Saro lopo sare

26. A vowel is elided before a vowel.

Sare saro lopanīyo hoti. Saroti kāriyīniddeso, lopoti kāriyaniddeso. Lopo= adassanaṃ anuccāraṇaṃ[M 0.0007], saroti jātyekavacanavasena vuttaṃ, sareti opasilesikādhārasattamī, tato vaṇṇa kāla byavadhāne kāriyaṃ na hoti, tva+masi, katamā cānanda aniccasaññāti. Evaṃ sabbasandhīsu.

When a vowel follows, a preceding vowel is to be elided. 'Saro' is the designation of the patient, 'lopo' is the designation of the operation. Elision is disappearance, non-utterance. 'Saro' is stated in the singular to denote the entire class. 'Sare' is the locative of proximity. Therefore, when there is an intervention of another letter or of time, the operation does not take place, as in: tvaṃ asi; katamā cānanda aniccasaññā. This applies to all sandhi rules.

Vidhīti vattate.

The term 'rule' is carried forward.

14. Sattamiyaṃ pubbassa

14. [The operation applies] to the preceding, [when the condition is stated] in the locative.

Therayaṭṭhinyāyena pavattate paribhāsā dubbalavidhino patiṭṭhābhāvato. Sattamīniddese pubbasseva vidhīti pubbasaralopo. Lokaggapuggalo, paññindriyaṃ, tīṇimāni, no hetaṃ, bhikkhunovādo, mātupaṭṭhānaṃ, sametāyasmā, abhibhāyatanaṃ, dhanaṃmatthi, sabbeva, tayassu dhammā, asante+ttha na dissanti. Pubbassa kāriyavidhānā sattamīniddiṭṭhassa paratā+va gamyateti pareti paravacanampi ghaṭate.

This meta-rule operates by the 'principle of the elder's staff,' because a weak rule has no standing. When a condition is specified in the locative case, the operation applies only to the preceding element; hence, the preceding vowel is elided. Examples: lokaggapuggalo, paññindriyaṃ, tīṇimāni, no hetaṃ, bhikkhunovādo, mātupaṭṭhānaṃ, sametāyasmā, abhibhāyatanaṃ, dhanaṃmatthi, sabbeva, tayassu dhammā, asantettha na dissanti. Because the operation is prescribed for the preceding element, the 'following' nature of what is specified in the locative is automatically understood; thus, the use of the word 'pare' (when following) in other rules is also appropriate.

Yassa idāni, saññā iti, chāyā iva, iti api, assamaṇī asi, cakkhu indriyaṃ, akataññū asi, ākāse iva, te api, vande ahaṃ, so ahaṃ, cattāro ime, vasalo iti, moggallāno asi bījako, kathā eva kā, pāto evātī+dha pubbassaralope sampatte “saro lopo sare” tveva.

In cases such as: yassa idāni, saññā iti, chāyā iva, iti api, assamaṇī asi, cakkhu indriyaṃ, akataññū asi, ākāse iva, te api, vande ahaṃ, so ahaṃ, cattāro ime, vasalo iti, moggallāno asi bījako, kathā eva kā, pāto eva—here, when the elision of the preceding vowel is applicable, the rule is still 'a vowel is elided before a vowel'.

27. Paro kvaci

27. Sometimes, the subsequent one.

Saramhā paro saro kvaci lopanīyo hoti. Yassa dāni, saññāti, chāyāva, itipi, assamaṇīsi, cakkhundriyaṃ, akataññūsi, ākāseva, tepi, vandehaṃ, sohaṃ, cattārome, vasa- lobhi[M 0.0008], moggallānosi bījako, kathāva kā, pātova. Kvacīti kiṃ, paññindriyaṃ, pañcindriyāni, sattuttamo, ekūnavīsati, yassete, sugatovādo, diṭṭhāsavo, diṭṭhogho, cakkhāyatanaṃ, taṃ kutettha labbhā. “Vivakkhāto sandhayo bhavantī”ti ñāyā vatticchāpi idha sijjhati. Kvacītya+dhikāro sabbasandhīsu, tena nātippasaṅgo. (Lopasandhi).

A subsequent vowel after a vowel is sometimes subject to elision. Examples: yassa dāni, saññāti, chāyāva, itipi, assamaṇīsi, cakkhundriyaṃ, akataññūsi, ākāseva, tepi, vandehaṃ, sohaṃ, cattārome, vasaloti, moggallānosi bījako, kathāva kā, pātova. What is meant by 'sometimes'? Examples: paññindriyaṃ, pañcindriyāni, sattuttamo, ekūnavīsati, yassete, sugatovādo, diṭṭhāsavo, diṭṭhogho, cakkhāyatanaṃ, taṃ kutettha labbhā. By the maxim 'Sandhis occur according to the speaker's intention,' even the desired expression is achieved here. The governing term 'kvaci' (sometimes) extends to all sandhis; hence, there is no over-application. (Elision Sandhi).

Saro paro veti ca vattate.

The terms 'saro paro' (a subsequent vowel) and 'vā' (optionally) also continue to apply.

Tassa idaṃ, vāta īritaṃ, na upeti, vāma ūru, ati iva aññehi, vi udakaṃ itīdha pubbassaralope –

Thus here, in the elision of a preceding vowel: Tassa idaṃ, vāta īritaṃ, na upeti, vāma ūru, ati iva aññehi, vi udakaṃ.

29. Yuvaṇṇāna+meo luttā

29. Elided i-vowels and u-vowels become e and o.

Luttā sarā paresaṃ ivaṇṇuvaṇṇānaṃ e+o honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Yathāsaṃkhyānuddeso samānānaṃ.

When a preceding vowel has been elided, the following i-vowels and u-vowels optionally become e and o respectively. The enumeration according to order applies to similar elements.

24. Vaṇṇaparena savaṇṇopi

24. By the mention of a sound, also its homogeneous counterpart.

Vaṇṇasaddo paro yasmā, tena savaṇṇopi gayhati sayañca rūpaṃti īūnampi e+o. Sabbattha rassassa jātiniddese dīghassāpi gahaṇatthaṃ ida+māraddhaṃ. Tassedaṃ, vāteritaṃ, nopeti, vāmoru, atevaññehi, vodakaṃ. Idañca pacchimodāharaṇadvayaṃ “avaṇṇe lutte eva e+o hontī”ti gāhassa nisedhanatthaṃ. Vātveva, tassidaṃ. Kathaṃ “paccorasmi”nti, yogavibhāgā. Pati urasminti vibhajja “yavā sare”ti yakāre “tavaggavaraṇā”dinā co, “vaggalasehi te”ti pubbarūpañca, “yuvaṇṇāna+meo”ti (yogavibhāgā) ussa o ca. Luttāti kiṃ, dasa ime [M 0.0009] dhammā, yathā idaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā. Atippasaṅgabādhakassa kvacisaddassānuvattanato na vikappavidhi niyatā, tena upeto, aveccāti evamādīsu vikappo. Tārakitā, yassindriyāni, mahiddhiko, sabbītiyo, tenupasaṅkami, lokuttarotiādīsu vidhi ca na hoti.

Because the word 'vaṇṇa' is subsequent, by that its homogeneous counterpart is also taken, as well as its own form; thus 'ī' and 'ū' also become 'e' and 'o'. This rule is introduced for the purpose of including long vowels in the generic designation of short vowels everywhere. Examples: Tassedaṃ, vāteritaṃ, nopeti, vāmoru, atevaññehi, vodakaṃ. This latter pair of examples serves to negate the view that 'e' and 'o' occur only when an a-vowel is elided. Optional forms: Vātveva, tassidaṃ. How is 'paccorasmi' formed? By a division of the rule. Dividing 'pati urasmi': the 'i' becomes 'y' by 'yavā sare'; the 't' becomes 'c' by 'tavaggavaraṇā...'; the 'y' assimilates to the preceding 'c' by 'vaggalasehi te'; and the 'u' becomes 'o' by a division of the rule 'yuvaṇṇānaṃ eo'. Why the word 'luttā' (elided)? To exclude cases like: dasa ime dhammā, yathā idaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā. Due to the continuation of the word 'kvaci', which prevents over-application, this optional rule is not universally applied; thus, in cases like upeto, avecca, and so on, there is an option. And in cases like tārakitā, yassindriyāni, mahiddhiko, sabbītiyo, tenupasaṅkami, lokuttaro, and so on, the rule does not apply.

Paṭisanthāravutti assa, sabbavitti anubhūyate, vi añjanaṃ, vi ākato, dāsī ahaṃ, ahuvā pure, anu addhamāsaṃ, anu eti, su āgataṃ, su ākāro, du ākāro, cakkhu āpāthaṃ, bahu ābādho, pātu akāsi, na tu eva, bhū āpanalānilaṃ itī+dha “yuvaṇṇānaṃ” “ve”ti ca vattate,

Herein: Paṭisanthāravutti assa, sabbavitti anubhūyate, vi añjanaṃ, vi ākato, dāsī ahaṃ, ahuvā pure, anu addhamāsaṃ, anu eti, su āgataṃ, su ākāro, du ākāro, cakkhu āpāthaṃ, bahu ābādho, pātu akāsi, na tu eva, bhū āpanalānilaṃ. Thus here, the rules concerning 'yuvaṇṇānaṃ' (i- and u-vowels) and 'vā' (optionally) are current.

30. Yavā sare

30. Y and v before a vowel.

Sare pare ivaṇṇuvaṇṇānaṃ yakāra+vakārā honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Paṭisanthāravutyassa, sabbavityanubhūyate, byañjanaṃ, byākato “byañjane dīgharassā”ti dīghe dāsyāhaṃ, ahāpure, anvaddhamāsaṃ, anveti, svāgataṃ, svākāro, dvākāro, cakkhvāpāthaṃ, bahvābādho, pātvākāsi, na tveva, bhvāpanalānilaṃ. Vātveva, viākato, sāgataṃ.

When a vowel follows, i-vowels and u-vowels optionally become y and v respectively. Examples: Paṭisanthāravutyassa, sabbavityanubhūyate, byañjanaṃ, byākato; with lengthening by 'byañjane dīgharassā': dāsyāhaṃ; ahāpure, anvaddhamāsaṃ, anveti, svāgataṃ, svākāro, dvākāro, cakkhvāpāthaṃ, bahvābādho, pātvākāsi, na tveva, bhvāpanalānilaṃ. Alternative forms where the rule is not applied: Vātveva, viākato, sāgataṃ.

Adhigato kho me ayaṃ dhammo, putto te ahaṃ, te assa pahīnā pañca, te ahaṃ, ye assa, te ajja, yāvatako assa kāyo, tāvatako assa byāmo, ko attho, atha kho assa, ahaṃ kho ajja, so ahaṃ, so ajja, so eva, yato adhikaraṇaṃ, so ahaṃ itī+dha “yavā sare” “ve”ti ca vattate,

Herein: Adhigato kho me ayaṃ dhammo, putto te ahaṃ, te assa pahīnā pañca, te ahaṃ, ye assa, te ajja, yāvatako assa kāyo, tāvatako assa byāmo, ko attho, atha kho assa, ahaṃ kho ajja, so ahaṃ, so ajja, so eva, yato adhikaraṇaṃ, so ahaṃ. Thus here, the rules 'yavā sare' and 'vā' (optionally) are current.

30. Eonaṃ

30. Of e and o.

Eonaṃ [M 0.0010] yakāra+vakārā honti vā sare pare yathākkamaṃ. “Byañjane dīgharassā”ti dīghe adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo, putto tyāhaṃ, tyāssa pahīnā pañca, tyāhaṃ, yyassa, tyajja, yāvatakvassa kāyo, tāvatakvassa byāmo, kvattho, atha khvassa, ahaṃ khvajja, svāhaṃ, svajja, sveva, yatvādhikaraṇaṃ, svāhaṃ. Vātveva, tejja, sohaṃ. Kvaci tveva, dhanamatthi, puttāmatthi, te nāgatā, asantettha, cattāro ime.

When a vowel follows, 'e' and 'o' optionally become 'y' and 'v' respectively. With lengthening by 'byañjane dīgharassā': adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo. Examples: putto tyāhaṃ, tyāssa pahīnā pañca, tyāhaṃ, yyassa, tyajja, yāvatakvassa kāyo, tāvatakvassa byāmo, kvattho, atha khvassa, ahaṃ khvajja, svāhaṃ, svajja, sveva, yatvādhikaraṇaṃ, svāhaṃ. Alternative forms: Vātveva, tejja, sohaṃ. However, only sometimes (kvaci): dhanamatthi, puttāmatthi, te nāgatā, asantettha, cattāro ime.

Go eḷakaṃ, go assaṃ, go ajinaṃ itī+dha “sare”ti vattate.

Herein: Go eḷakaṃ, go assaṃ, go ajinaṃ. Thus here, the rule concerning 'sare' (when a vowel follows) is current.

32. Gossā+vaṅa

32. For go, ava.

Sare pare gossa avavādeso hoti. Sa ca “ṭānubandhānekavaṇṇā sabbassā”ti sabbassa pasaṅge ‘antassā”ti vattate.

When a vowel follows, 'go' is replaced by the substitute 'ava'. And while, by the rule 'substitutions with a ṭ-anubandha or of more than one sound are for the whole', application to the whole is possible, the rule 'antassa' (of the last) is current.

18. Ṅa+nubandho

18. The ṅa-anubandha.

Ṅa-kāro anubandho yassa, so anekavaṇṇopi antassa hotīti okārasseva hoti. “Saṃketo+navayavo+nubandho”ti vacanā ṅa-kārassā+ppayogo. Uccāritānantarappadhaṃsino hi anubandhā, payojanaṃ anubandhoti saṃketo. Gaveḷakaṃ, gavāssaṃ, gavājinaṃ.

That which has 'ṅa' as an anubandha, even if it consists of more than one sound, applies to the last sound; thus, it applies only to the o-sound. By the statement 'an anubandha is a convention, not a component part,' the ṅa-sound itself is not applied. Indeed, anubandhas perish immediately after being uttered; the convention is that an anubandha serves a purpose. Examples: Gaveḷakaṃ, gavāssaṃ, gavājinaṃ.

Iti evā+tī+dha –

In the case of 'iti eva', thus here:

36. Vī+tisse+ve vā

36. V for the i of iti before eva, optionally.

Evasadde pare itissa vo hoti vā. Sa ca –

When the word 'eva' follows, the 'i' of 'iti' is optionally replaced by 'v'. And that:

17. Chaṭṭhiyantassa

17. Of that specified by the genitive.

Chaṭṭhīniddiṭṭhassa [M 0.0011] yaṃ kāriyaṃ, ta+dantassa viññeyyanti ikārassā+deso. Ādesiṭṭhāne ādissatīti ādeso. Itveva. Aññatra yādeso, “tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavaggabayañā”ti tassa co, “vaggalasehi te”ti yassa cakāro, icceva. Eveti kiṃ, iccāha. (Ādesasandhi).

Whatever operation is specified by the genitive case should be understood as applying to the final sound of that word; thus, this is a substitution for the i-sound. A substitute (ādeso) is so called because it is enjoined in the place of that which is to be replaced. Example: itveva. Elsewhere, there is the substitution of 'y'; by 'tavaggavaraṇānaṃ...', the 't' becomes 'c'; by 'vaggalasehi te', the 'y' assimilates to 'c', resulting in 'icceva'. Why the word 'eva'? To exclude cases like 'iccāha'. (End of Substitution Sandhi).

Ti aṅgulaṃ,ti aṅgikaṃ, bhū ādayo, migī bhantā udikkhatityādisandhayo vuccante. “Mayadā sare”ti vattate.

'Ti aṅgulaṃ', 'ti aṅgikaṃ', 'bhū ādayo', 'migī bhantā udikkhati'—sandhis such as these are now discussed. The rule 'Mayadā sare' is current.

45. Vanataragā cā+gamā

45. Va, na, ta, ra, and ga are also augments.

Ete mayadā ca āgamā honti vā sare kvaci. Āgamino aniyamepi –

These—ma, ya, da—also become augments, optionally and in some cases, before a vowel. Even when that to which the augment is attached is not specified:

Saroyevā+gami hoti, vanādinantu ñāpakā;

Aññathā hi padādīnaṃ, yukavidhāna+manatthakaṃ.

The vowel itself is that to which the augment is attached; 'vana' and so forth are merely indicators. Otherwise, the rule prescribing the 'yuk' augment for the beginning of words would be pointless.

Etthā+gamā aniyatāgamīnameva bhavanti ce, yakārāgameneva “nipajja”nti siddhe “padādīnaṃ kvacī”ti byañjanassa yukā+gamo niratthakoti adhippāyo. Tivaṅgulaṃ, tivaṅgikaṃ, bhūvādayo, migī bhantā vudikkhati, pavuccati, pāguññavujutā. Ito nāyati, cinitvā. Yasmātiha, tasmātiha, ajjatagge. Nirantaraṃ, nirālayo, nirindhano, nirīhakaṃ, niruttaro, nirojaṃ, duratikkamo, durāgataṃ, duruttaraṃ, pāturahosi, punarāgaccheyya, punaruttaṃ, punareva, punareti, dhīratthu, pātarāso, caturaṅgikaṃ, caturārakkhaṃ, caturiddhipādapaṭilābho, caturoghanittharaṇatthaṃ, bhatturatthe, vuttiresā, pathavīdhāturevesā[M 0.0012], nakkhattarājāriva tārakānaṃ, vijjurivabbhakuṭe, āraggeriva sāsapo, usabhoriva, sabbhireva samāsetha. Puthageva, rasse pageva. Lahumessati, gurumessati, idhamāhu, kena te idha mijjhati, bhadro kasāmiva, ākāse mabhipūjaye, ekamekassa, yena midhekacce. Bhātiyeva, hotiyeva, yathāyidaṃ, yathāyeva, māyidaṃ, nayidaṃ, nayidha, chayimāni, navayime dhammā, bodhiyāyeva, pathavīyeva dhātu, tesuyeva, teyeva, soyeva, pāṭiyekkaṃ, viyañjanaṃ, viyākāsi, pariyantaṃ, pariyādānaṃ, pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, pariyesati, pariyosānaṃ, niyāyogo. Udaggo, udayo, udāhaṭaṃ, udito, udīritaṃ, udeti, sakideva, kiñcideva, kenacideva, kismiñcideva, kocideva, sammadatto, sammadaññā vimuttānaṃ, sammadeva, yāvadatthaṃ, yāvadicchakaṃ, yāvadeva, tāvadeva, punadeva, yadatthaṃ, yadantaraṃ, tadantaraṃ, tadaṅgavimutti, etadatthaṃ, attadatthaṃ, tadatthaṃ, sadatthapasuto siyā, aññadatthu, manasādaññā vimuttānaṃ, bahudeva ratti. Vātveva, attaatthaṃ, dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ, pātuahosi. Vavatthitavibhāsattā vādhikārassa byañjanatopi, bhikkhunīnaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, ciraṃ nāyati, taṃyeva.

The meaning is this: if augments here were only for recipients that are not specified, then, since 'nipajjanti' is formed by the 'y' augment alone, the 'yuk' augment prescribed for a consonant by 'padādīnaṃ kvacī' would be pointless. Examples: Tivaṅgulaṃ, tivaṅgikaṃ, bhūvādayo, migī bhantā vudikkhati, pavuccati, pāguññavujutā, ito nāyati, cinitvā, yasmātiha, tasmātiha, ajjatagge, nirantaraṃ, nirālayo, nirindhano, nirīhakaṃ, niruttaro, nirojaṃ, duratikkamo, durāgataṃ, duruttaraṃ, pāturahosi, punarāgaccheyya, punaruttaṃ, punareva, punareti, dhīratthu, pātarāso, caturaṅgikaṃ, caturārakkhaṃ, caturiddhipādapaṭilābho, caturoghanittharaṇatthaṃ, bhatturatthe, vuttiresā, pathavīdhāturevesā, nakkhattarājāriva tārakānaṃ, vijjurivabbhakuṭe, āraggeriva sāsapo, usabhoriva, sabbhireva samāsetha, puthageva, rasse pageva, lahumessati, gurumessati, idhamāhu, kena te idha mijjhati, bhadro kasāmiva, ākāse mabhipūjaye, ekamekassa, yena midhekacce, bhātiyeva, hotiyeva, yathāyidaṃ, yathāyeva, māyidaṃ, nayidaṃ, nayidha, chayimāni, navayime dhammā, bodhiyāyeva, pathavīyeva dhātu, tesuyeva, teyeva, soyeva, pāṭiyekkaṃ, viyañjanaṃ, viyākāsi, pariyantaṃ, pariyādānaṃ, pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, pariyesati, pariyosānaṃ, niyāyogo, udaggo, udayo, udāhaṭaṃ, udito, udīritaṃ, udeti, sakideva, kiñcideva, kenacideva, kismiñcideva, kocideva, sammadatto, sammadaññā vimuttānaṃ, sammadeva, yāvadatthaṃ, yāvadicchakaṃ, yāvadeva, tāvadeva, punadeva, yadatthaṃ, yadantaraṃ, tadantaraṃ, tadaṅgavimutti, etadatthaṃ, attadatthaṃ, tadatthaṃ, sadatthapasuto siyā, aññadatthu, manasādaññā vimuttānaṃ, bahudeva ratti. Alternative forms: attaatthaṃ, dvādhiṭṭhitaṃ, pātuahosi. Because the governing rule 'vā' denotes a systematic option, augments may occur even after a consonant: bhikkhunīnaṃ vuṭṭhāpeyya, ciraṃ nāyati, taṃyeva.

Cha abhiññā, cha aṅgaṃ, cha asīti, cha aṃsā, cha āyatanaṃ itī+dha “vā sare” “āgamo”ti ca vattate.

Six higher knowledges, six factors, six eighties, six parts, six sense bases—herein, 'vā sare' and 'āgamo' are current.

49. Chā ḷo

49. After `cha`, `ḷ`.

Chasaddā parassa sarassa ḷakāro āgamo hoti vā. Chāti anukaraṇattā ekavacanaṃ. Chaḷabhiññā, chaḷaṅgaṃ, chaḷasīti, chaḷaṃsā, chaḷāyatanaṃ. Vātveva, chaabhiññā. (Āgamasandhi).

After the word `cha`, the letter `ḷ` is optionally an augment to the following vowel. `Cha` is singular because it is an imitation. Examples: Chaḷabhiññā, chaḷaṅgaṃ, chaḷasīti, chaḷaṃsā, chaḷāyatanaṃ. Alternatively, `chaabhiññā`. (Augment-sandhi).

Lopo [M 0.0013] adassanaṃ, ṭhāniṃ, ya+māmaddiya dissati;

Ādeso nāma so yā tu, asantuppatti āgamo.

Elision is the non-appearance of an original element, understood as suppressed. A substitution is that which replaces, while an augment is the arising of what was not previously present.

Sarasandhi.

Vowel Sandhi.

Kaññā iva, kaññāva iccādi sarasandhinisedho vuccati, pasaṅgapubbako hi paṭisedho. Pubbasarānaṃ lope sampatte “saro” “ve”ti ca vattate.

In cases such as 'Kaññā iva', 'kaññāva', and so forth, the prohibition of vowel sandhi is spoken of. For a prohibition is indeed preceded by a contingency. When the elision of preceding vowels is applicable, 'saro' and 've' are current.

28. Na dve vā

28. Not both, optionally.

Pubbaparassarā dvepi vā kvaci na lupyante. Kaññā iva, kaññeva, kaññāva.

Sometimes both the preceding and following vowels are optionally not elided. Examples: Kaññā iva, kaññeva, kaññāva.

Sāriputta idhekacco, ehi sivaka uṭṭhehi, āyasmā ānando, gāthā abhāsi, devā ābhassarā yathā, tevijjā iddhipattā ca, bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā, bhagavā eta+davoca, abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi, gantvā olokento, bhūtavādī atthavādī, yaṃ itthī arahaṃ assa, sāmāvatī āha, pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati, nadī ottharati, ye te bhikkhū appicchā, bhikkhū āmantesi, bhikkhū ujjhāyiṃsu, bhikkhū eva+māhaṃsu, imasmiṃ gāme ārakkhakā, sabbe ime, katame ekādasa, gambhīre odakantike, appamādo amataṃ padaṃ, saṅgho āgacchatu, ko imaṃ pathaviṃ vicessati, āloko udapādi, eko ekāya, cattāro oghā, are ahampi, sace imassa kāyassa, no atikkamo, aho acchariyo, atho anto ca, atha kho āyasmā, atho oṭṭhava+cittakā, tato ā- mantayi [M 0.0014] satthāti evamādayo idha kālabyavadhāneneva sijjhanti. Kvacīti kiṃ, āgatā+ttha, āgatā+mhā, katama+ssa vāro, appassutā+yaṃ puriso, camarī+va, sabbe+va, sve+va, ese+va nayo, parisuddhe+tthā+yasmanto, ne+ttha, kute+ttha labbhā, sace+sa brāhmaṇa, tathū+pamaṃ, yathā+ha, jīvhā+yatanaṃ, avijjo+gho, itthindriyaṃ, abhibhā+yatanaṃ, bhayatū+paṭṭhānaṃ, saddhī+dha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ. (Sarasandhinisedho)

Examples include: 'Sāriputta idhekacco', 'ehi sivaka uṭṭhehi', 'āyasmā ānando', 'gāthā abhāsi', 'devā ābhassarā yathā', 'tevijjā iddhipattā ca', 'bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā', 'bhagavā etadavoca', 'abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi', 'gantvā olokento', 'bhūtavādī atthavādī', 'yaṃ itthī arahaṃ assa', 'sāmāvatī āha', 'pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati', 'nadī ottharati', 'ye te bhikkhū appicchā', 'bhikkhū āmantesi', 'bhikkhū ujjhāyiṃsu', 'bhikkhū evaṃ āhaṃsu', 'imasmiṃ gāme ārakkhakā', 'sabbe ime', 'katame ekādasa', 'gambhīre odakantike', 'appamādo amataṃ padaṃ', 'saṅgho āgacchatu', 'ko imaṃ pathaviṃ vicessati', 'āloko udapādi', 'eko ekāya', 'cattāro oghā', 'are ahampi', 'sace imassa kāyassa', 'no atikkamo', 'aho acchariyo', 'atho anto ca', 'atha kho āyasmā', 'atho oṭṭhavacittakā', 'tato āmantayi satthā'ti, and so forth; these are accomplished here by means of temporal separation. Why 'sometimes' (`kvaci`)? [Because sandhi does occur in cases like:] 'āgatāttha', 'āgatāmhā', 'katamassa vāro', 'appassutāyaṃ puriso', 'camarīva', 'sabbeva', 'sveva', 'eseva nayo', 'parisuddhetthāyasmanto', 'nettha', 'kutettha labbhā', 'sacesa brāhmaṇa', 'tathūpamaṃ', 'yathāha', 'jivhāyatanaṃ', 'avijjogho', 'itthindriyaṃ', 'abhibhāyatanaṃ', 'bhayatūpaṭṭhānaṃ', 'saddhīdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ'. (Prohibition of Vowel Sandhi).

Tatra abhirati, tatra ayaṃ, buddha anussati, sa atthikā, saññāvā assa, tadā ahaṃ, yāni idha bhūtāni, gacchāmi iti, ati ito, kikī iva, bahu upakāraṃ, madhu udakaṃ, su upadhāritaṃ, sopi ayaṃ, idāni ahaṃ, sace ayaṃ, appassuto ayaṃ, itara itarena, saddhā idha vittaṃ, kamma upanissayo, tathā upamaṃ, ratti uparato, vi upasamo, lokassa iti, deva iti, vi atipatanti, vi atināmenti, saṅghāṭi api, jīvitahetu api, vijju iva, kiṃsu idha vittaṃ, sādhu iti, te assa pahīnā, so assa, madhuvā maññati bālo, evaṃ gāme muni care, khanti paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, na maṃku bhavissāmi, su akkhāto, yo ahaṃ, so ahaṃ, kāmato jāyati soko, kāmato jāyati bhayaṃ, sakko uju ca suhujuca, anupaghāto, durakkhaṃ, duramaṃ, dubharatā. Yiṭṭhaṃ vā hutaṃ vā loke, yadi vā sāvake, puggalā dhammadasā te, bhovādī nāma so hoti, yathābhāvī guṇena so, yathā idaṃ, sammā dakkhāto, parā kamo, taṇhā kkhayo, jhānassa lābhī amhi, thullaccayo itī+dha –

In these cases: Tatra abhirati, tatra ayaṃ, buddha anussati, sa atthikā, saññāvā assa, tadā ahaṃ, yāni idha bhūtāni, gacchāmi iti, ati ito, kikī iva, bahu upakāraṃ, madhu udakaṃ, su upadhāritaṃ, sopi ayaṃ, idāni ahaṃ, sace ayaṃ, appassuto ayaṃ, itara itarena, saddhā idha vittaṃ, kamma upanissayo, tathā upamaṃ, ratti uparato, vi upasamo, lokassa iti, deva iti, vi atipatanti, vi atināmenti, saṅghāṭi api, jīvitahetu api, vijju iva, kiṃsu idha vittaṃ, sādhu iti, te assa pahīnā, so assa, madhuvā maññati bālo, evaṃ gāme muni care, khanti paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, na maṃku bhavissāmi, su akkhāto, yo ahaṃ, so ahaṃ, kāmato jāyati soko, kāmato jāyati bhayaṃ, sakko uju ca suhujuca, anupaghāto, durakkhaṃ, duramaṃ, dubharatā, yiṭṭhaṃ vā hutaṃ vā loke, yadi vā sāvake, puggalā dhammadasā te, bhovādī nāma so hoti, yathābhāvī guṇena so, yathā idaṃ, sammā dakkhāto, parā kamo, taṇhā kkhayo, jhānassa lābhī amhi, thullaccayo.

33. Byañjane dīgharassā

33. Before a consonant, lengthening and shortening.

Rassa+dīghānaṃ [M 0.0015] kvaci dīgha+rassā honti byañjane. Tatrābhirati, tatrāyaṃ, buddhānussati, sātthikā, saññāvā+ssa, tadāhaṃ, yānī+dha bhūtāni, gacchāmīti, atīto, kikīva, bahūpakāraṃ, madhūdakaṃ, sūpadhāritaṃ, sopāyaṃ, idānāhaṃ, sacāyaṃ, appassutāyaṃ, itarītarena, saddhīdha vittaṃ, kammūpanissayo, tathūpamaṃ, rattūparato, vūpasamo, lokassāti, devāti, vītipatanti, vītināmenti, saṅghāṭīpi, jīvitahetūpi, vijjūva, kiṃsūdha vittaṃ, sādhūti, tyāssa pahīnā, svāssa, madhuvā maññatī bālo, evaṃ gāme munī care, khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, na maṃkū bhavissāmi, svākkhāto, yvāhaṃ, svāhaṃ, kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṃ, sakko ujū ca suhujū ca, anūpaghāto, dūrakkhaṃ, dūramaṃ, dūbharatā. Yiṭṭhaṃva hutaṃva loke, yadiva sāvake, puggala dhammadasā te, bhovādi nāma so hoti, yathābhāvi guṇena so, yathayidaṃ, sammadakkhāto, parakkamo, taṇhakkhayo, jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi, thullaccayo. Kvacīti kiṃ, tyajja, svassa, patiliyatīti dīghanisedho, māyidaṃ, manasādaññā vimuttānaṃ, yathākkamaṃ, ārakkhātītaṃ, dīyati, sūyatīti rassakāriyanisedho. Kathaṃ yāniva antalikkheti, “dīgharassā”ti yogavibhāgā. (Dīgha+rassasandhi).

Before a consonant, short and long vowels sometimes become long and short. Examples: Tatrābhirati, tatrāyaṃ, buddhānussati, sātthikā, saññāvāssa, tadāhaṃ, yānīdha bhūtāni, gacchāmīti, atīto, kikīva, bahūpakāraṃ, madhūdakaṃ, sūpadhāritaṃ, sopāyaṃ, idānāhaṃ, sacāyaṃ, appassutāyaṃ, itarītarena, saddhīdha vittaṃ, kammūpanissayo, tathūpamaṃ, rattūparato, vūpasamo, lokassāti, devāti, vītipatanti, vītināmenti, saṅghāṭīpi, jīvitahetūpi, vijjūva, kiṃsūdha vittaṃ, sādhūti, tyāssa pahīnā, svāssa, madhuvā maññatī bālo, evaṃ gāme munī care, khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, na maṃkū bhavissāmi, svākkhāto, yvāhaṃ, svāhaṃ, kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṃ, sakko ujū ca suhujū ca, anūpaghāto, dūrakkhaṃ, dūramaṃ, dūbharatā, yiṭṭhaṃva hutaṃva loke, yadiva sāvake, puggala dhammadasā te, bhovādi nāma so hoti, yathābhāvi guṇena so, yathayidaṃ, sammadakkhāto, parakkamo, taṇhakkhayo, jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi, thullaccayo. Why 'sometimes' (`kvaci`)? [Because the rule does not apply in cases like:] tyajja, svassa. In `patiliyati`, there is a prohibition of lengthening; [also in] māyidaṃ, manasādaññā vimuttānaṃ, yathākkamaṃ, ārakkhātītaṃ. In `dīyati` and `sūyati`, there is a prohibition of the shortening operation. How then is `yāniva antalikkhe` explained? By splitting the rule (`yogavibhāga`) `dīgharassā`. (Lengthening and Shortening Sandhi).

Byañjaneti vattate.

The word 'before a consonant' is carried forward.

34. Saramhā dve

34. After a vowel, two.

Saramhā parassa byañjanassa kvaci dve rūpāni honti. Ettha ca āvuttidvivacanaṃ ṭhānedvivacananti dvīsu ṭhānedvivacanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

After a vowel, the following consonant sometimes takes a double form. And here, doubling by repetition and doubling by position—in these two cases, doubling should be understood.

Tāni [M 0.0016] ca pa+pati+paṭi+kama+kusa+kudha+kī+gaha+juta+ñā+si+ su+sū+sambhū+sara+sasādīnamādibyañjanānañca hoti. Idha pamādo=idhappamādo, evaṃ appamādo, vippayutto, suppasanno, sammā padhānaṃ=sammappadhānaṃ rassattaṃ. Appativattiyo, adhippatipaccayo, suppatiṭṭhito,. Appaṭipuggalo, vippaṭisāro, suppaṭipatti. Pakkamo, paṭikkamo, hetukkamo, ākamati=akkamati, evaṃ pakkamati, yathākkamaṃ. Akkosati, paṭikkosati, anukkosati, ākosati=akkosati. Akkuddho, abhikkuddho. Dhanakkīto, vikkayo, anukkayo. Paggaho, viggaho, anuggaho, candaggāho, diṭṭhiggāho. Pajjoto, vijjoto, ujjoto. Kataññū, viññū, paññāṇaṃ, viññāṇaṃ, anaññāṇaṃ. Avassayo, nissayo, samussayo. Appassuto, vissuto, bahussuto. Āsavā=assavā. Passambhento, vissambhento. Aṭṭassaro, vissarati, anussarati, anussati. Passasanto, vissasanto, muhussasanto, āsāso=assāso. Ādisaddena avissajento, vissajento, abhikkantataro, pariccajento, upaddavo, upakkileso, mittadduno, āyabyayo, abbahi iccādi.

And this occurs for the initial consonants of words beginning with pa, pati, paṭi, kama, kusa, kudha, kī, gaha, juta, ñā, si, su, sū, sambhū, sara, and sasa, etc. For example: idha pamādo = idhappamādo; similarly, appamādo, vippayutto, suppasanno; sammā padhānaṃ = sammappadhānaṃ, with shortening. Appativattiyo, adhippatipaccayo, suppatiṭṭhito. Appaṭipuggalo, vippaṭisāro, suppaṭipatti. Pakkamo, paṭikkamo, hetukkamo; ākamati = akkamati; similarly, pakkamati, yathākkamaṃ. Akkosati, paṭikkosati, anukkosati; ākosati = akkosati. Akkuddho, abhikkuddho. Dhanakkīto, vikkayo, anukkayo. Paggaho, viggaho, anuggaho, candaggāho, diṭṭhiggāho. Pajjoto, vijjoto, ujjoto. Kataññū, viññū, paññāṇaṃ, viññāṇaṃ, anaññāṇaṃ. Avassayo, nissayo, samussayo. Appassuto, vissuto, bahussuto. Āsavā = assavā. Passambhento, vissambhento. Aṭṭassaro, vissarati, anussarati, anussati. Passasanto, vissasanto, muhussasanto; āsāso = assāso. By the word 'ādi' (etc.): avissajento, vissajento, abhikkantataro, pariccajento, upaddavo, upakkileso, mittadduno, āyabyayo, abbahi, etc.

Tika+taya+tiṃsa+vatādīna+mādibyañjanassa ca. Kusalattikaṃ, pītittikaṃ, hetuttikaṃ. Lokattayaṃ, bodhittayaṃ, vatthuttayaṃ. Ekattiṃsa, dvattiṃsa, tettiṃsa, catuttiṃsa. Sīlabbataṃ, subbato. Sappītiko, samannāgato, punappunaṃ iccādi.

And also of the initial consonant of words beginning with tika, taya, tiṃsa, vata, and so forth. Kusalattikaṃ, pītittikaṃ, hetuttikaṃ. Lokattayaṃ, bodhittayaṃ, vatthuttayaṃ. Ekattiṃsa, dvattiṃsa, tettiṃsa, catuttiṃsa. Sīlabbataṃ, subbato. Sappītiko, samannāgato, punappunaṃ, and so forth.

Vatu+vaṭa+disāna+mante, yathā vattati, vaṭṭati, dassanaṃ, phasso iccādi.

Of vatu, vaṭa, and dis, at the end, as in: vattati, vaṭṭati, dassanaṃ, phasso, and so forth.

U+du+niupasagga+ta+catu+cha+santasaddādesādīhi [M 0.0017] paresañca. Ukaṃso=ukkaṃso, evaṃ dukkaraṃ, nikkaṅkho, uggataṃ, duccaritaṃ, nijjaṭaṃ, ujjahaṃ, uccaṅgaṃ, unnamati, dukkaro, niddaro, unnato, duppañño, nimmalo, uyyutto, dullabho, nibbatto, ussāho, nissāro. Takkaro, tajjo, tanninno, tappabhavo, tammayo, catukkaṃ, catuddisaṃ, catuppado, catubbidhaṃ, catussālaṃ, chakkaṃ, channavuti, chappadiko, chabbassāni. Sakkāro, sagguṇo, sandiṭṭhi, sappuriso, mahabbalo.

And also of the following consonants after the prefixes u, du, and ni, and after ta, catu, cha, and the word santa, and so forth. Ukaṃso becomes ukkaṃso; similarly, dukkaraṃ, nikkaṅkho, uggataṃ, duccaritaṃ, nijjaṭaṃ, ujjahaṃ, uccaṅgaṃ, unnamati, dukkaro, niddaro, unnato, duppañño, nimmalo, uyyutto, dullabho, nibbatto, ussāho, nissāro. Takkaro, tajjo, tanninno, tappabhavo, tammayo, catukkaṃ, catuddisaṃ, catuppado, catubbidhaṃ, catussālaṃ, chakkaṃ, channavuti, chappadiko, chabbassāni. Sakkāro, sagguṇo, sandiṭṭhi, sappuriso, mahabbalo.

Apadantaākāravajjitadīghato yakārassa ca, niyyāti, suyyati, abhibhuyya, viceyya, vineyya, dheyyaṃ, neyyaṃ, seyyo, jeyyo, veyyākaraṇo. Ākāravajjitanti kiṃ, mālāya, dolāya, samādāya.

And of the letter 'y' (yakāra) after a long vowel, with the exception of a non-final 'ā': niyyāti, suyyati, abhibhuyya, viceyya, vineyya, dheyyaṃ, neyyaṃ, seyyo, jeyyo, veyyākaraṇo. What is meant by 'with the exception of a non-final ā'? Mālāya, dolāya, samādāya.

Chandānurakkhaṇe-nappajahe vaṇṇabalaṃ purāṇaṃ, ujjugatesu seyyo, gacchanti suggatiṃ. Saramhāti kiṃ, ñāyo, taṃkhaṇaṃ. Kvacitveva, nikāyo, nidānaṃ, nivāso, tato, chasaṭṭhi, upanīyati, sūyati.

In guarding the meter, one should not abandon the ancient strength of sounds. Among the upright, he is better; they go to a good destination. What is meant by 'after a vowel'? ñāyo, taṃkhaṇaṃ. But in some cases: nikāyo, nidānaṃ, nivāso, tato, chasaṭṭhi, upanīyati, sūyati.

35. Catutthadutiyesve+saṃ tatiyapaṭhamā

35. In the fourth and second, their third and first.

Catutthadutiyesu paresve+saṃ catutthadutiyānaṃ tabbagge tatiyapaṭhamā honti paccāsatyā. Vagge gha+jha+ḍha+dha+bhā catutthā, kha+cha+ṭha+tha+phā dutiyā, ga+ja+ḍa+da+bā tatiyā, ka+ca+ṭa+ta+pā paṭhamā. Pa+u+du-niādīhi paresaṃ ghādīnaṃ dvibhāve tatiyapaṭhamā honti. Pagarati=paggharati, evaṃ uggharati, nigghoso, ugghāṭeti. Esova tajjhānaphalo, paṭhamajjhānaṃ, abhijjhā-yati[M 0.0018], ujjhāyati. Daḍḍho, buḍḍho. Viddhaṃseti, uddhaṃsito, uddhāro, niddhano, niddhuto. Vibbhanto, ubbhanto, samubbhanto, dubbhikkhaṃ, nibbhayaṃ, tabbhāvo, catubbhi. Saddhā, saddhammo. Mahabbhayaṃ.

When fourth and second consonants follow, for these fourth and second consonants, the third and first of their own class occur respectively, due to proximity. In a class, gha, jha, ḍha, dha, bha are the fourth consonants; kha, cha, ṭha, tha, pha are the second; ga, ja, ḍa, da, ba are the third; ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa are the first. When the fourth consonants, etc., following pa, u, du, ni, and so forth, are doubled, the third and first consonants occur. Pagarati becomes paggharati; similarly, uggharati, nigghoso, ugghāṭeti. Eso'va tajjhānaphalo, paṭhamajjhānaṃ, abhijjhāyati, ujjhāyati. Daḍḍho, buḍḍho. Viddhaṃseti, uddhaṃsito, uddhāro, niddhano, niddhuto. Vibbhanto, ubbhanto, samubbhanto, dubbhikkhaṃ, nibbhayaṃ, tabbhāvo, catubbhi. Saddhā, saddhammo. Mahabbhayaṃ.

Rassasarehi paresaṃ vaggadutiyānaṃ dvibhāvo ce, paṭhamā. Pañcakkhandhā, evaṃ rūpakkhandho, akkhamo, abhikkhaṇaṃ, avikkhepo, jātikkhettaṃ, dhātukkhobho, āyukkhayo. Setacchattaṃ, evaṃ sabbacchannaṃ, vicchannaṃ, bodhicchāyā, jambucchāyā, samucchedo. Tatra ṭhito=tatraṭṭhito, evaṃ thalaṭṭhaṃ, jalaṭṭhaṃ, aṭṭhitaṃ, niṭṭhitaṃ, cattāriṭṭhānāni, garuṭṭhāniyo, samuṭṭhito. Sabbatthāmena, yasatthero, pattharati, vitthāro, abhitthuto, vitthambhito, anutthunaṃ. Papphoṭeti, mahapphalaṃ, anipphalaṃ, vipphāro, paripphuṭeyya, madhupphāṇitaṃ. Ākārato, ākhāto=akkhāto, evaṃ taṇhākkhayo, āṇākkhettaṃ, saññākkhandho. Āchādayi=acchādayi, evaṃ acchindati, nāvaṭṭhaṃ, attharati, apphoṭeti. Kvaci tveva, puvakhajjakaṃ, tassa chaviādīni chinditvā, yathāṭhitaṃ, kammaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ tassa jhāyino, ye jhānappasutā dhīrā, nidhanaṃ, mahādhanaṃ. (Dvibhāvasandhi).

If there is doubling of the second consonant of a class following short vowels, then it becomes the first consonant. Pañcakkhandhā; similarly, rūpakkhandho, akkhamo, abhikkhaṇaṃ, avikkhepo, jātikkhettaṃ, dhātukkhobho, āyukkhayo. Setacchattaṃ; similarly, sabbacchannaṃ, vicchannaṃ, bodhicchāyā, jambucchāyā, samucchedo. Tatra ṭhito becomes tatraṭṭhito; similarly, thalaṭṭhaṃ, jalaṭṭhaṃ, aṭṭhitaṃ, niṭṭhitaṃ, cattāriṭṭhānāni, garuṭṭhāniyo, samuṭṭhito. Sabbatthāmena, yasatthero, pattharati, vitthāro, abhitthuto, vitthambhito, anutthunaṃ. Papphoṭeti, mahapphalaṃ, anipphalaṃ, vipphāro, paripphuṭeyya, madhupphāṇitaṃ. Ākārato, ākhāto becomes akkhāto; similarly, taṇhākkhayo, āṇākkhettaṃ, saññākkhandho. Āchādayi becomes acchādayi; similarly, acchindati, nāvaṭṭhaṃ, attharati, apphoṭeti. But in some cases: puvakhajjakaṃ, tassa chaviādīni chinditvā, yathāṭhitaṃ, kammaphalaṃ, sīlaṃ tassa jhāyino, ye jhānappasutā dhīrā, nidhanaṃ, mahādhanaṃ. (Doubling Sandhi).

Akaramha se te, so kho byanti kāhiti, so gacchaṃ na nivattati, eso attho, eso ābhogo, eso idāni itī+dha “ve”ti vattate.

Akaramha se te, so kho byanti kāhiti, so gacchaṃ na nivattati, eso attho, eso ābhogo, eso idāni—in this case, the rule 've' applies.

37. Eona+ma vaṇṇe

37. Of e and o, a, when a consonant follows.

Eonaṃ vaṇṇe kvaci a hoti vā. Akaramha sa te, akaramha se te, evaṃ sa kho byanti kāhiti, sa gacchaṃ na nivattati, esa attho[M 0.0019], esa ābhogo, esa idāni. Vaṇṇeti kiṃ, amoghavacano ca so, gandhabbānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassi soti. “Na sandhisamāsā vaddhassā”ti vuttattā gāthāmajjhe sandhi na hotīti “tividhassā”ti vuttatimhi parepi vaṇṇo paro nāma na iti. (Sarabyañjanasandhi).

Of e and o, 'a' optionally occurs when a consonant follows. Akaramha sa te, akaramha se te; similarly, sa kho byanti kāhiti, sa gacchaṃ na nivattati, esa attho, esa ābhogo, esa idāni. What is the purpose of 'when a consonant follows'? amoghavacano ca so, gandhabbānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassi so'ti. Because it is said, 'There is no sandhi or compound for an augmented form,' sandhi does not occur in the middle of a verse; thus, even when 'tividhassā' is stated, a following sound is not considered to be following. (Vowel-Consonant Sandhi).

Ata yantaṃ, tatha yaṃ, mada yaṃ, budha yati, dhana yaṃ, seva yo, para yesanā, pokkharaṇa yo itī+dha –

Ata yantaṃ, tatha yaṃ, mada yaṃ, budha yati, dhana yaṃ, seva yo, para yesanā, pokkharaṇa yo—in this case—

48. Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ ye cavagga bayañā

48. Of the letters of the ta-class, va, and ra, when ya follows, the ca-class, ba, and ña.

Tavaggavaraṇānaṃ cavaggabayañā honti yathākkamaṃ yakāre. “Vaggalasehi te”ti pubbarūpaṃ. Accantaṃ, tacchaṃ, majjaṃ, bujjhati, dhaññaṃ, sebbo, payyesanā, pokkharañño. Apuccaṇḍakāyaṃ, jaccandho, yajjevaṃ, ajjhagamā, ajjhattaṃ, ajjhupagato, ajjhogāhetvā, dibbaṃ. Kvacitveva, ratyā.

For the letters of the ta-class, va, and ra, the ca-class letters, ba, and ña occur respectively when ya follows. The preceding form is 'Vaggalasehi te'. Accantaṃ, tacchaṃ, majjaṃ, bujjhati, dhaññaṃ, sebbo, payyesanā, pokkharañño. Apuccaṇḍakāyaṃ, jaccandho, yajjevaṃ, ajjhagamā, ajjhattaṃ, ajjhupagato, ajjhogāhetvā, dibbaṃ. But in some cases, ratyā.

Saka yate, ruca yate, paca yate, aṭa yate, lupa yate, kupa yate, sala yate, phala yate, disa yate, asa yate itī+dha “ye”ti vattate vakkhamānesu dvīsu.

Saka yate, ruca yate, paca yate, aṭa yate, lupa yate, kupa yate, sala yate, phala yate, disa yate, asa yate—in this case, 'ye' applies in the two rules about to be stated.

49. Vaggalasehite

49. After class consonants, la, and sa, they are assimilated.

Vaggalasehi parassa yakārassa kvaci te vaggalasā honti. Sakkate, ruccate, paccate, aṭṭate, luppate, kuppate, sallate, phallate, dissate, assate. Kvacitveva, kyāhaṃ.

Following class consonants, la, and sa, a following 'ya' sometimes becomes those very class consonants, la, and sa. Sakkate, ruccate, paccate, aṭṭate, luppate, kuppate, sallate, phallate, dissate, assate. But in some cases, kyāhaṃ.

Muha yati, guha yati itī+dha –

Muha yati, guha yati—in this case—

50. Hassa vipallāso

50. Transposition of 'ha'.

Hassa [M 0.0020] vipallāso hoti yakāre. Muyhati, guyhati.

The transposition of 'ha' occurs when 'ya' follows. Muyhati, guyhati.

Bahu ābādho itī+dha ussavakāre “hassa vipallāso”ti vattate.

Bahu ābādho—in this case, when 'va' follows, the rule 'transposition of ha' applies.

51. Ve vā

51. And of va, optionally.

Hassa vipallāso hoti vā vakāre. Bavhābādho. Vātveva, bahvābādho.

The transposition of 'ha' occurs optionally when 'va' follows. Bavhābādho. Or indeed, bahvābādho.

52. Tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā

52. Of ta, tha, na, and ra, ṭa, ṭha, ṇa, and la.

Tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Dukkataṃ=dukkaṭaṃ, evaṃ sukaṭaṃ, patthaṭo, pataṭo, uddhaṭo, visaṭo. Aṭṭhakathā. Paṇidhānaṃ, paṇipāto, paṇāmo, paṇītaṃ, pariṇato, pariṇāmo, duṇṇayo, niṇṇayo, oṇato. Paripanno=palipanno, evaṃ palibodho, pallaṅkaṃ, taluno, mahāsālo, māluto, sukhumālo. (Byañjanasandhi).

The letters ta, tha, na, and ra become ṭa, ṭha, ṇa, and la optionally and respectively. Dukkataṃ becomes dukkaṭaṃ; similarly, sukaṭaṃ, patthaṭo, pataṭo, uddhaṭo, visaṭo. Aṭṭhakathā. Paṇidhānaṃ, paṇipāto, paṇāmo, paṇītaṃ, pariṇato, pariṇāmo, duṇṇayo, niṇṇayo, oṇato. Paripanno becomes palipanno; similarly, palibodho, pallaṅkaṃ, taluno, mahāsālo, māluto, sukhumālo. (Consonant Sandhi).

Cakkhu udapādi, akkhi rujati, purima jāti, aṇu thūlāni, kattabba kusalaṃ bahuṃ, ta sampayuttā, tata sabhāvato itī+dha “ve”ti vattate yāva “mayadā sare”ti.

Cakkhu udapādi, akkhi rujati, purima jāti, aṇu thūlāni, kattabba kusalaṃ bahuṃ, ta sampayuttā, tata sabhāvato—in this case, the rule 've' applies up to 'mayadā sare'.

38. Niggahītaṃ

38. The Niggahīta.

Niggahītāgamo hoti vā kvaci. Sāmatthiyenā+gamova, sa ca rassasarasseva hoti… tassa rassasarānugatattā. Ṭhānīna+māliṅghiya gacchati pavattatīti āgamo. Cakkhuṃ udapādi, akkhiṃ [M 0.0021] rujati, purimaṃ jāti, aṇuṃ thūlāni, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ bahuṃ, taṃsampayuttā, taṃtaṃsabhāvato. Vāggahaṇena cakkhu udapādi iccādi. Avaṃsiro, yāvañcidaṃtiādi niccaṃ… vavatthitavibhāsattā vādhikārassa, vavatthitassa lakkhaṇassā+nurodhena lakkhaṇe pavattitā vibhāsā vavatthitavibhāsā. Vāsaddo hi atthadvaye vattate katthaci vikappe, katthaci yathāvavatthitarūpapariggaheti. Yadā pacchime, tadā nicca+manicca+masantañca vidhiṃ dīpeti. Ettha pana kvacisaddassā+nuvattanā tenevā+santavidhi siddhoti vāsaddeni+taradvayaṃ. Kvaci tveva, na hi etehi, idha ceva.

Sometimes there is an optional insertion of niggahīta. It is an āgama due to its capability, and it pertains only to a short vowel, because it follows a short vowel. It proceeds by clinging to the original element; thus, it is an āgama. [Examples:] Cakkhuṃ udapādi, akkhiṃ rujati, purimaṃ jāti, aṇuṃ thūlāni, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ bahuṃ, taṃsampayuttā, taṃtaṃsabhāvato. By the inclusion of 'vā', 'cakkhu udapādi' and so forth are indicated. Avaṃsiro, yāvañcidaṃ, and so forth are always so, because it is a determined option. A determined option is an option that proceeds in a rule in accordance with a determined rule. Indeed, the word 'vā' occurs in two senses: sometimes as an alternative, and sometimes in accepting a form as it is determined. When it is the latter, it indicates a rule that is constant, inconstant, or non-existent. Here, however, since the rule of non-existence is established by the continuation of the word 'kvaci' itself, the other two are indicated by the word 'vā'. Kvaci tveva, na hi etehi, idha ceva.

Saṃ rambho, saṃ ratto, saṃ rāgo, tāsaṃ ahaṃ santike, evaṃ ayaṃ, puṃ liṅgaṃ, kiṃ ahaṃ, tassa adāsiṃ ahaṃ itī+dha “niggahītā”dhikāro ā “mayadā sare”ti.

Saṃ rambho, saṃ ratto, saṃ rāgo, tāsaṃ ahaṃ santike, evaṃ ayaṃ, puṃ liṅgaṃ, kiṃ ahaṃ, tassa adāsiṃ ahaṃ—thus here the governing rule of 'niggahīta' extends up to 'mayadā sare'.

39. Lopo

39. Elision.

Niggahītassa lopo hoti vā kvaci. Dīghe sārambho saṃrambho, sāratto saṃratto, sārāgo saṃrāgo, pubbassaralope tāsāhaṃ santike, evāyaṃ, dvitte pulliṅgaṃ puṃliṅgaṃ, kyāhaṃ, tassa adāsahaṃ. Paṭisallāno, sallekho, pātukāmo, gantumano, ariyasaccāna dassanaṃ, etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ, avisāhāro, cirappavāsintiādīsu niccaṃ. Kvacīti kiṃ, eva+mayaṃ, ki+mahaṃ, etaṃ maṅgala+muttamaṃ.

Sometimes there is optional elision of the niggahīta. [Examples:] With lengthening of the preceding vowel: sārambho (from saṃrambho), sāratto (from saṃratto), sārāgo (from saṃrāgo); tāsāhaṃ santike (from tāsaṃ ahaṃ santike); evāyaṃ (from evaṃ ayaṃ); kyāhaṃ (from kiṃ ahaṃ); tassa adāsahaṃ (from tassa adāsiṃ ahaṃ). With doubling: pulliṅgaṃ (from puṃliṅgaṃ). In cases such as Paṭisallāno, sallekho, pātukāmo, gantumano, ariyasaccāna dassanaṃ, etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ, avisāhāro, cirappavāsi, and so forth, it is obligatory. Why 'sometimes' (kvaci)? [For cases such as:] evaṃ ayaṃ, kiṃ ahaṃ, etaṃ maṅgalaṃ uttamaṃ.

Kataṃ iti, abhinanduṃ iti, uttattaṃ iva, cakkaṃ iva, kaliṃiva, halaṃ idāni, kiṃ idāni, tvaṃ asi, idaṃ api, uttariṃ api, dātuṃ api, sadisaṃ eva itī+dha –

Kataṃ iti, abhinanduṃ iti, uttattaṃ iva, cakkaṃ iva, kaliṃ iva, halaṃ idāni, kiṃ idāni, tvaṃ asi, idaṃ api, uttariṃ api, dātuṃ api, sadisaṃ eva—thus here.

40. Parasarassa

40. Of the following vowel.

Niggahītamhā [M 0.0022] parasarassa lopo hoti vā kvaci. Katanti, abhinandunti, uttattaṃva, cakkaṃva, kaliṃva, halaṃdāni, kiṃdāni, tvaṃsi, idampi, uttarimpi, dātumpi, sadisaṃva. Vāti kiṃ, kataṃiti, kimiti, dātumapi, sadisaṃ eva.

Sometimes there is optional elision of the following vowel after a niggahīta. [Examples:] Katanti (from kataṃ iti), abhinandunti (from abhinanduṃ iti), uttattaṃva (from uttattaṃ iva), cakkaṃva (from cakkaṃ iva), kaliṃva (from kaliṃ iva), halaṃdāni (from halaṃ idāni), kiṃdāni (from kiṃ idāni), tvaṃsi (from tvaṃ asi), idampi (from idaṃ api), uttarimpi (from uttariṃ api), dātumpi (from dātuṃ api), sadisaṃva (from sadisaṃ eva). Why 'optionally' (vā)? [For cases such as:] kataṃ iti, kimiti, dātumapi, sadisaṃ eva.

Pupphaṃ assā uppajjati, evaṃ assa te āsavā itī+dha parassaralope –

Pupphaṃ assā uppajjati, evaṃ assa te āsavā—thus here, when the following vowel is elided.

53. Saṃyogādilopo

53. Elision of the initial of a conjunct.

Abyavahitānaṃ dvinnaṃ byañjanānaṃ ekatra ṭhiti saṃyogo, tasmiṃ saṃyoge yo ādibhūtāvayavo, tassa vā kvaci lopo hotītiādibyañjanassa lopo. Pupphaṃsā uppajjati, evaṃsa te āsavā. Tiṇṇaṃ saṃyogānaṃ visaye agyāgāraṃ, vutyassa iti hoti.

The standing together of two unseparated consonants is a conjunct; in that conjunct, the initial element is sometimes optionally elided—this is the elision of the initial consonant. [Examples:] Pupphaṃsā uppajjati, evaṃsa te āsavā. In the case of a conjunct of three consonants, [for example] agyāgāraṃ, the form vutyassa occurs.

Taṃ karoti, taṃ khaṇaṃ, saṃ gato, taṃ ghataṃ, dhammaṃ care, taṃ channaṃ, taṃ jātaṃ, taṃ jhānaṃ, taṃ ñāṇaṃ, taṃ ṭhānaṃ, taṃ ḍahati, taṃ tanoti, taṃ thiraṃ, taṃ dānaṃ, taṃ dhanaṃ, taṃ niccutaṃ, taṃ patto, taṃ phalaṃ, tesaṃ bodho, saṃ bhūto, taṃ mittaṃ, kiṃ kato, dātuṃ gato itī+dha –

Taṃ karoti, taṃ khaṇaṃ, saṃ gato, taṃ ghataṃ, dhammaṃ care, taṃ channaṃ, taṃ jātaṃ, taṃ jhānaṃ, taṃ ñāṇaṃ, taṃ ṭhānaṃ, taṃ ḍahati, taṃ tanoti, taṃ thiraṃ, taṃ dānaṃ, taṃ dhanaṃ, taṃ niccutaṃ, taṃ patto, taṃ phalaṃ, tesaṃ bodho, saṃ bhūto, taṃ mittaṃ, kiṃ kato, dātuṃ gato—thus here.

41. Vagge vagganto

41. The final of the class before a class consonant.

Niggahītassa kho vagge vagganto vā hotīti nimittānussarānaṃ paccāsatyā tabbaggapañcamo hoti. Paccāsatti nāma ṭhānato āsannatā guṇato vā, guṇatoti vaṇṇasaññādiguṇato. Niggahītassa [M 0.0023] anusarīyatīti pacchā katvā sarīyatīti anussarotipi vuccati. Taṅkaroti=taṃ karoti, evaṃ taṅkhaṇaṃ, saṅgato, taṅghataṃ. Dhammañcare, tañchannaṃ, tañjātaṃ, tañjhānaṃ, taññāṇaṃ. Taṇṭhānaṃ, taṇḍahati. Tantanoti, tanthiraṃ, tandānaṃ, tandhanaṃ, tanniccutaṃ, tampatto, tamphalaṃ, tesammodho, sambhūto, tammittaṃ. Kiṅkato, dātuṅgato, taṇhaṅkaro, raṇañjaho, saṇṭhito, jutindharo, sammatotiādīsu niccaṃ.

Indeed, the niggahīta optionally becomes the final of its class when followed by a class consonant; due to the proximity of the cause and that which follows, it becomes the fifth letter of that class. Proximity means nearness in place or in quality; by quality means by qualities such as the designation of the sound. It is also called 'anussara' because it is sounded after, or because it is sounded after being formed. [Examples:] Taṅkaroti (from taṃ karoti), and similarly taṅkhaṇaṃ, saṅgato, taṅghataṃ. Dhammañcare, tañchannaṃ, tañjātaṃ, tañjhānaṃ, taññāṇaṃ. Taṇṭhānaṃ, taṇḍahati. Tantanoti, tanthiraṃ, tandānaṃ, tandhanaṃ, tanniccutaṃ. Tampatto, tamphalaṃ, tesammodho, sambhūto, tammittaṃ. In cases such as Kiṅkato, dātuṅgato, taṇhaṅkaro, raṇañjaho, saṇṭhito, jutindharo, sammato, it is obligatory.

Ānantarikaṃ ya+māhu, yaṃ yadeva, paccattaṃ eva, taṃ hiitī+dha –

Ānantarikaṃ yaṃ āhu, yaṃ yadeva, paccattaṃ eva, taṃ hi—thus here.

42. Yevahisu ño

42. Ñ before ya, eva, and hi.

Ya+eva+hisaddesu niggahītassa vā ño hoti. “Vaggalasehi te”ti yassa ñakāro. Ānantarikañña+māhu=ānantarikaṃ ya+māhu, yaññadeva=yaṃyadeva, ñassa dvitte paccattaññeva, paccattaṃ eva, tañhi, tañhi. “Abyabhicārinā byabhicārī niyamyate”ti ñāyā evasaddasahacariyā “ya” iti sabbādiyasaddasseva gahaṇaṃ.

Before the words 'ya', 'eva', and 'hi', the niggahīta optionally becomes 'ñ'. The 'ñ' for 'ya' is by the rule 'Vaggalasehi te'. [Examples:] Ānantarikaññaṃ āhu (from ānantarikaṃ yaṃ āhu), yaññadeva (from yaṃ yadeva); with doubling of ñ: paccattaññeva (from paccattaṃ eva), tañhi (from taṃ hi). By the maxim 'The variable is determined by the invariable,' due to its association with the word 'eva', 'ya' is taken to mean only the pronoun 'ya' and its derivatives.

Saṃyogo, saṃyojanaṃ, saṃyato, saṃyācikāya itī+dha –

Saṃyogo, saṃyojanaṃ, saṃyato, saṃyācikāya—thus here.

43. Ye saṃssa

43. Of 'saṃ' before 'y'.

Saṃsaddassa yaṃ niggahītaṃ, tassa vā ño hoti yakāre. Saññogo=saṃyogo, evaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, saññato, saññācikāya. Idha yakāramattova gayhate. Saṃssāti kiṃ, etaṃ yojanaṃ, taṃ yānaṃ, taṃ saraṇaṃ yanti.

Of the niggahīta of the word 'saṃ', there is optionally 'ñ' before 'y'. [Examples:] Saññogo (from saṃyogo); similarly saññojanaṃ, saññato, saññācikāya. Here, only 'y' is taken. Why 'of saṃ'? [For cases such as:] etaṃ yojanaṃ, taṃ yānaṃ, taṃ saraṇaṃ yanti.

Taṃ [M 0.0024] eva, taṃ ahaṃ brūmi, yaṃ āhu, dhanaṃ eva, kiṃ etaṃ, nindituṃ arahati, taṃ idaṃ, yaṃ aniccaṃ, taṃ anattā, etaṃ avoca, etaṃ eva itī+dha –

Taṃ eva, taṃ ahaṃ brūmi, yaṃ āhu, dhanaṃ eva, kiṃ etaṃ, nindituṃ arahati, taṃ idaṃ, yaṃ aniccaṃ, taṃ anattā, etaṃ avoca, etaṃ eva—thus here.

44. Mayadā sare

44. M, y, d before a vowel.

Niggahītassa ma ya dā honti vā sare kvaci. Tameva taṃ eva, tamahaṃ brūmi=taṃ ahaṃ brūmi, yamāhu, dhanameva, kimetaṃ, ninditumarahati. Tayidaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ, tadanattā, etadavoca, etadeva. “Mayadā”ti yogavibhāgā buddhama saraṇama iccādi bhavati.

Of the niggahīta, 'm', 'y', and 'd' are sometimes optionally substituted before a vowel. [Examples:] Tameva (from taṃ eva), tamahaṃ brūmi (from taṃ ahaṃ brūmi), yamāhu (from yaṃ āhu), dhanameva (from dhanaṃ eva), kimetaṃ (from kiṃ etaṃ), ninditumarahati (from nindituṃ arahati). Tayidaṃ (from taṃ idaṃ). Yadaniccaṃ (from yaṃ aniccaṃ), tadanattā (from taṃ anattā), etadavoca (from etaṃ avoca), etadeva (from etaṃ eva). By splitting the rule 'mayadā', forms such as 'buddhama', 'saraṇama', etc., are derived.

47. Tadaminādīni

47. Tadaminā and so forth.

Tadaminādīni nippajjanti. “Ya+dalakkhaṇikaṃ, taṃ nipātanā”ti ñāyā lakkhaṇantarena avihitā desa+lopā+gama+vipallāsā, sabbattha imināva daṭṭhabbā. Idañca paresaṃ pisodarādimiva daṭṭhabbaṃ. Phusitaṃ=jalabindu, phusita+mudara+massa pisodaraṃ. Issa akāre taṃ iminā=tadaminā, sakiṃ āgāmī=sakadāgāmī, dhassa dakāre ekaṃ idha ahaṃ=eka+midā+haṃ, vidhassa vidādeso saṃvidhāya avahāro=saṃvidāvahāro, vārisaddassa vakāre, hassa lakāre ca kate vārivāhako=valāhako, jīvanassa jīādeso, jīvanassa muto=jīmūto. Chavassa suādese, sayanassa sānādese ca kate chavassa sayanaṃ=susānaṃ. Uddhassa uduādese, khassa khalaādese ca “saramhā dve”ti dvittādimhi ca kate uddhaṃ khaṃ assa udukkhalaṃ. Pisitassa piādese, asassa sācādese ca kate pisitāso=pisāco.

The forms `tadaminā` and so on are derived. By the maxim, 'That which is not covered by a rule is an irregular formation,' substitutions, elisions, augmentations, and transpositions not prescribed by another rule are to be understood everywhere by this very rule. And this should be understood as similar to the `pisodarādi` group of other grammarians. `Phusitaṃ` means a drop of water; `pisodaraṃ` is from `phusitaṃ udaraṃ assa`. With `i` becoming `a`: `taṃ iminā` becomes `tadaminā`. `sakiṃ āgāmī` becomes `sakadāgāmī`. With `dha` becoming `da`: `ekaṃ idha ahaṃ` becomes `ekamidāhaṃ`. With `vidha` being substituted by `vidā`: `saṃvidhāya avahāro` becomes `saṃvidāvahāro`. With the `va` of `vāri` and `ha` becoming `la`: `vārivāhako` becomes `valāhako`. With `jīvana` being substituted by `jī`: `jīvanassa muto` becomes `jīmūto`. With `chava` being substituted by `su` and `sayana` by `sāna`: `chavassa sayanaṃ` becomes `susānaṃ`. With `uddha` being substituted by `udu` and `kha` by `khala`, and with doubling etc. by the rule 'saramhā dve': `uddhaṃ khaṃ assa` becomes `udukkhalaṃ`. With `pisita` being substituted by `pi` and `asa` by `sāca`: `pisitāso` becomes `pisāco`.

Mahīsaddassa [M 0.0025] mayūādese, ravatissa rādese ca kate mahiyaṃ ravatīti mayūro. Eva+maññepi payogato+nugantabbā. Ettha ca –

With the word `mahī` being substituted by `mayū`, and `ravati` by `ra`, `mayūro` (peacock) is formed from `mahiyaṃ ravati` (it cries on the earth). Similarly, other instances are to be inferred from usage. And here –

Vaṇṇāgamo vaṇṇavipariyāyo,

Dve cā+pare vaṇṇavikāra+nāsā;

Dhātussa atthātisayena yogo,

Ta+duccate pañcavidhaṃ niruttaṃti.

The augmentation of letters, the transposition of letters, and two others: the modification and elision of letters; the connection of a root with an extended meaning—these are called the five kinds of etymology.

Yathā dvāre niyutto=dovārikoti okaāgamo. Hiṃsasaddassa sīhoti vipallāso. Nijako=niyakoti vikāro. Mehanassa khassa mālā mekhalāti vaṇṇalopo, ha+na+makārānaṃ lopo. Mayūroti atthe ravatissa atissayayogoti.

Just as `dovārika` (gatekeeper) is from `dvāre niyutto` (appointed at the door), this is an addition of `oka`. The word `sīha` (lion) from `hiṃsa` (to harm) is a transposition. `Niyako` from `nijako` is an alteration. The elision of a letter (`vaṇṇalopo`) is as in `mekhalā` from `mehana` with the elision of `kha`, and in `mālā` with the elision of the letters `ha`, `na`, and `ma`. In the sense of `mayūro` (peacock), it is an excessive connection with `ravati` (to cry).

Yathariva tathariveti nipātāva. “Jaraggavā vicintesuṃ, vara+mhākaṃ bhusāmive”ti ettha ivasaddo evakārattho. Niggahītasandhi.

`Yathariva` and `tathariva` are particles. In the verse, “The old cows considered, ‘She is exceedingly excellent for us,’” the word `iva` has the meaning of `eva` (indeed). This is niggahīta sandhi.

Sandhissarānaṃ paṭisedhasandhi,

Atho byañjana+sarabyañjanānaṃ;

Sandhi ca+tho niggahītassa sandhi,

Bhavanti sandhi pana pañcadhā ve.

Sandhi of vowels, prohibitive sandhi, then sandhi of consonants and of vowels-and-consonants; and also the sandhi of the niggahīta; indeed, sandhi are thus of five kinds.

Iti payogasiddhiyaṃ sandhikaṇḍo paṭhamo.

Thus ends the first chapter on Sandhi in the Payogasiddhi.

2. Nāmakaṇḍa

2. The Chapter on Nouns

Atha [M 0.0026] nāmāni vuccante. Taṃ atthābhimukhaṃ namanato, attanā ca+tthassa nāmanato nāmaṃ, dabbābhidhānaṃ. Taṃ duvidhaṃ saliṅgā+liṅgato, anvattharuḷhito ca, tividhaṃ pumi+tthi+napuṃsakaliṅgato, rukkho, latā, vananti. Catubbidhaṃ sāmañña+guṇa+kriyā+yadicchānāmato, rukkho, nīlo, pācako, sirivaḍḍhoti. Aṭṭhavidhaṃ avaṇṇi+vaṇṇu+vaṇṇo+kāra+niggahītantapakatibhedato, ettha kiṃsaddo niggahītanto. Paccayā paṭhamaṃ karīyatīti pakati, saddo, dhātu ca.

Now nouns are explained. It is called `nāma` because it inclines towards meaning and because by itself it names the meaning; it is the designation of a substance. It is twofold: having gender and not having gender, and also etymological and conventional. It is threefold according to masculine, feminine, and neuter genders: `rukkho` (tree), `latā` (creeper), `vanaṃ` (forest). It is fourfold according to common, quality, action, and arbitrary names: `rukkho` (tree), `nīlo` (blue), `pācako` (cook), `sirivaḍḍho` (Sirivaḍḍha). It is eightfold by the distinction of stems ending in the vowels a, i, u, the letter o, and niggahīta. Here, the word `kiṃ` is one ending in niggahīta. Because it is formed first, before the suffix, it is a stem (`pakati`), namely, a word and a root.

Tattha saliṅgesu tāva akārantato pulliṅgā sugatasaddā satta vibhattiyo parā yojīyante. Sugataiti ṭhite –

Therein, among the gendered nouns, first, from the a-ending masculine noun `sugata`, the seven inflections are applied hereafter. When `sugata` stands thus—

1. Dve dve+kānekesu nāmasmā siyo aṃyo nā hi sa naṃ smā hi sa naṃ smiṃ su

1. Two by two, in the singular and plural respectively, from the noun stem are: `si, yo`; `aṃ, yo`; `nā, hi`; `sa, naṃ`; `smā, hi`; `sa, naṃ`; `smiṃ, su`.

Etesaṃ dve dve honti ekānekatthesu vattamānato nāmasmā yathākkamaṃ. Yato ime satta dukā honti, “atthavanta+madhātuka+mapaccayaṃ pāṭipadikaṃ kitaka+taddhita+samāsā ce”ti vuttattā taṃ nāmaṃ pāṭipadikaṃ nāma. Keci sakattha+dabba+liṅga+saṅkhyā+kammādipañcakaṃ pāṭipadikanti vadanti. Tene+taṃ vuccati –

These occur in pairs from the noun stem in singular and plural meanings, in respective order. Since these are seven pairs, and it is said: 'A nominal base is that which is meaningful, not a root, not a suffix, and also primary derivatives, secondary derivatives, and compounds,' that noun is therefore called a nominal base. Some say that the nominal base is the pentad of: its own meaning, substance, gender, number, and action, etc. Therefore it is said:

Sakattha+dabba+liṅgāni, saddattha+mabravuṃ pare;

Saṅkhyā+kammādikānantu, vibhatti vācakā matā.

Its own meaning, substance, and gender—others have declared these to be the meaning of the word; but number, action, and so forth, are held to be expressed by the inflection.

Sakattha+dabba+liṅgāni, saṅkhyā+kammādipañcakaṃ;

Saddattha+mabravuṃ keci, vibhatti pana jotakāti ca.

Its own meaning, substance, gender, and the pentad of number, action, and so forth—some have declared these to be the meaning of the word, while the inflection is merely an illuminator.

Tato [M 0.0027] ekamhi vattabbe ekavacanaṃ bahumhi vattabbe bahuvacanañcāti aniyamena pasaṅge “nāmasmā”ti adhikāro.

Then, when one is to be expressed, the singular is used; when many are to be expressed, the plural is used. Thus, in the event of a lack of regulation, 'from the noun stem' is the governing rule.

37. Paṭhamā+tthamatte

37. In the mere sense of the stem.

Nāmassā+bhidheyyamatte paṭhamāvibhatti hotīti vatticchāvasā paṭhamāye+kavacanabahuvacanāni. Si yoiti paṭhamā. Sissi+kārassā+nubandhattā appayogo. Payojanaṃ “ki+maṃsisū”ti saṃketo, tathā aṃvacanassā+kārassa. Ettha tathāti vuttassātideso aññadīyadhammāna+maññatthapāpana+matideso. Ekamhi vattabbe paṭhamekavacanaṃ si.

When the mere meaning of the noun is to be denoted, the nominative inflection occurs. By the speaker's intention, the nominative has singular and plural forms. `Si` and `yo` are the nominative. Because the `i` of `si` is a marker (`anubandha`), it is not used. Its purpose is for the technical convention `ki-aṃ-si-su`; similarly for the `a` of the ending `aṃ`. Here, what is stated as 'similarly' (`tathā`) is an extension (`atidesa`). An extension is the application of the properties belonging to one thing to another. When one is to be expressed, the nominative singular is `si`.

Atoti vattate, atoti nāmavisesanattā “vidhibbisesanantassā”ti paribhāsato akārantato nāmasmā vidhi.

`Ato` is carried forward. Because `ato` is a qualifier of the noun, according to the meta-rule, 'a rule applies to that which ends with its qualifier,' the rule applies to a noun ending in `a`.

109. Sisso

109. `Si` becomes `o`.

Akārantato nāmasmā sissa o hoti. Pubbasaralope sugato tiṭṭhati. Bahumhi vattabbe bahuvacanaṃ yo. Evaṃ uparipi yojetabbaṃ.

After a noun ending in `a`, `si` becomes `o`. With the elision of the preceding vowel, it becomes `sugato`. For example: `Sugato tiṭṭhati` (The Well-farer stands). When many are to be expressed, the plural is `yo`. This should be applied similarly hereafter.

41. Ato yonaṃ ṭāṭe

41. After `a`, the two `yo` endings become `ā` and `e`.

Akārantato nāmasmā paṭhamādutiyāyonaṃ ṭāṭe honti yathākkamaṃ. Ṭakārānubandhattā “ṭānubandhā+nekavaṇṇā sabbassā”ti sabbādeso. Sugatā tiṭṭhanti.

After a noun ending in `a`, the `yo` endings of the nominative and accusative become `ā` and `e` respectively. Because of the `ṭa` marker, according to the rule, 'a polysyllabic substitute with a `ṭa` marker replaces the whole,' this is a total substitution. For example: `Sugatā tiṭṭhanti` (The Well-farers stand).

“Paṭhamā+tthamatte”ti vattate.

The rule `Paṭhamā-atthe-matte` is carried forward.

38. Āmantaṇe

38. In the vocative.

Āmantaṇādhike [M 0.0028] atthamatte paṭhamāvibhatti hotīti ekasmiṃ ekavacanaṃ si.

In the mere sense of the stem with the addition of addressing, the nominative inflection occurs. For one, the singular is `si`.

112. Go syā+lapane

112. `Si` in the vocative is `ga`.

Ālapane si gasañño hoti.

In the vocative, `si` has the designation `ga`.

“Lopo”ti vattate.

`Lopo` (elision) is carried forward.

117. Gasīnaṃ

117. Of `ga` and `si`.

Nāmasmā ga+sīnaṃ lopo hoti. Bho sugata ciraṃ tiṭṭha.

After a noun stem, `ga` and `si` are elided. For example: `Bho sugata, ciraṃ tiṭṭha` (O Well-farer, may you remain long!).

“Ge”ti vattate.

`Ge` is carried forward.

59. Ayunaṃ vā dīgho

59. Of `a`, `i`, `u`, optionally long.

Aiuiccetesaṃ vā dīgho hoti ge pare tiliṅge+ti dīghe bho sugata sugatā ciraṃ tiṭṭha. Sakkate sugatāti dīghaṃ dūrālapaneyevi+cchanti, samīpālapanepi dassanato taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Bahuvacane yossa ṭā, sugatā ciraṃ tiṭṭhatha.

Of `a`, `i`, and `u`, there is optional lengthening when `ge` follows, in all three genders. Thus, the lengthened form is `sugatā`, and the unlengthened is `sugata`. For example: `Bho sugatā, ciraṃ tiṭṭha` (O Well-farer, may you remain long). In Sanskrit, they desire the lengthening as in `sugatā` only in distant address, but since it is also seen in near address, that restriction should not be adopted. In the plural, `yo` becomes `ā`. For example: `Sugatā, ciraṃ tiṭṭhatha` (O Well-farers, may you remain long).

2. Kamme dutiyā

2. In the object (kamma), the second case (accusative).

Tasmiṃ kammakārake dutiyāvibhatti hoti. Aṃyoiti dutiyā. Ettha dutiyātatiyādibhāvo vibhattisutte siyo iti paṭhamāvibhatyādīni+mupādāya vuccati, taṃ taṃ upādāya paññattattā. Dutiyekavacanaṃ aṃ, akārassā+payogo. Sugataṃ passa. Dutiyābahuvacanaṃ yo, tassa ṭe, sugate passa.

In that object-case (kammakāraka), the second case ending occurs. 'Aṃ' and 'yo' are the second case endings. Here, the state of being the second, third, and so forth, is spoken of in the Sutta on Case Endings by taking 'si', 'yo', etc., the first case endings, as the basis, because they are designated by taking those respective endings as a basis. The second singular is 'aṃ'; the 'a' is for non-application. For example: 'Sugataṃ passa' (See the Sugata). The second plural is 'yo'; for that, 'e' is substituted. For example: 'Sugate passa' (See the Sugatas).

19. Kattukaraṇesu tatiyā

19. In the agent and instrument, the third case (instrumental).

Tasmiṃ [M 0.0029] kattari karaṇe ca kārake tatiyāvibhatti hoti. Nā+hiiti tatiyāvibhatti. Tatiyāekavacanaṃ nā.

In that agent-case and instrument-case, the third case ending occurs. 'Nā' and 'hi' are the third case endings. The third singular is 'nā'.

“Nāssā”ti vattate.

'Nāssa' is understood.

108. Ate+na

108. Ato ena.

Akārantato nāmasmā parassa nāvacanassa enādeso hoti niccaṃ. Sugatena kataṃ.

After a noun ending in 'a', the ending 'nā' is always substituted by 'ena'. For example: 'Sugatena kataṃ' (It was done by the Sugata).

98. Suhisva+sse

98. Su and hi become 'e'.

Akārantassa suhisve+hoti. Sugatehi.

For a noun ending in 'a', 'su' and 'hi' become 'e'. For example: 'Sugatehi' (by the Sugatas).

“Ve”ti vattate.

'Ve' is understood.

95. Smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi

95. Smā, hi, and smiṃ become mhā, bhi, and mhi.

Nāmasmā paresaṃ smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi honti yathākkamaṃti hissa bhiādese sugatebhi. Karaṇe sugatena loko puññaṃ karoti, sugatehi sugatehi vā.

After a noun, the endings 'smā', 'hi', and 'smiṃ' become 'mhā', 'bhi', and 'mhi' respectively. Thus, for 'hi', the substitution is 'bhi', as in 'sugatebhi'. In the instrumental case: 'Sugatena loko puññaṃ karoti' (The world makes merit by the Sugata), or 'sugatehi', or 'sugatebhi'.

24. Catutthī sampadāne

24. The fourth case (dative) is for the recipient (sampadāna).

Tasmiṃ sampadānakārake catutthī siyā. Sa+naṃiti catutthī. Catutthe+kavacanaṃ sa. Vibhattisutte ssa+naṃti dīghapāṭhena sugatassāti siddhepi “jhalā sassa no” tyādikāriyasuttesu ssassāti akkharagāravatā hotīti lāghavattha+mida+māraddhaṃ –

In that recipient-case (sampadānakāraka), the fourth case may occur. 'Sa' and 'naṃ' are the fourth case endings. The fourth singular is 'sa'. Although 'sugatassa' is established in the Sutta on Case Endings by the long reading 'ssa' and 'naṃ', this short form is introduced for the sake of brevity, because in operative rules such as 'jhalā sassa no', the form 'ssassa' would be phonetically heavy.

51. Suña sassa

51. The augments 'su' and 'ña' for 'sa'.

Nāmasmā [M 0.0030] parassa sassa suñāgamo hoti. Sa ca “chaṭṭhiyā”ti vattamāne –

After a noun, the ending 'sa' receives the augments 'su' and 'ña'. And that occurs when 'chaṭṭhiyā' (of the sixth case) is understood—

1,20. Ñākānu bandhā+dyantā

Ñ- and K-markers are at the beginning and end.

Chaṭṭhīniddiṭṭhassa ñānubandha+kānubandhā ādyantāhontīti ādyavayavo. Ukāro uccāraṇattho, ññakāro asmiṃ sutte saṃketattho. Sugatassa dānaṃ deti.

For that which is specified by the sixth case, the markers 'ñ' and 'k' indicate placement at the beginning and end respectively; thus, the augment with the 'ñ' marker is an initial component. The vowel 'u' is for the sake of pronunciation; the letter 'ñ' in this rule is a technical indicator. For example: 'Sugatassa dānaṃ deti' (He gives a gift to the Sugata).

1,58. “Bahulaṃ”tya+dhikāro

The governing rule 'Bahulaṃ' (variously).

Bahulādhikāraṃ kappadumamiva maññanti saddikā. Tañca –

Grammarians (saddikā) consider the governing rule 'bahulaṃ' to be like a wish-fulfilling tree (kappaduma). And that is as follows:

Kvaci pavattya+pavatti, kvaca+ññaṃ kvaci vā kvaci;

Siyā bahulasaddena, vidhi sabbo yathāgamaṃti –

Sometimes application, sometimes non-application; sometimes another rule, sometimes optionally. By the word 'bahulaṃ', the entire rule proceeds according to tradition.

Catubbidhaṃ bahulaṃ samikkhanti.

They consider 'bahulaṃ' to be fourfold.

“Ato vā”tveva,

The rule 'Ato vā' (after 'a', optionally) is also understood.

44. Sassāya catutthiyā

44. For 'sa' of the fourth case, 'āya'.

Akārantato parassa catutthiyā sassa āyo hoti vā bahulaṃ. Sugatāya. Yebhuyyena tādattheyevā+ya+māyo dissatīti ito paraṃ no+dāharīyate. Catutthībahuvacanaṃ naṃ,

After a noun ending in 'a', 'sa' of the fourth case optionally becomes 'āya', according to the principle of 'bahulaṃ'. For example: 'Sugatāya' (for the Sugata). Since this 'āya' is mostly seen in the sense of 'for the sake of that', no further example is given hereafter. The fourth plural is 'naṃ'.

“Dīgho”ti vattate.

'Dīgho' (lengthening) is understood.

89. Sunaṃhisu

89. Before su, naṃ, and hi.

Nāmassa [M 0.0031] dīgho hoti sunaṃhisu. Sugatānaṃ.

A noun is lengthened before 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'. For example: 'Sugatānaṃ' (to/of the Sugatas).

29. Pañcamya+vadhismā

29. The fifth case (ablative) is in the sense of the point of separation (avadhi).

Etasmā avadhikārakā pañcamīvibhatti hoti. Smā+hiiti pañcamī. Pañcamyekavacanaṃ smā,

From this case of separation (avadhikāraka), the fifth case ending occurs. 'Smā' and 'hi' are the fifth case endings. The fifth singular is 'smā'.

“Ato” “ṭāṭe” “ve”ti ca vattate.

The terms ‘ato’, ‘ṭāṭe’, and ‘ve’ are carried forward.

43. Smā+smiṃnaṃ

43. Of smā and smiṃ

Akārantato nāmasmā paresaṃ smā+smiṃnaṃ ṭā+ṭe honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Sugatā apehi sugatamhā sugatasmā vā. Pañcamībahuvacanañhi, sugatebhi sugatehi.
