After a noun ending in 'a', the suffixes `smā` and `smiṃ` are optionally replaced by `ṭā` and `ṭe` respectively. For example: `sugatā apehi` (go away from the Sugata); or `sugatamhā`, `sugatasmā`. For the ablative plural: `sugatebhi`, `sugatehi`.

39. Chaṭṭhī sambandhe

39. The Sixth Case: In the Sense of Relation

Kārakehi añño sambandho, tatra chaṭṭhīvibhatti hoti. Sa+naṃiti chaṭṭhī, chaṭṭhekavacanaṃ sa, sugatassa vihāro, chaṭṭhībahuvacanaṃ naṃ, sugatānaṃ.

When there is a relation other than the kārakas, the sixth case-ending occurs. `Sa` and `naṃ` are the sixth case-endings; `sa` is the singular of the sixth case, as in `sugatassa vihāro` (the monastery of the Sugata); `naṃ` is the plural of the sixth case, as in `sugatānaṃ` (of the Sugatas).

14. Sattamyā+dhāre

14. The Seventh Case: In the Sense of Location

Ādhārakārake sattamīvibhatti hoti. Smiṃ+suiti sattamī. Sattamyekavacanaṃ smiṃ, sugate patiṭṭhitaṃ sugatamhi sugatasmiṃ vā. Sattamībahuvacanaṃ su, “su+hisva+sse”ti e, sugatesu.

In the locative kāraka, the seventh case-ending occurs. `Smiṃ` and `su` are the seventh case-endings. The locative singular is `smiṃ`, as in `sugate patiṭṭhitaṃ` (established in the Sugata), or `sugatamhi`, `sugatasmiṃ`. The locative plural is `su`; by the rule `suhisu a sse`, the preceding `a` becomes `e`, as in `sugatesu` (in the Sugatas).

Sugato, sugatā. Bho sugata, bho sugatā, bhavanto sugatā. Sugataṃ, sugate. Sugatena, sugatebhi[M 0.0032], sugatehi. Karaṇe sugatena, sugatebhi, sugatehi. Sugatassa, sugatāya, sugatānaṃ. Sugatā, sugatamhā, sugatasmā, sugatebhi, sugatehi. Sugatassa, sugatānaṃ. Sugate, sugatamhi, sugatasmiṃ, sugatesu.

Sugato, sugatā. Bho sugata, bho sugatā, bhavanto sugatā. Sugataṃ, sugate. Sugatena, sugatebhi, sugatehi. In the instrumental case: sugatena, sugatebhi, sugatehi. Sugatassa, sugatāya, sugatānaṃ. Sugatā, sugatamhā, sugatasmā, sugatebhi, sugatehi. Sugatassa, sugatānaṃ. Sugate, sugatamhi, sugatasmiṃ, sugatesu.

Sugato sugato. Sugataṃ namati. Sugatena kato. Sugatena jito. Sugatassa dade. Sugatā vigato. Sugatassa suto. Sugate ramate. Evaṃ –

The Well-gone, the Well-gone. He bows to the Well-gone. Done by the Well-gone. Conquered by the Well-gone. He gives to the Well-gone. Departed from the Well-gone. Heard from the Well-gone. He delights in the Well-gone. Thus—

Sūrā+sura+naro+raga+nāga+yakkhā,

Gandhabba+kinnara+manussa+pisāca+petā;

Mātaṅga+jaṅgama+turaṅga+varāha+sīhā,

Byaggha+ccha+kacchapa+taraccha+miga+ssa+soṇā.

Gods, asuras, men, serpents, nāgas, yakkhas; Gandharvas, kinnaras, humans, pisācas, pretas; Elephants, moving creatures, horses, boars, lions; Tigers, bears, tortoises, hyenas, deer, horses, and dogs.

Āloka+loka+nilayā+nila+cāga+yogā,

Vāyāma+gāma+nigamā+gama+dhamma+kāmā;

Saṅgho+gha+ghosa+paṭighā+sava+kodha+lobhā,

Sārambha+thambha+mada+māna+pamāda+makkhā.

Light, world, abodes, wind, giving, yogas; Effort, villages, towns, scriptures, Dhamma, desires; Sangha, floods, sounds, aversion, outflows, anger, greed; Agitation, obstinacy, conceit, pride, negligence, disparagement.

Punnāga+pūga+panasā+sana+campaka+mba-

Hintāla+tāla+vakula+jjuna+kiṃsukā ca;

Mandāra+kunda+pucimanda+karañja+rukkhā,

Ñeyyā mayūra+sakuṇa+ṇḍaja+koñca+haṃsā.

Punnāga, pūga, breadfruit, asana, champak, mango, hintāla, fan-palm, bakula, arjuna, and flame trees; Mandāra, kunda, nimba, and karañja trees; And peacocks, birds, egg-born creatures, herons, and swans may be known.

Sugatasaddova, yato sabbo saddo, na saddatālitatthova, atha kho saṃyogādivasenapi atthaṃ vadanti. Tene+taṃ vuccati –

Like the word 'Sugata', since not every word is meaningful from its sound alone, but also expresses meaning by means of connection and so forth, therefore it is said:

Saṃyogā vippayogā ca, sāhacariyā+virodhato;

Atthā pakaraṇā liṅgā, saddantarasamīpato.

From connection and separation, from association and opposition; from meaning, context, and indicatory mark, from proximity to another word.

Sāmatthyo+citra+desehi[M 0.0033], kāla+byattā+nurūpato;

Upacāra+kākubheda, sambandhehu+palakkhaṇā.

From capability, convention, and place; from time, gender, and suitability; from figurative usage, difference in intonation, relationship, and implication.

Vacanā ca tadaṅgattā, padhānattātiādihi;

Sadda+tthā pavibhajjante, na saddādeva kevalāti.

And from number, from being a part thereof, from prominence and so forth; the meanings of words are distinguished, not from the words alone.

Ettha saṃyogato tāva, “sakisorā dhenu dīyatū”ti, kisoro assapotako, taṃsaṃyogato vaḷavā eva patīyate.

Here, first, from connection: 'Let the cow with the calf be given'—the calf is a foal; thus, by connection with that, a mare is indeed understood.

Vippayogato – “akisorā ānīyatū”ti tappaṭisedhā vaḷavā eva patīyate.

From separation: 'Let one without a foal be brought'—by that negation, a mare is indeed understood.

Sahacaraṇato – “rāma+lakkhaṇa”iti ubhinnaṃ sahacaraṇena rāmoti dāsarathi eva rāmo, na aññābhidhāno jāmadaganyādi. Lakkhaṇopi somitti eva, na tu yo koci lakkhaṇo.

From association: 'Rāma and Lakkhaṇa'—by the companionship of the two, Rāma is understood as Dasaratha’s son, indeed Rāma, not another of that name like Jāmadagnya. Lakkhaṇa too is understood as Sumitrā’s son, not just any person named Lakkhaṇa.

Virodhato – “rāma+jjunā” iti bhaggavo sahassabāhu ca aññamaññaviruddhāti te eva patīyante, na dāsarathi sabyasāci ca.

From opposition: 'Rāma and Arjuna'—since Bhaggava and Sahassabāhu are mutually opposed, they are indeed understood, not Dasaratha's son and Sabyasācī.

Atthato – “sindhava+mānaya, pavisāmi raṇaṅgaṇa”miti raṇaṅgaṇapaveso vāhanavisesena hotīti atthato turaṅgapatīti, na tu lavaṇavisesaṃ.

From purpose: 'Bring the Sindhu, I shall enter the battlefield'—since entering the battlefield is done with a special mount, a horse is understood from the purpose, not a type of salt.

Pakaraṇato-bhojanavidhimhi upasaṅkhariyamāne “sindhava+mānaye”ti, atra hi saddantarassā+bhāvepi bhojanopakaraṇasamavāya+mālokitabhāvato lavaṇe paṭipatti, tādiso hi patthāvoti.

From context: When food preparation is being undertaken, and one says, 'Bring the Sindhu'—here, even in the absence of another word, because of observing the collection of items for a meal, salt is understood; for such is the occasion.

Liṅgato [M 0.0034] – “devadattaṃ paṭhama+mupavesaya samārādhitaguruṃ”ti, atra samārādhitaguruttena liṅgena tassa bāhussacca+mavagamyate, na tu yo koci devaguṇo.

From indication: 'First seat Devadatta, who has pleased his teacher'—here, by the indication of having pleased his teacher, his great learning is understood, not just any divine quality.

Sannidhānato – “ajjuno katavīriyoti” patīyate, no akatavīriyo ajjunoti.

From proximity: 'Arjuna is one of accomplished valor' is understood, not 'Arjuna is one of unaccomplished valor.'

Sāmatthiyato – “anudarā kaññā”ti udare asati kaññā eva natthīti tassā kisāṅgiyā majjhapadesoti patīyate.

From capability: 'A maiden without a belly'—since without a belly a maiden would not exist, her slender middle region is understood.

Ocitrato – “rāmasadiso+yaṃ” iti, atra hi rāmo payuttadāsarathismiṃ bhiyyo sādhāraṇo paricayoti dāsarathi eva patīyate, na bhaggavarāmo.

From convention: 'He is like Rāma'—here, since Rāma is more commonly known in usage as Dasaratha’s son, Dasaratha's son is indeed understood, not Bhaggava’s Rāma.

Desato – “poṭṭhapā” iti kismiñci dese pasaṃsāvacanaṃ. Kismiñci akkosavacanaṃ.

From place: 'Poṭṭhapāda'—in a certain place, it is a term of praise; in another, a term of abuse.

Kālato – “pace”ti dakkhiṇāpathe katthaci pubbaṇhe yāgupāke, sāyaṇhe tu odanapāke.

From time: 'Cook'—in the southern region, at some time in the morning it means cooking gruel, but in the evening, it means cooking rice.

Byattito – “gāmassa addha” miti samabhāge, napuṃsakattā. “Gāmassa addho”ti pumattena tu asamabhāge.

From gender: 'Half of the village' (`gāmassa addhaṃ`) is understood as an equal division, due to its neuter gender. 'Half of the village' (`gāmassa addho`), however, is understood as an unequal division, due to its masculine gender.

Anurūpato – “narapati sādhu rakkhati gomaṇḍala”miti mahīmaṇḍalapālanaṃ rājino+nurūpa+miti mahīmaṇḍalapālaneva patīti, na tu goyūtharakkhane.

From suitability: 'The king protects the `gomaṇḍala` well'—since protecting the circle of the earth is fitting for a king, it is the protection of the earth that is indeed understood, not the guarding of a herd of cows.

Upacārato – ataṃsabhāve taṃsabhāvāropana+mupacāro, sa ca tadaṭṭho, taddhammo, taṃsahacariyo, taṃsamīpoti catubbidho[M 0.0035], tattha yathākkamaṃ mañcā ukkosanti, aggi māṇavo, yaṭṭhiṃ pavesaya, gaṅgāyaṃ vajoti.

From figurative usage: The application of the nature of one thing to that which does not possess its nature is figurative usage. And it is of four kinds: for that purpose, of that quality, associated with that, and in proximity to that. The respective examples are: 'The couches call out,' 'The boy is a fire,' 'Bring in the staff,' and 'The hamlet on the Ganges.'

Kākuto-kākusaddo itthiyaṃ, sa ca vikāra+soka+bhīti+dhanirūpesu dissati, vattu kāyavikārā kathañci taṃ akatavāapi kenaci aññena “kiṃ tvaṃ taṃ akāsi “iti puṭṭho kopena bhamubhedā “ahaṃ katavā amhī”ti katheti, tassa bhamubhedakriyā akriyāpaṭiññaṃ sūcayati.

From intonation: The term 'kāku' refers to intonation, and it is seen in the forms of alteration, sorrow, fear, and sound. For instance, regarding a speaker's bodily alteration: although one has not done something, when asked by another, 'Did you do that?' one might, with anger and a knitting of the brows, say, 'I did it.' That action of knitting the brows indicates a denial of the action not done.

Sambandha to – “mātari sammā vattitabbaṃ, pitari sussūyitabbaṃ” iti, atra hi samātari sapitarīti sambandhisaddābhāvepi sā mātā so pitā ca assa puttassāti patīyate.

From relationship: 'One should behave properly toward the mother; one should attend to the father.' Here, even in the absence of relational words, it is understood that she is the mother and he is the father of that son.

Upalakkhaṇato – “kākehi rakkhitabbaṃ dadhī”ti kākasaddo sabbesa+mupaghātakānaṃ sāmaññaṃ upalakkhetīti sunakhādisabbehipi nivārīyate.

From implication: 'Curds should be protected from crows.' Here, the word 'crow' indicates all destructive creatures in general; therefore, dogs and all such others are also to be kept away.

Vacanato – “dārā”iti dārasaddo kalatte bahuvacananto, aññattha aniyatavacano.

From number: 'Dārā'—the word 'dāra' is plural when referring to a wife; in other contexts, its number is indeterminate.

Tadaṅgattā – “sajjitaṃ bhojana”miti vutte tapparikkhārattā tadupakaraṇa āsana, pāti, byañjanādīnaṃ sampādanampi patīyate.

From being a component thereof: When it is said, 'The meal is prepared,' it is also understood, by virtue of being its requisites, that its accessories—seats, bowls, curries, and so forth—are also provided.

Padhānabhāvato – “niggacchati avaninātho”ti rañño niggamanena tadupajīvīnampi niggamanaṃ viññāyati.

From prominence: 'The lord of the earth departs'—by the king's departure, the departure of those who depend on him is also understood.

Vuttañca –

And it has been said:

Neyyanītatthasuttesu[M 0.0036], ñeyyaṃ saddatthamattakaṃ;

Ne+ttha vattabbaatthena, suttaṃ nītatthakaṃ bhaveti.

In suttas of explicit meaning, the meaning to be understood is only the literal meaning of the words; a sutta becomes of implied meaning when its meaning must be further explained.

Eva+maññesampi akārantānaṃ pulliṅgānaṃ saddānaṃ rūpanayo kriyā+bhisambandho ca. Sugatasaddato yassa saddassa viseso atthi, taṃ vakkhāma. Ito paraṃ chaṭṭhiyā catutthīsamattā pañcamībahuvacanassa ca tatiyābahuvacanena samattā na tā dassiyante.

Similarly, the declension and connection with verbs of other masculine nouns ending in -a are to be understood. We will state the special features of any word that differs from the word 'Sugata.' From this point on, since the sixth case (genitive) is the same as the fourth (dative), and the fifth case plural (ablative) is the same as the third case plural (instrumental), they will not be shown.

Gumba si, “ato” “sissā”ti ca vattate.

Regarding `gumba` with the `si` suffix: the rules 'ato' and 'sissa' also apply.

110. Kvace+vā.

110. And sometimes optionally.

Akārantato nāmasmā parassa sissa e hoti vā kvaci. Gumbe gumbo, gumbā. Bho gumba gumbā, bhavanto gumbā iccādi sugatasamaṃ. Evaṃ phussitagge phussitaggo, vattabbe vattabbo iccādi. Sisso+kārassa niccattā katthaci pakkhe ekāratta+mida+māraddhanti sisso+kārapakkhe eva bhavatīti “aṃ napuṃsake”ti a+mādesena ekārassa napuṃsakavisaye bādhitattā “bahulaṃ” vidhānā napuṃsakepi sukhe dukkheti kvaci hoteva.

After a noun ending in -a, the suffix `si` sometimes optionally becomes `e`. For example: `gumbe` or `gumbo`; plural `gumbā`. The vocative `bho gumba`, `gumbā`, `bhavanto gumbā`, and so on, are the same as for `sugata`. Similarly: `phussitagge`, `phussitaggo`; `vattabbe`, `vattabbo`, etc. Since the change of `si` to `o` is the regular rule, this change to `e` is introduced as an occasional alternative; thus it occurs only as an alternative to the `o` form. And because this change to `e` is obstructed in the neuter by the substitution of `aṃ` (by the rule 'aṃ napuṃsake'), it is due to the 'bahulaṃ' (variously) provision that it sometimes occurs even in the neuter, as in `sukhe` and `dukkhe`.

“Yossa” “ṭe”ti ca vattate.

The rules concerning `yo` and `ṭe` are also carried forward.

135. Ekaccādīha+to

135. From `ekacca` and other such words:

Akārantehi ekaccādīhi yonaṃ ṭe hoti. Ekacco, ekacce. Bho ekacca ekaccā, ekacce. Ekaccaṃ, ekacce. Evaṃ esa+sa+paṭhamasaddānaṃ.

After `ekacca` and other such words ending in -a, the `yo` suffixes become `ṭe`. For example: `ekacco`, `ekacce`. Vocative: `bho ekacca`, `ekaccā`, `ekacce`. Accusative: `ekaccaṃ`, `ekacce`. The same applies to the words `esa`, `sa`, and `paṭhama`.

Kodho[M 0.0037], kodhā. Bho kodha kodhā, kodhā. Kodhaṃ, kodhe.

Nominative: `kodho`, `kodhā`. Vocative: `bho kodha`, `kodhā`. Accusative: `kodhaṃ`, `kodhe`.

“Nāssa” “sā”ti ca vattate.

The rule that `nā` becomes `sā` is also carried forward.

107. Kodhādīhi

107. From `kodha` and other such words:

Kodhādīhi nāssa sā hoti vā. Kodhasā kodhena. Atthasā atthena. “Ye uttamatthāni tayi labhimhā”ti atthasaddo napuṃsakaliṅgopi dissati.

After `kodha` and other such words, the suffix `nā` (instrumental singular) optionally becomes `sā`. For example: `kodhasā` or `kodhena`; `atthasā` or `atthena`. The word `attha` is also seen in the neuter gender, as in 'Ye uttamatthāni tayi labhimhā' (Which highest meanings we obtained in you).

“Smino ṭī”ti ca vattate.

The rule that `smiṃ` becomes `ṭi` is also carried forward.

175. Divādito

175. From `diva` and other such words:

Divādīhi nāmehi smino ṭi hoti niccaṃ. Divi, evaṃ bhuvi. Etthaṭimhi niccaṃ vakārāgamo rasso ca. Ettha bhūsaddo vadhūsaddasamaṃ.

After nouns such as `diva` and others, the suffix `smiṃ` (locative singular) always becomes `ṭi`. For example: `divi`; similarly `bhuvi`. In the latter case, when `ṭi` is the suffix, there is always the insertion of `v` and the shortening of the preceding vowel. In other respects, the word `bhū` is declined like the word `vadhū`.

“Ve”ti vattate.

The term `vā` (optionally) is carried forward.

144. Manādīhi smiṃ+saṃ+nā+smānaṃ si+so+o+sā+sā

144. After `mana` and other such words, the suffixes `smiṃ`, `sa`, `nā`, `smā`, and `naṃ` are replaced by `si`, `so`, `o`, `sā`, and `sā` respectively.

Manādīhi smi+mādīnaṃ si+so+o+sā+sā honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Mano, manā. Bho mana manā, manā. Mano, manaṃ, mane. Manasā manena, manehi manebhi. Manaso manassa, manānaṃ. Manasā manā manamhā manasmā, manehi manebhi. Manasi manamhi manasmiṃ, manesu.

After `mana` and other such words, `smiṃ` and the other suffixes optionally become `si, so, o, sā, sā` respectively. The paradigm is as follows: Nominative: `mano`, `manā`. Vocative: `bho mana`, `manā`. Accusative: `mano`, `manaṃ`; `mane`. Instrumental: `manasā`, `manena`; `manehi`, `manebhi`. Genitive: `manaso`, `manassa`; `manānaṃ`. Ablative: `manasā`, `manā`, `manamhā`, `manasmā`; `manehi`, `manebhi`. Locative: `manasi`, `manamhi`, `manasmiṃ`; `manesu`.

Evaṃ [M 0.0038] vaco payo tejo,

Tapo ceto tamo yaso.

Similarly: `vaco` (speech), `payo` (milk, water), `tejo` (radiance, fire), `tapo` (austerity), `ceto` (mind), `tamo` (darkness), `yaso` (fame).

Ayo vayo siro saro,

Uro+tye+te manādayo.

`ayo` (iron), `vayo` (age), `siro` (head), `saro` (lake), `uro` (chest)—these belong to the `manādi` group.

Rūpasiddhiyaṃ aha+rahasaddā manādīsu paṭhitā. Ahassa āpādittā rahoti nipātattā rahasīti vibhatyantapaṭirūpakanipātattā idha na gahitā.

In the Rūpasiddhi, the words `aha` and `raha` are listed in the `manādi` group. They are not included here because `aha` is a stem, and `raho` is a particle, while `rahasi` is an indeclinable particle that resembles an inflected form.

Gacchanta si, “sissa” “ve”ti ca vattate. Parato bhiyyo nānuvattayissāma, vuttiyā eva anuvattassa gamyamānattā.

Regarding `gacchanta` with the `si` suffix: the rules concerning the suffix `si` and `vā` (optionally) are also carried forward. From this point on, we will not explicitly state what is carried forward, because it will be understood from the commentary itself.

148. Ntassaṃ

148. For `nta`, `aṃ`.

Simhi ntapaccayassa aṃ hoti vā. “Sutānumitesu sutasambandhova balavā”ti ñāyā “ntassā”ti sutattā ntasseva aṃ, na tadantassa anumitassa saddassa. Eva+muparipi nta+ntūnaṃ ādesavidhānaṭṭhānesu. “Gasinaṃ”ti silopo. Gacchaṃ gacchanto.

In the nominative singular (`si`), the `nta` suffix optionally becomes `aṃ`. By the maxim, 'Among what is heard and what is inferred, the connection to what is heard is stronger,' because 'ntassa' is explicitly stated, `aṃ` is for `nta` itself, not for the inferred word ending in it. Likewise, this applies in subsequent places where substitutions for `nta` and `ntu` are prescribed. By 'Gasinaṃ', there is elision of `si`. Examples: `gacchaṃ`, `gacchanto`.

215. Nta+ntūnaṃ nto yomhi paṭhame

215. For `nta` and `ntu`, `nto` in the nominative plural (`yo`).

Paṭhame yomhi nta+ntūnaṃ savibhattīnaṃ ntoiccādeso hoti vā. Sa ca bahulādhikārā pumeva, gacchanto gacchantā.

In the nominative plural (`yo`), `nto` is optionally substituted for `nta` and `ntu` together with their inflections. And this, due to the governing `bahula` rule, occurs mostly in the masculine gender. Examples: `gacchanto`, `gacchantā`.

218. Ṭa+ṭā+aṃ ge

218. `Ṭa`, `ṭā`, and `aṃ` in the vocative (`ge`).

Ge pare nta+ntūnaṃ savibhattīnaṃ ṭa+ṭā+aṃiccādesā niccaṃ honti bahulaṃ. Bho gaccha gacchā gacchaṃ, gacchanto gacchantā.

When the vocative (`ge`) follows, `ṭa`, `ṭā`, and `aṃ` are, by the `bahula` rule, variously substituted for `nta` and `ntu` together with their inflections. Examples: `bho gaccha`, `gacchā`, `gacchaṃ`; alternatively, `gacchanto`, `gacchantā`.

92. Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃ+se

92. And for `nta`, `ṭa` optionally in the accusative plural (`aṃse`).

Aṃsesu [M 0.0039] ntapaccayassa ṭa hoti vā ntussa ca. Vavatthitavibhāsā+yaṃ. Gacchaṃ gacchantaṃ, gacchante.

In the accusative plural (`aṃsesu`), `ṭa` optionally occurs as a substitute for the `nta` suffix, and also for `ntu`. This is a case of restricted optionality. Examples: `gacchaṃ`, `gacchantaṃ`, `gacchante`.

217. To+tā+ti+tā sa+smā+smiṃ nāsu

217. `To`, `tā`, `ti`, `tā` for `sa`, `smā`, `smiṃ`, and `nā`.

Sa+smā+smiṃ+nāsu nta+ntūnaṃ savibhattīnaṃ to+tā+ti+tā honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Gacchatā gacchantena, gacchantehi gacchantebhi. Gacchato gacchassa gacchantassa.

When the endings `sa` (genitive singular), `smā` (ablative singular), `smiṃ` (locative singular), and `nā` (instrumental singular) follow, `to`, `tā`, `ti`, and `tā` are optionally substituted respectively for `nta` and `ntu` together with their inflections. Examples: `gacchatā`, `gacchantena` (instrumental singular); `gacchantehi`, `gacchantebhi` (instrumental/ablative plural); `gacchato`, `gacchassa`, `gacchantassa` (genitive singular).

216. Taṃ naṃmhi

216. `Taṃ` in `naṃ`.

Naṃmhi nta+ntūnaṃ savibhattīnaṃ taṃ vā hoti. Gacchataṃ gacchantānaṃ. Gacchatā gacchantā gacchantamhā gacchantasmā. Gacchati gacchante gacchantamhi gacchanthasmiṃ, cchentesu.

In the genitive plural (`naṃ`), `taṃ` is an optional substitute for `nta` and `ntu` together with their inflections. Examples: `gacchataṃ`, `gacchantānaṃ` (genitive plural); `gacchatā`, `gacchantā`, `gacchantamhā`, `gacchantasmā` (ablative singular); `gacchati`, `gacchante`, `gacchantamhi`, `gacchantasmiṃ` (locative singular); `gacchantesu` (locative plural).

Evaṃ mahaṃ caraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ, dadaṃ bhuñjaṃ suṇaṃ pacaṃ;

Jayaṃ jīraṃ vacaṃ pīyaṃ, saraṃ kubbaṃ japaṃ vajaṃ.

Similarly: `mahaṃ` (honoring), `caraṃ` (walking), `tiṭṭhaṃ` (standing), `dadaṃ` (giving), `bhuñjaṃ` (eating), `suṇaṃ` (hearing), `pacaṃ` (cooking); `jayaṃ` (conquering), `jīraṃ` (growing old), `vacaṃ` (speaking), `pīyaṃ` (drinking), `saraṃ` (remembering), `kubbaṃ` (doing), `japaṃ` (muttering), `vajaṃ` (going).

Iccādayo.

And so forth.

Bhavanta si,

For `bhavanta`, in `si`,

149. Bhūto

149. From `bhū`.

Niyamasutta+midaṃ. Bhūdhātuto ntassa aṃ hoti simhi niccaṃ punabbidhānā. Bhavaṃ.

This is a restrictive rule. From the root `bhū`, the `nta` suffix always becomes `aṃ` in the nominative singular (`si`), due to this re-statement of the rule. Example: `bhavaṃ`.

146. Bhavato vā bhontoga+yo+nā+se

146. For `bhavanta`, `bhonto` optionally before `ga`, `yo`, `nā`, and `se`.

Bhavantasaddassa bhontādeso vā hoti ga+yo+nā+se. Ntoādeso, bhonto bhontā bhavanto bhavantā. Ge [M 0.0040] pana bho bhonta bhontā bhava bhavā bhavaṃ, bhonto bhontā bhavanto bhavantā. Bhontādesapakkhe ṭa+ṭā+aṃādesā bahulādhikārā na honti. Bhavaṃ bhavantaṃ, bhonte bhavante. Bhotā bhontena bhavatā bhavantena, bhavantehi bhavantebhi. Bhoto bhontassa bhavato bhavassa bhavantassa, bhavataṃ bhavantānaṃ. Bhavatā iccādi gacchantasamaṃ.

For the word `bhavanta`, the substitution `bhonto` optionally occurs before `ga` (vocative), `yo` (nominative/accusative plural), `nā` (instrumental), and `se` (accusative plural). Nominative plural forms: `bhonto`, `bhontā`, `bhavanto`, `bhavantā`. In the vocative plural (`ge`), however, the forms are `bho bhonta`, `bhontā`, `bhava`, `bhavā`, `bhavaṃ`; `bhonto`, `bhontā`, `bhavanto`, `bhavantā`. In the case where `bhonta` is substituted, the substitutions `ṭa`, `ṭā`, and `aṃ` do not occur, due to the governing `bahula` rule. Accusative singular: `bhavaṃ`, `bhavantaṃ`. Accusative plural: `bhonte`, `bhavante`. Instrumental singular: `bhotā`, `bhontena`, `bhavatā`, `bhavantena`. Instrumental/Ablative plural: `bhavantehi`, `bhavantebhi`. Genitive singular: `bhoto`, `bhontassa`, `bhavato`, `bhavassa`, `bhavantassa`. Genitive plural: `bhavataṃ`, `bhavantānaṃ`. The declension from `bhavatā` onwards is like that of `gacchanta`.

Bhoiti āmantaṇe nipāto, “kuto nu āgacchatha bho tayo janā”ti bahuvacanepi dassanato. Evaṃ bhanteti. Bhaddeti bhaddasaddantarena siddhaṃ. Bhaddantaiti dassa dvibhāvena.

The word `bho` is a particle used in the vocative, as seen even in the plural, for example, 'kuto nu āgacchatha bho tayo janā' (Where indeed do you three men come from?). Similarly with `bhante`. The form `bhaddeti` is derived from the alternative word `bhadda`. The form `bhaddanta` is formed by the doubling of `d`.

Saṃ santo, santo santā. Bho sa sā saṃ, santo santā. Saṃ santaṃ “saṃyogādilopoti nassa lope “yaṃ yañhi rāja bhajati, santaṃ vā yadi vā asaṃ”, sante. Satā santena.

Nominative singular: `saṃ` (neuter), `santo` (masculine). Nominative plural: `santo`, `santā`. Vocative: `bho sa` (masculine singular), `sā` (feminine singular), `saṃ` (neuter singular); `santo`, `santā` (plural). Accusative singular: `saṃ`, `santaṃ`. By the rule 'saṃyogādilopo', the `n` is elided in certain cases, as in the verse: 'yaṃ yañhi rāja bhajati, santaṃ vā yadi vā asaṃ' (Whatever a king associates with, whether good or bad). Locative singular: `sante`. Instrumental singular: `satā`, `santena`.

145. Sato saba bhe

145. For `santa`, `saba` before `bhi`.

Santasaddassa saba bhavati bhakāre. Sabbhi santehi. Niccattā santebhīti na hoti. Sato sassa santassa iccādi gacchantasamaṃ.

For the word `santa`, `saba` is substituted before the `bhi` ending. Examples: `sabbhi`, `santehi`. Because this rule is obligatory, the form `santebhi` does not occur. The forms `sato`, `sassa`, `santassa`, etc., are like those of `gacchanta`.

150. Mahantā+rahantānaṃ ṭā vā

150. For `mahanta` and `arahanta`, `ā` optionally.

Simhi mahantā+rahantānaṃ ntassa ṭā vā hoti. Mahā mahaṃ mahanto, mahanto mahantā. Arahā arahaṃ, arahanto arahantā iccādi gacchantasamaṃ.

In the nominative singular (`si`), for `mahanta` and `arahanta`, `ā` is an optional substitute for the `nta` ending. Examples: `mahā`, `mahaṃ`, `mahanto` (nominative singular); `mahanto`, `mahantā` (nominative plural). `arahā`, `arahaṃ` (nominative singular); `arahanto`, `arahantā` (nominative plural). The rest of the declension is like `gacchanta`.

Asma si,

For `asman`, in `si`.

154. Rājādīyuvāditvā

154. Because they belong to the `rājādi` and `yuvādi` groups.

Rājādīhi [M 0.0041] yuvādīhi ca parassa sissa ā hoti. Asmā,

After stems of the `rājādi` and `yuvādi` groups, the nominative singular ending `si` becomes `ā`. Example: `asmā`.

156. Yona+māno

156. For `yo`, `āno`.

Rājādīhi yuvādīhi ca yona+māno vā hoti. Asmāno asmā. Bho asma asmā, asmāno asmā.

After stems of the `rājādi` and `yuvādi` groups, `āno` is an optional substitute for the nominative plural ending `yo`. Examples (nominative plural): `asmāno`, `asmā`. Examples (vocative): `bho asma`, `asmā` (singular); `asmāno`, `asmā` (plural).

155. Vā+mhā+naṅa

155. Vā+mhā+naṅa

Rājādīnaṃ yuvādīnañca ānaṅa hoti vā aṃmhi. Asmānaṃ asmaṃ, asmāno asme.

For words of the rājādi and yuvādi groups, ānaṅa optionally occurs in the aṃ case. Asmānaṃ asmaṃ, asmāno asme.

80. Nāsse+no

80. Nāsse+no

Kammādito nāvacanassa eno vā hoti. Asmena asmanā, asmehi asmebhi. Asmassa, asmānaṃ. Asmā asmamhā asmasmā iccādi.

From the kamma group onwards, for the nā ending, eno optionally occurs. Asmena asmanā, asmehi asmebhi. Asmassa, asmānaṃ. Asmā asmamhā asmasmā, etc.

79. Kammādito

79. Kammādito

Kammādito smino ni hoti vā. Asmani asme asmamhi asmasmiṃ, asmesu. Kamma camma vesma bhasma brahma atta ātuma ghamma muddhaiti kammādayo. Muddha gaṇḍivadhanva aṇima laghimādayo asmasamā. Rāja brahma sakha atta ātuma gaṇḍivadhanva asma aṇima laghimādayo rājādayo.

From the kammādi group onwards, for the smiṃ ending, ni optionally occurs. Asmani, asme, asmamhi, asmasmiṃ, asmesu. Kamma, camma, vesma, bhasma, brahma, atta, ātuma, ghamma, muddha—these are the kammādi group. Muddha, gaṇḍivadhanva, aṇima, laghimā, etc., are like asma. Rāja, brahma, sakha, atta, ātuma, gaṇḍivadhanva, asma, aṇima, laghimā, etc., are the rājādi group.

“Dhammo vā+ññatthe”ti gaṇasuttena rājādīsu paṭṭhitattā daḷadhammo daḷadhammāti vā hoti. Yuva sā suvā maghava puma [M 0.0042] vattahāti yuvādayo. Rājā, rājāno rājā. Bhorāja rājā, rājāno rājā. Rājānaṃ rājaṃ, rājāno rāje.

By the group rule 'Dhammo vā aññatthe', because it is established among the rājādi group, daḷadhammo and daḷadhammā optionally occur. Yuva, sā, suvā, maghavā, pumā, vattahā—these are the yuvādi group. Rājā, rājāno rājā. Bho rāja, rājāno rājā. Rājānaṃ rājaṃ, rājāno rāje.

123. Rājassi nāmhi

123. Rājassi nāmhi

“Sabbadattena rājinā”ti pāṭhampati ida+māraddhaṃ. Rājassi vā hoti nāmhi. Rājinā.

This rule is commenced with reference to the reading 'Sabbadattena rājinā'. For rāja, i is optionally added in the nā case. Rājinā.

222. Nā+smāsu raññā

222. Nā+smāsu raññā

Nā+smāsu rājassa savibhattissa raññā hoti niccaṃ. Anekavaṇṇattā sabbassa. Raññā.

In the nā (instrumental singular) and smā (ablative singular) cases, for rāja with its case ending, raññā is the constant substitution. Because it consists of more than one letter, it replaces the whole. Raññā.

124. Su+naṃ+hisū

124. Su+naṃ+hisū

Rājassa ū hoti vā su+naṃ+hisu. “Chaṭṭhiyantassāti antassa hoti. Rājūhi rājehi rājūbhi rājebhi.

For rāja, ū optionally occurs in the su (locative plural), naṃ (genitive plural), and hi (instrumental plural) cases. As it is specified in the genitive case, the substitution occurs at the end. Rājūhi rājehi, rājūbhi rājebhi.

223. Rañño+raññassa+rājino se

223. Rañño+raññassa+rājino se

Se rājassa savibhattissa ete ādesā honti. Rañño raññassa rājino, rājūnaṃ.

In the se (genitive singular) case, for rāja with its case ending, these substitutions occur. Rañño, raññassa, rājino, rājūnaṃ.

221. Rājassa raññaṃ

221. Rājassa raññaṃ

Naṃmhi rājassa savibhattissa raññaṃ vā hoti. Raññaṃ. Raññā, rājūhi rājehi rājūbhi rājebhi.

In the naṃ (genitive plural) case, for rāja with its case ending, raññaṃ optionally occurs. Raññaṃ. Raññā, rājūhi rājehi, rājūbhi rājebhi.

224. Smimhi raññe+rājini

224. Smimhi raññe+rājini

Smimhi rājassa savibhattissa raññe+rājini honti niccaṃ. Raññe rājini, rājūsu rājesu.

In the smiṃ (locative singular) case, for rāja with its case ending, raññe and rājini are the constant substitutions. Raññe rājini, rājūsu rājesu.

225. Samāse vā

225. Samāse vā

Iti [M 0.0043] gaṇasuttena rājassa nā+smā+smiṃsu yaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ vā hoti. Kāsiraññā kāsirājinā kāsirājena, kāsirājūbhi kāsirājebhi kāsirājūhi kāsirājehi. Kāsirañño kāsiraññassa kāsirājino kāsirājassa. Kāsiraññā kāsirājasmā. Kāsirājūnaṃ kāsirājānaṃ. Kāsiraññe kāsirājini kāsirāje kāsirājamhi kāsirājasmiṃ, kāsirājūsu kāsirājesu.

Thus, by the group rule, what was stated for rāja in the nā (instrumental singular), smā (ablative singular), and smiṃ (locative singular) cases, that optionally occurs. Kāsiraññā kāsirājinā kāsirājena, kāsirājūbhi kāsirājebhi kāsirājūhi kāsirājehi. Kāsirañño kāsiraññassa kāsirājino kāsirājassa. Kāsiraññā kāsirājasmā. Kāsirājūnaṃ kāsirājānaṃ. Kāsiraññe kāsirājini kāsirāje kāsirājamhi kāsirājasmiṃ, kāsirājūsu kāsirājesu.

Addhā, addhāno addhā. Bho addha addhā, addhāno addhā. Addhānaṃ addhaṃ, addhāno addhe.

Addhā, addhāno addhā. Bho addha addhā, addhāno addhā. Addhānaṃ addhaṃ, addhāno addhe.

192. Puma+kamma+thāma+ddhānaṃ sa+smāsu ca

192. Puma+kamma+thāma+ddhānaṃ sa+smāsu ca

Pumādīna+mu hoti vā sa+smāsu nāmhi ce+ti utte addhunā, kammādittā “nāsse+no”ti vā eno, addhena addhanā, addhehi addhebhi. Se ukāre ca –

For words of the pumādi group, u optionally occurs in the sa (genitive singular), smā (ablative singular), and nā (instrumental singular) cases; thus addhunā is formed. Because it belongs to the kammādi group, eno optionally occurs by the rule 'nāsse+no', giving addhena and addhanā. Addhehi addhebhi. And in the se (genitive singular) case, when u is applied –

1,9. Iyuvaṇṇā jhalā nāmassa+nte

1,9. Iyuvaṇṇā jhalā nāmassa+nte

Nāmaṃ pāṭipadikaṃ, tassa ante vattamānā ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalasaññā honti yathākkamaṃ. I ca u ca iyu, iyu ca te vaṇṇā ceti iyuvaṇṇā, “dvandante sūyamānaṃ pacceka+mabhisambandhiya te”ti vuttattā vaṇṇasaddaṃ pacceka+mabhisambandhiya “ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā”ti vuttaṃ.

The stem is a nāma (noun); the i-vowel and u-vowel occurring at its end are designated jhala, respectively. I and u are iyu; and those iyu are vowels, thus iyuvaṇṇā. Because it is said, 'what is heard at the end of a dvanda compound is connected to each element', the word vaṇṇa (vowel) is connected to each element individually, and thus it is said 'i-vowel and u-vowel'.

81. Jhalā sassa no

81. Jhalā sassa no

Jhalato sassa no vā hoti. Addhuno addhussa addhassa, addhānaṃ.

After jhala, the genitive singular ending sa optionally becomes no. Addhuno, addhussa, addhassa, addhānaṃ.

82. Nā smāssa

82. Nā smāssa

Jhalato [M 0.0044] smāssa nā hoti vā, addhunā addhumhā addhusmā addhā addhamhā addhasmā. “Kammādito”ti smino ni, addhani addhe addhamhi addhasmiṃ, addhesu. Addhasaddo ce+tthakāla+ddhānavāci, na bhāgavācī.

After jhala, the ablative singular ending smā optionally becomes nā. Addhunā, addhumhā, addhusmā, addhā, addhamhā, addhasmā. By the rule 'Kammādito smino ni', ni is substituted for the locative singular ending. Addhani, addhe, addhamhi, addhasmiṃ, addhesu. The word addha here denotes time and path, not a share.

Attā, attāno iccādi yāva dutiyā rājāva, kammādittā ene attena attanā.

The words attā, attāno, and so forth, up to the accusative case, are declined like rājan. Due to its inclusion in the kammādi group, the instrumental singular forms ena, attena, and attanā occur.

195. Su+hisu naka

195. The augment naka is inserted before su and hi.

Atta+ātumānaṃ su+hisu nakāgamo hoti. “Ñakānubandhā+dyantā”ti paribhāsato kakāro antāvayavattho, attanehi atthehi attanebhi attebhi.

After the stems attan and ātuman, the augment naka is inserted before the endings su (locative plural) and hi (instrumental plural). By the meta-rule ñakānubandhādyantā, the letter ka functions as the final component. Examples: attanehi, attehi, attanebhi, attebhi.

194. No+ttātumā

194. The ending no after attan and ātuman.

Atta+ātumehi sassa no vā hoti. Attano attassa, attānaṃ.

After the stems attan and ātuman, the genitive singular ending ssa is optionally replaced by no. Examples: attano, attassa; attānaṃ.

196. Smāssa nā brahmā ca

196. For brahman, nā replaces smā.

Brahmā atta+ātumehi ca parassa smāssa nā hoti niccaṃ. Attanā. Smimhi kammādittā ni, attani atte attamhi attasmiṃ, attanesu attesu. Ātumā attāva.

After brahman, and also after attan and ātuman, the ablative ending smā is always replaced by nā. Example: attanā. In the locative singular (smiṃ), due to inclusion in the kammādi group, the ending is ni. The forms are: attani, atte, attamhi, attasmiṃ (locative singular); attanesu, attesu (locative plural). The declension of ātuman is like that of attan.

Brahmā, brahmāno brahmā, “brahmassu vā”ti sutte “brahmassū”ti yogavibhāgā ānomhi brahmassa u, parassaralope brahmunotipi sijjhati. Ayañca brahmasaṃyutte dissati. Brahmā ge-

Forms: Brahmā (nominative singular); brahmāno, brahmā (nominative plural). In the rule brahmassu vā, by splitting the rule (yogavibhāga) at brahmassū, the vowel u is added to brahmassa (genitive singular), and with the elision of the following vowel, the form brahmuno is also accomplished. This form is seen in the Brahmasaṃyutta. The stem brahman before the vocative singular ending...

60. Gha+brahmādite

60. In the vocative singular, for brahman and other stems.

Ākatigaṇo+yaṃ[M 0.0045], ākatīti jāti, jātipadhānagaṇotya+ttho. Ghasaññato brahma+kattu+isi+sakhādīhi ca gasse+vā hoti. Bho brahme brahmā, brahmāno brahmā. Brahmānaṃ brahmaṃ, brahmāno brahme.

This is an ākatigaṇa (a class-based group). Ākati means 'class'; the meaning is that this is a group where the class is primary. After stems with the designation gha, and after brahman, kattar, isi, sakhar, and so forth, the vocative singular ending is optionally replaced by e. Examples: Bho brahme, brahmā (vocative singular); brahmāno, brahmā (nominative plural). Brahmānaṃ, brahmaṃ (accusative singular); brahmāno, brahme (accusative plural).

191. Nāmhi

191. In the instrumental singular.

Brahmassu hoti nāmhi niccaṃ. Brahmunā, brahmehi brahmebhi.

For the stem brahman, the vowel u is always inserted before the instrumental singular ending (nā). Example: brahmunā (instrumental singular); brahmehi, brahmebhi (instrumental plural).

190. Brahmassu vā

190. For brahman, u is optionally inserted.

Brahmassu vā hoti sa+naṃsu. “Jhalā sassa no”ti no. Brahmuno brahmussa brahmassa, brahmūnaṃ brahmānaṃ. “Smāssa nā brahmā ce”ti smāssa nā, ukāre brahmunā. “Ambvādīhi”ti smino ni, imassa ākatigaṇattā brahmassa kammādittepi ettha vuttā. Brahmani brahme brahmamhi brahmasmiṃ, brahmesu.

For the stem brahman, the vowel u is optionally inserted before the endings sa (genitive singular), naṃ (genitive plural), and su (locative plural). By the rule jhalā sassa no, the ending no also occurs. The forms are: brahmuno, brahmussa, brahmassa (genitive singular); brahmūnaṃ, brahmānaṃ (genitive plural). By the rule smāssa nā brahmā ca, nā replaces smā; with the vowel u, the form is brahmunā. By the rule ambvādīhi, ni replaces smiṃ; because this stem belongs to an ākatigaṇa, its inclusion in the kammādi group is also mentioned here. The forms are: brahmani, brahme, brahmamhi, brahmasmiṃ (locative singular); brahmesu (locative plural).

Sakhā, rājādittā ā.

The form is sakhā. Due to its inclusion in the rājādi group, the nominative singular ending is ā.

2,157. Āyo no ca sakhā

2,157. For sakhar, āyo and no also [replace yo].

Sakhato yona+māyo no honti vā āno ca. Sakhāyo sakhāno.

After the stem sakhar, the nominative plural ending yo is optionally replaced by āyo and no, and also by āno. Examples: sakhāyo, sakhāno.

159. No+nā+sesvi

159. Not in the vocative, instrumental, and remaining cases.

Sakhassa i hoti niccaṃ no+nā+sesu. Sakhino.

For the stem sakhar, the vowel i is always inserted, except before the vocative, instrumental, and remaining case endings. Example: sakhino.

161. Yo+svaṃ+hisu cā+raṅa

161. The replacement āraṅa also occurs before yo, aṃ, and hi.

Sakhassa vā āraṅa hoti yo+svaṃ+hisu smā+naṃsuca.

For the stem sakhar, the replacement āraṅa optionally occurs before the endings yo, aṃ, hi, smā, and naṃ.

171. Āraṅasmā

171. After the replacement āraṅa.

Āravādesato [M 0.0046] paresaṃ yonaṃ ṭo hoti. Sakhāro sakhā. Ge tu “gha+brahmādite”ti e, sakhe sakha sakhā. Bahuvacanaṃ paṭhamā viya. Aṃmhi “vā+mhā+naṅa”ti ānaṅa, sakhānaṃ sakhāraṃ sakhaṃ, sakhāyo sakhāno sakhino.

After the replacement āra, the ending yo becomes o. Examples: sakhāro (nominative plural), sakhā (nominative singular). In the vocative singular (ge), however, by the rule gha-brahmādite, the ending is e. Forms: sakhe, sakha, sakhā. The vocative plural is like the nominative plural. In the accusative singular (aṃ), by the rule vā amhā naṅa, the replacement is ānaṅa. Forms: sakhānaṃ, sakhāraṃ, sakhaṃ (accusative singular); sakhāyo, sakhāno, sakhino (accusative plural).

172. Ṭo ṭe vā

172. The ending yo is optionally replaced by o or e.

Āravādesamhā yonaṃ ṭo ṭe vā honti yathākkamaṃti ṭe. Aññattha “āraṅasmā”ti ṭo. Sakhāre sakhāro sakhe. Ṭoggahaṇaṃ lāghavatthaṃ. Sakhinā, sakhārehi sakhehi. “Jhalā sassa no”ti jhato sassa no, sakhino sakhissa, sakhārānaṃ.

After the replacement āra, the ending yo is optionally replaced by o or e. The word 'sequentially' implies that e is used for the accusative plural. Elsewhere, by the rule āraṅasmā, o is used. Examples: sakhāre (accusative plural), sakhāro (nominative plural), sakhe (vocative singular). The mention of ṭo (o) is for brevity. Instrumental forms: sakhinā; sakhārehi, sakhehi. By the rule jhalā sassa no, after jha-class stems, ssa is replaced by no. Genitive forms: sakhino, sakhissa; sakhārānaṃ.

160. Smā+naṃsu vā

160. Optionally before smā and naṃ.

Sakhassa vā i hoti smā+naṃsu. Sakhīnaṃ sakhānaṃ.

For the stem sakhar, the vowel i is optionally inserted before the endings smā and naṃ. Examples: sakhīnaṃ, sakhānaṃ.

171. Ṭā nā+smānaṃ

171. The endings nā and smā are replaced by ā.

Āravādesamhā nā+smānaṃ ṭā hoti niccaṃ. Sakhārā, bahulādhikārā sakhārasmā. “Nā smāssā”ti nā, sakhinā sakhismā sakhā sakhamhā sakhasmā.

After the replacement āra, the endings nā (instrumental) and smā (ablative) are always replaced by ā. Example: sakhārā. By the principle of extensive application, the form sakhārasmā also occurs. By the rule nā smāssa, the ending is nā. Other forms are: sakhinā (instrumental); sakhismā, sakhamhā, sakhasmā (ablative); sakhā (nominative).

158. Ṭe smino

158. The ending smiṃ is replaced by e.

Sakhato smino ṭe hoti niccaṃ. Sakhe, sakhāresu sakhesu. Sakhi sakhīti itthiyaṃyeva payogo dissati, tasmā “nadādito ṅī”ti vīmhi ālapanattā vā rasso.

After the stem `sakha`, `ṭe` is always the substitute for the `smiṃ` ending. Examples: `Sakhe`, `sakhāresu`, `sakhesu`. The words `sakhi` and `sakhī` are seen to be used only in the feminine; therefore, the vowel is shortened either by the rule 'nadādito ṅī' or because it is a vocative.

Yuvādittā [M 0.0047] ā, yuvā.

After the `yuvādi` group of words, `ā` is substituted for the `si` ending, as in `yuvā`.

181. Yonaṃ no+ne vā

181. For the `yo` endings, `no` and `ne` are optional substitutes.

Yuvādīhi yonaṃ no+ne vā honti yathākkamaṃ. “Yona+māno”ti ānomhi siddhepi “dutiyassa ne”ti ganthagāravo hotīti yathākkamaṃpati lāghavatthaṃ noggahaṇaṃ.

After the `yuvādi` group of words, `no` and `ne` are optionally substituted for the `yo` endings in sequential order. Although the substitution of `āno` for `yo` is already established, the mention of `ne` for the second case ending shows respect for the textual tradition; thus, the inclusion of `no` is for the sake of brevity in establishing this sequence.

179. No+nā+nesvā

179. When `no`, `nā`, and `nesu` follow, `ā` is substituted.

No+nā+nesu yuvādīna+mā hoti. Yuvāno yuvā. Bho yuva yuvā, yuvāno yuvā. Yuvānaṃ yuvaṃ, yuvāno yuvāne yuve. Yuvānā.

When `no`, `nā`, and `nesu` follow, the final vowel of the `yuvādi` words becomes `ā`. Examples: `Yuvāno`, `yuvā`. O `yuva`, `yuvā`; `yuvāno`, `yuvā`. `Yuvānaṃ`, `yuvaṃ`; `yuvāno`, `yuvāne`, `yuve`. `Yuvānā`.

178. Yuvādīnaṃ su+hisvā+naṅa

178. For the `yuvādi` group of words, `ānaṅa` is optionally substituted for the `su` and `hi` endings.

Su+hisu yuvādīna+mānaṅa hoti. Yuvānehi yuvānebhi.

For the `yuvādi` group of words, `ānaṅa` is substituted for the `su` and `hi` endings. Examples: `Yuvānehi`, `yuvānebhi`.

193. Yuvā sassi+no

193. After `yuva`, `ino` is substituted for the `ssa` ending.

Yuvā sassa vā ino hoti. Yuvino yuvassa, yuvānaṃ.

After `yuva`, `ino` is optionally substituted for the `ssa` ending. Examples: `Yuvino`, `yuvassa` (genitive singular); `yuvānaṃ` (genitive plural).

180. Smā+smiṃnaṃ nā+ne

180. For `smā` and `smiṃ`, `nā` and `ne` are the substitutes.

Yuvādahi smā+smiṃnaṃ nā+ne niccaṃ honti yathākkamaṃ. Yuvānā, yuvānehi yuvānebhi. Yuvāne, yuvānesu. Maghava+puma+vattahasaddā yuvasaddasamā. Ayaṃ viseso –

After the `yuvādi` group of words, `nā` and `ne` are always substituted for `smā` and `smiṃ` respectively. Examples: `Yuvānā`; `yuvānehi`, `yuvānebhi`. `Yuvāne`; `yuvānesu`. The words `maghava`, `puma`, and `vattaha` are declined like the word `yuva`. This is the distinction:

187. Gassaṃ

187. For the `ssa` ending, `aṃ` is substituted.

Pumasaddato gassa aṃ vā hoti. Pumaṃ puma pumā, pumāno pumā. Pumānaṃ pumaṃ, pumāno pumāne pume.

After the word `puma`, `aṃ` is optionally substituted for the `ssa` ending. Examples: `Pumaṃ`, `puma`, `pumā`; `pumāno`, `pumā`. `Pumānaṃ`, `pumaṃ`; `pumāno`, `pumāne`, `pume`.

185. Nāmhi

185. When the `nā` ending follows.

Pumassā [M 0.0048] hoti nāmhi. Pumānā. “Lakkhaṇikapaṭipadottesu paṭipadottasseva gahaṇaṃ, na lakkhaṇikassā”ti ñāyā paṭipadottanāvibhatti eva gayhati, na nāsmāssa, katalakkhaṇikattā. Paṭipadanti ca “nāmhī”ti nāvibhattiyā paṭipadabhūto anukaraṇasaddo. Na lakkhaṇiko nā. “Puma+kamma+thāma+ddhānaṃ vā sa+smāsu ce”ti vā utte pumunā pumena. Pumuno pumussa pumassa. Pumunā pumā.

For `puma`, the final vowel becomes `ā` when the `nā` ending follows. Example: `Pumānā`. According to the maxim, 'Between a term defined by a rule and the rule itself, the rule itself is to be taken, not the term defined by it,' only the instrumental ending `nā` which is the subject of the rule is taken, not the `nā` derived from `smā`, because that is a defined form. The term `paṭipada` refers to the primary form, which is the `nā` ending in the rule 'nāmhi', not the derived `nā`. By another rule, `u` is optionally substituted, yielding `pumunā` and `pumena`. Other forms are: `Pumuno`, `pumussa`, `pumassa`. `Pumunā`, `pumā`.

184. Pumāti

184. Regarding `puma`:

Smino ne vā hoti. Pumāne pume pumamhi pumasmiṃ.

For the `smiṃ` ending, `ne` is an optional substitute. Examples: `Pumāne`, `pume`, `pumamhi`, `pumasmiṃ`.

186. Sumhā ca

186. And in the case of the `su` ending.

Pumassa sumhi pumādīnaṃ yaṃ niccaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ vā hotīti ānaṅa vā hoti ā ca. Pumānesu pumāsu pumesu. Vattahā, vattahāno vattahā iccādi yuvasaddasamaṃ.

For `puma`, in the case of the `su` ending, the operation stated as mandatory for the `pumādi` group occurs optionally; that is, `ānaṅa` is an optional substitute, as is `ā`. Examples: `Pumānesu`, `pumāsu`, `pumesu`. The word `vattaha` is declined like `yuva`, as in `vattahā`, `vattahāno`, `vattahā`, and so on.

189. Vattahā sa+naṃnaṃ no+nānaṃ

189. After `vattaha`, `no` and `nānaṃ` are substituted for `sa` and `naṃ` respectively.

Vattahā sanaṃnaṃ nonānaṃ niccaṃ honti yathākkamaṃ. Vattahāno vattahānānaṃ.

After `vattaha`, `no` and `nānaṃ` are always substituted for `sa` and `naṃ` respectively. Examples: `Vattahāno`, `vattahānānaṃ`.

Akārantaṃ.

Stems ending in `a`.

Sā si,

The nominative singular form `sā`.

64. Ekavacana+yosva+ghonaṃ

64. Of stems not designated `gha`, the final vowel is shortened in the singular and when `yo` endings follow.

Gho ca o ca gho, na gho agho. “Aghonaṃ”ti ghappaṭisedhe akate ssa+mādīsu paresu ghassa vikappena rasso, ekavacanādīsu [M 0.0049] yosu ca paresu ghassa niccena rassoti viruddhatthagahaṇanivattanattho ghapaṭisedho. Oggahaṇa+muttaratthaṃ. Ekavacane yosu ca gha+okārantavajjitānaṃ nāmānaṃ rasso hoti tiliṅgeti rasse sampatte –

`Gho` refers to stems designated `gha` and those ending in `o`; `agho` is what is not `gho`. The term 'aghonaṃ' is used to prevent a contradiction. If this prohibition were not made, the final vowel of `gha` stems would be optionally shortened before `ssa` and other endings, but obligatorily shortened in the singular and before `yo` endings. The inclusion of `o` is for a subsequent rule. For nouns in all three genders, except those designated `gha` or ending in `o`, the final vowel is shortened in the singular and when `yo` endings follow. When this shortening is thus applicable:

66. Sismiṃ nā+napuṃsakassati

66. But in the case of the `si` ending, this does not apply to non-neuter stems.

Anapuṃsakassa rasso na hotīti simhi tu na rasso. Sā. “Pajjunnova lakkhaṇapavutti jalepi vassati, thalepi vassatī”ti ñāyā yuvādittā sissa ā. Yosu rasse “yonaṃ no+ne vā”ti yossa no. “No nānesvā”ti ā, sāno. Nottābhāvapakkhe “yona+māno”ti vādhikārassa vavatthitavibhāsattā nicca+māno, tasmā no+neabhāvapakkhe sā, seti rūpapasaṅgo na hoti. Sāno. Tathā nettābhāvapakkhe.

For a non-neuter stem, shortening does not occur; thus, before the `si` ending, there is no shortening. Example: `Sā`. According to the maxim, 'Just as Pajjunna, whose nature is to rain, rains on water and on land alike,' because this stem belongs to the `yuvādi` group, `ā` is substituted for `si`. Before `yo` endings, after shortening, `no` is substituted for `yo` by the rule 'yonaṃ no+ne vā'. Then, by 'no nānesvā', the stem vowel becomes `ā`, resulting in `sāno`. In the case where `no` is not substituted, because the option from the governing rule 'yona+māno' is a fixed option, `āno` is always substituted. Therefore, when `no` and `ne` are not applied, the undesirable forms `sā` and `se` do not arise. Example: `Sāno`. The same applies in the case where `ne` is not substituted.

188. Sāssaṃ+se cā+naṅa

188. After `sā`, `ānaṅa` is substituted for the `aṃ` and `se` endings.

Sāsaddassa ānaṅa hoti aṃ+se ge ca niccaṃ. Bho sāna sānā, sāno. Sānaṃ, sāne sāno. Sānā, sānehi sānebhi. Sānassa, sānaṃ. Sānā, sānehi sānebhi. Sāne, sānesu.

For the word `sā`, `ānaṅa` is always substituted for the `aṃ`, `se`, and `ge` endings. Examples: O `sāna`, `sānā`; `sāno`. `Sānaṃ`; `sāne`, `sāno`. `Sānā`; `sānehi`, `sānebhi`. `Sānassa`; `sānaṃ`. `Sānā`; `sānehi`, `sānebhi`. `Sāne`; `sānesu`.

Suvā yuvāva. “Ekavacanayosva+ghonaṃ”ti rassattaṃ viseso. Ge tu –

Suvā is like yuvā. The shortening mentioned in the rule 'ekavacanayosva+ghonaṃ' is a special feature. But in the case of 'ge':

130. Ge vā

130. Optionally in 'ge'

Aghonaṃ ge vā rasso hoti tiliṅge. Bho suva suvā.

For a stem not designated 'gha', shortening optionally occurs in the case of 'ge' in all three genders. (Examples:) Bho suva, suvā.

Ākārantaṃ.

Stems ending in -ā.

Muni [M 0.0050] silopo. Jhe kate –

Muni and the elision of 'si'. When 'jhe' is applied:

93. Yosu jhissa pume

93. In the 'yo' endings, for 'jha', in the masculine

Jhasaññassa issa yosu vā ṭa hoti pulliṅge. Munayo, jhaggahaṇaṃ kiṃ, ikārantasamudāyassa mā siyā. Iggahaṇaṃ kiṃ, īkārassa vāti. Atoti sāmaññaniddesā lakkhaṇikaakārato yonaṃ ṭāṭe sampattāpi avidhānasāmatthiyā na honti. Sāmatthiyañca aññathā anupapatti.

For that which is designated 'jha', 'ṭa' optionally occurs for 'i' in the 'yo' endings in the masculine gender. (Example:) Munayo. Why the inclusion of 'jha'? So that it does not apply to a group of words ending in 'i'. Why the inclusion of 'i'? So that it does not apply to 'ī'. Thus, because of the general designation 'ato', even though 'ṭā' and 'ṭe' would be applicable to 'yo' after an 'a' produced by a rule, they do not occur due to the power of this non-prescription. And this power is due to the impossibility of it being otherwise.

114. Lopo

114. Elision

Jhalato yonaṃ lopo hotīti yolope –

Elision of the 'yo' endings occurs after a stem designated 'jhala'; thus, when 'yo' is elided:

88. Yolopa+nisu dīgho

88. Lengthening when 'yo' is elided and before 'ni' and 'su'

Yonaṃ lopenisu ca dīgho hoti. Muni. Munayoti ettha yolopo kimatthaṃ na hoti, akkena jhattassa nāsitattā. Kinti paṭhamaṃ na hoti, antaraṅgattā jhattassa. Bho muni munī, munayo munī. Muniṃ, munayo munī. Muninā, munīhi munībhi. “Yolopanisu” “vīmantuvantūna” miccādiñāpakā ikārukārānaṃ sunaṃhisu dīghassā+niccattā munihi muninaṃ munisu itipi hoti. “Jhalā sassa no”ti no, munino munissa, munīnaṃ. “Nāsmāssā”ti nā, muninā munimhā munismā. Munimhi munismiṃ, munīsu. “Ito kvaci sassa ṭānubandho” (gaṇasutta)ti brahmādīsu pāṭhā “yo ca sisso mahāmune”ti ettha “gha+brahmādite”ti sassa eṭa.

Lengthening occurs when the 'yo' endings are elided, and before 'ni' and 'su'. (Example:) Munī. Why does the elision of 'yo' not occur in 'munayo'? Because its 'jha' designation has been destroyed by the substitution of 'a'. Why does it not occur first? Because the 'jha' designation is internal. (Forms:) Bho muni, munī; munayo, munī. Muniṃ; munayo, munī. Muninā; munīhi, munībhi. The rules 'Yolopanisu', 'vīmantuvantūna', etc., are indicators that the lengthening of i- and u-vowels before 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi' is optional; therefore, munihi, muninaṃ, and munisu also occur. According to 'Jhalā sassa no', 'no' (occurs); (forms:) munino, munissa; munīnaṃ. According to 'Nāsmāssā', 'nā' (occurs); (forms:) muninā; munimhā, munismā. (Forms:) Munimhi, munismiṃ; munīsu. According to the reading in the brahmādi group, (from the rule) 'Ito kvaci sassa ṭānubandho' (Gaṇasutta), in 'yo ca sisso mahāmune', 'eṭa' occurs for 'sa' according to 'gha+brahmādite'.

Evaṃ –

Similarly:

Joti [M 0.0051] pāṇi gaṇṭhi muṭṭhi, kucchi vatthi sāli vīhi;

Byādhi odhi bodhi sandhi, rāsi kesi sāti dīpi.

Light, hand, knot, fist; belly, bladder, rice, paddy; disease, limit, enlightenment, joint; heap, lion, Sāti, leopard.

Isi gini maṇi dhani, giri ravi kavi kapi;

Asi masi nidhi vidhi, ahi kimi pati hari.

Sage, fire, gem, wealthy person; mountain, sun, poet, monkey; sword, ink, treasure, method; snake, worm, master, Hari.

Ari timi kali bali, jaladhi ca gahapati;

Uramiti varamati, nirupadhi adhipati;

Añjali sārathi atithi, samādhi udadhippabhutayo.

Enemy, large fish, Kali (age), offering; ocean, and householder; Uramati, Varamati, one without substratum, lord; salutation, charioteer, guest; concentration, ocean, and so forth.

Aggi+isīnaṃ ayaṃ viseso –

For 'aggi' and 'isi', this is the special rule:

147. Sissā+ggito ni

147. For 'si' after 'aggi', 'ni'

Aggismā sissa ni hoti vā. Aggini aggi, aggayo iccādi munisaddasamaṃ.

After 'aggi', 'ni' optionally occurs for 'si'. (Forms:) Aggini, aggi; aggayo, etc., are like the word 'muni'.

133. Ṭe sissi+sismā

133. For 'si' after 'isi', 'ṭe'

Isismā sissa ṭe vā hoti. Ise isi. “Gha+brahmādite”ti gassa e vā, bho ise isi, isayo isī. Isiṃ.

After 'isi', 'ṭe' optionally occurs for 'si'. (Forms:) Ise, isi. According to 'Gha+brahmādite', 'e' optionally occurs for 'gha'; (forms:) bho ise, isi; isayo, isī. Isiṃ.

134. Dutiyassa yossa

134. For the second 'yo'

“Dutiyā yossā”ti avatvā “dutiyassa yossā”ti visuṃ karaṇaṃ “ekayoganiddiṭṭhāna+mapye+kadeso+nuvattate, na [M 0.0052] tve+kavibhattiyuttānaṃ”ti ñāyā dutiyāyossāti nānuvattiya yossāti sāmaññena anuvuttiya ekaccādito paṭhamā yossāpi ṭevidhānatthaṃ. Isismā parassa dutiyā yossa ṭe vā hoti. Ise isayo isī, sesaṃ munisamaṃ.

The separate mention of 'dutiyassa yossa' instead of 'dutiyā yossā' is according to the maxim: 'Even a part of what is designated in a single rule may be carried over, but not what is connected by a single case ending.' Thus, 'dutiyāyossā' is not carried over, but 'yossā' is carried over generally, for the purpose of prescribing 'ṭe' even for the first 'yo' from 'ekaccādi'. After 'isi', 'ṭe' optionally occurs for the second 'yo'. (Forms:) Ise; isayo, isī; the rest is like 'muni'.

Ādi, ādayo iccādi, smimhi –

Ādi, ādayo, etc.; in the case of 'smiṃ':

55. Ratyādīhi ṭo smino

55. After 'rati', etc., 'ṭo' for 'smiṃ'

Ratyādīhi smino ṭo vā hoti. Ādo ādimhi ādismiṃ, ādīsu.

After 'rati' and so forth, 'ṭo' optionally occurs for 'smiṃ'. (Examples:) Ādo; ādimhi, ādismiṃ; ādīsu.

Samāse ikārantato yo+smiṃsu viseso.

In compounds, for stems ending in -i, there is a special rule for the 'yo' and 'smiṃ' case endings.

182. Ito+ññatthe pume

182. From a stem ending in -i, in another context, in the masculine

Aññatthe vattamānato ikārantato nāmasmā yonaṃ no+ne vā honti yathākkamaṃ pulliṅge. Ariyavuttino ariyavuttayo ariyavuttī. Bho ariyavutti ariyavuttī, ariyavuttino ariyavuttayo ariyavuttī. Ariyavuttiṃ, ariyavuttino ariyavuttayo ariyavuttī. Ariyavuttinā iccādi tu munisaddasamaṃ.

From a noun ending in -i, when it occurs in another context, for the 'yo' endings, 'no' and 'ne' optionally occur respectively in the masculine gender. (Examples:) Ariyavuttino, ariyavuttayo, ariyavuttī. Bho ariyavutti, ariyavuttī; ariyavuttino, ariyavuttayo, ariyavuttī. Ariyavuttiṃ; ariyavuttino, ariyavuttayo, ariyavuttī. 'Ariyavuttinā', etc., is similar to the word 'muni'.

183. Ne smino kvaci

183. Sometimes 'ne' for 'smiṃ'

Aññatthe ikārantato nāmasmā smino ne vā hoti kvaci. Ariyavuttine ariyavuttimhi ariyavuttismiṃ, ariyavuttīsu. Evaṃ tomaraṅkusapāṇino sāramatino iccādi. Kvaciggahaṇā na sabbattha neādeso.

In another context, from a noun ending in -i, 'ne' optionally occurs for 'smiṃ' sometimes. (Examples:) Ariyavuttine; ariyavuttimhi, ariyavuttismiṃ; ariyavuttīsu. Similarly, tomaraṅkusapāṇino, sāramatino, etc. Due to the inclusion of 'kvaci' (sometimes), the substitution of 'ne' does not occur everywhere.

Ikārantaṃ.

Ending in -i.

Daṇḍī[M 0.0053], silopo. “Ekavacane” ccādinā rasse sampatte anapuṃsakattā “sismiṃnā+napuṃsakassā”ti nisedho. Yomhi ekavacane ca sabbattha rasso.

Daṇḍī, with elision of 'si'. By the rule 'ekavacane', etc., when shortening of the vowel is to be applied, it is prohibited for non-neuter nouns by the rule 'sismiṃ nā napuṃsakassa'. Before the yo ending and in the singular, the vowel is shortened everywhere.

75. Yonaṃ no+ne pume

75. For 'yo', 'no' and 'ne' occur in the masculine gender.

Jhasaññito yonaṃ no+ne vā honti yathākkamaṃ pulliṅge. Daṇḍino.

After a stem designated 'jha', 'no' and 'ne' are optionally and respectively substituted for the 'yo' ending in the masculine gender. Example: Daṇḍino.

115. Jantuhetvīghapehi vā

115. Optionally after 'jantu', 'hetu', stems ending in 'ī', and stems designated 'gha' and 'pa'.

Jantu+hetūhi īkārantehi gha+pasaññehi ca paresaṃ yonaṃ vā lopo hoti. “Yolopanisu dīgho”ti dīghe daṇḍī daṇḍiyo. Ge tu “ge vā”ti vā rasso. Bho daṇḍi daṇḍī, daṇḍino daṇḍī daṇḍiyo.

After 'jantu', 'hetu', stems ending in 'ī', and stems designated 'gha' and 'pa', the following 'yo' ending is optionally elided. By the rule 'yolopanisu dīgho', upon lengthening, the forms are daṇḍī and daṇḍiyo. Before the 'ge' (vocative singular) ending, however, by the rule 'ge vā', shortening is optional. Examples: Bho daṇḍi, daṇḍī; daṇḍino, daṇḍī, daṇḍiyo.

74. Naṃ jhīto

74. 'Naṃ' after a 'jha'-designated stem.

Jhasaññīto aṃvacanassa naṃ vā hoti. Daṇḍinaṃ daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍine.

After a stem designated 'jha', 'naṃ' is optionally substituted for the 'aṃ' (accusative singular) ending. Examples: Daṇḍinaṃ, daṇḍiṃ; daṇḍine.

76. No

76. 'No'.

Jhīto yonaṃ no vā hoti pulliṅge. Daṇḍino daṇḍī daṇḍiyo. Daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi daṇḍībhi. “Jhalā sassa no”ti nomhi kate daṇḍino daṇḍissa, daṇḍīnaṃ. “Nā smāssā”ti smāssa nā, daṇḍinā daṇḍimhā daṇḍismā.

After a stem designated 'jha', 'no' is optionally substituted for the 'yo' ending in the masculine gender. Examples: Daṇḍino, daṇḍī, daṇḍiyo; Daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi. By the rule 'jhalā sassa no', when 'no' is substituted for 'sa', the forms are daṇḍino, daṇḍissa; daṇḍīnaṃ. By the rule 'nā smāssā', 'nā' is substituted for 'smā', resulting in daṇḍinā, daṇḍimhā, daṇḍismā.

77. Smino ni

77. For 'smiṃ', 'ni'.

Jhīto smiṃvacanassa ni hoti vā. Daṇḍini daṇḍismiṃ, daṇḍīsu, bahulādhikārā smimhi gāmaṇī+senānī+sudhīpabhutīnaṃ niādesābhāvo ca viseso. Evaṃ –

After a stem designated 'jha', 'ni' is optionally substituted for the 'smiṃ' (locative singular) ending. Examples: Daṇḍini, daṇḍismiṃ; daṇḍīsu. And due to the governing principle of 'bahula' (diverse application), the non-substitution of 'ni' for 'smiṃ' for stems such as gāmaṇī, senānī, sudhī, and so forth, is a special case. Thus:

Dhammī [M 0.0054] saṅghī ñāṇī hatthī, cakkī pakkhī dāṭhī raṭṭhī;

Chattī mālī cammī yogī, bhāgī bhogī kāmī sāmī.

Dhammī, saṅghī, ñāṇī, hatthī; cakkī, pakkhī, dāṭhī, raṭṭhī; Chattī, mālī, cammī, yogī; bhāgī, bhogī, kāmī, sāmī.

Dhajī gaṇī sasī kuṭṭhī, jaṭī yānī sukhī sikhī;

Dantī mantī karī cāgī, kusalī musalī balī; (Vācī, rū)

Dhajī, gaṇī, sasī, kuṭṭhī, jaṭī, yānī, sukhī, sikhī; Dantī, mantī, karī, cāgī, kusalī, musalī, balī; (Vācī, rū).

Pāpakārī sattughātī, mālyakārī dīghajīvī;

Dhammavādī sīhanādī, bhūmisāyī sīghayāyī.

Doer of evil, killer of beings, maker of garlands, long-lived; Speaker of the Dhamma, lion-roarer, one who sleeps on the ground, swift-goer.

Īkārantaṃ.

Ending in -ī.

Bhikkhu, silopo. Lasaññāyaṃ –

Bhikkhu, with elision of 'si'. Regarding the 'la' designation:

83. Lā yonaṃ vo pume

83. After a 'la'-designated stem, for 'yo', 'vo' occurs in the masculine gender.

Lato yonaṃ vo hoti vā pulliṅge.

After a stem designated 'la', 'vo' is optionally substituted for the 'yo' (plural nominative) ending in the masculine gender.

94. Ve+vosu lussa

94. Of a 'la'-designated stem, before 've' and 'vo'.

Lasaññassa ussa ve+vosu ṭa hoti. Ettha “pumālapane vevo” tya+tra vossa sahacaritañāyā anissitattā jātivasena “lā yonaṃ” tyādo vo ca gayhati. Bhikkhavo. Aññatra “lopo”ti yolopo. “Yolopanisu dīgho”ti dīghe bhikkhū. Bho bhikkhu bhikkhū.

Of a 'la'-designated stem, the 'u' becomes 'a' before 've' and 'vo'. Here, in the rule 'pumālapane vevo', because the 'vo' is not dependent on the principle of association and by its own nature, the 'vo' from rules such as 'lā yonaṃ' is also included. Example: Bhikkhavo. In other cases, by the rule 'lopo', the 'yo' is elided. By the rule 'yolopanisu dīgho', upon lengthening, the form is bhikkhū. Examples: Bho bhikkhu, bhikkhū.

96. Pumā+lapane vevo

96. In the masculine vocative, 've' and 'vo'.

Lasaññato uto yossā+lapane ve+vo honti vā pulliṅge. Bhikkhave bhikkhavo bhikkhū. Bhikkhuṃ, bhikkhavo bhikkhū. Bhikkhunā[M 0.0055], bhikkhūhi bhikkhūbhi. “Jhalā sassa no”ti lato sassa no vā, bhikkhuno bhikkhussa, bhikkhūnaṃ. “Nā smāssā”ti lato vā smāssa nā, bhikkhunā bhikkhumhā bhikkhusmā. Bhikkhumhi bhikkhusmiṃ. Evaṃ –

After a 'la'-designated stem ending in 'u', 've' and 'vo' are optionally substituted for the 'yo' of the vocative in the masculine gender. Examples: Bhikkhave, bhikkhavo, bhikkhū. Bhikkhuṃ; bhikkhavo, bhikkhū. Bhikkhunā; bhikkhūhi, bhikkhūbhi. By the rule 'jhalā sassa no', after a 'la'-designated stem, 'no' is optionally substituted for 'sa', resulting in bhikkhuno, bhikkhussa; bhikkhūnaṃ. By the rule 'nā smāssā', after a 'la'-designated stem, 'nā' is optionally substituted for 'smā', resulting in bhikkhunā, bhikkhumhā, bhikkhusmā. Bhikkhumhi, bhikkhusmiṃ. Thus:

Setu ketu rāhu bhāṇu, saṃku ucchu veḷu maccu. (Paṅgu, rū) sindhu bandhu neru meru, sattu kāru hetu jantu. Ruru paṭu – iccādayo.

Setu, ketu, rāhu, bhāṇu, saṅku, ucchu, veḷu, maccu; (Paṅgu, rū) sindhu, bandhu, neru, meru, sattu, kāru, hetu, jantu; Ruru, paṭu – and so on.

Jantu+hetūnaṃ yosva+yaṃ bhedo. “Jantu+hetvī+gha+pehi vā”ti yolope –

For 'jantu' and 'hetu', this is the distinction regarding the 'yo' ending. By the rule 'Jantuhetvīghapehi vā', upon the elision of 'yo':

84. Jantvādito no ca

84. After 'jantu', etc., also 'no'.

Jantvādito yonaṃ no hoti vo ca pulliṅge. Jantuno jantavo jantuyo. Bho jantu jantū, jantuno, “pumālapane vevo”ti ve+vo, jantave jantavo jantuyo. Jantuṃ, jantū jantuno jantavo jantuyo. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

After 'jantu' and so forth, for the 'yo' ending, 'no' and also 'vo' occur in the masculine gender. Examples: Jantuno, jantavo, jantuyo. Vocative: Bho jantu, jantū, jantuno; by the rule 'pumālapane vevo', 've' and 'vo' occur, resulting in jantave, jantavo, jantuyo. Accusative: Jantuṃ; jantū, jantuno, jantavo, jantuyo. The remaining forms are the same as for 'bhikkhu'.

Hetu, hetū hetavo. “Yomhi vā kvacī”ti lasaññassa ussa vā ṭādeso, hetayo. Yomhi antaraṅgattā paṭhamaṃ ṭādese kate pacchā yolopābhāvo, tathā hi antaraṅga+bāhiraṅgavidhānesva+ntaraṅgavidhiyeva balavā. Ettha ca pakatinissita+mantaraṅgaṃ, paccayanissitaṃ bāhiraṅgaṃ. Hetuyo. Bho hetu, hetū hetave hetavo hetayo hetuyo. Sesaṃ pubbasamaṃ.

Hetu; hetū, hetavo. By the rule 'Yomhi vā kvacī', for a 'la'-designated stem, the 'u' is optionally substituted by 'a', resulting in hetayo. Before the 'yo' ending, because the substitution of 'a' is an internal operation, it is performed first, and consequently, the elision of 'yo' does not occur; for indeed, between an internal and an external rule, the internal rule is stronger. Here, that which depends on the stem is internal; that which depends on the suffix is external. Example: Hetuyo. Vocative: Bho hetu; hetū, hetave, hetavo, hetayo, hetuyo. The rest is as before.

Bahuto [M 0.0056] naṃmhi –

From the plural, before the 'naṃ' ending:

48. Bahukatinnaṃ

48. Of 'bahu', 'kati', and 'ti', 'innaṃ'.

Naṃmhi bahuno katissa ca nuka hoti tiliṅge. Bahunnaṃ. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

When `naṃ` follows, for `bahu` and `kati`, `nuka` occurs in the three genders. `Bahunnaṃ`. The rest is like `bhikkhu`.

Vattu si,

The stem `vattu` with `si`.

57. Ltu+pitādīna+mā simhi

57. For stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `ā` is the substitute in the nominative singular.

Ltupaccayantānaṃ pitu+mātu+bhātu+dhītu+duhitu+jāmātu+nattu+hotu+potūnañcā hoti simhi. Vattā. “Kattari ltu+ṇakā”ti vihitaltupaccayassa gahaṇā yato dhātuto hi so vihito, “paccayaggahaṇe yasmā so vihito, tadādino tadantassa ca gahaṇaṃ”ti ñāyā tadavinābhāvato tadantadhātunopi gahaṇaṃti ltupaccayantānaṃti vuttaṃ.

For stems ending in the `ltu` suffix, and for `pitu`, `mātu`, `bhātu`, `dhītu`, `duhitu`, `jāmātu`, `nattu`, `hotu`, and `potu`, `ā` occurs in the nominative singular. Example: `Vattā`. The `ltu` suffix taken here is the one prescribed by the rule, 'In the sense of agent, `ltu` and `ṇaka`...' Since it is prescribed after a verbal root, by the maxim, 'When a suffix is mentioned, that after which it is prescribed is taken, from its beginning up to its end,' and due to this inseparability, the verbal root ending in that suffix is also included. Therefore, the phrase 'for stems ending in the `ltu` suffix' is stated.

162. Ltu+pitādīna+ma se

162. For stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `a` occurs in the case of `sa`.

Ltupaccayantānaṃ pitādīnañcā+raṅa hoti sato+ññatra. “Āraṅasmā”ti ṭo, vattāro.

For stems ending in the `ltu` suffix and for `pitu` and so on, the substitute `āraṅa` occurs, except in the case of `sa`. By the rule `Āraṅasmā`, `o` occurs. Example: `vattāro`.

58. Ge a ca

58. In the vocative singular (`ge`), `a` also occurs.

Geltu+pitādīnaṃ a hoti ā ca. Bho vatta vattā, vattāro. Vattāraṃ, vattāre vattāro. Nāvacanassa “ṭā nāsmānaṃ”ti ṭā, vattārā.

In the vocative singular (`ge`), for stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `a` occurs, and also `ā`. Examples: `Bho vatta, vattā, vattāro`. Accusative: `Vattāraṃ, vattāre, vattāro`. For the instrumental singular ending `nā`, by the rule `ṭā nāsmānaṃ`, `ṭā` occurs. Example: `vattārā`.

166. Su+hisvā+raṅa

166. When `su` and `hi` follow, `āraṅa` is an optional substitute.

Su+hisu ltu+pitādīna+māraṅa vā hoti. Vattārehi vattārebhi vattūhi vattūbhi.

When `su` and `hi` follow, for stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `āraṅa` is an optional substitute. Examples: `vattārehi, vattārebhi, vattūhi, vattūbhi`.

165. Salopo

165. Elision of `sa`.

Ltu+pitādīhi [M 0.0057] sassa lopo vā hoti. Vattu vattuno vattussa.

After stems ending in `ltu` and after `pitu` and so on, the elision of `sa` optionally occurs. Examples: `vattu, vattuno, vattussa`.

163. Naṃmhi vā

163. Optionally, when `naṃ` follows.

Naṃmhi ltu+pitādīna+māraṅa vā hoti. Vattārānaṃ.

When `naṃ` follows, for stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `āraṅa` is an optional substitute. Example: `Vattārānaṃ`.

164. Ā

164. Ā

Naṃmhi ltu+pitādīna+mā vā hoti. Vattānaṃ vattūnaṃ. Smāssa ṭā, vattārā.

When `naṃ` follows, for stems ending in `ltu` and for `pitu` and so on, `ā` optionally occurs. Examples: `Vattānaṃ, vattūnaṃ`. For `smā`, `ṭā` is the substitute. Example: `vattārā`.

174. Ṭi smino

174. `Ṭi` is the substitute for `smiṃ`.

Āravā+desamhā smino ṭi hoti.

After the substitute `āra`, `ṭi` occurs for `smiṃ`.

176. Rassā+raṅa

176. Shortening of `āraṅa`.

Smimhi āro rasso hoti. Vattari, vattāresu vattūsu vattusu. Evaṃ –

When `smiṃ` follows, `āro` becomes short. Examples: `vattari; vattāresu, vattūsu, vattusu`. Thus—

Evaṃ bhattu kattu netu, sotu ñātu jetu chettu;

Bhettu dātu dhātu boddhu, viññāpetādayopi ca.

Likewise: `bhattu` (husband, supporter), `kattu` (doer), `netu` (leader), `sotu` (hearer), `ñātu` (knower), `jetu` (conqueror), `chettu` (cutter); `bhettu` (breaker), `dātu` (giver), `dhātu` (bearer), `boddhu` (knower, awakened one), and also `viññāpetu` and so on.

Satthusaddassa pana nāmhi bahulādhikārā “ltu+pitādīna+mase”ti vā āravādese satthārā satthunā. Sesaṃ vattusamaṃ.

However, for the word `satthu`, in the instrumental singular (`nā`), due to the governing rule of 'variously', by the rule `ltu-pitādīnam-ārase`, with the optional substitution of `āra`, the forms are `satthārā` and `satthunā`. The rest is like `vattu`.

Simhi ā, pitā. “Ltu+pitādīna+mase”ti āravādese –

In the nominative singular (`simhi`), `ā` occurs; for example, `pitā`. With the substitution of `āra` by the rule `ltu-pitādīnam-ārase`—

177. Pitādīna+manatvādīnaṃ

177. For `pitu` and so on, excluding `nattu` and so on.

Natvādivajjitānaṃ [M 0.0058] pitādīna+māro rasso hoti sabbāsu vibhattīsu. “Ltu+pitādīna+mase” “su+hisvā+raṅa” “naṃmhi vā”ti ettha vuttavibhattīsu paresu āraṅa hotīti tā vibhattiyo paṭicca sabbāsūti vuttaṃ. Pitaro. Bho pita pitā, pitaro. Pitaraṃ, pitare pitaro. Pitarā, pitarehi pitarebhi pitūhi pitūbhi. Pitu pituno pitussa, pitarānaṃ pitūnaṃ. “Pitunnaṃ”ti naṃmhi dīghe rassa+dvittānīti vuttaṃ. “Sānuvuttaṃ suttaṃ”ti ñāyā “bahukatinnaṃ”ti ettha nuka-iti yogavibhāgenapi sijjhati ettha anuvattitanaṃmhi. Pañcamīchaṭṭhī tatiyācatutthīsamaṃ. Pitari, pitaresu pītūsu, rassābhāvo. Nattā, nattāro. Bho natta nattā, nattāro iccādi vattusamaṃ.

For `pitu` and so on, excluding `nattu` and so on, `āro` becomes short before all case endings. The phrase 'before all case endings' refers to those case endings mentioned in the rules `ltu-pitādīnam-ārase`, `su-hisu vā āraṅa`, and `naṃmhi vā`, before which `āraṅa` occurs. Examples: `Pitaro`. Vocative: `Bho pita, pitā, pitaro`. Accusative: `Pitaraṃ, pitare, pitaro`. Instrumental: `Pitarā; pitarehi, pitarebhi, pitūhi, pitūbhi`. Genitive: `Pitu, pituno, pitussa; pitarānaṃ, pitūnaṃ`. Regarding `Pitunnaṃ`, it is said that before `naṃ`, there is lengthening, then shortening and doubling. By the maxim 'A rule has what is carried forward from a previous rule,' this is also accomplished for `bahukatinnaṃ` by splitting the rule for `nuka` when `naṃ` is carried forward. The fifth and sixth cases are similar to the third and fourth. Locative: `Pitari; pitaresu, pitūsu`; here there is an absence of shortening. For `nattu`: `Nattā, nattāro`. Vocative: `Bho natta, nattā, nattāro`, and so on, is like `vattu`.

Guṇavantu si,

The stem `guṇavantu` with `si`.

151. Ntussa

151. For `ntu`.

Simhi ntussa ṭā hoti. Guṇavā. Yomhi “ntantūnaṃ nto yomhi paṭhame”ti savibhattissa ntussa nto hoti. Ettha ca “ntu vantu+mantā+vantu+tavantusambandhī”ti paribhāsato ntu ca vantvādisambandhīyeva gayhate, na jantu tantādīnaṃ. Guṇavanto. Aññatra –

In the nominative singular (`simhi`), `ā` occurs for `ntu`. Example: `Guṇavā`. In the nominative plural (`yomhi`), by the rule `nt-antūnaṃ nto yomhi paṭhame`, `nto` is the substitute for `ntu` together with its case ending. Here, according to the metarule `ntu vantu-mantā-vantu-tavantu-sambandhī`, only the `ntu` related to `vantu`, `mantu`, etc., is taken, not that of `jantu`, `tantu`, and so on. Example: `Guṇavanto`. Elsewhere—

91. Yvādo ntussa

91. For `ntu`, when `yo` and other endings follow.

Yoādīsu ntussa a hoti. Guṇavantaiti akārantā ṭā+ṭeādesā honti, guṇavantā. “Ṭaṭāaṃ ge”ti ṭādayo[M 0.0059], bho guṇava guṇavā guṇavaṃ, guṇavanto guṇavantā. “Ntassa ca ṭa vaṃ+se”ti aṃsesu ntassa ṭo vā, guṇavaṃ guṇavantaṃ, guṇavante. “To+tā+ti+tā sa+smā+smiṃ+nāsū”ti tāādayo honti, guṇavatā guṇavantena, guṇavantehi guṇavantebhi. “Lakkhaṇikapaṭipadottesu paṭipadottasseva gahaṇaṃ, na lakkhaṇikassā”ti ñāyā “na lakkhaṇikassā”ti vuttabyattipakkha+manapekkhitvā “ato”ti rassākārajātiyā pekkhitattā guṇavantenāti “atenā” tya+nena sijjhati. Jāti=sāmaññaṃ, byatti=viseso. Guṇavato guṇavassa guṇavantassa, “taṃ naṃmhi”ti naṃmhī taṃ vā, guṇavataṃ guṇavantānaṃ. Guṇavatā guṇavantā guṇavantamhā guṇavantasmā. Guṇavati guṇavante guṇavantamhi guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantesu. “Ntassa ca ṭa vā”ti yogavibhāgā yosu ca ntussa vā ṭādese kate yossa ṭā, “cakkhumā andhitā honti”, “vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhu vaṇṇavā” iccādī honti.

When `yo` and other endings follow, `a` is the substitute for `ntu`. Since `guṇavanta` is now an `a`-ending stem, the substitutes `ā` and `e` occur, giving `guṇavantā`. By rules such as `Ā ge`, the vocative forms are: `bho guṇava, guṇavā, guṇavaṃ; guṇavanto, guṇavantā`. By a rule such as `Ntassa ca aṃ vaṃsesu`, before the endings `aṃ` and `e`, `nta` is optionally substituted, giving: `guṇavaṃ, guṇavantaṃ; guṇavante`. By the rule `To tā ti tā sa-smā-smiṃ-nāsu`, the substitutes `tā`, etc., occur: `guṇavatā, guṇavantena; guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi`. By the maxim, 'Between a term defined by a characteristic and a term explicitly stated, the explicitly stated term is to be taken, not the one defined by a characteristic.' Disregarding the specific instance (`byatti`) mentioned in 'not for the one defined by a characteristic,' but considering the general class (`jāti`) of the short vowel `a`, the form `guṇavantena` is accomplished by the rule `Ato nena`. `Jāti` is the general class; `byatti` is the specific instance. Genitive: `guṇavato, guṇavassa, guṇavantassa`. By `Taṃ naṃmhi`, `taṃ` optionally occurs before `naṃ`: `guṇavataṃ, guṇavantānaṃ`. Ablative: `guṇavatā, guṇavantā, guṇavantamhā, guṇavantasmā`. Locative: `guṇavati, guṇavante, guṇavantamhi, guṇavantasmiṃ; guṇavantesu`. By splitting the rule `Ntassa ca... vā`, an optional substitution for `ntu` also occurs before `yo`, resulting in `yo` becoming `ā`, as in: `cakkhumā andhitā honti` and `vaggumudātīriyā bhikkhu vaṇṇavā`.

Evaṃ gaṇavā kulavā phalavā yasavā dhanavā sutavā bhagavā himavā balavā sīlavā paññavā iccādī.

Likewise: `gaṇavā` (possessing a following), `kulavā` (possessing a good family), `phalavā` (possessing fruit), `yasavā` (possessing fame), `dhanavā` (possessing wealth), `sutavā` (possessing learning), `bhagavā` (the Blessed One), `himavā` (possessing snow), `balavā` (possessing strength), `sīlavā` (possessing virtue), `paññavā` (possessing wisdom), and so on.

153. Himavato vā o

153. From the Himālaya, or

Himavato simhi ntussa o vā hoti, himavanto himavā. Sesaṃ purimasamaṃ.

For Himavant, in the nominative singular (si), the ending -ntu optionally becomes o, resulting in himavanto or himavā. The rest is as before.

Āyasmantusaddo kammavācāya kvaci bahulādhikārā dvivacanena āyasmantā, tiṇṇaṃ vacanena āyasmantoti dissati.

The word āyasmantu in the Kammavācā, due to the governing rule of bahula (diverse application), sometimes appears as āyasmantā for the dual and is seen as āyasmanto for the plural.

Evaṃ [M 0.0060] satimā dhitimā gatimā mutimā matimā jutimā sirimā hirimā thutimā ratimā yatimā sucimā kalimā balimā kasimā rucimā buddhimā cakkhumā bandhumā hetumā setumā ketumā rāhumā bhāṇumā khāṇumā vijjumā iccādayo.

Thus: mindful, resolute, swift, thoughtful, wise, luminous, glorious, modest, praised, joyous, self-controlled, pure, skilled, strong, diligent, delightful, intelligent, clear-sighted, kindred, reasoning, bridging, banner-like, obscuring, radiant, firm, lightning-like, and so forth.

Ukārantaṃ.

Ending in u.

Vessabhū silopo. Te ca rassābhāvova viseso. “Ekavacanayosva+ghonaṃ”ti rasse “lā yonaṃ vo pume”ti vo, vessabhuvo, “vevosu lussā”ti vuttattā na ṭādeso, “lopoti yolope vessabhū. “Ge vā”ti vā rasse bho vessabhu vessabhū, vessabhuvo vessabhū. Vessabhuṃ, vessabhuvo vessabhū. Vessabhunā iccādi bhikkhusamaṃ. Evaṃ sayambhū parābhibhū abhibhūādayo. Gotrabhū+sahabhūsaddehi pana yonaṃ “jantvādito no vā”ti no, vo vā, gotrabhuno gotrabhuvo gotrabhū. Sahabhuno sahabhuvo sahabhū, sesaṃ vessabhūsamaṃ.

Vessabhū: there is elision of si. The distinction is only the absence of shortening. When shortened by 'Ekavacanayosva+ghonaṃ', the plural ending yo becomes vo by 'lā yonaṃ vo pume', giving vessabhuvo. Because 'vevosu lussā' is stated, there is no substitution for ṭā. With the elision of yo by 'lopo...', the form is Vessabhū. By 'Ge vā', with optional shortening in the vocative: 'O Vessabhu', 'Vessabhū'. [Nominative/Accusative plural:] 'Vessabhuvo', 'Vessabhū'. [Accusative singular:] 'Vessabhuṃ'. From 'Vessabhunā' onwards, it is like bhikkhu. Similarly for Sayambhū, Parābhibhū, Abhibhū, and others. However, for the words Gotrabhū and Sahabhū, the plural ending yo optionally becomes no or vo by 'jantvādito no vā', giving: gotrabhuno, gotrabhuvo, gotrabhū; and sahabhuno, sahabhuvo, sahabhū. The rest is like Vessabhū.

85. Kūto

85. From kū.

Kūpaccayantato yonaṃ no vā hoti pulliṅge. Sabbaññuno. Aññatra “lā yonaṃ vo pume”ti na vo, “kūto”ti jantvādīhi puthakkaraṇā. Yolope sabbaññū. Bho sabbaññu sabbaññū, sabbaññuno sabbaññū iccādi.

After a stem ending in the suffix kū, the plural ending yo optionally becomes no in the masculine. For example, sabbaññuno. Otherwise, it does not become vo by the rule 'lā yonaṃ vo pume', because the rule 'kūto' separates these from the jantu group. With the elision of yo, the form is sabbaññū. [The forms are:] 'O Sabbaññu', 'Sabbaññū'; 'Sabbaññuno', 'Sabbaññū', etc.

Evaṃ maggaññū dhammaññū atthaññū kālaññū rattaññū mattaññū kataññū kathaññū viññū vidū iccādayo. Ettha “vidā kū” “vito ñāto” [M 0.0061] “kammā”ti tīsu suttesu kūpaccayassa gahitattā vedagūādayo rūpaccayantā na gahitā.

Thus: maggaññū, dhammaññū, atthaññū, kālaññū, rattaññū, mattaññū, kataññū, kathaññū, viññū, vidū, etc. Here, because the suffix kū is specified in the three suttas—'vidā kū', 'vito ñāto', and 'kammā'—words such as vedagū, which end in the suffix rū, are not included.

Ūkārantaṃ.

Ending in ū.

Go, si, silopo. Go.

Go; the nominative singular ending si is elided, giving Go.

67. Gossā+ga+si+hi+naṃsu gāva+gavā

67. For go, before the endings ā, ga, si, hi, and naṃ, the stem optionally becomes gāva or gavā.

Ga+si+hi+naṃvajjitāsu vibhattīsu gosaddassa gāva+gavā honti niccaṃ.

In case endings other than ga, si, hi, and naṃ, the word go always becomes gāva or gavā.

170. Ubha+gohi ṭo

170. After ubha and go, ṭo [is substituted for yo].

Ubha+gohi yonaṃ ṭo hoti. Gāvo gavo. Bho go, gāvo gavo.

After ubha and go, the plural ending yo becomes ṭo. The forms are: Gāvo, gavo. Vocative: 'O Go', gāvo, gavo.

72. Gāvu+mhi

72. Gāvu before mhi.

Aṃvacane gossa gāvu vā hoti. Gāvuṃ gāvaṃ gavaṃ, gāvo gavo.

In the accusative singular, go optionally becomes gāvu. The forms are: Gāvuṃ, gāvaṃ, gavaṃ; [plural:] gāvo, gavo.

71. Nāssā

71. For the ending nā, ā [is substituted].

Goto nāssa ā hoti vā. Ekavaṇṇattā na sabbādeso. “Pañcamiyaṃ parasse”ti vattante “ādissā”ti nāssa ā hoti, paralopo, gāvā gāvena gavā gavena, gohi gobhi.

After go, the instrumental ending nā optionally becomes ā. Because it is a single letter, it is not a substitution for the whole ending. While 'Pañcamiyaṃ parasse' is in effect, nā becomes ā by 'ādissā', with elision of the preceding vowel. The forms are: gāvā, gāvena, gavā, gavena; [plural:] gohi, gobhi.

69. Gavaṃ sena

69. Gavaṃ [is substituted] for go with the ending sa.

Gossa se vā gavaṃ hoti saha sena. Gavaṃ gāvassa gavassa. Kaccāyane “gavaṃ ce taramānānaṃ”ti pāḷiṃ paṭicca naṃmhi bahuvacanameva sādhitaṃ, idha “gavaṃva siṅgino saṅgaṃ”ti dassanato ekavacanañca.

For go, the stem together with the genitive singular ending sa optionally becomes gavaṃ. The forms are: gavaṃ, gāvassa, gavassa. In Kaccāyana's grammar, citing the Pāli passage 'gavaṃ ce taramānānaṃ', only the plural form of gavaṃ is derived for the genitive plural ending naṃ; here, from the example 'gavaṃva siṅgino saṅgaṃ', the singular is also derived.

70. Gunnañca naṃnā

70. Gunnaṃ and with naṃ.

Naṃvacanena [M 0.0062] saha gossa gunnaṃ hoti gavañca vā. Gunnaṃ gavaṃ gonaṃ. Gāvā gāvamhā gāvasmā gavā gavamhā gavasmā. Gāve gāvamhi gāvasmiṃ gave gavamhi gavasmiṃ.

Together with the ending naṃ, go becomes gunnaṃ, and optionally gavaṃ. Genitive plural: Gunnaṃ, gavaṃ, gonaṃ. Ablative singular: Gāvā, gāvamhā, gāvasmā; gavā, gavamhā, gavasmā. Locative singular: Gāve, gāvamhi, gāvasmiṃ; gave, gavamhi, gavasmiṃ.

68. Sumhi vā

68. Optionally before su.

Sumhi gossa gāva+gavā honti vā. Gāvesu gavesu gosu. Gossa goṇādeso na kato, saddantarattā. Goṇasaddo hi sattasu vibhattīsu dissatīti.

Before the locative plural ending su, go optionally becomes gāva or gavā. The forms are: Gāvesu, gavesu, gosu. The substitution of goṇa for go is not made, because it is a different word. Indeed, the word goṇa is seen in the seven cases.

Usu+bhūmi+pasu+raṃsi-disā+vācā+mbu+cakkhusu;

Dasasva+tthesu go vutto, lagge ca vajire iti.

The word go is used in the following ten meanings: arrow, earth, cattle, ray, direction, speech, water, eye, lagga, and vajira.

Okārantaṃ.

Ending in o.

Iti pulliṅgaṃ.

Thus ends the masculine gender.

Kaññā, silopo.

Kaññā; elision of si.

1,11. Ghā

1.11. Ghā.

Itthiyaṃ vattamānassa nāmassa+nte vattamāno ākāro ghasañño hoti. “Jantu+hetvī+gha+pehi vā”ti yolopo vā. Kaññā kaññāyo. “Gha+brahmādite”ti gassa e vā, kaññe kaññā, yomhi kaññā kaññāyo. “Gho ssaṃ+ssā yaṃ+tiṃsū”ti aṃmhi rasso. Kaññaṃ, kaññā kaññāyo.

The vowel ā at the end of a feminine noun is termed gha. By 'Jantuhetvīghapehi vā,' the elision of yo is optional: kaññā, kaññāyo. By 'Ghabrahmādite,' e is the optional substitute for ga (the vocative singular): kaññe, kaññā. In the case of yo: kaññā, kaññāyo. By 'Ghossaṃssāyaṃtiṃsū,' in the case of aṃ, shortening occurs: kaññaṃ; kaññā, kaññāyo.

45. Gha+pate+kasmiṃ nādīnaṃ ya+yā

45. After gha and pa: for nā, etc., up to smiṃ, there are ya and yā.

Ghapato [M 0.0063] smiṃvibhattipariyantānaṃ ekatte nādīnaṃ ya+yā honti yathākkamaṃ. Kaññāya, kaññābhi kaññāhi. Kaññāya, kaññānaṃ.
