After stems termed gha and pa, for the singular case endings from nā up to smiṃ, ya and yā are the respective substitutes. Kaññāya, kaññābhi, kaññāhi. Kaññāya, kaññānaṃ.

103. Yaṃ

103. Yaṃ.

Ghapato smino yaṃ vā hoti. Kaññāyaṃ kaññāya. “Gha+ pate+kasmiṃ nādīnaṃ ya+yā” “yaṃ”ti ca imesaṃ apavādādīnaṃ visaye mhissa ussaggattā pavatti natthīti smino bahulādhikārā “smā+hi+sminna” miccādinā mhikate “dasasahassimhi dhātumhī”ti sijjhati. Kaññāsu. Evaṃ –

After stems termed gha and pa, yaṃ is the optional substitute for smiṃ: kaññāyaṃ, kaññāya. Since 'Ghapatekasmiṃ nādīnaṃ yayā' and 'Yaṃ' are specific rules (apavāda), the general rule (ussagga) substituting mhi does not apply in their domain. However, because the substitution for smiṃ is governed by the principle of bahula (variously), when mhi is substituted by 'Smāhisminnaṃ...' etc., the form dasasahassimhi dhātumhī is accomplished. Kaññāsu. Likewise –

Saddhā medhā paññā vijjā, cintā mantā taṇhā vīṇā;

Icchā mucchā ejā māyā, mettā mattā sikkhā bhikkhā.

Faith, intelligence, wisdom, knowledge; thought, counsel, craving, lute; desire, infatuation, agitation, illusion; loving-kindness, measure, training, alms.

Jaṅghā gīvā jīvhā vācā, chāyā āsā gaṅgā nāvā;

Gāthā senā lekhā sālā, mālā velā pūjā khiḍḍā.

Shin, neck, tongue, speech; shadow, hope, Ganges, boat; verse, army, writing, hall; garland, time, worship, play.

Pipāsā vedanā saññā, cetanā tasinā pajā;

Devatā vaṭṭakā godhā, balākā parisā sabhā.

Thirst, feeling, perception; volition, craving, progeny; deity, quail, iguana; crane, assembly, meeting hall.

Ūkā sephālikā laṅkā, salākā vālukā sikhā;

Visākhā visikhā sākhā, vācā vañjhā jaṭā ghaṭā.

Louse, jasmine, Lanka; ticket-stick, sand, crest; Visākhā, street, branch; speech, barren woman, matted hair, crowd.

Jeṭṭhā soṇḍā vitaṇḍā ca, karuṇā vanitā latā;

Kathā niddā sudhā rādhā, vāsanā siṃsapā papā.

Eldest, elephant's trunk, and sophistry; compassion, woman, creeper; discourse, sleep, nectar, Rādhā; impression, sissoo tree, a place for drinking water.

Pabhā [M 0.0064] sīmā khamā chāyā, khattiyā sakkharā surā;

Dolā tulā silā lilā, lāle+lā mekhalā kalā.

Light, boundary, patience, shade; noblewoman, gravel, spirits; palanquin, balance, stone, sport; saliva, cardamom, girdle, art.

Vaḷavā+lambusā mūsā, mañjusā sulasā disā;

Nāsā juṇhā guhā īhā, lasikā vasudhādayo.

Mare, a celestial nymph, crucible; casket, holy basil, direction; nose, moonlight, cave, effort; synovial fluid, earth, etc.

“Na+mmādīhī”ti ammā+annā+ambāhi gassa ekārā+bhāve –

By the rule 'Nammādīhi,' for ammā, annā, and ambā, in the absence of the substitution of e for ga –

62. Rasso vā

62. Optional Shortening.

Ammādīnaṃ ge rasso vā hoti. Amma ammā iccādi. Sesaṃ kaññāva. Evaṃ annā ambā. Sabhāparisāhi smino “tiṃ sabhāparisāyā”ti tiṃ vā hoti. “Ghossa” mādinā rasse sabhatiṃ sabhāyaṃ sabhāya. Parisatiṃ parisāyaṃ parisāya.

For ammā and others, in the case of ge (vocative singular), shortening is optional: amma, ammā, etc. The rest is like kaññā. Likewise for annā and ambā. After sabhā and parisā, tiṃ is the optional substitute for smiṃ by the rule 'Tiṃ sabhāparisāya'. With shortening by 'Ghossa...' etc., the forms are: sabhatiṃ, sabhāyaṃ, sabhāya; parisatiṃ, parisāyaṃ, parisāya.

Ākārantaṃ.

The section on ā-stems is concluded.

Mati, yomhi –

For mati, in the case of yo –

1,10. Pi+tthiyaṃ

1.10. Pa in the feminine.

Itthiyaṃ vattamānassa nāmassa+nte vattamānā ivaṇṇu+vaṇṇā pasaññā honti.

The final vowels i and u of a feminine noun are termed pa.

116. Ye passi+vaṇṇassa

116. Of a vowel termed pa, before ye.

Pasaññassa ivaṇṇassa lopo hoti vā yakāre. “Paro kvacī”ti anuvattitakvaciggahaṇā ye pare ca-kāra+pubbarūpā- ni [M 0.0065] na honti. Matyo. Aññatra “jantvā”dinā yolopo, dīgho, matī matiyo. Bho mati matī, matyo matī matiyo. Matiṃ, matyo matī matiyo. Matiyā, matīhi matībhi. Matyā matiyā, matīnaṃ. Smino yaṃ, matyaṃ matiyaṃ matyā matiyā, matīsu. Evaṃ –

Of an i-vowel termed pa, there is optional elision before ya. Because kvaci (sometimes) is carried over from 'Paro kvaci', when ye follows, coalescence (pubbarūpa) with a preceding ca does not occur: matyo. Alternatively, by 'Jantv...' etc., there is elision of yo and lengthening: matī, matiyo. Vocative: bho mati, matī; matyo, matī, matiyo. Accusative: matiṃ; matyo, matī, matiyo. Instrumental: matiyā; matīhi, matībhi. Genitive/Ablative: matyā, matiyā; matīnaṃ. Locative (smiṃ becomes yaṃ): matyaṃ, matiyaṃ, matyā, matiyā; matīsu. Likewise –

Patti yutti vutti kitti, mutti titti khanti kanti;

Santi tanti siddhi suddhi, iddhi vuddhi buddhi bodhi.

Attainment, propriety, practice, fame; release, satisfaction, patience, loveliness; peace, tradition, success, purity; psychic power, growth, intelligence, enlightenment.

Bhūmi jāti pīti suti, nandi sandhi soṇi koṭi;

Diṭṭhi vuṭṭhi tuṭṭhi yaṭṭhi, pāḷi āḷi nāḷi keḷi.

Earth, birth, joy, hearing, delight, connection, hip, peak; view, rain, satisfaction, staff; Pāli, row, tube, sport.

Sati muti gati cuti, dhiti yuvati vikati;

Rati ruci rasmi asani, vasani osadhi aṅguli;

Dhūli dudrabhi doṇi, aṭavi chavi iccādi.

Mindfulness, thought, course, decease; resolve, young woman, transformation; delight, liking, ray, thunderbolt; dwelling, medicine, finger; dust, drum, trough; forest, complexion, etc.

55. Ratyādīhi ṭo smino

55. After rati, etc., ṭo for smiṃ.

Ratyādīhi smino ṭo vā hoti. Ratto ratyaṃ rattiyaṃ ratyā rattiyā, rattīsu. Sesaṃ matisamaṃ.

After rati and others, ṭo is the optional substitute for smiṃ. For example: ratto, ratyaṃ, rattiyaṃ, ratyā, rattiyā; rattīsu. The rest is the same as mati.

Ikārantaṃ.

The section on i-stems is concluded.

Dāsī, silopo. “Ekavacane”ccādinā rasso. “Ye passi+vaṇṇassā”ti īlopo, dāsyo. “Jantvā” dinā yolopo. Dāsī dāsiyo. “Ge vā”ti rasso. Bho dāsi dāsī, dāsyo dāsī dāsiyo.

For dāsī, there is elision of si. By 'Ekavacane...' etc., shortening occurs. By 'Ye passivaṇṇassa,' the ī is elided: dāsyo. By 'Jantv...' etc., yo is elided: dāsī, dāsiyo. By 'Ge vā,' shortening is optional. Vocative: bho dāsi, dāsī; dāsyo, dāsī, dāsiyo.

73. Yaṃ pito

73. Yaṃ after pi.

Pasaññīto aṃvacanassa yaṃ vā hoti. Dāsyaṃ dāsiyaṃ dāsiṃ, dāsyo dāsī dāsiyo. “Ghapatekā”dinā yā. Dāsyā dāsiyā[M 0.0066], dāsīhi dāsībhi. Dāsyā dāsiyā, dāsīnaṃ. Dāsyaṃ dāsiyaṃ dāsyā dāsiyā, dāsīsu. Evaṃ –

After a stem termed pa, yaṃ is the optional substitute for the case ending aṃ. Accusative: dāsyaṃ, dāsiyaṃ, dāsiṃ; dāsyo, dāsī, dāsiyo. By 'Ghapatekā...' etc., yā is substituted. Instrumental: dāsyā, dāsiyā; dāsīhi, dāsībhi. Genitive/Ablative: dāsyā, dāsiyā; dāsīnaṃ. Locative: dāsyaṃ, dāsiyaṃ, dāsyā, dāsiyā; dāsīsu. Likewise –

Mahī vetaraṇī vāpī, pāṭalī kadalī ghaṭī;

Nārī kumārī taruṇī, vāruṇī brāhmaṇī sakhī.

Mahī, Vetaraṇī, vāpī, Pāṭalī, kadalī, ghaṭī; Nārī, kumārī, taruṇī, Vāruṇī, brāhmaṇī, sakhī.

Gandhabbī kinnarī nāgī, devī yakkhī ajī migī;

Vānarī sūkarī sīhī, haṃsī kākī ca kukkuṭī.

Gandhabbī, kinnarī, nāgī, devī, yakkhī, ajī, migī; Vānarī, sūkarī, sīhī, haṃsī, kākī, and kukkuṭī.

Iccādayo.

And so on.

Ettha ca īkāralope ññakārapubbarūpo, vetarañño vetaraṇiyo. Vetaraññaṃ vetaraṇiyaṃ vetaraṇiṃ, vetarañño vetaraṇiyo iccādi. Yosu –

And here, with the elision of the letter ī, assimilation to the preceding form with the letter ñña occurs: vetarañño, vetaraṇiyo. Vetaraññaṃ, vetaraṇiyaṃ, vetaraṇiṃ, vetarañño, vetaraṇiyo, and so on. Regarding the plural ending 'yo' –

167. Najjā dhayāsvāma

167. Najjā dhayāsvāma.

Yosu nadīsaddassa āma vā hoti. Suña+naka+āma ityādi ññakāra+kakāra+makārā āgamaliṅgā. Sa ca “mānubandho sarāna+mantā paro”ti mānubandhattā sarāna+mantā paro hotīti īkārā paro. “Yavā sare”ti ye dassa jo, yassa ca pubbarūpaṃ, najjāyo. Vā pa-lopa+yolopesu najjo nadī nadiyo iccādi.

Before the plural ending 'yo', the augment 'āma' is optionally added to the word 'nadī'. In 'suña', 'naka', 'āma', etc., the letters 'ñña', 'ka', and 'ma' are augment indicators. And that augment, because it has 'm' as an indicator, is inserted after the final vowel according to the rule 'mānubandho sarānamantā paro'; that is, it comes after the letter 'ī'. By the rule 'Yavā sare', 'ya' becomes 'ja', and there is assimilation to the preceding form, resulting in najjāyo. Optionally, with 'pa'-elision and 'yo'-elision, the forms are najjo, nadī, nadiyo, and so on.

Īkārantaṃ.

End of the ī-final stems.

Yāgu, yāgū yāguyo. Bho yāgu, yāgū yāguyo. Yāguṃ, yāgū yāguyo. Yāguyā, yāgūhi yāgūbhi. Yāguyā, yāgūnaṃ. Yāguyaṃ yāguyā, yāgūsu. Evaṃ dhātu+dhenu+kāsu+daddu+kaṇḍu+kacchu+rajju+kareṇu+sassu+piyaṅgu [M 0.0067] ādayo.

Nominative: Yāgu, yāgū, yāguyo. Vocative: O yāgu, yāgū, yāguyo. Accusative: Yāguṃ, yāgū, yāguyo. Instrumental/Ablative: Yāguyā, yāgūhi, yāgūbhi. Dative/Genitive: Yāguyā, yāgūnaṃ. Locative: Yāguyaṃ, yāguyā, yāgūsu. Thus are declined dhātu, dhenu, kāsu, daddu, kaṇḍu, kacchu, rajju, kareṇu, sassu, piyaṅgu, and others.

Ettha dhātusaddo “manodhātunā”ti abhidhammāvatāre vuttattā pulliṅgepi dissati, taṃ sakkaṭamatena vuttanti keci.

Here, the word 'dhātu', because it is stated in the Abhidhammāvatāra as 'manodhātunā', is also seen in the masculine gender; some, however, say that this is stated according to the Sanskrit view.

Mātā, mātaro. Bho māta mātā, mātaro. Mātaraṃ, mātare mātaro. Mātarā, nāssa yādese “ye passā”ti yogavibhāgā palopo, anuññāto ahaṃ matyā, aññatra mātuyā, mātarehi mātarebhi mātūhi mātūbhi. Salope mātu, pasaññattā ‘no’ na hoti, matyā mātuyā, mātarānaṃ mātānaṃ mātūnaṃ. Chaṭṭhivisaye “mātussa saratī”tipi dissati. Mātari, mātaresu mātūsu. Visesā+ññatra pitusamaṃ. Evaṃ dhītu+duhitusaddā.

Mātā, mātaro. Vocative: O māta, mātā, mātaro. Accusative: Mātaraṃ, mātare, mātaro. Instrumental: Mātarā; for the ending 'nā', when 'yā' is substituted, there is elision by splitting the rule 'ye passā', as in 'anuññāto ahaṃ matyā'; elsewhere, mātuyā; mātarehi, mātarebhi, mātūhi, mātūbhi. Genitive: With the elision of the ending 'sa', the form is mātu; because it is a specific term, 'no' is not added; matyā, mātuyā; mātarānaṃ, mātānaṃ, mātūnaṃ. In the context of the genitive case, the form 'mātussa sarati' is also seen. Locative: Mātari; mātaresu, mātūsu. Apart from these special cases, it is like 'pitu'. Thus are declined the words dhītu and duhitu.

Ukārantaṃ.

End of the u-final stems.

Rassanisedhe silope ca kate jambū. “Jantvā”dinā yolope, jambū jambuyo. “Ge vā”ti rasse bho jambu, jambū jambuyo. Jambuṃ, jambū jambuyo. Jambuyā, jambūhi jambūbhi. Jambuyā, jambūnaṃ. Jambuyaṃ jambuyā, jambūsu.

When shortening is prohibited and the nominative singular ending 'si' is elided, the form is jambū. By the rule 'Jantvā...' etc., with the optional elision of the plural ending 'yo', the forms are jambū and jambuyo. By the rule 'Ge vā', there is optional shortening in the vocative: O jambu, jambū, jambuyo. Accusative: Jambuṃ, jambū, jambuyo. Instrumental/Ablative: Jambuyā, jambūhi, jambūbhi. Dative/Genitive: Jambuyā, jambūnaṃ. Locative: Jambuyaṃ, jambuyā, jambūsu.

Evaṃ vadhū ca sarabhū, sarabū sutanū camū;

Vāmūrū nāganāsurū, samānā khalu jambuyā.

Similarly, vadhū, sarabhū, sarabū, sutanū, camū, vāmūrū, and nāganāsurū are indeed declined like jambū.

Ūkārantaṃ.

End of the ū-final stems.

Go, gāvo gavo iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Go, gāvo, gavo, etc., are declined like the masculine.

Itthiliṅgaṃ.

End of the feminine gender.

Napuṃsaka[M 0.0068], si –

Neuter, regarding the ending 'si' –

111. Aṃ napuṃsake

111. Aṃ napuṃsake.

Akārantato nāmasmā sissa aṃ hoti napuṃsake. Napuṃsakaṃ.

After a noun ending in the letter 'a', the nominative singular ending 'si' becomes 'aṃ' in the neuter. For example: napuṃsakaṃ.

112. Yonaṃ ni

112. Yonaṃ ni.

Akārantato yonaṃ ni hoti napuṃsake. Nīnaṃ niccavidhānepi “ninaṃ vā”ti pakkhe ṭāṭe honti, dīghe napuṃsakā napuṃsakāni. Bho napuṃsaka napuṃsakā, napuṃsakā napuṃsakāni. Napuṃsakaṃ, napuṃsake napuṃsakāni. Napuṃsakena, iccādi sugatasaddasamaṃ. Evaṃ –

After an a-final stem, the plural endings 'yo' become 'ni' in the neuter. Although the substitution of 'nī' is prescribed as obligatory, according to the alternative rule 'ninaṃ vā', other endings also occur; with lengthening, the forms are napuṃsakā, napuṃsakāni. Vocative: O napuṃsaka, napuṃsakā, napuṃsakāni. Accusative: Napuṃsakaṃ, napuṃsake, napuṃsakāni. The remaining cases, beginning with the instrumental 'napuṃsakena', are like the word 'sugata'. Thus –

Puñña+pāpa+phala+rūpa+sādhanaṃ,

Sota+ghāna+sukha+dukkha+kāraṇaṃ;

Dāna+sīla+dhana+jhāna+locanaṃ,

Mūla+kūla+bala+jāla+maṅgalaṃ.

Puñña, pāpa, phala, rūpa, sādhanaṃ, sota, ghāna, sukha, dukkha, kāraṇaṃ; dāna, sīla, dhana, jhāna, locanaṃ, mūla, kūla, bala, jāla, maṅgalaṃ.

Naḷina+liṅga+mukha+ṅga+jala+mbujaṃ,

Pulina+dhañña+hirañña+phalā+mataṃ;

Paduma+paṇṇa+susāna+vanā+yudhaṃ,

Hadaya+cīvara+vattha+kuli+ndriyaṃ.

Naḷina, liṅga, mukha, aṅga, jala, ambujaṃ, pulina, dhañña, hirañña, phala, amataṃ; paduma, paṇṇa, susāna, vana, āyudhaṃ, hadaya, cīvara, vattha, kula, indriyaṃ.

Nayana+vadana+yāno+dana+sopāna+pānaṃ,

Bhavana+bhuvana+lohā+lāta+tuṇḍa+ṇḍa+pīṭhaṃ,

Karaṇa+maraṇa+ñāṇā+rammaṇā+rañña+tāṇaṃ,

Tagara+nagara+tīra+cchatta+chiddo+dakāni.iccādi;

Nayana, vadana, yāna, odana, sopāna, pānaṃ, bhavana, bhuvana, loha, ālāta, tuṇḍa, aṇḍa, pīṭhaṃ, karaṇa, maraṇa, ñāṇa, ārammaṇa, arañña, tāṇaṃ, tagara, nagara, tīra, chatta, chidda, udakāni; and so on.

Ekaccaṃ,

Ekaccaṃ,

136. Na [M 0.0069] nissa ṭā

136. Na nissa ṭā.

Ekaccādīhi parassa nissa ṭā na hoti, ekaccāni. Bho ekacca, ekaccā ekaccāni. Ekaccaṃ, ekacce ekaccāni. Sesaṃ napuṃsakaṃva.

After 'ekacca' and similar words, the substitution 'ṭā' for 'ni' does not occur; hence 'ekaccāni'. Vocative: O ekacca, ekaccā, ekaccāni. Nominative/Accusative: Ekaccaṃ, ekacce, ekaccāni. The rest is like 'napuṃsaka'.

Evaṃ paṭhamaṃ, paṭhamāni iccādi. Padaṃ, padā padāni iccādi napuṃsakasamaṃ. Nāsmiṃsu bhedo.

Similarly, paṭhamaṃ, paṭhamāni, etc. Padaṃ, padā, padāni, etc., are like 'napuṃsaka'. There is no difference in them.

106. Nāssa sā

106. Nāssa sā.

Padādīhi nāssa sā hoti vā. Padasā padena.

After 'pada' and similar words, the instrumental singular ending 'nā' optionally becomes 'sā'. Examples: padasā, padena.

105. Padādīhi

105. From 'pada' and similar words.

Padādīhi smino si hoti vā. Padasi pade padamhi padasmiṃ, padesu. Evaṃ bilasaddo.

For 'pada' and similar words, 'smiṃ' optionally becomes 'si'. Examples: 'padasi', 'pade', 'padamhi', 'padasmiṃ', 'padesu'. Thus also the word 'bila'.

Kammasaddato nāssa “nāsse+no”ti eno vā, kammena, “pumakammathāmā”dinā utte kammunā kammanā. Imināva sasmāsu uttaṃ, ussa lasaññāyaṃ sa+smānaṃ yathāyogaṃ no+nā niccaṃ, vavatthitavibhāsattā vādhikārassa. Kammuno kammassa. Kammunā kammā kammamhā kammasmā. “Kammādito”ti smino vā nimhi kammani kamme kammamhi kammasmiṃ, sesaṃ napuṃsakasamaṃ. Camma+vesma+bhasmādayo kammasamā uttato+ññatra.

From the word 'kamma', the suffix `nā` optionally becomes `ena` by the rule 'nāsse no', yielding 'kammena'. By the rule 'pumakammathāmā' and so on, when `u` is substituted, the forms are 'kammunā' and 'kammanā'. By this same rule, `u` is also substituted in the ablative cases (`sasmā`). For this substituted `u`, the suffixes `sa` (gen.) and `smā` (abl.) are always replaced by `no` and `nā` respectively, or due to the fixed optionality of the governing rule. Genitive: 'kammuno', 'kammassa'. Ablative: 'kammunā', 'kammā', 'kammamhā', 'kammasmā'. By the rule 'kammādito', the suffix `smiṃ` is optionally replaced by `ni` or `mhi` in the locative, yielding: 'kammani', 'kamme', 'kammamhi', 'kammasmiṃ'. The remaining forms are like those of a standard neuter noun. Words such as 'camma', 'vesma', 'bhasma', and so on are declined like 'kamma', except for the substitution of `u`.

Gacchanta, si. “Ntassaṃ”ti vā aṃmhi silopo gacchaṃ. Aññatra sissa daṃ, gacchantaṃ, gacchantā gacchantāni. Bho gaccha gacchā gacchaṃ, gacchantā gacchantāni. Gacchaṃ gacchantaṃ, gacchante gacchantāni. Gacchatā gacchantene+ccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ. Evaṃ yajanta+vajantādayo.

The word 'gacchanta', with the suffix 'si'. By the rule 'Ntassaṃ', the final `nta` optionally becomes `aṃ` and `si` is elided, resulting in 'gacchaṃ'. Otherwise, `daṃ` is substituted for `si`, giving 'gacchantaṃ'. Nominative plural: 'gacchantā', 'gacchantāni'. Vocative: 'Bho gaccha', 'gacchā', 'gacchaṃ', 'gacchantā', 'gacchantāni'. Accusative: 'gacchaṃ', 'gacchantaṃ', 'gacchante', 'gacchantāni'. Instrumental 'gacchatā', 'gacchantena', and so on, are like the masculine declension. Thus also 'yajanta', 'vajanta', and so on.

Akārantaṃ.

End of the `a`-stems.

Aṭṭhi[M 0.0070], silopo.

'Aṭṭhi', with elision of 'si'.

113. Jhalā vā

113. After `jhala`, optionally.

Jhalato yonaṃ ni hoti vā napuṃsake. Aṭṭhīni. “Lopo”ti yolope dīgho, aṭṭhī. Bho aṭṭhi aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni aṭṭhī. Aṭṭhiṃ, aṭṭhīni aṭṭhī. Aṭṭhinā iccādi munisaddasamaṃ. Evaṃ pacchi+akkhi+dadhi+satthi+vāri+acciādayo.

After `jhala` consonants, the suffix `yo` optionally becomes `ni` in the neuter. Example: 'aṭṭhīni'. By the rule beginning with 'Lopo', when `yo` is elided, the preceding vowel is lengthened, resulting in 'aṭṭhī'. Vocative: 'Bho aṭṭhi', 'aṭṭhī', 'aṭṭhīni', 'aṭṭhī'. Accusative: 'aṭṭhiṃ', 'aṭṭhīni', 'aṭṭhī'. Instrumental 'aṭṭhinā', and so on, are like the word 'muni'. Thus also: 'pacchi', 'akkhi', 'dadhi', 'satthi', 'vāri', 'acci', and so on.

Ikārantaṃ.

End of the `i`-stems.

Daṇḍi, napuṃsakattā “ekavacane”ccādinā rasse silopo. Daṇḍīni daṇḍī. “Ge vā”ti rasse bho daṇḍi daṇḍī, daṇḍīni daṇḍī. “Naṃ jhīto”ti naṃ. Daṇḍinaṃ daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍīni daṇḍī. Sesaṃ pulliṅge daṇḍīsamaṃ. Evaṃ sukhakārī+sīghayāyīādayo.

The word 'daṇḍī'. Because it is neuter, by the rule 'ekavacane' and so on, the final vowel is shortened and `si` is elided, yielding 'daṇḍi'. Plural forms: 'daṇḍīni', 'daṇḍī'. By the rule 'Ge vā', with shortening, the vocative forms are: 'Bho daṇḍi', 'daṇḍī', 'daṇḍīni', 'daṇḍī'. By the rule 'Naṃ jhīto', the accusative suffix is `naṃ`. Accusative forms: 'daṇḍinaṃ', 'daṇḍiṃ', 'daṇḍīni', 'daṇḍī'. The remaining forms are like 'daṇḍī' in the masculine. Thus also 'sukhakārī', 'sīghayāyī', and so on.

Īkārantaṃ.

End of the `ī`-stems.

Cakkhu, cakkhūni cakkhū. Sesaṃ aṭṭhisamaṃ. Evaṃ āyu+vasu+dhanu+dāru+tipu+madhu+siṅgu+hiṅgu+vatthu+jatu+ambu+ assuādīni. Āyusaddato nāssa kodhādittā sāva viseso.

'Cakkhu', 'cakkhūni', 'cakkhū'. The remaining forms are like those of 'aṭṭhi'. Thus also 'āyu', 'vasu', 'dhanu', 'dāru', 'tipu', 'madhu', 'siṅgu', 'hiṅgu', 'vatthu', 'jatu', 'ambu', 'assu', and so on. For the word 'āyu', because it belongs to the `kodhādi` group, the special form for the instrumental suffix `nā` is `sā`.

Ukārantaṃ.

End of the `u`-stems.

Gotrabhu, rasse silopo. Gotrabhūni gotrabhū. Bho gotrabhu gotrabhū, gotrabhūni gotrabhū. Gotrabhuṃ, gotrabhūni gotrabhū iccādi pulliṅge vessabhūsamaṃ. Evaṃ sayambhū+abhibhū+dhammaññū ādayo.

The word 'gotrabhū'. The final vowel is shortened and `si` is elided, yielding 'gotrabhu'. Plural forms: 'gotrabhūni', 'gotrabhū'. Vocative: 'Bho gotrabhu', 'gotrabhū', 'gotrabhūni', 'gotrabhū'. Accusative: 'gotrabhuṃ', 'gotrabhūni', 'gotrabhū', and so on, are like 'vessabhū' in the masculine. Thus also 'sayambhū', 'abhibhū', 'dhammaññū', and so on.

Ūkārantaṃ.

End of the `ū`-stems.

Visadā+visadākāra-vohāro+bhayamuttako[M 0.0071];

Pumādijānane hetu-bhāvato liṅga+mīrito.

Clear, of clear form, a matter of usage, and free from both sexes; because it is the cause for knowing the masculine and so on, it is called 'liṅga'.

Thana+kesāvatī nārī, massuvā puriso siyā;

Ubhinna+mantaraṃ etaṃ, itaro+bhayamuttako.

A woman is one with breasts and long hair; a man is one with a beard. This is the difference between the two; the other is free from both.

Ese+sā eta+mīti ca,

Pasiddhiatthesu yesu lokassa;

Thī+puma+napuṃsakānī+ti,

Vuccante tāni nāmāni.

Those nouns which, in the established usage of the world, are referred to by 'eso' (masc.), 'sā' (fem.), and 'etaṃ' (neut.), are called masculine, feminine, and neuter.

Napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ.

End of the Neuter Gender.

Atha sabbādīnaṃ rūpanayo niddisiyate,

Now, the method for the forms of 'sabba' and similar words is explained.

Sabba katara katama ubhaya itara añña aññatara aññatama, pubba+parā+para+dakkhiṇu+ttarā+dharāni vavatthāya+masaññāyaṃ. “Ūnapūrattha+madhikapadodāharaṇa+majjhāhāro”ti ñāyā sabbādīsu paṭhīyanteti yojetabbaṃ. Ya tya ta eta ima amu kiṃ eka tumha amha iccete sabbādayo. Kaccāyane adassitassāpi tyasaddassa –

Sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya, itara, añña, aññatara, aññatama; pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara—these, in the sense of specification and when not used as proper nouns. By the principle of 'filling a deficiency, providing an example of an additional word, and inserting a middle term', it should be understood that they are recited in the `sabbādi` group. Ya, tya, ta, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ, eka, tumha, amha—these are the `sabbādi` words. Although the word 'tya' is not shown in Kaccāyana's grammar—

Khiḍḍā paṇihitā tyāsu, rati tyāsu patiṭṭhitā;

Bījāni tyāsu ruhanti, yadidaṃ sattā pajāyareti –

Play is directed towards them, delight is established in them; seeds grow in them, whereby beings are generated.

Pāḷiyaṃ dissamānattā idha saṅgaho.

Because it is seen in the Pāli Canon, it is included here.

Tattha sabbasaddo niravasesattho. Katara+katamasaddā pucchanatthā. Ubhayasaddo dviavayavasamudāyavacano. Itarasaddo vuttapaṭiyogīvacano. Aññasaddo adhikatāparavacano. Añña- tara+aññatamasaddā [M 0.0072] aniyamatthā. Pubbādayo disādivavatthāvacanā. Yasaddo aniyamattho. Tya+tasaddā parammukhavacanā. Eta+ima+amu+kiṃ iccete samīpa+accantasamīpa+dūra+pucchanatthavacanā. Ekasaddo saṃkhyādivacano. Tumha+amhasaddā para+atta niddesavacanā.

Therein, the word 'sabba' means 'all, without remainder'. The words 'katara' and 'katama' are for asking questions. The word 'ubhaya' denotes a collection of two components. The word 'itara' refers to the counterpart of what has been stated. The word 'añña' refers to something additional or distinct. The words 'aññatara' and 'aññatama' indicate indefiniteness. 'Pubba' and the like express distinctions of directions and so on. The word 'ya' indicates indefiniteness. The words 'tya' and 'ta' refer to something not present. The words 'eta', 'ima', 'amu', and 'kiṃ' express nearness, extreme nearness, distance, and questioning respectively. The word 'eka' expresses number and so on. The words 'tumha' and 'amha' indicate reference to another and to oneself.

Sabbo, sissa o,

'Sabbo'. For the suffix `si`, `o` is substituted.

138. Yona+meṭa

138. For `yo`, `e`.

Akārantehi sabbādīhi yonaṃ eṭa hoti niccaṃ. Sabbe. Bho sabba sabbā, sabbe. Sabbaṃ, sabbe. Sabbena, sabbehi sabbebhi. Evaṃ karaṇe. Sabbassa.

After `a`-stem `sabbādi` words, the suffix `yo` always becomes `e`. Example: 'sabbe'. Vocative: 'Bho sabba', 'sabbā', 'sabbe'. Accusative: 'sabbaṃ', 'sabbe'. Instrumental: 'sabbena', 'sabbehi', 'sabbebhi'. Thus in the instrumental. Genitive: 'sabbassa'.

99. Sabbādīnaṃ naṃmhi ca

99. And for `sabbādi` words before `naṃ`.

Akārantānaṃ sabbādīnaṃ e hoti naṃmhi su+hisu ca. Ettha ādisaddo avayave, vuttañhi –

For `a`-stem `sabbādi` words, the final vowel becomes `e` before the suffixes `naṃ`, `su`, and `hi`. Here, the word `ādi` in `sabbādi` is used in the sense of a member of a class, for it has been said:

Mariyādāyaṃ pakāre ca, samīpe+vayave tathā;

Catūsva+tthesu medhāvī, ādisaddaṃ pakāsayeti.

In the sense of limit and type, likewise in proximity and as a member of a class; the wise one should explain the word `ādi` in these four meanings.

100. Saṃ+sānaṃ

100. Of `saṃ` and `sānaṃ`.

Sabbādito naṃvacanassa saṃ+sānaṃ honti. Sabbesaṃ sabbesānaṃ. Sabbā sabbamhā sabbasmā. Sabbe sabbamhi sabbasmiṃ, sabbesu.

After the pronouns beginning with `sabba`, the genitive plural ending `naṃ` becomes `saṃ` and `sānaṃ`. [Examples:] `Sabbesaṃ`, `sabbesānaṃ`. `Sabbā`, `sabbamhā`, `sabbasmā`. `Sabbe`, `sabbamhi`, `sabbasmiṃ`, `sabbesu`.

Itthiyaṃ “itthiya+matvā”ti āpaccaye tassa ghasaññā. Sesaṃ kaññāva. Sabbā, sabbā sabbāyo. Bho sabbe, sabbā sabbāyo. “Gho ssaṃ+ssā+ssāyaṃ+tiṃ sū”-ti rasse [M 0.0073] sabbaṃ, sabbā sabbāyo. Sabbāya, sabbāhi sabbābhi.

In the feminine, when the suffix `ā` is present, indicating the feminine, the stem is designated as `gha`. The remaining forms are like `kaññā`. [Nominative:] `Sabbā`; [plural] `sabbā`, `sabbāyo`. [Vocative:] O `sabbe`; [plural] `sabbā`, `sabbāyo`. By the rule 'Gho ssaṃ+ssā+ssāyaṃ+tiṃ sū', with shortening: [Accusative singular:] `sabbaṃ`; [plural] `sabbā`, `sabbāyo`. [Instrumental singular:] `Sabbāya`; [plural] `sabbāhi`, `sabbābhi`.

101. Ghapā sassa ssā vā

101. From a `gha` stem, `ssa` optionally becomes `ssā`.

Sabbādīnaṃ ghapato sassa ssā vā hoti. Amussāti rūpassa “ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhī”ti ssādesena siddhattā vāggahaṇa+muttaratthaṃ. Rasse sabbassā sabbāya, sabbāsaṃ sabbāsānaṃ. Pañcamiyaṃ sabbāya.

For the pronouns beginning with `sabba` which are designated `gha`, the genitive singular ending `ssa` optionally becomes `ssā`. Since the form `amussā` is established by the rule 'ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhī', the inclusion of 'optionally' (`vā`) is for the sake of a subsequent rule. With shortening: `sabbassā`, `sabbāya`; `sabbāsaṃ`, `sabbāsānaṃ`. In the ablative: `sabbāya`.

102. Smino ssaṃ

102. `Smiṃ` becomes `ssaṃ`.

Sabbādīnaṃ ghapato smino ssaṃ vā hoti. Sabbassaṃ sabbāyaṃ sabbāya, sabbāsu.

For the pronouns beginning with `sabba` which are designated `gha`, the locative singular ending `smiṃ` optionally becomes `ssaṃ`. [Examples:] `Sabbassaṃ`, `sabbāyaṃ`, `sabbāya`; `sabbāsu`.

Napuṃsake sabbaṃ. “Yonaṃ nī”ti napuṃsake yossa nimhi –

In the neuter: `sabbaṃ`. By the rule 'Yonaṃ nī', in the neuter, for the ending `yo`, when `ni` is the substitute—

137. Sabbādīhi

137. From `sabba` and others.

Sabbādīhi parassa nissa ṭā na hoti. Dīghe sabbāni. Bho sabba sabbā, sabbāni. Sabbaṃ, sabbe sabbāni. Nādīsu pumeva. Katarakatamaubhayā tīsu liṅgesu sabbasamā. Evaṃ itaraaññasaddā. Ssā+ssaṃsu viseso.

After the pronouns beginning with `sabba`, the substitution of `ṭā` for `ni` does not occur. With lengthening: `sabbāni`. [Vocative:] O `sabba`, `sabbā`, `sabbāni`. [Accusative:] `Sabbaṃ`; `sabbe`, `sabbāni`. In the cases beginning with `nā`, it is like the masculine. The words `katara`, `katama`, and `ubhaya` are like `sabba` in the three genders. Likewise the words `itara` and `añña`. There is a special rule for `ssā` and `ssaṃ`.

52. Ssaṃ+ssā+ssāyesvi-tare+ka+ññe+ti+māna+mi

52. In `ssaṃ`, `ssā`, and `ssāya`, `i` for `itara`, `eka`, `añña`, `eta`, `ima`.

Ssamādīsu itara+eka+añña+eta+ima iccetesaṃ i hoti niccaṃ. Itarissā itarāya, aññissā aññāya, aññāsaṃ [M 0.0074] aññāsānaṃ. Aññissaṃ aññāyaṃ aññāya. Aññatara+ññatamā liṅgattaye sabbasamā.

Before the endings beginning with `ssa`, for the words `itara`, `eka`, `añña`, `eta`, and `ima`, the final vowel always becomes `i`. [Examples:] `Itarissā`, `itarāya`; `aññissā`, `aññāya`; `aññāsaṃ`, `aññāsānaṃ`. `Aññissaṃ`, `aññāyaṃ`, `aññāya`. The words `aññatara` and `aññatama` are like `sabba` in the three genders.

Pubbo,

`Pubba`.

143. Pubbādīhi chahi

143. From the six words beginning with `pubba`.

Etehi chahi savisaye eṭa vā hotīti yossa eṭa, pubbe pubbā. Bho pubba pubbā, pubbe pubbā. Pubbaṃ, pubbe. Pubbena. Sesaṃ sabbaliṅge sabbasamaṃ. Evaṃ parādayo pañca.

For these six words, in their own domain, `eṭa` is an optional substitute for `yo`. [Thus:] `pubbe`, `pubbā`. [Vocative:] O `pubba`, `pubbā`; `pubbe`, `pubbā`. [Accusative:] `Pubbaṃ`; `pubbe`. [Instrumental:] `Pubbena`. The remaining forms are like `sabba` in all genders. Likewise for the five words beginning with `para`.

139. Nā+ññañca nāma+ppadhānā

139. Not when used as a noun or when not principal.

Taṃnāmabhūtehi appadhānehi ca sabbādīhi sabbādikāriyaṃ na hoti. Te sabbā, sabbanāmā teti attho. Te piyasabbā, te atisabbā. Nāmabhūte ca aññapadatthādo appadhānavisaye ca sabbādikāriyanisedhena “paramasabbe tiṭṭhanti” tyādito padhānapadantato eṭaādayo honti, visesanasamāsassa uttarapadatthapadhānattā.

For the pronouns beginning with `sabba` that have become proper nouns or are not the principal element [of a compound], the operations specific to the `sabbādi` group do not apply. For example, `Te sabbā`, meaning 'they are the Sabbas'. Or, `Te piyasabbā` and `Te atisabbā`. By this prohibition of `sabbādi` operations when the word has become a noun or is non-principal (as in a bahubbīhi compound), in expressions like `paramasabbe tiṭṭhanti`, the substitutions such as `eṭa` do occur because the final member is principal, due to the principal nature of the final member's meaning in a karmadhāraya compound.

140. Tatiyatthayoge

140. In connection with the instrumental sense.

Tatiyatthena yoge ca sabbādikāriyaṃ na hoti. Māsena pubbā māsapubbā iccādi.

And when in connection with the instrumental sense, the operations for the `sabbādi` group do not apply. For example, `māsena pubbā` becomes `māsapubbā`, and so on.

141. Catthasamāse

141. In a dvanda compound.

Catthasamāsavisaye sabbādikāriyaṃ na hoti. Dakkhiṇuttarapubbānantiādi.

In the case of a dvanda compound, the operations for the `sabbādi` group do not apply. For example, `dakkhiṇuttarapubbānaṃ`, and so on.

142. Ve+ṭa

142. Optionally `eṭa`.

Iti [M 0.0075] catthasamāse sabbādikāriyaṃ na hoti, niccena eṭaādesappasaṅge ayaṃ sampattavibhāsā. Pubbuttare pubbuttarā. Sesaṃ sugatasamaṃ.

Thus, in a dvanda compound, the `sabbādi` operations do not apply. When the substitution of `eṭa` would otherwise be invariable, this rule provides an option. [Examples:] `Pubbuttare`, `pubbuttarā`. The remaining forms are like `sugata`.

Yo, ye. Yā, yāyo. Yaṃ, yāni iccādi sabbasamaṃ. Yādīna+mālapane rūpaṃ na sambhavati.

[The declension of `ya`:] `Yo`, `ye`. `Yā`, `yāyo`. `Yaṃ`, `yāni`, and so on, is like `sabba`. For the pronouns beginning with `ya`, a vocative form does not exist.

Tya si –

For `tya`, with `si`—

128. Tya+te+tānaṃ tassa so

128. For `tya`, `ta`, and `eta`, `so` replaces `ta`.

Tya+te+tāna+manapuṃsakānaṃ tassa so hoti simhi. Syo, tye. Syā, tyā, tyāyo. Tyaṃ, tyāni iccādi sabbasamaṃ.

For the non-neuter stems `tya`, `ta`, and `eta`, their `ta` becomes `so` before the nominative singular ending `si`. [Examples for `tya`:] `Syo`, `tye`. `Syā`; `tyā`, `tyāyo`. `Tyaṃ`, `tyāni`, and so on, are like `sabba`.

So,

`So`.

131. Tatassa no sabbāsu

131. For `ta`, `na` in all cases.

Tasaddassa tassa no vā hoti sabbāsu vibhattīsu. “Tya+te+tānaṃ tassā”ti ca ettha tyādīnaṃ takāraggahaṇaṃ syā sā esā nāyoti itthiyaṃ sabbasamā hotīti. Ne te. Naṃ taṃ, ne te. Nena tene, nehi nebhi tehi tebhi.

For the word `ta`, its `ta` optionally becomes `na` in all case endings. And in the rule 'Tya+te+tānaṃ tassā', the inclusion of the letter `t` for `tya` etc. is so that in the feminine, `syā`, `sā`, `esā`, and `nāyo` are formed like `sabbā`. [Examples:] `Ne`, `te`. `Naṃ`, `taṃ`; `ne`, `te`. `Nena`, `tena`; `nehi`, `nebhi`, `tehi`, `tebhi`.

132. Ṭa sasmāsmiṃssāyassaṃssāsaṃmhāmhisvi+massa ca

132. And `ṭa` for `ima` before `sasmā`, `smiṃ`, `ssāya`, `ssaṃ`, `ssā`, `saṃ`, `mhā`, `mhi`, and `svi`.

“Ṭa sa+smā+smiṃ+naṃsmi+massa cā”ti vuttepi tesaṃ vibhattīnaṃ ādesesu ssāyādīsu paresu “tadādesā tadiva [M 0.0076] bhavantī”ti ñāyā ṭādese siddhepi yādiādesantare pare nivattanatthaṃ ssādīnaṃ gahaṇaṃ.

Even though it is stated, 'And `ṭa` for `ima` before `sa`, `smā`, `smiṃ`, `naṃsmi`,' and even though the substitution of `ṭa` is established by the maxim, 'substitutes for them behave like them,' when `ssāya` and other substitutes for those case endings follow, the inclusion of `ssā`, etc., is for the purpose of preventing other substitutions, such as `ya`.

Sādīsvi+massa tasaddatakārassa ca ṭo vā hoti. Pubbassaralopo. Eva+muparipi. Assa nassa tassa, nesaṃ nesānaṃ tesaṃ tesānaṃ. Amhā asmā namhā nasmā tamhā tasmā. Amhi asmiṃ namhi nasmiṃ tamhi tasmiṃ, nesu tesu.

Before `sa` and other endings, `ṭa` is optionally substituted for `ima` and for the letter `ta` of the word `ta`. Elision of the preceding vowel occurs. Thus also in the following. [Examples:] `assa`, `nassa`, `tassa`; `nesaṃ`, `nesānaṃ`, `tesaṃ`, `tesānaṃ`; `amhā`, `asmā`, `namhā`, `nasmā`, `tamhā`, `tasmā`; `amhi`, `asmiṃ`, `namhi`, `nasmiṃ`, `tamhi`, `tasmiṃ`; `nesu`, `tesu`.

Itthiyaṃ sā, nā nāyo tā tāyo. Naṃ taṃ, nā nāyo tā tāyo. Nāmhi –

In the feminine: `sā`; `nā`, `nāyo`, `tā`, `tāyo`. `naṃ`, `taṃ`; `nā`, `nāyo`, `tā`, `tāyo`. Before `nā`—

46. Ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhi

46. Optionally `ssā` after `ta`, `eta`, `ima`, and `amu`.

Ghapasaññehi ta+eta+ima+amūhi ekatte nādīnaṃ ssā vā hoti. Antassarānaṃ ghapavohārena taṃsahacaritāpi saddā “kunte pavesayā”ti ñāyā gayhantīti “ghapasaññehi ta+eta+ima+amūhī”ti vuttaṃ. Vāṭādese assā nassā nāya.

After `ta`, `eta`, `ima`, and `amu`, which have the `gha` designation, `ssā` is optionally substituted for `nā` and other endings in the singular. Because, by the application of the `gha` designation to the final vowels, words associated with them are also included by the maxim 'let the spears enter,' it is said, 'after `ta`, `eta`, `ima`, and `amu`, which have the `gha` designation.' With the optional `ṭa` substitution: `assā`, `nassā`; [the alternative is] `nāya`.

53. Tāya vā

53. Optionally `tāya`.

Ssaṃssāssā yesu tassa vā i hoti. Tissā tassā tāya, nāhi nābhi tāhi tābhi. Sassa vā ssāmhi assā nassā tissā tassā.

`i` is optionally substituted for `ta` before the endings `ssaṃ` and `ssā`. [Examples:] `tissā`, `tassā`, `tāya`; `nāhi`, `nābhi`, `tāhi`, `tābhi`. For the genitive ending `sa`, or in the locative `ssāṃ`: `assā`, `nassā`, `tissā`, `tassā`.

54. Te+ti+māto sassa ssāya

54. After `ta`, `eta`, and `ima`, `ssāya` for `sa`.

Tā+etā+imāto sassa ssāyo hoti vā. Assāya nassāya tissāya tassāya, “ghapate”ccādinā yādese [M 0.0077] nāya tāya. Naṃvacanassa sa+mādese takārassa ca vā ṭādese āsaṃ nāsaṃ nāsānaṃ tāsaṃ tāsānaṃ. Sattamiyaṃ assaṃ assā nassaṃ nassā nāyaṃ nāya tissaṃ tissā tassaṃ tassā tāyaṃ tāya, nāsu tāsu.

After `ta`, `eta`, and `ima`, `ssāyo` is optionally substituted for `sa`. [Examples:] `assāya`, `nassāya`, `tissāya`, `tassāya`. When `ya` is substituted by the rule 'ghapate...' etc., [the forms are] `nāya`, `tāya`. For the plural ending `naṃ`, with the substitution of `saṃ`, and the optional substitution of `ṭa` for the letter `ta`, [the forms are] `āsaṃ`, `nāsaṃ`, `nāsānaṃ`, `tāsaṃ`, `tāsānaṃ`. In the seventh case (locative): `assaṃ`, `assā`, `nassaṃ`, `nassā`, `nāyaṃ`, `nāya`, `tissaṃ`, `tissā`, `tassaṃ`, `tassā`, `tāyaṃ`, `tāya`; `nāsu`, `tāsu`.

Napuṃsake naṃ taṃ, nāni tāni. Naṃ taṃ, ne nāni te tāni. Sesaṃ pumeva.

In the neuter: `naṃ`, `taṃ`; `nāni`, `tāni`. `naṃ`, `taṃ`; `ne`, `nāni`, `te`, `tāni`. The rest is as in the masculine.

“Yaṃtaṃsaddā niccasambandhā”ti ñāyā yaṃsaddena aniyamitatthaṃ taṃsaddo niyameti.

By the maxim 'the words `ya` and `ta` are always connected,' the word `ta` defines the indefinite meaning introduced by the word `ya`.

Pasiddhe anubhūtatthe, pakkantavisaye tathā;

Yaṃsadda+manapekkheva, taṃsaddo yujjate sadāti –

In a well-known, experienced meaning, and likewise in a past context, the word `ta` is always used without depending on the word `ya`.

Vuttattā ettheva taṃsaddo yaṃsaddaṃ nāpekkhati. Yathākkamaṃ tatri+da+mudāharaṇaṃ –

Because it has been stated, in this case the word `ta` does not depend on the word `ya`. In sequence, here is the example for that:

(.) “Namo tassā”ti ca, (.) “aggimpa+kkhinā…pe… ñātakārī hi so jino”ti ca, (..) Purimagāthāya vuttamunisadda+mapekkhitvā “savāsane kilese so”ti ca.

(.) 'Homage to her,' and (.) 'the fires are extinguished... for that Conqueror is one who acts for his kin,' and (..) referring to the word 'muni' mentioned in the previous verse, 'He [conquered] the defilements along with their latent tendencies.'

Eso, ete. Esā, etā etāyo, etaṃ, etāni iccādi ṭa+nādesābhāvova viseso.

`Eso`, `ete`. `Esā`, `etā`, `etāyo`. `Etaṃ`, `etāni`, etc. The only distinction is the absence of the `ṭa` and `na` substitutions.

Ima si,

After `ima`, `si`.

127. Simha+napuṃsakassā+yaṃ

127. Before `si`, `ayaṃ` for non-neuter `ima`.

Imasaddassa anapuṃsakassa ayaṃ hoti simhi. Ayaṃ, ime. Imaṃ, ime.

For non-neuter `ima`, `ayaṃ` occurs before `si`. [Examples:] `ayaṃ`, `ime`; `imaṃ`, `ime`.

126. Nāmha+ni+mi

126. [The substitutions] `ana` and `imi` before `nā`.

Imasaddassa [M 0.0078] anitthiyaṃ nāmhi ana+imiiccādesā honti. “Ate+nā”ti ene anena iminā. Himhi –

For `ima`, when not feminine, before the ending `nā`, `ana`, `imi`, etc., are the substitutions. By 'Atenā', [the forms are] `ena`, `anena`, `iminā`. Before `hi`—

125. Imassā+nitthiyaṃ ṭe

125. For non-feminine `ima`, `e`.

Imassā+nitthiyaṃ ṭe hoti vā su+naṃ+hisu. “Nāmaggahaṇe liṅgavisiṭṭhassāpi gahaṇaṃ”ti ñāyā ‘anitthiyaṃ’ti itthiliṅganisedhā imassāti nāmaggahaṇavisaye liṅgavisesitassa imasaddassāpi gahaṇaṃ. Tassa phalaṃ “tatassa no sabbāsu” tyādo liṅgattaye kāriyasiddhi. Ehi ebhi imehi imebhi. “Ṭa sasmāsmi”miccādinā sabbassi+massa vā ṭādese assa imassa, vā ṭe esaṃ esānaṃ imesaṃ imesānaṃ. Amhā asmā imamhā imasmā. Amhi asmiṃ imamhi imasmiṃ, esu imesu.

For non-feminine `ima`, `e` is optionally substituted before `su`, `naṃ`, and `hi`. By the maxim 'in the mention of a stem, its gender-specific form is also included,' the prohibition 'non-feminine' implies that when the stem `ima` is mentioned, the gender-specific word `ima` is also included. Its result is the successful application of the rule in all three genders, as in 'tatassa no sabbāsu', etc. [Examples:] `ehi`, `ebhi`, `imehi`, `imebhi`. By 'Ṭa sasmāsmi...' etc., with the optional substitution of `ṭa` for the whole of `ima`: `assa`, `imassa`. With the optional substitution of `e`: `esaṃ`, `esānaṃ`, `imesaṃ`, `imesānaṃ`. [Ablative:] `amhā`, `asmā`, `imamhā`, `imasmā`. [Locative:] `amhi`, `asmiṃ`, `imamhi`, `imasmiṃ`; `esu`, `imesu`.

Itthiyaṃ ayaṃ, imā imāyo. Imaṃ, imā imāyo. Nā “ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhī”ti ssā vā, vā ṭādese “ssa” miccādinā iādese ca kate assā imissā imāya, imāhi imābhi. Assā imissā assāya imissāya imāya. Naṃvacanassa sa+mādese imassa ca vā ṭādese assa “sunaṃhi sū”ti dīghe ca kate āsaṃ, aññatra imāsaṃ imāsānaṃ. Sattamiyaṃ assaṃ imissaṃ assā imissā imāyaṃ imāya, imāsu.

In the feminine: `ayaṃ`; `imā`, `imāyo`. `Imaṃ`; `imā`, `imāyo`. Before `nā`, by the rule 'ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhī', `ssā` is optional; with the optional `ṭa` substitution, and with the `i` substitution by 'ssa...' etc., [the forms are] `assā`, `imissā`, `imāya`; `imāhi`, `imābhi`. [Other forms are] `assā`, `imissā`, `assāya`, `imissāya`, `imāya`. For the plural ending `naṃ`, with the substitution of `saṃ`, the optional `ṭa` substitution for `ima`, and lengthening by 'sunaṃhi sū', `āsaṃ` is formed; otherwise, `imāsaṃ`, `imāsānaṃ`. In the seventh case (locative): `assaṃ`, `imissaṃ`, `assā`, `imissā`, `imāyaṃ`, `imāya`; `imāsu`.

Napuṃsake –

In the neuter—

201. Imassi+daṃ vā

201. Optionally `idaṃ` for `ima`.

Aṃsisu [M 0.0079] saha tehi imassi+daṃ hoti vā napuṃsake. Idaṃ imaṃ, ime imāni. Idaṃ imaṃ, ime imāni. Anena iminā iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

Before the endings `aṃ` and `si`, `idaṃ` is optionally substituted for `ima` (along with those endings) in the neuter. [Examples:] `idaṃ`, `imaṃ`; `ime`, `imāni`. `idaṃ`, `imaṃ`; `ime`, `imāni`. `Anena`, `iminā`, etc., are the same as in the masculine.

197. Ime+tāna+menā+nvādese dutiyāyaṃ

197. For `ima` and `eta`, `ena` in the second case in anaphoric use.

Imaetasaddānaṃ kathitānukathanavisaye dutiyāya+menādeso hoti. Imaṃ bhikkhuṃ vinaya+majjhāpaya, atho enaṃ dhamma+majjhāpaya. Ime bhikkhū vinaya+majjhāpaya, atho ene dhamma+majjhāpaya. Eva+metassa ca yojanīyaṃ.

For the words `ima` and `eta`, the substitution of `ena` occurs in the second case in the context of subsequent mention. [Examples:] 'Instruct this bhikkhu in the Vinaya, then instruct him in the Dhamma. Instruct these bhikkhus in the Vinaya, then instruct them in the Dhamma.' This should be applied to `eta` as well.

Amu si,

After `amu`, `si`.

129. Massā+mussa

129. Of `amu`, `sa` for `ma`.

Anapuṃsakassā+mussa makārassa so hoti simhi. Asu, yo –

Of `amu`, when not neuter, `sa` is substituted for the letter `ma` in the nominative singular (`simhi`). Examples: `asu`, `yo` –

86. Lopo+musmā

86. Elision after `amu`.

Niyamasutta+midaṃ, amusaddato yonaṃ lopo hoti niccaṃ pulliṅge. Dīghe amū. Jhalato yonaṃ “lopo”ti lope siddhepi vo+pavādo+ya+mārambho.

This is a restrictive rule. After the word `amu`, the elision of `yo` always occurs in the masculine gender. With lengthening, the form is `amū`. Although the elision of `yo` after a `jhala` consonant is established by the rule 'lopo', this commencement is an exception.

Ārambho vacanampatti, lakkhaṇaṃ yogalakkhaṇaṃ;

Vākyaṃ satthañca iccādi, suttāna+mabhidhāyakā.

`Ārambho` (commencement), `vacanampatti` (origination of a rule); `lakkhaṇaṃ` (characteristic), `yogalakkhaṇaṃ` (characteristic of application); `vākyaṃ` (sentence), `satthañca` (and teaching), etc., are the designators of suttas.

Amuṃ, amū. Amunā, amūhi amūbhi.

`Amuṃ`, `amū`. `Amunā`, `amūhi`, `amūbhi`.

87. Na no sassa

87. `no` is not substituted for `sa`.

Amusmā [M 0.0080] sassa no na hoti. Amussa, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ. “Nāsmāssā”ti lato smāssa nā, amunā amumhā amusmā. Amumhi amusmiṃ, amūsu.

After `amu`, `no` is not substituted for the genitive ending `sa`. Examples: `amussa`, `amūsaṃ`, `amūsānaṃ`. By the rule 'Nāsmāssā', `nā` is substituted for `smā`; the forms are `amunā`, `amumhā`, `amusmā`. Locative forms: `amumhi`, `amusmiṃ`, `amūsu`.

Itthiyaṃ asu, amū amuyo. Amuṃ, amū amuyo. Nā, “ssā vā te+ti+mā+mūhī”ti nādyekavacanānaṃ ssā vā, amussā amuyā, amūhi amūbhi. Amussā amuyā, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ. Sattamiyaṃ amussaṃ amussā amuyaṃ amuyā, amūsu.

In the feminine gender: `asu`; `amū`, `amuyo`. `Amuṃ`; `amū`, `amuyo`. For the singular case endings beginning with `nā`, `ssā` is an optional substitute, yielding `amussā` and `amuyā`; plural forms are `amūhi`, `amūbhi`. Dative/Genitive: `amussā`, `amuyā`; `amūsaṃ`, `amūsānaṃ`. In the seventh case (locative): `amussaṃ`, `amussā`, `amuyaṃ`, `amuyā`; `amūsu`.

Napuṃsake –

In the neuter gender –

202. Amussā+duṃ

202. `aduṃ` for `amu`.

Aṃsisu saha tehi amussa aduṃ hoti vā napuṃsake. Aduṃ, silopo, amuṃ. “Jhalā vā”ti vāniādese amūni amū. Aduṃ amuṃ, amūni amū. Amunā iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the neuter, in the presence of `aṃ` and `si`, `aduṃ` is optionally substituted for the stem `amu`. The forms are `aduṃ` and `amuṃ`. By the rule 'Jhalā vā', with the optional substitution of `ni` for `yo`, the forms are `amūni` and `amū`. The forms are: `aduṃ`, `amuṃ`; `amūni`, `amū`. `Amunā` and so forth are the same as in the masculine.

“Sakatte”ti kapaccaye –

With the `ka` suffix in its own sense –

130. Ke vā

130. Optionally, when `ka` follows.

Amu eva amukoti sakatthe kapaccaye taddhitavuttittā “ekatthatāyaṃ”ti silope ca kate “nimittābhāve nemittikassābhāvo”ti ñāyā nimittabhūtassa sissā+bhāve nemittikassa “massā+mussā”ti kattabbassa sakārassa nivuttīti ‘ke vā’ti vikappena massa sakārattha+ mida+māraddhaṃ[M 0.0081]. Amussa massa ke sa hoti vā. Asuko amukā, asukā amukā. Asukaṃ amukaṃ iccādi.

`amuko` means 'that very one', formed with the `ka` suffix in its own sense. Because this is a derivative formation, `si` is elided by the rule 'ekatthatāyaṃ'. Then, by the maxim 'in the absence of the cause, there is an absence of the effect', with the absence of the causal `si` suffix, the substitution of `sa` for `ma` prescribed by 'massā mussā' is prevented. Therefore, this rule 'ke vā' is commenced to optionally substitute `sa` for `ma`. For the `ma` of `amu`, `sa` is optionally substituted when `ka` follows. Examples: `asuko`, `amuko`; `asukā`, `amukā`; `asukaṃ`, `amukaṃ`, etc.

Kiṃ si.

`kiṃ si`.

198. Kissa ko sabbāsu

198. For `kiṃ`, `ka` in all cases.

Sabbāsu vibhattīsu kissa ko hoti. Sisso, ko, ke. Kaṃ, ke. Kena, kehi kebhi.

In all inflections, `ka` is substituted for the stem `kiṃ`. Examples: `ko`, `ke`. `Kaṃ`, `ke`. `Kena`, `kehi`, `kebhi`.

199. Ki sasmiṃsu vā nitthiyaṃ

199. Optionally `ki` in the `sa` and `smiṃ` cases, not in the feminine.

Anitthiyaṃ kissa ki vā hoti sasmiṃsu. Kissa kassa, kesaṃ kesānaṃ. Kamhā kasmā. Kimhi kismiṃ kamhi kasmiṃ, kesu.

When not in the feminine, the stem `ki` is optionally used in the `sa` (genitive) and `smiṃ` (locative) cases. Examples: `kissa`, `kassa`; `kesaṃ`, `kesānaṃ`. `kamhā`, `kasmā`. `kimhi`, `kismiṃ`, `kamhi`, `kasmiṃ`; `kesu`.

Itthiyaṃ vibhattīsu paresu kādese kate akārantattā majjhe āpaccayakaraṇa+maviruddhanti ā, kā, kāyo. Kaṃ, kā kāyo iccādi sabbāva.

In the feminine, when the substitution `ka` is made before the inflections, since it is an `a`-stem, the application of the suffix `ā` is not inconsistent. Thus: `kā`, `kāyo`. `Kaṃ`; `kā`, `kāyo`, etc., like the declension of `sabbā`.

Napuṃsake –

In the neuter –

200. Ki+maṃsisu saha napuṃsake

200. `kiṃ` with `aṃ` and `si` in the neuter.

Aṃsisu saha tehi kiṃ saddassa kiṃhoti napuṃsake. Kādesassa sāmaññattā “visesavihitā vidhayo sāmaññavidhayo nisedhentī”ti ñāyā kiṃādesena kādesanivutti. Kiṃ, kāni. Kiṃ, ke kāni. Kene+ccādi pubbeva.

In the neuter, in the presence of `aṃ` and `si`, the word `kiṃ` becomes `kiṃ`. Because the `ka` substitution is general, by the maxim 'specific rules prohibit general rules', the `ka` substitution is prevented by the `kiṃ` substitution. `Kiṃ`, `kāni`. `Kiṃ`, `ke`, `kāni`. `Kena`, etc., as before.

Ekasaddo [M 0.0082] saṃkhyā+tulya+ñña+sahāyavacano. Yadā saṃkhyāvacano, tadā ekavacananto, atra ekasaddo saṃkhyeyyavāpī. Aññatra tulyādīsu bahuvacanantopi. Eko, eke. Ekā, ekā ekāyo. Ekaṃ, ekāni+ccādi sabbasamaṃ tiliṅge.

The word `eka` signifies number, similarity, otherness, or solitude. When it signifies number, it is in the singular number; in this sense, the word `eka` also applies to that which is counted. In other meanings, such as 'similar', it can also be in the plural number. `Eko`, `eke`. `Ekā`, `ekā`, `ekāyo`. `Ekaṃ`, `ekāni`, etc., are the same as `sabba` in the three genders.

Tulye eko vilāso dvinnaṃ kumārānaṃ, eke vaṇṇasaddā dvinnaṃ kumārānaṃ. Aññatthe eko ācariyo eva+māha, eke ācariyā eva+māhaṃsu. Asahāyate ekova araññaṃ pavisitvā.

In the sense of similarity: the charm of the two youths is one and the same; the descriptions of the two youths are similar (`eke`). In the sense of otherness: one teacher speaks thus; other (`eke`) teachers spoke thus. In the sense of being without a companion: he entered the forest alone.

Eko, eke. Ekā, ekā ekāyo. Ekaṃ ekāni+ccādi sabbasamaṃ tiliṅge. Ssā+ssaṃsu pana “ssa”mādinā i, ekissā ekāya, ekissaṃ ekāyaṃ ekāya.

`Eko`, `eke`. `Ekā`, `ekā`, `ekāyo`. `Ekaṃ`, `ekāni`, etc., are the same as `sabba` in the three genders. However, in the `ssa` and `ssaṃ` cases, `i` is inserted by the rule beginning 'ssa', etc.: `ekissā`, `ekāya`; `ekissaṃ`, `ekāyaṃ`, `ekāya`.

Idha attaparagāravavasena ekassāpi “amhākaṃ rañño”tipi “eke ācariyā”tipi bahuvacanassa lokena icchitattā bahulavidhānā bahuvacaneneva sijjhati.

Here, even in the case of one, due to respect for oneself or others, as in 'of our king' or 'other teachers', since the plural is desired by people, it is frequently accomplished by the plural alone.

Tumha+amhasaddā aliṅgā, tathā ubha+kati+dvisaddā, pañcādayo aṭṭhārasantā ca. Tumha si, amha si.

The words `tumha` and `amha` are without gender, as are the words `ubha`, `kati`, `dvi`, and those from `pañca` up to `aṭṭhārasa` (eighteen). `Tumha si`, `amha si`.

212. Tumhassa tuvaṃtva+mamhi ca

212. For `tumha`, `tuvaṃ` and `tvaṃ` in the `si` case.

Amhi simhi ca tumhassa savibhattissa tuvaṃ+tvaṃ honti. Tuvaṃ tvaṃ.

When the endings am and si follow, for the inflected stem tumha, the forms tuvaṃ and tvaṃ occur. Tuvaṃ, tvaṃ.

211. Simha+haṃ

211. When si follows, ahaṃ.

Simhi amhassa savibhattissa ahaṃ hoti. Ahaṃ, yevasve+ṭa, tu mhe.

When the ending si follows, for the inflected stem amha, ahaṃ is the substitute. Ahaṃ, yevasveṭa, tumhe.

2,209. Maya+masmā+mhassa

For amha: mayaṃ, asmā.

Yosva+mhassa [M 0.0083] savibhattissa maya+masmā vā honti yathākkamaṃ. Mayaṃ amhe.

When the plural ending yo follows the inflected stem amha, mayaṃ and asmā are optionally the substitutes, respectively. Mayaṃ, amhe.

227. Aṃmhi taṃ+maṃ+tavaṃ+mamaṃ

227. When the ending aṃ follows: taṃ, maṃ, tavaṃ, mamaṃ.

Aṃmhi tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ taṃ+maṃ+tavaṃ+mamaṃ honti yathākkamaṃ. Taṃ, maṃ, tavaṃ, mamaṃ.

When the ending aṃ follows, for the inflected words tumha and amha, the forms taṃ, maṃ, tavaṃ, and mamaṃ occur respectively. Taṃ, maṃ, tavaṃ, mamaṃ.

231. Dutiyā yomhi vā

231. Optionally, when the second case plural ending yo follows.

Tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ paccekaṃ ṅaṃ+ṅākaṃ vā honti yomhi dutiye, tumhaṃ tumhākaṃ tumhe, amhaṃ amhākaṃ amhe.

For the inflected words tumha and amha, the substitutes ṅaṃ and ṅākaṃ optionally occur for each, when the second case plural ending yo follows. Tumhaṃ, tumhākaṃ, tumhe; amhaṃ, amhākaṃ, amhe.

228. Nāsmāsu tayā+mayā

228. When nā and smā follow: tayā, mayā.

Nāsmāsu tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tayā+mayā honti yathākkamaṃ. “Nāsmāsū”ti bahuvacanesupi vibhattikkama+manapekkhitvā saddakkamena paccekaṃ dve dve honti.

When the endings nā and smā follow, for the inflected words tumha and amha, the substitutes are tayā and mayā, respectively. By the rule ‘Nāsmāsu’, even in the plural, disregarding the order of the case endings, two forms occur for each according to the order of the stems.

213. Tayātayīnaṃ tva vā tassa

213. Optionally, tva for the t of tayā and tayī.

Tumhassa tayātayīnaṃ takārassa tva hoti vā. Tvayā tayā, mayā. Tumhehi tumhebhi, amhehi amhebhi.

For the letter t of tumha in the forms tayā and tayī, tva is the optional substitute. Tvayā, tayā; mayā. Tumhehi, tumhebhi; amhehi, amhebhi.

229. Tava+mama+tuyhaṃ+mayhaṃ se

229. When se follows: tava, mama, tuyhaṃ, mayhaṃ.

Se tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ ete ādesā honti yathākkamaṃ. Tava tuyhaṃ, mama mayhaṃ.

When the ending se follows, for the inflected words tumha and amha, these are the substitutes, respectively: tava, tuyhaṃ; mama, mayhaṃ.

211. Naṃsesva+smākaṃ+mamaṃ.

211. When naṃ and se follow: asmākaṃ, mamaṃ.

Naṃsesva+mhassa [M 0.0084] savibhattissa asmākaṃ+mamaṃ honti yathākkamaṃ. Mamaṃ.

When the endings naṃ and se follow, for the inflected stem amha, the substitutes are asmākaṃ and mamaṃ, respectively. Mamaṃ.

230. Ṅaṃ+ṅākaṃ naṃmhi

230. When naṃ follows: ṅaṃ, ṅākaṃ.

Naṃmhi tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savitattīnaṃ ṅaṃ+ṅākaṃ honti paccekaṃ. Tumhaṃ tumhākaṃ amhaṃ amhākaṃ asmākaṃ. Kaccāyane ekavacanassa aṃvidhānatthaṃ sutta+māraddhaṃ, ettha pana attagāravavasena aṃmhi tumhaṃ amhaṃbhi sijjhanti bahulādhikārā.

When the ending naṃ follows, for the inflected words tumha and amha, ṅaṃ and ṅākaṃ are the substitutes for each. Tumhaṃ, tumhākaṃ; amhaṃ, amhākaṃ, asmākaṃ. In Kaccāyana's grammar, a rule was introduced to prescribe aṃ for the singular, but here, due to the principle of expressing self-respect, tumhaṃ and amhaṃ are also accomplished when aṃ follows, because of the governing principle of extensive application.

214. Smāmhi tvamhā

214. When smā follows, tvamhā.

Smāmhi tumhassa savitattissa tvamhā hoti vā. Tvamhā tvayā tayā, mayā.

When the ending smā follows, for the inflected stem tumha, tvamhā is an optional substitute. Tvamhā, tvayā, tayā; mayā.

226. Smimhi tumhamhānaṃ tayi+mayi

226. When smiṃ follows, for tumha and amha: tayi, mayi.

Smimhi tumhaamhasaddānaṃsavibhattīnaṃ tayi+mayi hoti yathākkamaṃ. Tvayi tayi, mayi. Tumhesu.

When the ending smiṃ follows, for the inflected words tumha and amha, the substitutes are tayi and mayi, respectively. Tvayi, tayi; mayi. Tumhesu.

203. Sumhā+mhassā+smā

203. When su follows, for amha, asmā.

Amhassa asmā hoti vā sumhi. Asmāsu amhesu. Sabbādayo vutta+mapekkhantā vakkhamānaṃ vāti ida+mesaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ.

For the stem amha, asmā is an optional substitute when the ending su follows. Asmāsu, amhesu. The pronouns beginning with sabba, which refer to what has been said or what is about to be said—this is their characteristic.

232. Apādādo padate+kavākyeti

232. Not at the beginning of a verse-quarter, in the same sentence.

Adhikāro. Ettha pādo nāma gāthāya catutthaṃso, tasmā “tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappakaṃ”ti ettha vo na hoti. Ettha padanti vutta saddo sabhāvato –

This is a governing rule. Here, a pāda is the name for a fourth part of a verse; therefore, in the line tumhehi puññaṃ pasutaṃ anappakaṃ, the form vo does not occur. Here, a pada (word) is said to be sound by its very nature—

Ākāsavāyuppabhavo [M 0.0085] sarīrā,

Samuccaraṃ vatta+mupeti nādo;

Ṭhānantare suppaṭihaññamāno,

Vaṇṇatta+māgacchati so tu saddoti –

Sound, arising from space and wind within the body, becomes an utterance as it is articulated; being well-obstructed in the various places of articulation, that very sound attains the state of a phoneme.

Vuttattā ekeko vaṇṇo saddo nāma, tabbaṇṇasamūho padaṃ, tappadasamūho vākyañca. Tathā hi –

Because it has been said, each individual phoneme is called sadda (sound), a collection of those phonemes is a pada (word), and a collection of those padas is a vākya (sentence). For thus it is said—

Vitatyantaṃ padaṃ tassa, ca yo vākyanti manvayaṃ;

Upacārā vaṇṇasadda-vāccaṃ taṃ na pariccaje.

Its word (pada) is that which is extended with meaning, and what is called a sentence (vākya) is its syntactical connection (anvaya); though designated metaphorically by phoneme and sound, it does not abandon that essential nature.

Taṃ padañca –

And that word—

Padaṃ catubbidhaṃ vuttaṃ, nāmā+khyāto+pasaggajaṃ;

Nipātajañca taññū hi, asso khalvā+bhidhāvatīti.

The word is said to be fourfold: born of a noun, a verb, a prefix, and a particle; for those who know it say so, as in 'the horse indeed runs'.

Taṃ vākyañca –

And that sentence—

Ekākhyāto padaccayo, siyā vākyaṃ sakārakoti –

A collection of words with one finite verb may be a sentence with its kārakas—

Vuttaṃ. Tasmā “vibhatyantaṃ padaṃ, padasamūho vākya”nti ca vuccati.

It is said. Therefore, it is also said: 'A word ending in an inflection is a pada, and a collection of padas is a vākya.'

233. Yonaṃhisva+pañcamyā vo+no

233. For the plural cases, excluding the fifth, `vo` and `no`.

Apañcamiyāyonaṃhisva+pādādo vattamānānaṃ padasmā paresa+mekavākye ṭhitānaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ vo+no honti vā yathākkamaṃ. Gāmaṃ vo gaccheyyātha, gāmaṃ tumhe gaccheyyātha. Gāmaṃ no gaccheyyāma, gāmaṃ amhe gaccheyyāma. Pahāya vo gamissāmi, mā no vikantiṃsu. Dīyate vo, dīyate tumhaṃ. Dīyate [M 0.0086] no, dīyate amhaṃ. Tuṭṭho+smi vo pakatiyā, tuṭṭho+smi tumhaṃ. Satthā no bhagavā, eso amhākaṃ satthā. Kataṃ vo, kataṃ tumhehi. Kataṃ no, kataṃ amhehi.

For the plural cases, excluding the fifth, of the inflected words `tumha` and `amha` standing in a single sentence, not at the beginning of a pāda, and after another word, `vo` and `no` optionally become the substitutes, respectively. (Examples:) You all should go to the village, you should go to the village. We should go to the village, we should go to the village. Leaving you, I will go; may they not sell us. It is given to you, it is given to you. It is given to us, it is given to us. I am pleased with you by nature, I am pleased with you. The Blessed One is our teacher, this is our teacher. It is done by you, it is done by you. It is done by us, it is done by us.

234. Te+me nāse

234. In the singular cases, `te` and `me`.

Nāmhi se ca apādādo vattamānānaṃ dasmā paresa+mekavākye ṭhitānaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ te+me vā honti yathākkamaṃ. Kataṃ te, kataṃ tayā. Kataṃ me, kataṃ mayā. Dīyate te, dīyate tava. Dīyate me, dīyate mama. Dhanaṃ te, dhanaṃ tava. Dhanaṃ me, dhanaṃ mama.

In the instrumental, locative, and dative/genitive singular, when the inflected forms of 'tumha' and 'amha' are present in a single sentence, not at the beginning of a pāda, and after other words, 'te' and 'me' optionally occur in order. (Examples:) Done by you, done by you. Done by me, done by me. Given to you, given to you. Given to me, given to me. Wealth is yours, wealth is yours. Wealth is mine, wealth is mine.

237. Na ca+vā+hā+he+vayoge

237. Not when conjoined with `ca`, `vā`, `hā`, `he`, and `va`.

Cādīhi yoge tumhaamhasaddānaṃ vo+no, te+me na honti. Gacchāma tumhe ca mayañca, passati tumhe ca amhe ca, kataṃ tumhehi ca amhehi ca, dīyate tumhañca amhañca, dhanaṃ tumhañca amhañca, kataṃ tayā ca mayā ca, dīyate tava ca mama ca, dhanaṃ tava ca mama ca. Evaṃ vādiyogepi.

When conjoined with `ca` and so on, the substitutions `vo`, `no`, `te`, and `me` do not occur for the words `tumha` and `amha`. (Examples:) We go, both you and I. He sees both you and us. It is done by both you and us. It is given to both you and us. Wealth is for both you and us. It is done by both you and me. It is given to both you and me. Wealth is for both you and me. Likewise, also when conjoined with `vā` and so on.

235. Anvādese

235. In the case of subsequent mention.

Kathitānukathitavisaye tumhaamhasaddānaṃ ādesā niccaṃ honti punabbidhānā. Gāmo tumhaṃ pariggaho, atho janapado vo pariggaho. Anvādese atho athoti vāradvayābhāvā niccanti vuttaṃ. Athosaddo kathitasseva puna kathanato anvādesajotako.

In the context of what has been said and subsequently said, the substitutions for the words `tumha` and `amha` are always obligatory due to re-statement. (Example:) The village is your possession; then the district is your possession. In the case of subsequent mention, it is said to be obligatory because of the absence of two instances of `atho`. The word `atho` indicates subsequent mention because it is a re-statement of what has already been said.

236. Sapubbā paṭhamantā vā

236. With a preceding word, or after a nominative, optionally.

Vijjamānapubbasmā [M 0.0087] paṭhamantā paresaṃ tumhāmhānaṃ ādesā vā honti anvādese. Gāme paṭo tumhākaṃ atho nagare kambalo vo atho nagare kambalo tumhākaṃ, athoti anukathanavāradvayattā vikappo sapubbāti kiṃ, paṭo tumhākaṃ, atho kambalo vo. Paṭhamantāti kiṃ, paṭo nagare tumhākaṃ, atho kambalo gāme vo.

In the case of subsequent mention, the substitutions for `tumha` and `amha` optionally occur when they follow a preceding word, or when they follow a word in the nominative case. (Example:) 'In the village, the cloth is yours; and in the city, the blanket is yours; or in the city, the blanket is yours.' Because of the two instances of the word `atho` indicating repetition, there is an option. What is meant by 'with a preceding word'? (Example:) 'The cloth is yours, and the blanket is yours.' What is meant by 'after a nominative'? (Example:) 'The cloth in the city is yours, and the blanket in the village is yours.'

238. Dassanatthe+nālocane

238. In the sense of seeing, but not of addressing.

Dassanatthe ālovacanavajjite payujjamāne tumhaamhāna+mādesā na honti. Gāmo tumhe uddissa āgato, gāmo amhe uddissa āgato. Anālocaneti kiṃ, gāmo vo āloceti, gāmo no āloceti.

When a word is used in the sense of seeing, but not of addressing, the substitutions for `tumha` and `amha` do not occur. (Examples:) The villager has come on your account; the villager has come on our account. What is meant by 'not of addressing'? (This is to allow the substitution in cases like:) The villager addresses you; the villager addresses us.

239. Āmantaṇaṃ pubba+masantaṃva

239. A preceding vocative is as if non-existent.

Āmantaṇaṃ pubba+vijjamānaṃ viya hoti tumhāmhāna+mādesavisaye. Devadatta tava pariggaho. Āmantaṇanti kiṃ, kambalo te pariggaho.

In the context of the substitutions for `tumha` and `amha`, a preceding vocative is treated as if it were non-existent. (Example:) 'Devadatta, your possession.' Why specify 'vocative'? (To contrast with:) 'The blanket is your possession.'

240. Na sāmaññavacana+mekatthe

240. Not a general term with the same referent.

Samānādhikaraṇe parato sāmaññavacana+māmantaṇaṃ ekatthe asantaṃ viya na hoti māṇavaka jaṭilaka te pariggaho. Parāmanthaṇe asatipi pubba+mupādāya ādeso.

A general term which is a vocative, following in apposition with the same referent, is not treated as if non-existent. (Example:) 'Young man, ascetic, your possession.' Even if there is no subsequent mention, the substitution occurs on account of the preceding word.

241. Bahūsu vā

241. Optionally in the plural.

Bahūsu [M 0.0088] vattamāna+māmantaṇaṃ sāmaññavacana+mekatthe asantaṃ viya vā na hoti. “Siddhe satyārambho nīyamāya vā vikappāyavā”ti vuttattā vikappattha+midaṃ. Brāhmaṇā guṇavanto tumhākaṃ pariggaho, brāhmaṇā guṇavanto vo pariggaho.

A general term which is a vocative, referring to many and with the same referent, is optionally not treated as if non-existent. Because it is said, 'When something is established, the commencement of a rule is for the sake of restriction or for option,' this is for the purpose of an option. (Examples:) 'Virtuous brahmins, your possession,' 'Virtuous brahmins, your possession.'

Ubha+katisaddā bahuvacanantā. “Ubha+gohi ṭo”ti yonaṃ ṭo, ubho. Kathaṃ “ubhayo vasemase”ti, ṭomhi yakārāgamo. Ubho.

The words `ubha` and `kati` are always plural. By the rule 'Ubhago hi ṭo', `ṭo` is substituted for `yo` (nominative/accusative plural), resulting in `ubho`. How then is `ubhayo vasemase` ('may we both dwell') formed? In this case, `y` is an augment to `ṭo`. The standard form is `ubho`.

59. Suhisu+bhasso

59. Before `su` and `hi`, the stem becomes `ubho`.

Ubhassa suhisvo hoti. Ubhohi ubhobhi.

For `ubha`, the stem becomes `ubho` before the `hi` ending. The forms are `ubhohi`, `ubhobhi`.

50. Ubhi+nnaṃ

50. The substitution `innaṃ` for `ubha`.

Ubhā naṃvacanassa innaṃ hoti. Ubhinnaṃ, ubhosu.

For `ubha`, `innaṃ` is the substitute for the `naṃ` ending. The forms are `ubhinnaṃ` and `ubhosu`.

168. Ṭi katimhā

168. After `kati`, `ṭi`.

Katimhā yonaṃ ṭi hoti. Kati, kati. Jhato yolopapasaṅge dīghanivattanatthaṃ ṭiādeso. Katīhi katībhi. “Bahukatinnaṃ”ti nuka, katinnaṃ, katīsu.

After `kati`, `ṭi` is substituted for the `yo` ending. The forms are `kati`, `kati`. The substitution of `ṭi` is for the sake of preventing lengthening when the elision of `yo` after a `jha` class consonant would apply. The forms are `katīhi`, `katībhi`. By the rule 'Bahukatinnaṃ', there is a `nu` augment, giving `katinnaṃ`. The locative is `katīsu`.

1,54. Vicchā+bhikkhaññesu dve

1.54. In distribution and repetition, two.

Vicchāya+mābhikkhaññe ca dve rūpāni honti. Kriyā+guṇa+dabbehi byāpetu+micchā vicchā. Rukkhaṃ rukkhaṃ siñcanti, gāmo gāmo ramaṇīyo, gāme gāme pānīyaṃ. Ābhikkhaññaṃ=ponopuññaṃ, pacati pacati, papacati papacati.

In distribution and repetition, two forms occur. Distribution is the desire to pervade through action, quality, and substance. For example: 'They water tree after tree,' 'Village after village is delightful,' 'In every village there is drinking water.' Repetition is frequency. For example: 'He cooks and cooks,' 'He thoroughly cooks and cooks.'

1,55. Syādilopo pubbasse+kassa

1.55. Elision of the `syādi` case ending of the preceding one.

Vicchāya+mekassa [M 0.0089] dvitte pubbassa syādilopo hoti. Ekassa ekassāti dvitte ekekassa. Kathaṃ “matthakamatthakenā”ti, “syādilopo pubbassā”ti yogavibhāgā, yogavibhāgā ca iṭṭhapasiddhīti.

In distribution, when a single word is duplicated, the `syādi` case ending of the preceding word is elided. When `ekassa` is duplicated, `ekassa ekassa` becomes `ekekassa`. How is `matthakamatthakena` formed? By the division of the rule, 'elision of the `syādi` case ending of the preceding word.' And by the division of a rule, the desired form is accomplished.

1,56. Sabbādīnaṃ vītihāre

1.56. For `sabbādi` words, in reciprocal action.

Sabbādīnaṃ vītihāre dve bhavanti. Pubbassa syādilopo ca, aññassa aññassa bhojakā aññamaññassa bhojakā, evaṃ itarītarassa.

For `sabbādi` words, in reciprocal action, they are duplicated. And the `syādi` case ending of the preceding word is elided. For example: `aññassa aññassa bhojakā` (eaters of one another) becomes `aññamaññassa bhojakā`. Similarly, `itarītarassa`.

1,57. Yāvabodhaṃ sambhame

1.57. Until understood, in agitation.

Turitenā+pāyahetupadassanaṃ sambhamo, tasmiṃ sati vattu yāvantehi saddehi so+ttho viññāyate, tāvanto payujjante. Sappo sappo sappo, bujjhassu bujjhassu bujjhassu, bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho, bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho.

Agitation is the quick showing of a cause of danger. When that is present, as many words as are needed for that meaning to be understood are employed. For example: 'A snake! A snake! A snake!' 'Understand! Understand! Understand!' 'The Saṅgha is split! The Saṅgha is split!'

Bhaye kodhe pasaṃsāyaṃ, turite kotūhala+cchare;

Hāse soke pasāde ca, kare āmeḍitaṃ budho.

In fear, in anger, in praise, in haste, in curiosity and wonder; in laughter, in sorrow, and in joy, the wise one makes a repetition.

Saṅkhyākaṇḍa

The Section on Numerals

Atha saṅkhyāsaddā vuccante. Ekādayo aṭṭhārasantā saṅkhyeyyavacanā. Vīsatiādayo “bhikkhūnaṃ vīsatī”tiādīsu saṅkhyāvacanā, “vīsati bhikkhavo”tiādīsu saṅkhyeyyavacanā. Ekasaddo sabbādīsu vuttova. Dvādayo aṭṭhārasantā bahuvacananthāva.

Now, numeral words are stated. Words from `eka` (one) up to `aṭṭhārasa` (eighteen) are terms denoting the enumerated. Words from `vīsati` (twenty) onwards, as in `bhikkhūnaṃ vīsati` (twenty of the monks), are numeral words; and in phrases like `vīsati bhikkhavo` (twenty monks), they are terms denoting the enumerated. The word `eka` has already been mentioned among the `sabbādi` words. Words from `dvi` (two) up to `aṭṭhārasa` (eighteen) are always in the plural.

219. Yomhi dvinnaṃ duve+dve

219. For `dvi`, in the `yo` case ending, `duve` and `dve`.

Yomhi [M 0.0090] dvissa savibhattissa duve+dve honti paccekaṃ. Duve dve, duve dve, dvīhi dvībhi.

In the `yo` case ending, for `dvi` with its case ending, `duve` and `dve` occur individually. `Duve`, `dve`; `duve`, `dve`; `dvīhi`, `dvībhi`.

220. Duvinnaṃ naṃmhi vā

220. For `dvi`, in the `naṃ` case ending, optionally `duvinnaṃ`.

Naṃmhi dvissa savibhattissa duvinnaṃ hoti vā. Duvinnaṃ, aññatra –

For `dvi` with its case ending, in the `naṃ` case, `duvinnaṃ` optionally occurs. `Duvinnaṃ`; elsewhere –

47. Naṃmhi nuka dvādīnaṃ sattarasannaṃ

47. In the `naṃ` case ending, the augment `nuka` for the numbers from `dvi` up to `sattarasa`.

Dvādīnaṃ sattarasannaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ nuka hoti naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Ukāro uccāraṇattho, kakāro antāvayavattho. Ettha nāgamo vibhattissa ādyāvayavo ce, “āgamā tagguṇībhūtā taggahaṇena gayhante”ti ñāyā nāgamopi taṃgahaṇena gayhatīti “sunaṃhisū”ti dīghappasaṅge pakatiyā antāvayavabhūte sarantatā natthīti na dīgho. Dvinnaṃ, dvīsu.

For the numbers from `dvi` (two) up to `sattarasa` (seventeen), `nuka` is the augment in the `naṃ` case ending. The `u` is for pronunciation, and the `k` indicates the final component. Here, if the augment were the initial component of the case ending, then by the principle that 'augments, having become absorbed into that to which they are attached, are taken by the apprehension of that,' even the augment would be taken by its apprehension. Thus, in the context of the possibility of lengthening by the rule `sunaṃhisū`, since there is no vowel as the final component of the stem, there is no lengthening. `Dvinnaṃ`, `dvīsu`.

207. Pume tayo+cattāro

207. In the masculine, `tayo` and `cattāro`.

Yomhi savibhattīnaṃ ti+catunnaṃ tayo+cattāro honti yathākkamaṃ pulliṅge. Tayo, tayo, tīhi tībhi.

For `ti` and `catu` with their case endings, in the `yo` case, `tayo` and `cattāro` occur respectively in the masculine gender. `Tayo`, `tayo`, `tīhi`, `tībhi`.

49. Ṇṇaṃ+ṇṇannaṃ tito jhā

49. After `ti`, for the `jha`-designated ending, `ṇṇaṃ` and `ṇṇannaṃ`.

Jhasaññito tito naṃvacanassa ṇṇaṃ+ṇṇannaṃ honti. Tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ, tīsu.

After `ti`, for the `naṃ` case ending which is designated `jha`, `ṇṇaṃ` and `ṇṇannaṃ` occur. `Tiṇṇaṃ`, `tiṇṇannaṃ`, `tīsu`.

Itthiyaṃ –

In the feminine –

205. Tisso catasso yomhi savibhattīnaṃ

205. For `ti` and `catu` with their case endings, in the `yo` case, `tisso` and `catasso`.

Vibhattisahitānaṃ ticatunnaṃ yomhi tisso+catasso honti itthiyaṃ yathākkamaṃ. Tisso, tisso, tīhi tībhi.

For `ti` and `catu` with their case endings, in the `yo` case, `tisso` and `catasso` occur respectively in the feminine. `Tisso`, `tisso`, `tīhi`, `tībhi`.

204. Naṃmhi ticatunna+mitthiyaṃ tissa+catassā

204. In the `naṃ` case ending, for `ti` and `catu` in the feminine, `tissa` and `catassā`.

Naṃmhi [M 0.0091] ticatunnaṃ tissa+catassā honti+tthiyaṃ yathākkamaṃ. Naṃmhīti catutthīchaṭṭhīnaṃ sāmaññavacanaṃ, no ce naṃsūti vadati, yathākkamaṃti saddadvayāpekkhaṃ. Eva+mīdisa+maññampi. Tissannaṃ tīsu.

In the `naṃ` case ending, for `ti` and `catu`, `tissa` and `catassā` occur respectively in the feminine. 'Naṃmhi' is a general term for the fourth and sixth cases; if it were not, it would say 'naṃsu'. 'Respectively' refers to the two words. And similarly for other such instances. `Tissannaṃ`, `tīsu`.

206. Tīṇi+cattāri napuṃsake

206. In the neuter, `tīṇi` and `cattāri`.

Yomhi savibhattīnaṃ ticatunnaṃ yathākkamaṃ tīṇi+cattāri honti napuṃsake. Tīṇi, tīṇi, tīhi iccādi pulliṅgeva.

For `ti` and `catu` with their case endings, in the `yo` case, `tīṇi` and `cattāri` occur respectively in the neuter gender. `Tīṇi`, `tīṇi`; `tīhi`, etc., are like the masculine.

Catu yo,

For `catu`, `yo`,

208. Caturo vā catussa

208. `caturo` optionally for `catu`.

Catussa savibhattissa yomhi caturo hoti vā pulliṅge. Caturo cattāro. Kathaṃ “caturo nimitte nāddasāsi”nti, liṅgavipallāsena siddhaṃ, cattāri nimittānīti attho. Vipallāso tividho liṅgavipallāso vacanavipallāso vibhattivipallāsoti. Catūhi catūbhi. Catunnaṃ, catūsu.

For the declined form of 'catu' (four), in the masculine gender, 'caturo' is an optional form for the 'yo' case ending. The forms are 'caturo' and 'cattāro'. How is it in the phrase, 'you did not see the four signs'? This is established by a gender inversion; the meaning is 'the four signs' (cattāri nimittāni). Inversion is threefold: gender inversion, number inversion, and case inversion. By/with four: 'catūhi', 'catūbhi'. Of four: 'catunnaṃ'. In four: 'catūsu'.

Itthiyaṃ catasso. Catasso. Catūhi catūbhi. Catassannaṃ. Catassannaṃ. Catūsu.

In the feminine: 'catasso'. 'Catasso'. By/with four: 'catūhi', 'catūbhi'. Of four: 'catassannaṃ'. Of four: 'catassannaṃ'. In four: 'catūsu'.

Napuṃsake cattāri. Cattāri. Catūhi catūbhi. Iccādi pumeva.

In the neuter: 'cattāri'. 'Cattāri'. By/with four: 'catūhi', 'catūbhi'. The rest is as in the masculine.

169. Ṭa pañcādīhi cuddasahi

169. The suffix 'ṭa' is applied after the numerals from five up to fourteen.

“Sutte liṅgavacanamatta”nti ñāyā ṭa-iti vuttaṃ. Pañcādīhi cuddasahi saṅkhyāhi yonaṃ ṭa hoti. Pañca. Pañca. Yonaṃ ṭā+ṭenivatthanatthaṃ ṭa-vidhānaṃ.

According to the maxim, 'In a grammatical rule, gender and number are merely indicative,' thus 'ṭa' is stated. After the numerals from five to fourteen, 'ṭa' replaces the 'yo' suffix. For example: 'pañca', 'pañca'. The prescription of 'ṭa' is for the purpose of preventing the application of 'ṭā' and 'ṭena' in place of the 'yo' suffix.

90. Pañcādīnaṃ cuddasanna+ma

90. Of the numerals from five to fourteen, there is shortening.

Pañcādīnaṃ [M 0.0092] cuddasannaṃ sunaṃhisva hoti. Etta+dīghāpavādo+yaṃ. Apavādati bādhetīti apavādo. Tasmā “pakapyāpavādavisayamussaggā abhinivisante”ti ñāyā “suhisva+sse” “sunaṃhisu”ti ca ussaggā “pañcādīnaṃ cuddasanna+ma” iti apavādavisayaṃ na pavisanti, sāmaññattā. Eva+muparipi “pañcamiyaṃ parassa” “ādissā”ti. Pañcahi pañcabhi pañcannaṃ. Pañcannaṃ. Pañcasu. Evaṃ chādayo aṭṭhārasantā.

For the numerals from five to fourteen, the vowels in the suffixes 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi' are shortened. This is an exception to lengthening. An exception (apavāda) is that which supersedes. Therefore, according to the maxim, 'General rules do not enter the domain of an exception,' the general rules 'suhisva+sse' and 'sunaṃhisu' do not apply to the domain of the exception 'pañcādīnaṃ cuddasannaṃ a', due to their generality. The same principle applies above to rules such as 'pañcamiyaṃ parassa' and 'ādissā'. By/with five: 'pañcahi', 'pañcabhi'. Of five: 'pañcannaṃ'. Of five: 'pañcannaṃ'. In five: 'pañcasu'. Thus it is for the numerals from six up to eighteen.

“Catthe”ti eko ca dasa cāti cattasamāse “amādī”ti ekena adhikā dasāti tatiyāsamāse vā kate “ekatthatāya”nti vibhattilopo. Eva+mupari ca.

In the sense of 'ca' (and), when a dvanda compound 'eko ca dasa ca' (one and ten) is formed, or when an instrumental compound (tatiyāsamāsa) 'ekena adhikā dasa' (ten exceeded by one) is formed, the case ending is elided for the sake of a unified meaning, according to the rule 'amādī'. And so it is for the subsequent numerals.

3,102. Ekaṭṭhāna+mā

3,102. For 'eka' and 'aṭṭha', the final vowel becomes 'ā'.

Ekaaṭṭhānaṃ ā hoti dase pare.

The final vowel of 'eka' and 'aṭṭha' becomes 'ā' when 'dasa' (ten) follows.

3,103. Ra saṃkhyāto vā

3,103. After a numeral, 'ra' is an optional substitute.

Saṃkhyāto parassa dasassa ra hoti vibhāsā. Sa ca “pañcamiyaṃ parassā”ti vattamāne “ādissā”ti dakārasseva hoti. Ekārasa ekādasa. Ekārasahi ekādasahi. Ekārasannaṃ ekādasannaṃ. Ekārasasu ekādasasu. Eva+mekādasaiccādipi.

After a numeral, 'ra' is an optional substitute for the 'da' of a following 'dasa'. And this substitution, according to the rule 'ādissā' (of the beginning), applies only to the initial 'da' sound. For example: 'ekārasa', 'ekādasa'. By/with eleven: 'ekārasahi', 'ekādasahi'. Of eleven: 'ekārasannaṃ', 'ekādasannaṃ'. In eleven: 'ekārasasu', 'ekādasasu'. Thus also for 'dvādasa' and so on.

3,94. Ā saṃkhyāyā satādo nāññatthe

3,94. For a numeral, 'ā' is the substitute, but not before 'sata' etc., nor in another sense.

Saṃkhyāya+muttarapade [M 0.0093] dvissā hoti asatādo nāññatthe.

When a numeral is the latter part of a compound, 'ā' replaces 'dvi', but not before 'sata' etc., nor in another sense.

Āviṭṭhaliṅgattā saṃkhyāyaṃ uttarapade saliṅgeneva visesanaṃ bhavati.

Due to having an inherent gender, a numeral in the latter part of a compound becomes an adjective agreeing in its own gender.

Suddhaṃ missañca saṃkiṇṇaṃ, upasajjanameva ca;

Āviṭṭha+matha vā+byattaṃ, chadhā liṅgaṃ vivaṃyate.

Pure, mixed, and combined; also secondary; inherent, or invariable; gender is thus distinguished in six ways.

Ettha yathākkamaṃ rukkho latā paṇṇaṃti suddhaṃ. Ghaṭo ghaṭī, vajiro vajiraṃ, vedanā vedanaṃti missaṃ. Taṭo taṭī taṭaṃti saṃkiṇṇaṃ. Sukko paṭo, sukkā paṭi, sukkaṃ vatthaṃti upasajjanaṃ. Rājā saraṇaṃ, guṇo pamāṇaṃti āviṭṭhaṃ. Tuvaṃ ahaṃ kati pañcāti abyattaṃ. Iti liṅgaṃ veditabbaṃ. Dvādasa.

Here, in order: 'rukkho' (tree), 'latā' (creeper), 'paṇṇaṃ' (leaf)—these are pure. 'Ghaṭo', 'ghaṭī' (pot); 'vajiro', 'vajiraṃ' (thunderbolt); 'vedanā', 'vedanaṃ' (feeling)—these are mixed. 'Taṭo', 'taṭī', 'taṭaṃ' (bank)—these are combined. 'Sukko paṭo' (white cloth, masc.), 'sukkā paṭī' (white cloth, fem.), 'sukkaṃ vatthaṃ' (white garment, neut.)—these are secondary. 'Rājā saraṇaṃ' (a king is a refuge), 'guṇo pamāṇaṃ' (virtue is the measure)—these are inherent. 'Tuvaṃ' (you), 'ahaṃ' (I), 'kati' (how many), 'pañca' (five)—these are invariable. Thus, gender should be understood. 'Dvādasa' (twelve).

3,98. Bā cattālīsā do

3,98. 'Bā' is a substitute for 'dvi'; 'do' is a substitute before 'cattālīsā'.

Dvissa bā vā hoti cattālīsā do nāññatthe. Rāde se bārasa.

For 'dvi', 'bā' is an optional substitute. Before 'cattālīsā', 'do' is the substitute for 'dvi', and not in other contexts. In the Rāṭha dialect, the form is 'bārasa'.

3,95. Tisse

3,95. For 'ti', 'e' is the substitute.

Saṃkhyāya+muttarapade tissa e hota+satādo nā+ññatthe.

When a numeral is the latter part of a compound, 'e' replaces 'ti', but not before 'sata' etc., nor in another sense.

3,104. Chatīhi ḷo ca

3,104. After 'cha' and 'ti', 'ḷo' is also a substitute.

Chatīhi parassa dasassa ḷo hoti ro ca. Teḷasa terasa.

After 'cha' and 'ti', for a following 'dasa', 'ḷo' and also 'ro' are substitutes. For example: 'teḷasa', 'terasa'.

3,100. Catussa cuco dase

3,100. For 'catu', 'cu' and 'co' are substituted before 'dasa'.

Catussa cu+co honti vā dase pare. Dvitte cuddasa coddasa catuddasa.

For 'catu', 'cu' and 'co' are optional substitutes when 'dasa' follows. The forms are 'cuddasa', 'coddasa', and 'catuddasa'.

3,99. Vīsatidasesu pañcassa paṇṇa+pannā

3,99. Before 'vīsati' and 'dasa', 'paṇṇa' and 'pannā' are substituted for 'pañca'.

Vīsati [M 0.0094] sesu paresu pañcassa paṇṇa+pannā honti yathākkamaṃ. Pannarasa pañcadasa.

When 'vīsati' and 'dasa' follow, 'paṇṇa' and 'pannā' are substituted for 'pañca', respectively. For example: 'pannarasa', 'pañcadasa'.

3,101. Chassa so

3,101. For 'cha', 'so' is the substitute.

Chassa so-icca+ya+mādeso hoti se pare. Soḷasa sorasa. Sattarasa sattadasa. “Ekaṭṭhāna+mā”ti ā, aṭṭhārasa aṭṭhādasa.

For 'cha', this substitute 'so' occurs when 'dasa' follows. For example: 'soḷasa', 'sorasa'. 'Sattarasa', 'sattadasa'. According to the rule 'Ekaṭṭhānam ā', the final vowel becomes 'ā', giving 'aṭṭhārasa', 'aṭṭhādasa'.

Ūnā ca sā vīsati cāti “visesana+mekatthene”ti visesanasamāse “itthiyaṃ bhāsitapumi+tthī pume+vekatthe”ti pumatte ca kate ekena ūnā vīsatīti tatiyāsamāse ekūnavīsati.

When 'ūnā ca sā vīsati ca' (deficient, and that twenty) is formed as a descriptive compound (visesanasamāsa) by the rule 'visesanam ekatthena', and when it is rendered masculine by the rule 'itthiyaṃ bhāsitapumitthī pumevekatthe', the result is 'ekūnavīsati'. This is also analyzed as an instrumental compound (tatiyāsamāsa) from 'ekena ūnā vīsati' (twenty deficient by one).

Vīsatiādayo ānavutiyā itthiliṅge+kavacanā. Bho ekūnavīsati. Ekūnavīsatiṃ. Ekūnavīsatyā ekūnavīsatiyā. Ekūnavīsatyaṃ ekūnavīsatiyaṃ ekūnavīsatyā ekūnavīsatiyā. Matisamaṃ.

The numbers from twenty up to ninety are feminine singular. O nineteen. Nineteen (accusative). By/with/from/of nineteen (instrumental, ablative, and genitive). In/on nineteen (locative). It is like mati.

Evaṃ vīsati, ekavīsati, dvāvīsati bāvīsati, tevīsati catuvīsatippabhutayo. Paṇṇaādese paṇṇavīsati pañcavīsati. Evaṃ chabbīsati, sattavīsati, aṭṭhavīsati.

Thus, twenty, twenty-one, twenty-two (dvāvīsati or bāvīsati), twenty-three, twenty-four, and so on. With the substitution of paṇṇa, [the forms are] paṇṇavīsati [and] pañcavīsati. Thus, twenty-six, twenty-seven, twenty-eight.

Ekena ūnā tiṃsati tiṃsā vāti ekūnatiṃsati ekūnatiṃsā vā. Karaṇe ekūnatiṃsāya. Ekūnatiṃsāya, ekūnatiṃsāya, ekūnatiṃsāya, ekūnatiṃsāyaṃ. Evaṃ tiṃsatiṇiṃsāvabhutayo[M 0.0095]. Tiṃsāsaddassa pana silope “dīghasso”ti yogavibhāgā rasso, tiṃsa. Niggahītāgamo, tiṃsaṃ. Bhotiṃse+ccādi pumeva.

Thirty less one is ekūnatiṃsati or ekūnatiṃsā. In the instrumental case: ekūnatiṃsāya. The forms are: ekūnatiṃsāya (instrumental, ablative, genitive), ekūnatiṃsāyaṃ (locative). Thus also for thirty (tiṃsati/tiṃsā) and so on. However, for the word tiṃsā, when the si suffix is elided, the vowel is shortened to tiṃsa by a splitting of the rule 'dīgho rasso'. With the augment of a niggahīta, it becomes tiṃsaṃ. The forms bho tiṃsa, etc., are like the masculine.

Cattālīsādīsupi yathāsambhavaṃ evameva. Dvitte ekattiṃsati ekattiṃsā. Rassadvitte dvattiṃsati dvattiṃsa. Evaṃ tettiṃsati tettiṃsādayo yāva ekūnacattālīsati ekūnacattālīsā. Cattālīsāya simhi cattārīsā cattālīsā cattālīsaṃ, bho cattālīse+ccādi hoti. Evaṃ ekacattārīsā.

For the forties and so on, it is likewise as far as possible. For thirty-one: ekattiṃsati, ekattiṃsā. For thirty-two, with shortening: dvattiṃsati, dvattiṃsa. Thus, tettiṃsati, tettiṃsā and so on, up to ekūnacattālīsati, ekūnacattālīsā. For cattālīsā (forty), with the si suffix, the forms cattārīsā, cattālīsā, cattālīsaṃ, and bho cattālīse, etc., occur. Thus also ekacattārīsā.

3,97. Dvīssā ca

3.97. And for dvi, ā.

Asatādo nāññatthe cattālīsādo dvissa e vā hoti ā ca. Dvecattālīsā dvecattālīsa dvecattālīsaṃ, evaṃ dvācattālīsa-iccādi. Dvecattārīsā dvecattārīsa dvecattārīsaṃ, evaṃ dvācattārīsā dvācattārīsa iccādi. Cattālīsati ekacattālīsati dvecattālīsati dvācattālīsati iccādi ekūnavīsatisamaṃ.

From forty onwards, and not elsewhere, for dvi, there is optionally e, and also ā.
