78. The suffix 'mantu' is used in the sense of 'that is here for him'.

Paṭhamantā ettha assa atthīti etesva+tthesu mantu hoti. Gāvo ettha dese assa vā purisassa santīti gomā, gomanto iccādi guṇavantusamaṃ.

From words ending in the first case, the suffix 'mantu' occurs in the senses of 'is here' or 'exists for him.' Thus, from 'cows exist in this region for him or for a person,' the forms 'gomā,' 'gomanto,' etc., are derived, similar to 'guṇavantu'.

Atthīti vattamānakālopādānato bhūtāhi bhavissantīhi vā gohi na gomā. Kathaṃ gomā āsi, gomā bhavissatīti. Tadāpi vattamānāhiyeva gohi gomā, āsi bhavissatīti padantarā kālantaraṃ. Itisaddato visayaniyamo. Vuttañhi –

Because 'atthi' (exists) refers to the present tense, one is not 'gomā' (possessing cows) by means of past or future cows. How then can one say, 'he was gomā' or 'he will be gomā'? Even then, one is 'gomā' only by means of presently existing cows; 'was' and 'will be' are other words indicating another time. From the word 'iti,' there is a restriction of the scope. For it is said:

Pahūte ca pasaṃsāyaṃ, nindāyañcā+tisāyane;

Niccayoge ca saṃsagge, honti+me mantuādayoti.

In the senses of abundance and praise, blame and excess, constant connection and association, these suffixes beginning with 'mantu' occur.

134. Āyussā+yasa mantumhi

134. For 'āyu,' there is the substitution 'āyasa' when the suffix 'mantu' follows.

Mantumhi āyussa āyasādeso hoti. Āyu assa atthīti āyasmā. Go assoti jātisaddānaṃ dabbābhidhāna- sāmatthiyā [M 0.0201] mantvādayo na honti, tathā guṇasaddānaṃ seto paṭoti. Yesaṃ tu guṇasaddānaṃ dabbābhidhānasāmatthiyaṃ natthi, tehi honteva, buddhi assa atthīti buddhimā. “Vantva+vaṇṇā”ti vantumhi rūpavā rasavā gandhavā saddavā. “Daṇḍāditvi+kaī vā”ti ika+ī, rasī rasiko, rūpī rūpiko, gandhī gandhikoti.

When the suffix 'mantu' follows, 'āyu' is substituted with 'āyasa.' From 'he has life' ('āyu assa atthi'), we get 'āyasmā.' Suffixes beginning with 'mantu' do not follow words denoting species, such as 'go' (cow) and 'assa' (horse), because of their capacity to denote a substance; likewise for quality words, as in 'seto paṭo' (white cloth). However, they do occur after those quality words that do not have the capacity to denote a substance; for example, from 'he has intelligence' ('buddhi assa atthi'), we get 'buddhimā.' By the rule 'Vantva+vaṇṇā,' with the suffix 'vantu,' we have 'rūpavā' (having form), 'rasavā' (having taste), 'gandhavā' (having smell), and 'saddavā' (having sound). By the rule 'Daṇḍāditvi+kaī vā,' the suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' are added, for example: 'rasī,' 'rasiko'; 'rūpī,' 'rūpiko'; 'gandhī,' 'gandhiko'.

79. Vantva+vaṇṇāti

79. The suffix 'vantu' is used after words not ending in 'a'.

Vantu. Pasatthaṃ sīla+massa atthīti sīlavā. Pahutā pasatthā vā paññā assa atthīti paññavā.

The suffix 'vantu.' From 'he has esteemed virtue' ('pasatthaṃ sīlaṃ assa atthi'), we get 'sīlavā.' From 'he has abundant or esteemed wisdom' ('pahutā pasatthā vā paññā assa atthi'), we get 'paññavā'.

80. Daṇḍāditvi+ka+ī vāti

80. From 'daṇḍa' and so forth, the suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' are used optionally.

Ika+ī honti vā mantatthe. Bahulaṃvidhānā kutocisaddato dve honti, kuto ce+kamekaṃva. Niccayutto daṇḍo assa atthīti daṇḍiko daṇḍī. Gandhiko gandhī. Vātveva, daṇḍavā.

The suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' occur optionally in the sense of possession ('mantatthe'). By the principle of diverse application, from some words two forms occur, while from others only one. From 'he has a stick that is always with him' ('niccayutto daṇḍo assa atthi'), we get 'daṇḍiko' or 'daṇḍī.' Similarly, 'gandhiko' and 'gandhī.' Because of the option ('vā'), 'daṇḍavā' is also a valid form.

“Uttamiṇeva dhanā iko”ti gaṇasuttena iko dhaniko. Añño dhanī dhanavā.

By the gaṇasutta 'Uttamiṇeva dhanā iko,' the suffix 'ika' is added to 'dhana' to form 'dhaniko' (a creditor). Other forms are 'dhanī' and 'dhanavā'.

“Asannihite atthā” asannihito attho assa atthīti atthiko atthī. Sannihite atthavā. “Tadantā ca” puññattho assa atthīti puññatthiko puññatthī.

By the rule 'Asannihite atthā,' from 'he has a need' ('attho assa atthi') where that need is not at hand, we get 'atthiko' or 'atthī.' When the object is at hand, the form is 'atthavā.' And by the rule 'Tadantā ca' (and from words ending in 'attha'), from 'he has a need for merit' ('puññattho assa atthi'), we get 'puññatthiko' or 'puññatthī'.

“Vaṇṇantā īyeva”. Brahmavaṇṇaṃ assa atthīti brahmavaṇṇī, devavaṇṇī.

By the rule 'Vaṇṇantā īyeva' (from words ending in 'vaṇṇa,' only 'ī' is used): from 'he has the complexion of Brahmā' ('brahmavaṇṇaṃ assa atthi'), we get 'brahmavaṇṇī'; similarly, 'devavaṇṇī' (having the complexion of a deva).

“Hatthadantehi [M 0.0202] jātiyaṃ”. Hattha+massa atthīti hatthī, dantī. Aññatra hatthavā dantavā.

By the rule 'Hatthadantehi jātiyaṃ' (from 'hattha' and 'danta' in the sense of a species): from 'it has a trunk' ('hatthaṃ assa atthi'), we get 'hatthī' (an elephant); similarly, 'dantī' (a tusked creature, an elephant). In other senses, the forms are 'hatthavā' or 'dantavā'.

“Vaṇṇato brahmacārimhi”. Vaṇṇo assa atthīti vaṇṇiko brahmacārī.

By the rule 'Vaṇṇato brahmacārimhi' (from 'vaṇṇa' in the sense of a 'brahmacārī'): from 'he has social standing' ('vaṇṇo assa atthi'), we get 'vaṇṇiko,' meaning a 'brahmacārī'.

“Pokkharādito dese”. Pokkharaṃ jalaṃ padumaṃ vā assa atthīti pokkharī, “yuvaṇṇehi nī”ti nīmhi “gharaṇyādayo”ti īssa attaṃ, nassa ṇo ca, pokkharaṇī, uppalinī, kumudinī, bhisinī, mulālinī, sālukinī.

The rule 'Pokkharādito dese' (From `pokkhara`, etc., in the sense of a place). Because it has water (`pokkharaṃ jalaṃ`) or lotuses (`padumaṃ`), it is `pokkharī`. By the rule 'Yuvaṇṇehi nī', when the suffix `nī` is added, and by 'Gharaṇyādayo', `ī` becomes `a` and `n` becomes `ṇ`, resulting in `pokkharaṇī`. Similarly: `uppalinī`, `kumudinī`, `bhisinī`, `mulālinī`, `sālukinī`.

“Kvacā+desepi”. Paduma+massa atthīti padumī paduminī paduminīpaṇṇaṃ. Desato+ññatra pokkharavā hatthī.

The rule 'Kvacādesepi' (And sometimes not in the sense of a place). Because it has lotuses (`paduma`), it is `padumī` or `paduminī`; for example, `paduminīpaṇṇaṃ` (a lotus leaf). Other than in the sense of a place: `pokkharavā hatthī` (an elephant possessing a trunk).

“Nāvāyi+ko” nāviko. Sikhī, bālī, sīlī, balī.

By 'Nāvāyiko', `nāviko` (a boatman) is formed. Other examples: `sikhī` (having a crest), `bālī` (having hair), `sīlī` (having virtue), `balī` (having strength).

“Sukhadukkhā ī”. Sukhī dukkhī. “Balā bāhūrupubbā ca”. Bāhubalī, ūrubalī.

The rule 'Sukhadukkhā ī' (From `sukha` and `dukkha`, the suffix `ī`). `sukhī` (happy), `dukkhī` (suffering). And the rule 'Balā bāhūrupubbā ca' (And from `bala` when preceded by `bāhu` or `ūru`). `bāhubalī` (strong-armed), `ūrubalī` (strong-thighed).

81. Tapādīhi ssīti

81. The rule 'Tapādīhi ssī' (From `tapa` and so on, the suffix `ssī` is added).

Ssī. Tapo assa atthīti tapassī, yasassī, tejassī, manassī, payassī. Vātveva, yasavā.

The suffix `ssī`. Because one has austerity (`tapo`), one is `tapassī` (an ascetic); similarly, `yasassī` (famous), `tejassī` (splendid), `manassī` (mindful), `payassī` (possessing vitality). The suffix `vā` is also used: `yasavā`.

82. Mukhādito roti

82. The rule 'Mukhādito ro' (From `mukha` and so on, the suffix `ro` is added).

Ro. Ninditaṃ mukha+massa atthīti mukharo. Susi=chiddaṃ assa atthīti susiro. Ūso=khāramattikā asmiṃ atthīti ūsaro[M 0.0203]. Madhuro guḷo, madhurā sakkharā, madhuraṃ khīraṃ. Khaṃ=gīvāya vivaraṃ assa atthīti kharo gadrabho. Kuñjo=hanu assa atthīti kuñjaro. Nagaro.

The suffix `ro`. Because one has a blameworthy mouth (`ninditaṃ mukhaṃ`), one is `mukharo` (talkative). Because it has a hole (`susi=chiddaṃ`), it is `susiro` (hollow). Because it has alkaline soil (`ūso=khāramattikā`) in it, it is `ūsaro` (saline). `madhuro guḷo` (sweet molasses), `madhurā sakkharā` (sweet sugar), `madhuraṃ khīraṃ` (sweet milk). Because it has an opening in its neck (`khaṃ=gīvāya vivaraṃ`), it is `kharo` (harsh), as in `kharo gadrabho` (a harsh-voiced donkey). Because it has a curved jaw (`kuñjo=hanu`), it is `kuñjaro` (an elephant). `nagaro` (a city-dweller).

“Dantassa ca unnatadante”ti gaṇasuttena dantassa u ca, unnataṃ danta+massa atthīti danturo.

By the `gaṇasutta` 'Dantassa ca unnatadante' (And for `danta` in the sense of prominent teeth), `u` is added to `danta`. Thus, because one has prominent teeth (`unnataṃ dantaṃ`), one is `danturo`.

83. Tuṭṭhyādīhi bhoti

83. The rule 'Tuṭṭhyādīhi bho' (From `tuṭṭhi` and so on, the suffix `bho` is added).

Bho vā. Tuṭṭhi assa atthīti tuṭṭhibho, sālibho, vālibho.

The suffix `bho` is optional. Because one has contentment (`tuṭṭhi`), one is `tuṭṭhibho`. Similarly: `sālibho` (possessing rice), `vālibho` (possessing hair).

84. Saddhāditva

84. The rule 'Saddhāditva' (From `saddhā` and so on, the suffix `a` is added).

Iti vā a hoti. Atisayā saddhā assa atthīti saddho, pañño, paññavā, saddhā kaññā, saddhaṃ kulaṃ.

Thus, the suffix `a` occurs optionally. Because one has exceeding faith (`atisayā saddhā`), one is `saddho` (faithful). Similarly: `pañño` (wise), and also `paññavā` (possessing wisdom). In other genders: `saddhā kaññā` (a faithful maiden), `saddhaṃ kulaṃ` (a faithful family).

85. Ṇo tapāti

85. The rule 'Ṇo tapā' (From `tapa`, the suffix `ṇo` is added).

Ṇo, tāpaso, sakāgamo. Tāpasī.

The suffix `ṇo`. This forms `tāpaso` (an ascetic), with the insertion of `s` (`sakāgamo`). The feminine form is `tāpasī`.

86. Ālva+bhijjhādīhiti

86. The rule 'Ālvabhijjhādīhi' (From `abhijjhā` and so on, the suffix `ālu` is added).

Ālu vā. Abhijjhā assa atthīti abhijjhālu, sītālu, dhajālu, dayālu, dayāvā. Abhijjhālu eva abhijjhāluko.

The suffix `ālu` is optional. Because one has covetousness (`abhijjhā`), one is `abhijjhālu` (covetous). Similarly: `sītālu` (sensitive to cold), `dhajālu` (bannered), `dayālu` (compassionate), or alternatively `dayāvā`. `Abhijjhālu` itself can become `abhijjhāluko`.

87. Picchāditvi+loti

87. The rule 'Picchādito ilo' (From `piccha` and so on, the suffix `ilo` is added).

Ilo vā. Piccha+massa atthīti picchilo, picchavā. Pheṇilo, jaṭilo, tuṇḍilo. Ninditā vācā assa atthīti vācāloti parassaralopo.

The suffix `ilo` is optional. Because it has slime (`piccha`), it is `picchilo` (slimy), or alternatively `picchavā`. Other examples: `pheṇilo` (foamy), `jaṭilo` (having matted hair), `tuṇḍilo` (pot-bellied). Because one has blameworthy speech (`ninditā vācā`), one is `vācālo` (talkative); here, elision of the following vowel (`parassaralopo`) has occurred.

88. Sīlādito voti

88. The rule 'Sīlādito vo' (From `sīla` and so on, the suffix `vo` is added).

Vo [M 0.0204] hoti vā. Sīlavo, sīlavā. Kesavo, kesavā.

The suffix `vo` occurs optionally. `sīlavo` (virtuous), or `sīlavā`. `kesavo` (hairy), or `kesavā`.

“Aṇṇā niccaṃ” aṇṇavo. “Gaṇḍīrājīhi saññāyaṃ” gaṇḍī=meṇḍasiṅgaṃ assa atthīti gaṇḍīvaṃ dhanu, rājīvaṃ paṅkajaṃ.

By the rule 'Aṇṇā niccaṃ' (From `aṇṇa`, invariably), `aṇṇavo` (the ocean) is formed. By 'Gaṇḍīrājīhi saññāyaṃ' (From `gaṇḍī` and `rājī` in the sense of a specific name): because it has a node like a ram's horn (`gaṇḍī=meṇḍasiṅgaṃ`), it is `gaṇḍīvaṃ dhanu` (the Gāṇḍīva bow); `rājīvaṃ paṅkajaṃ` (a lotus).

89. Māyā medhāhi vīti

89. The rule 'Māyāmedhāhi vī' (From `māyā` and `medhā`, the suffix `vī` is added).

Vī. Māyāvī, medhāvī pumā. Nīmhi medhāvinī. Medhāvī kulaṃ, “ekavacanayosva+ghonaṃ”ti simhi rasso. Evaṃ māyāvī.

The suffix `vī`. `māyāvī` (magician), `medhāvī` (wise man), in the masculine (`pumā`). With the suffix `nī`, the feminine is `medhāvinī`. In the neuter: `medhāvī kulaṃ` (a wise family); by the rule 'Ekavacanayosvagho naṃ', the vowel is shortened in the nominative singular (`simhi rasso`). `māyāvī` is formed in the same way.

90. Si+ssare āmyu+vāmī

90. The rule 'Sissare āmyuvāmī' (From `sa` and `su` in the sense of 'lord', `āmī` and `suvāmī` are respectively formed).

Issare+bhidheyye sasaddā āmī+uvāmī honti mantvatthe. Saṃ=āyattaṃ assa atthīti sāmī suvāmī. Suvāminī kaññā.

When 'lord' is the meaning (`issare abhidheyye`), from the words `sa` and `su`, `sāmī` and `suvāmī` are formed in the sense of possession (`mantvatthe`). Because one has mastery (`saṃ=āyattaṃ`), one is `sāmī` (master) or `suvāmī` (good master). `suvāminī kaññā` (a good lady).

91. Lakkhyā ṇo a ca

91. The rule 'Lakkhyā ṇo a ca' (From `lakkhī`, the suffix `ṇo` is added, and the final vowel becomes `a`).

Lakkhīsaddā ṇo hoti mantvatthe a ca+ntassa. Lakkhī assa atthīti lakkhaṇo.

From the word `lakkhī`, the suffix `ṇo` occurs in the sense of possession (`mantvatthe`), and `a` replaces the final vowel. Because one has a characteristic mark (`lakkhī`), one is `lakkhaṇo` (possessed of marks).

92. Aṅgā no kalyāṇeti

92. The rule 'Aṅgā ṇo kalyāṇe' (From `aṅga`, the suffix `ṇo` is added in the sense of 'beautiful').

Aṅgasmā no hoti. Kalyāṇāni sobhaṇāni aṅgāni assā atthīti aṅganā.

From the word `aṅga`, the suffix `ṇo` occurs. Because she has beautiful (`kalyāṇāni`), lovely (`sobhaṇāni`) limbs (`aṅgāni`), she is an `aṅganā` (a woman).

93. So lomāti

93. The suffix 'sa' [is added] to 'loma'.

Lomā [M 0.0205] so, pahūtā lomā assa atthīti lomaso, lomasā kaññā.

He has hair. One who has abundant hair is 'lomaso' (hairy); for example, a hairy maiden.

94. Imi+yāti

94. The suffixes 'ima' and 'iya'.

Ima+iyā honti, putto assa atthīti puttimo, kittimo, puttiyo, kappiyo, jaṭiyo, hānabhāgiyo, seniyo. (Atthyatthataddhitaṃ).

The suffixes 'ima' and 'iya' occur. 'He has a son,' thus 'puttimo'; also 'kittimo', 'puttiyo', 'kappiyo', 'jaṭiyo', 'hānabhāgiyo', 'seniyo'. (This is the Atthyattha-taddhita formation).

95. To pañcamyā

95. The suffix 'to' for the fifth case.

Pañcamyantā bahulaṃ to hoti vā. Toādipaccayantā nipphannanipātā, tehi parāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ “asaṃkhyehi sabbāsaṃ”ti lopova. Gāmato āgacchatīti gāmasmā āgacchati, corato bhāyatīti corehi bhāyati, satthato parihīno satthā parihīno. Evaṃ purisato, rājato, aggito, hatthito, hetuto, yuttito, itthito, bhikkhunito, yāguto, jambuto, cittato, āyuto. Sabbādito-sabbato, yato, tato iccādi.

After a word ending in the fifth case, the suffix 'to' frequently and optionally occurs. Words formed ending in the suffix 'to' and so on are indeclinable particles. After them, case endings are elided according to the rule 'asaṃkhyehi sabbāsaṃ'. 'Gāmato āgacchati' means 'gāmasmā āgacchati'—he comes from the village. 'Corato bhāyati' means 'corehi bhāyati'—he fears the thieves. 'Satthato parihīno' means 'fallen away from the teacher'. Similarly: purisato (from a man), rājato (from a king), aggito (from fire), hatthito (from an elephant), hetuto (from a cause), yuttito (from reason), itthito (from a woman), bhikkhunito (from a nun), yāguto (from rice-gruel), jambuto (from a rose-apple tree), cittato (from the mind), āyuto (from life). From 'sabba', etc.: sabbato (from all), yato (from which), tato (from that), and so on.

96. Ito+te+tto kuto

96. The irregular forms: ito, ato, etto, kuto.

Tomhi imassa ṭi nipaccate etassa ṭa+eṭa kiṃ saddassa kuttañca. Ito imasmā, ato etto etasmā, kuto kasmā.

With the suffix 'to', 'ima' is irregularly substituted by 'i'; 'eta' is substituted by 'a' or 'e'; and the word 'kiṃ' is substituted by 'ku'. 'Ito' (from this) is from 'imasmā'; 'ato' and 'etto' (from that) are from 'etasmā'; 'kuto' (from what/where) is from 'kasmā'.

97. Abhyādīhiti

97. From 'abhi' and so on, thus.

To. Abhito, parito, pacchato, heṭṭhato.

The suffix 'to'. Examples: abhito (around), parito (on all sides), pacchato (behind), heṭṭhato (below).

98. Ādyādīhiti

98. From 'ādi' and so on, thus.

Sattamyantehi [M 0.0206] to hoti. Ādo ādito, majjhato, antato, piṭṭhito, passato, mukhato. Paṭhamantā yato+dakaṃ ta+dādittaṃ, yaṃ udakaṃ, tadevā+dittanti attho.

The suffix 'to' occurs after words ending in the seventh case. For example: ādito (from the beginning), majjhato (from the middle), antato (from the end), piṭṭhito (from the back), passato (from the side), mukhato (from the mouth). From a word ending in the first case: 'yato udakaṃ tadādittaṃ'. The meaning is 'yaṃ udakaṃ, tadeva ādittan'ti' (which water, that very thing is burning).

99. Sabbādito sattamyā tra+tthā

99. From 'sabba' and so on, in the seventh case, the suffixes 'tra' and 'tthā'.

Sabbādīhi sattamyantehi tra+tthā vā honti. Sabbatra sabbattha sabbasmiṃ, yatra yattha, tatra tattha iccādi. Bahulādhikārā na tumhaamhehi.

After 'sabba' and so on, with words ending in the seventh case, 'tra' and 'tthā' optionally occur. Examples: sabbatra, sabbattha (in everything, everywhere); yatra, yattha (wherever, in whatever place); tatra, tattha (there, in that place); and so on. Due to the governing rule of 'bahula', they are not formed from 'tumha' and 'amha'.

100. Katthe+ttha+kutrā+tra kve+hi+dha

100. Kattha, ettha, kutra, atra, kva, iha, idha.

Etehi “sabbādito”tiādinā tra+tthā. Sesādesā ca paccayā ca imināva nipaccante. Iminā kissa ka+ku ca, etassa ṭe+ṭā ca, vapaccaye kissa ilopo ca, ha+dhapaccayesu imassa ṭi ca nipaccate. Kasmiṃ kattha kutra kva, etasmiṃ ettha atra, imasmiṃ iha idha.

For these, the suffixes 'tra' and 'tthā' are applied according to the rule 'sabbādito', etc. The remaining substitutions and suffixes are also irregularly formed by this rule. By this rule: for 'kiṃ', the substitutions are 'ka' and 'ku'; for 'eta', the substitutions are 'e' and 'a'; before the 'va' suffix, the 'i' of 'kiṃ' is elided; and before the 'ha' and 'dha' suffixes, 'ima' is irregularly substituted by 'i'. Examples: kasmiṃ, kattha, kutra, kva (in what); etasmiṃ, ettha, atra (in that); imasmiṃ, iha, idha (in this).

101. Dhi sabbā vāti

101. The suffix 'dhi' after 'sabba', optionally, thus.

Sabbasmā dhi vā. Sabbasmiṃ sabbadhi sabbatra.

After 'sabba', the suffix 'dhi' optionally occurs. Examples: sabbasmiṃ, sabbadhi, sabbatra (in everything, everywhere).

102. Yā hinti

102. The suffix 'hiṃ' after 'ya', thus.

Yasaddā hiṃ, yasmiṃ yahiṃ yatra.

From the word 'ya', the suffix 'hiṃ' is formed. Examples: yasmiṃ, yahiṃ, yatra (wherever).

103. Tā hañcati

103. The suffix 'haṃ', etc., from 'ta', thus.

Tasaddā haṃ hoti hiñca. Tahaṃ tahiṃ tatra.

From the word 'ta', the suffixes 'haṃ' and 'hiṃ' are formed. Examples: tahaṃ, tahiṃ, tatra (there).

104. Kuhiṃ kahanti

104. Kuhiṃ, kahaṃ, thus.

Hiṃ [M 0.0207] haṃ nipaccante kissa ku+kā ca. Kuhiṃ kahaṃ. Kuhiñcanaṃti nipātantaraṃ.

The suffixes 'hiṃ' and 'haṃ' are irregularly formed, and for 'kiṃ', the substitutions are 'ku' and 'ka'. Examples: Kuhiṃ, kahaṃ (where). 'Kuhiñcanaṃ' is another indeclinable particle.

105. Sabbe+ka+ñña+ya+tehi kāle dā

105. From 'sabba', 'eka', 'añña', 'ya', and 'ta', in the sense of time, the suffix 'dā'.

Etehi kāle dā hoti vā. Sabbasmiṃ kāle sabbadā, ekadā, aññadā, yadā, tadā.

From these, in the sense of time, the suffix 'dā' optionally occurs. Examples: sabbadā (at all times), ekadā (at one time), aññadā (at another time), yadā (when), tadā (then).

106. Kadā kudā sadā+dhune+dāni

106. Kadā, kudā, sadā, adhunā, idāni.

Ete saddā nipaccante. Kasmiṃkāle kadā kudā, sabbasmiṃ kāle sadā, imasmiṃ kāle adhunā idāni.

These words are irregularly formed. Examples: kadā, kudā (when, at what time); sadā (always, at all times); adhunā, idāni (now, at this time).

107. Ajja sajjva+parajjve+tarahi karahā

107. Ajja, sajju, aparajju, etarahi, karaha.

Pakati paccayo ādeso kālavisesoti sabba+metaṃ nipātanā labbhati. Imassa ṭo jjo cā+hani nipaccante, asmiṃ ahani ajja. Samānassa sa-bhāvo jju cā+hani. Samāne ahani sajju. Aparasmā jju, aparasmiṃ ahani aparajju. Imassa eto, kāle rahi ca, imasmiṃkāle etarahi. Kiṃ saddassa ko, raha cā+najjatane. Kasmiṃ kāle karaha.

The base, suffix, substitution, and specific time—all this is obtained by irregular formation. For 'ima', 'a' and 'jja' are irregularly formed with 'ahani'; 'asmiṃ ahani' (on this day) becomes 'ajja' (today). For 'samāna', 'sa' and 'jju' are formed with 'ahani'; 'samāne ahani' (on the same day) becomes 'sajju'. From 'apara', 'jju' is formed; 'aparasmiṃ ahani' (on another day) becomes 'aparajju'. For 'ima', 'eta' is substituted, and 'rahi' is the suffix in the sense of time; 'imasmiṃ kāle' (at this time) becomes 'etarahi' (now). For the word 'kiṃ', 'ka' is substituted, and 'raha' is the suffix, in the sense of non-present time; 'kasmiṃ kāle' (at what time) becomes 'karaha'.

108. Sabbādīhi pakāre thā

108. From 'sabba' and so on, in the sense of manner, the suffix 'thā'.

Sāmaññassa bhedako viseso pakāro, tasmiṃ thāpaccayo hoti. Sabbena pakārena sabbathā, yathā, tathā.

A 'pakāra' (manner) is a particularity that distinguishes a generality; in that sense, the suffix 'thā' occurs. Examples: sabbathā (in every way) from 'sabbena pakārena'; yathā (as); tathā (thus).

109. Katha+mitthaṃ

109. Kathaṃ, itthaṃ.

Ki+mimehi [M 0.0208] thaṃpaccayo, ka+ittaṃ tesaṃ yathākkamaṃ. Kena pakārena kathaṃ, iminā pakārena itthaṃ.

From 'kiṃ' and 'ima', the suffix 'thaṃ' is applied, with 'ka' and 'itta' as their respective substitutes. Examples: kathaṃ (how, by what manner); itthaṃ (thus, by this manner).

110. Dhā saṅkhyāhiti

110. From numerals, the suffix 'dhā'.

Pakāre dhā hoti. Dvīhi pakārehi dve vā pakāre karoti dvidhā karoti, bahudhā karoti, ekaṃ rāsiṃ pañcappakāraṃ karoti pañcadhā karoti. Pañcappakāra+mekappakāraṃ karoti ekadhā karoti.

The suffix 'dhā' occurs in the sense of manner. Examples: 'dvidhā karoti' (he makes twofold) from 'dvīhi pakārehi' (by two manners) or 'dve vā pakāre karoti' (or he makes two manners); 'bahudhā karoti' (he makes manifold); 'pañcadhā karoti' (he makes fivefold) from 'ekaṃ rāsiṃ pañcappakāraṃ karoti' (he makes one heap into five kinds); 'ekadhā karoti' (he makes onefold) from 'pañcappakāraṃ ekappakāraṃ karoti' (he makes five kinds into one kind).

111. Ve+kā+jjhanti

111. Optionally from 'eka', the suffix 'jjhaṃ'.

Ekasmā pakāre jjhaṃ vā hoti. Ekena pakārena ekaṃ vā pakāraṃ karoti ekajjhaṃ karoti, ekadhā karoti vā.

From 'eka', in the sense of manner, the suffix 'jjhaṃ' optionally occurs. Examples: 'ekajjhaṃ karoti' (he makes onefold) from 'ekena pakārena' (by one manner) or 'ekaṃ pakāraṃ karoti' (he makes one manner); or 'ekadhā karoti' (he makes onefold).

112. Dvitīhe+dhāti

112. From 'dvi' and 'ti', the suffix 'edhā'.

Edhā vā. Dvīhi pakārehi dve vā pakāre karoti dvedhā, tedhā. Dvidhā tidhā.

The suffix 'edhā' optionally occurs. Examples: 'dvedhā' (twofold) from 'dvīhi pakārehi' (by two manners) or 'dve vā pakāre karoti' (he makes two manners); 'tedhā' (threefold). Alternatively, 'dvidhā', 'tidhā'.

113. Tabbati jātiyo

113. In the sense of 'that kind', the suffix 'jātiyo'.

Pakāravati taṃsāmaññavācakā saddā jātiyo hoti. Paṭujātiyo, mudujātiyo.

From a word denoting a generality of that kind, in the sense of manner, the suffix 'jātiyo' occurs. Examples: paṭujātiyo (of a clever kind), mudujātiyo (of a soft kind).

114. Vārasaṅkhyāya kkhattuṃ

114. From a numeral denoting a number of times, the suffix 'kkhattuṃ'.

Vārasambandhiniyā saṃkhyāya kkhattuṃ hoti. Dve vāre bhuñjati dvikkhattuṃ divasassa bhuñjati. Vāraggahaṇaṃ kiṃ, pañca bhuñjati. Saṅkhyāyāti kiṃ, pahūte vāre bhuñjati.

From a numeral connected with 'vāra' (time), the suffix 'kkhattuṃ' occurs. He eats two times: 'dvikkhattuṃ divasassa bhuñjati' (he eats twice a day). Why the inclusion of 'vāra'? [To prevent application in cases like] 'pañca bhuñjati' (he eats five things). Why 'numeral'? [To prevent application in cases like] 'pahūte vāre bhuñjati' (he eats many times).

115. Katimhāti

115. From 'kati'.

Kkhattuṃ [M 0.0209] hoti. Kati vāre bhuñjati katikkhattuṃ bhuñjati.

The suffix 'kkhattuṃ' occurs. 'Kati vāre bhuñjati' (How many times does he eat?) becomes 'katikkhattuṃ bhuñjati'.

116. Bahumhā dhā ca paccāsattiyaṃ

116. From 'bahu', the suffix 'dhā', and in the sense of proximity.

Vārasambandhiniyā bahusaṃkhyāya dhā hoti kkhattuñca, vārānaṃ ce paccāsatti hoti. Bahuvāre bhuñjati bahudhā divasassa bhuñjati, bahukkhattuṃ vā. Paccāsattiyaṃti kiṃ, bahukkhattuṃ māsassa bhuñjati.

From the numeral 'bahu' related to a number of times, the suffix 'dhā' occurs, and also 'kkhattuṃ', if there is proximity of the times. For example, 'bahuvāre bhuñjati' (he eats many times) becomes 'bahudhā divasassa bhuñjati' (he eats many times a day), or 'bahukkhattuṃ'. Why 'in proximity'? [Consider the counter-example:] 'bahukkhattuṃ māsassa bhuñjati' (he eats many times a month).

117. Sa kiṃ vāti

117. Optionally, the suffix 'kiṃ', and 'sa' as a substitute.

Kiṃpaccayo ekassa sādeso ca nipaccate. Ekaṃ vāraṃ bhuñjati sakiṃ bhuñjati, ekakkhattuṃ vā.

The suffix 'kiṃ' and the substitute 'sa' for 'eka' are applied. 'Ekaṃ vāraṃ bhuñjati' (he eats one time) becomes 'sakiṃ bhuñjati' (he eats once), or 'ekakkhattuṃ'.

118. So vicchā+pakāresu

118. The suffix 'so' in the senses of distribution and manner.

Vicchāyaṃ pakāre ca so hoti. Khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ karoti khaṇḍaso karoti. Puthuppakārena puthuso. Sabbena pakārena sabbaso.

The suffix 'so' occurs in the senses of distribution and manner. For example, 'khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ karoti' (he makes it piece by piece) becomes 'khaṇḍaso karoti' (he makes it in pieces). 'Puthuppakārena' (in diverse manners) becomes 'puthuso' (in diverse ways). 'Sabbena pakārena' (in every manner) becomes 'sabbaso' (in every way).

119. Abhūtatabbhāve karā+sa+bhūyoge vikārā cī

119. In the sense of becoming that which it was not, when in connection with the roots 'kar', 'as', and 'bhū', the suffix 'cī' is applied to a word denoting a transformation.

Avatthāvato+vatthantarenā+bhūtassa tāyā+vatthāya bhāve karā+sa+bhūhi sambandhe sati vikāravācakācī hoti. Adhavalaṃ dhavalaṃ karoti dhavalī karoti. Adhavalo dhavalo siyā dhavalī siyā. Adhavalo dhavalo bhavati dhavalī bhavati. Abhūtatabbhāveti kiṃ, ghaṭaṃ karoti, dadhi atthi, ghaṭo bhavati[M 0.0210]. Karāsabhūyogeti kiṃ, adhavalo dhavalo jāyate. Vikārāti kiṃ, pakatiyā mā hotu, suvaṇṇaṃ kuṇḍalī karoti. (Nipātataddhitaṃ).

When a thing that was not previously in a certain state comes to be in that state, and there is a connection with the roots 'kar', 'as', or 'bhū', the suffix 'cī' is applied to a word denoting that transformation. For example, 'adhavalaṃ dhavalaṃ karoti' (he makes what is not white, white) becomes 'dhavalī karoti' (he whitens it). 'Adhavalo dhavalo siyā' (what is not white might be white) becomes 'dhavalī siyā' (it might become white). 'Adhavalo dhavalo bhavati' (what is not white becomes white) becomes 'dhavalī bhavati' (it becomes white). Why is 'abhūtatabbhāve' (in the state of becoming that which it was not) specified? To prevent application in cases like 'ghaṭaṃ karoti' (he makes a pot), 'dadhi atthi' (curd exists), or 'ghaṭo bhavati' (a pot comes into being). Why is 'kar-as-bhū-yoge' (in connection with 'kar', 'as', and 'bhū') specified? To prevent application in cases like 'adhavalo dhavalo jāyate' (what is not white is born white). Why is 'vikārā' (from a word denoting transformation) specified? So that it may not be applied to a natural state. (End of Indeclinable Derivatives).

120. Dissanta+ññepi paccayāti

120. Other suffixes are also seen.

Vuttato+ññepi paccayā dissanti. Vividhā mātaro vimātaroti visesanasamāso, tāsaṃ puttā vemātikāti rikaṇapaccaye rānubandhattā ulope vuddhimhi kate vemātikā. Pathaṃ gacchantīti pathāvino, āvī. Issā assa atthīti issukī, ukī. Dhuraṃ vahantīti dhorayhā, yhaṇa.

Suffixes other than those mentioned are also seen. 'Vividhā mātaro' (diverse mothers) becomes 'vimātaro'; this is a descriptive compound. Their sons are 'vemātikā'. With the suffix 'rikaṇa', 'r' being an indicatory letter is elided, and upon the application of vṛddhi, the form becomes 'vemātikā'. 'Pathaṃ gacchanti' (they go on the path), hence 'pathāvino'; the suffix is 'āvī'. 'Issā assa atthi' (he has envy), hence 'issukī'; the suffix is 'ukī'. 'Dhuraṃ vahanti' (they bear the yoke), hence 'dhorayhā'; the suffix is 'yhaṇa'.

Sāmaññañca viseso ca, bhāvajo ca nipātajo;

Iti viññūhi viññeyyo, taddhito tu catubbidho.

General and specific, abstract and indeclinable—thus should the wise understand the taddhita to be fourfold.

Iti payogasiddhiyaṃ ṇādikaṇḍo pañcamo.

Thus ends the fifth chapter, the Ṇādi Section, in the Payogasiddhi.

6. Tyādikaṇḍa

6. The Tyādi Chapter

Atha [M 0.0211] tyādayo kriyāvācīhi dhātūhi vuccante.

Now, the 'tya' and other suffixes are explained in relation to verbal roots that denote action.

Kriyaṃ ācikkhatīti ākhyātanti kriyāpadassa pubbācariyasaññā. Kāla+kāraka+purisaparidīpakaṃ kriyālakkhaṇaṃ tyādyantaṃ aliṅgañca, vuttampi ce+taṃ –

What declares action is called an 'ākhyāta' (verb); this is the designation for a verbal word by former teachers. The characteristic of a verb is that it indicates time, agent, and person, ends in 'ti' and so forth, and is without gender. And it is also said:

Yaṃ tikālaṃ tipurisaṃ, kriyāvācī tikārakaṃ;

Atiliṅgaṃ dvivacanaṃ, ta+dākhyātanti vuccati.

That which relates to the three times and the three persons, expresses action, relates to the three factors, is beyond gender, and has two numbers—that is called a verb.

14. Kriyatthā bahulaṃ –ti

14. Mostly conveying action—thus.

Ca sabbattha vattate. Kriyā attho etassāti kriyattho dhātu, so ca duvidho sakammakā+kammakavasena. Tattha yasmiṃ kriyatthe kattuvācimhā kammaṃ gavesīyate, so sakammako. Itaro akammako.

And 'ca' occurs everywhere. A root whose meaning is action is a 'kriyattho' (one with the meaning of action); and that is twofold, by way of being transitive and intransitive. Therein, that root with the meaning of action from which an object is sought from the agent-expressing form is transitive. The other is intransitive.

Tatra sakammakā kammāpekkhaṃ kriyaṃ vadanti, yathā kaṭaṃ karoti, gāmaṃ gacchati, odanaṃ pacati. Akammakā kammanirapekkhaṃ kriyaṃ vadanti, yathā acchati seti tiṭṭhati. Kriyāti ca gamanapacanādiko asattasammato kattari kamme vā patiṭṭhito kārakasamūhasādhiyo padattho vuccati. Api ca –

Therein, transitive verbs speak of action that requires an object, such as 'kaṭaṃ karoti' (makes a mat), 'gāmaṃ gacchati' (goes to the village), or 'odanaṃ pacati' (cooks rice). Intransitive verbs speak of action that does not require an object, such as 'acchati' (sits), 'seti' (lies down), or 'tiṭṭhati' (stands). And 'action' is said to be the meaning of a word, such as going, cooking, etc., which is established in the agent or object, is considered not a substance, and is accomplished by a group of grammatical factors. Moreover—

Karaṇaṃ bhavanaṃ cāpi, kara+bhūhi kathīyate;

Tato kriyādivācattaṃ, pākādīnaṃ kathaṃ bhave.

Doing and becoming are also spoken of by the roots 'kar' and 'bhū'; hence, how can the expression of action by cooking, etc., be possible?

Kara+bhūdhātūhi karaṇañca bhavanañca vuccati, pāka+gamanādīhi tesaṃ kriyābhavanānaṃ vāccattaṃ kathaṃ bhavatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Punapi –

By the roots 'kar' and 'bhū', doing and becoming are expressed; how then can the expression of these actions and states of being come from roots such as 'pac' (cooking), 'gam' (going), and so forth? — this is what is said. Again—

Pākādīnañhi [M 0.0212] vāccattaṃ, karabhūsu na yujjati;

Taṃ bahutaravāccattaṃ, pākādīsu na yujjati.

For the meaning of cooking and so forth is not suitable for 'kar' and 'bhū'; and that more general meaning is not suitable for cooking and so forth.

Taṃ nāma –

That is to say—

Kāriyarūpā hi dhātvatthā, sattāyuttā ca te+khilā;

Tato kriyā ca bhāvo ca, sāmaññaṃ tesu gamyate.

For the meanings of roots are in the form of what is to be effected, and all of them are connected with a substance; hence, action and state of being are generally understood in them.

1. Vattamāneti anti si tha mi ma te ante se vhe e mhe.

1. In the present tense: ti, anti, si, tha, mi, ma, te, ante, se, vhe, e, mhe.

Vattamāne āraddhāparisamatte atthe vattamānato kriyatthā tyādayo honti. Kriyādhikārattā “kriyatthā”ti vuttaṃ. Tesa+maniyame –

In the present tense, in the sense of an action that has begun but is not yet completed, the endings beginning with 'ti' occur, conveying the meaning of action. Because action is the governing topic, it is said 'kriyatthā' (conveying the meaning of action). Regarding their non-restriction—

14. Pubbaparacchakkāna+mekānekesu tumhā+mha+sesesu dve dve majjhimu+ttama+paṭhamā

14. Of the preceding and following sets of six, in singular and plural, with reference to 'tumha' (you), 'amha' (I/we), and the rest, there are two endings each for the second, first, and third persons respectively.

Ekānekesu tumhaamhasaddavacanīyesu tadaññasaddavacanīyesu ca kārakesu pubbacchakkānaṃ paracchakkānañca majjhimu+ttama+paṭhamā dve dve honti yathākkamaṃ. Tatthati antīti paṭhamapuriso, ādo niddiṭṭhattā. Si tha iti majjhimapuriso, majjhe niddiṭṭhattā. Mi ma iti uttamapuriso. Uttamasaddo+yaṃ sabhāvato tipabhutīna+manta+māha. Paracchakkepi te antetiādinā evaṃ yojetabbaṃ. Evaṃ sesesu bhavissatiādīsu sattasu paccayavidhānasuttesupi yojetabbaṃ.

In singular and plural, with reference to the agent denoted by the words 'tumha' (you) and 'amha' (I/we), and by other words, for the preceding set of six and the following set of six, there are two endings each for the second, first, and third persons, respectively. Therein, 'ti' and 'anti' are the third person, because they are indicated at the beginning. 'Si' and 'tha' are the second person, because they are indicated in the middle. 'Mi' and 'ma' are the first person. This word 'uttama' (highest/last) by its nature refers to the end of the group beginning with 'ti'. In the following set of six also, 'te', 'ante', and so forth should be construed in this way. Likewise, it should be construed in the remaining seven rules for the formation of suffixes, such as 'bhavissati', etc.

Idāni bhūvādīna+maṭṭhagaṇānaṃ bhūvādigaṇesu bhū=sattāya+miti paṭhamadhātuto parā tyādayo yojīyante. Tattha “ekamhi vattabbe [M 0.0213] ekavacanaṃ”ti tyādīsu parabhūtesu kattu+kamma+bhāvesuyeva kyavikaraṇalavikaraṇā hontīti “kyo bhāvakammesva+parokkhesu māna+nta+tyādīsu” “kattari lo” iccādinā tesaṃ vikaraṇānaṃ vidhānā tyādayo kattu+kamma+bhāvesveva viññāyantīti kattari timhilo. Ke te vikaraṇā –

Now, of the eight groups of roots beginning with 'bhū', in the 'bhū' group, the endings beginning with 'ti' are applied after the first root, 'bhū', in the sense of 'existence'. Therein, by the rule 'when one is to be spoken of, the singular is used', when the 'tyādi' endings follow, the 'kya' and 'la' infixes occur only in the agent, object, and impersonal senses. Because of the rules for those infixes, such as 'kya in the impersonal and object senses, in the non-aorist, with māna, nta, tyādi' and 'la in the agent sense', the 'tyādi' endings are understood to be only in the agent, object, and impersonal senses. Thus, in the agent sense, these endings are applied. What are those infixes?

Pubbāparabhāgaṭṭhānā, bhinnadhātuvibhattiyo;

Nissāya paccayā honti, ete vikaraṇā siyuṃ.

Affixes that stand between the preceding part (root) and the following part (ending), being distinct from the root and the personal ending, and occur dependently—these are the infixes.

5,82. Yuvaṇṇāna+me, o paccaye

5.82. Of i-vowels and u-vowels, 'e' and 'o' [are substituted respectively], when a suffix follows.

Ivaṇṇu+vaṇṇantānaṃ kriyattānaṃ e+o honti yathākkamaṃ paccayeti ūsso+kāro.

For verbal roots ending in i-vowels and u-vowels, 'e' and 'o' occur respectively when a suffix follows.

5,89. Eona+maya+vā sare

5.89. Of 'e' and 'o', 'ay' and 'av' [are substituted] respectively, optionally, before a vowel.

Sare pare eona+mayavā honti yathākkamaṃti ossa avādeso. So puriso sādhu bhavati, sā itthī sādhu bhavati, cittaṃ sādhu bhavati.

When a vowel follows, 'ay' and 'av' are substituted for 'e' and 'o' respectively; thus, for 'o' there is the substitution 'av'. That man becomes good, that woman becomes good, the mind becomes good.

Uttattā kattu ākhyāte, tatiyā na ca kattari;

Paṭhamāvibhatti hoteva, atthamattaṃ apekkhiya.

When the agent is expressed by the verb, the third case is not used for the agent; the first case indeed occurs, having regard only for the meaning of the base word.

Satipi kriyāyekatte kattūnaṃ bahuttā “bahumhi vattabbe bahuvacanaṃ”ti anti.

Even when the action is singular, due to the plurality of agents, by the rule 'when many are to be expressed, the plural is used'—thus the ending 'anti'.

161. Kvaci vikaraṇānanti

161. Sometimes, of the infixes—

Vikaraṇānaṃ kvaci lopo hotīti lavikaraṇassa lopo, sesaṃ purimasadisaṃ. Te purisā bhavanti. Majjhimapuri- sekavacanaṃ [M 0.0214] si, tvaṃ bhavasi. Bahuvacanaṃ thapaccayo, tumhe bhavatha. Uttamapurisekavacanaṃ mipaccayo.

Sometimes there is elision of the infixes—thus the elision of the 'la' infix; the rest is as before. Those men become. The second person singular is 'si'; you become. The plural is the 'tha' suffix; you (pl.) become. The first person singular is the 'mi' suffix.

57. Himimesva+ssa

57. Before 'hi', 'mi', and 'ma', the preceding 'a' becomes long.

Akārassa dīgho hoti himimesu. Ahaṃ bhavāmi. Bahuvacanaṃ mapaccayo, mayaṃ bhavāma. Evaṃ paracchekkepi-bhavate, bhavante. Bhavase, bhavavhe. Bhave, bhavamhe. Keci dīghaṃ katvā paṭhanti, “byañjane dīgharassā”ti dīgho, bhavāmhe.

The vowel 'a' becomes long before 'hi', 'mi', and 'ma'. I become: ahaṃ bhavāmi. The plural is the 'ma' suffix: we become, mayaṃ bhavāma. Thus, in the following set of six as well: bhavate, bhavante; bhavase, bhavavhe; bhave, bhavamhe. Some read it with a long vowel, justifying the length by a rule such as 'long and short before a consonant', thus: bhavāmhe.

Ettha ca –

And herein—

Lajjā sattā ṭhiti jāgaraṇaṃ,

Vuddhi kkhaya jīvita maraṇaṃ;

Kīḷā ruci rocate ityevaṃ,

Vuttā akammakadhātu sabbe.

Shame, existence, standing, vigilance, growth, decay, life, death, play, inclination, shining—thus, all roots with these meanings are said to be intransitive.

–Ti vuttattā kammaṃ dutiyā na.

—Because it is said thus, the object is not in the second case.

Paca=pāke, akāro uccāraṇattho, eva+muparipi. Paca iti ṭhite lavikaraṇaṃ, vikaraṇalopādi purimasamaṃ. So odanaṃ pacati, te pacanti. Tvaṃ pacasi, tumhe pacatha. Ahaṃ pacāmi, mayaṃ pacāma. Paracchakke-pacate, pacante. Pacase, pacavhe. Pace, pacāmhe.

'Paca'—in the sense of cooking; the 'a' is for pronunciation, likewise in the preceding examples. When 'paca' stands, the 'la' infix is added; the elision of the infix, etc., is as before. He cooks rice, they cook. You cook, you (pl.) cook. I cook, we cook. In the following set of six—pacate, pacante. Pacase, pacavhe. Pace, pacāmhe.

1,22. Vippaṭisedhe

1.22. In Case of Conflict

Vippaṭisedhanaṃ=aññamaññapaṭisedhanaṃ vippaṭisedho. Paṭhamamajjhimapurisānaṃ dvinnaṃ ekattha pasaṅge majjhimapurisabahuvacanaṃ thapaccayo. So [M 0.0215] ca pacati, tvañca pacasi, tumhe pacatha. Tulyabalavirodhino hi vippaṭisedhā paṭhamamajjhimauttamapurisānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ ekattha pasaṅge uttamapurisabahuvacanaṃ hoti, so ca pacati, tvañca pacasi, ahañca pacāmi mayaṃ pacāmāti bhavati.

Mutual exclusion (vippaṭisedha) is the negation of one another. When the third and second persons occur together in one instance, the second person plural, the suffix 'tha', is used. For example: 'He cooks, and you cook' becomes 'You (pl.) cook' (tumhe pacatha). Indeed, in a conflict between those of equal strength, when the third, second, and first persons occur together in one instance, the first person plural is used. For example: 'He cooks, you cook, and I cook' becomes 'We cook' (mayaṃ pacāma).

Ama+gama=gamane –

The root am and gam, in the sense of going –

5,173. Gama yami+sā+sa disānaṃ vā cchaṅa

5.173. For the roots gam, yam, sā, sa, and dis, ccha is an optional substitute.

Etesaṃ dhātūnaṃ cchaṅa vā hoti nta+māna+tyādīsu. So gāmaṃ gacchati. Anti –

For these roots, ccha is an optional substitute before the suffixes nta, māna, ti, and so on. For example: So gāmaṃ gacchati (He goes to the village). Anti –

74. Garupubbā rassā re+ntentīnaṃ

74. Of nte and ntī, re after a short vowel preceded by a heavy syllable.

Garupubbasmā rassā nte+ntīnaṃ re vā hoti.

After a short vowel preceded by a heavy syllable, re is optionally substituted for nte and ntī.

Akkharaniyamo chandaṃ,

Garulahuniyamo bhave vutti;

Dīgho saṃyogādipubbo,

Rasso garu lahu tu rasso.

The regulation of syllables is meter (chanda); the regulation of heavy and light syllables is prosody (vutti). A long vowel is heavy, as is a short vowel preceding a conjunct consonant; but a short vowel is otherwise light.

Gacchare gacchanti. Tvaṃ gacchasi, tumhe gacchatha. Ahaṃ gacchāmi, mayaṃ gacchāma. Cchādesābhāvapakkhe “ū lasse”ti ekāre gameti. Paralope gamenti. Gamesi, gametha. Gamemi, gamema. Paracchakkepi so gacchate, gacchare gacchante. Gacchase, gacchavhe. Gacche, gacchāmhe.

Gacchare, gacchanti (They go). Tvaṃ gacchasi (You go), tumhe gacchatha (you all go). Ahaṃ gacchāmi (I go), mayaṃ gacchāma (we go). In the case where there is no substitution of ccha, by the rule 'ū lassa', with the vowel e, the form is gameti. With elision of the following vowel, it is gamenti. The forms are: gamesi, gametha; gamemi, gamema. Also in the middle voice: so gacchate, gacchare, gacchante; gacchase, gacchavhe; gacche, gacchāmhe.

Pure adhammo dibbati, purā marāmīti ca taṃsamīpe tabbohārūpacārena vattamānavacanaṃ. Vuttañhi –

In the expressions 'Formerly unrighteousness flourishes' (pure adhammo dibbati) and 'Formerly I die' (purā marāmi), the present tense is used for a proximate time by way of figurative speech. For it is said:

Āraddhā+niṭṭhitaṃ [M 0.0216] kiccaṃ, vattamānanti vuccati;

Vattamānasamīpañca, vattamānanti vuccati.

An action begun but not completed is called 'present'; and that which is near the present is also called 'present'.

Kimiva te –

In what way is this so?

Gaṅgāca taṃsamīpañca, yato gaṅgāti ñāyate;

Gaṅgāyaṃ pātu+māgaccha, ghoso gaṅgāya+mityapi.

Just as both the river Ganges and its vicinity are known as 'Ganges', so one says, 'Come to drink at the Ganges', and also, 'a settlement on the Ganges'.

Mukhyā+mukhyatthabhedena, vattamānaṃ tato dvidhā;

Mukhyañhi ruḷhi+māpannaṃ, ta+dāropā amukhyatāti.

By the distinction between primary and secondary meaning, the present tense is therefore twofold; the primary is indeed that which is established by convention, while the secondary is a transference of meaning.

Pure+purāsaddehi vā anāgatatā gamyate, tadā tassa vattamānattā. Kālabyattayo vā eso, bhavantyeva hi kālantarepi tyādayo bāhulakā “santesu parigūhāmi” “kāyassa bhedā abhisamparāyaṃ, sahabyataṃ gacchati vāsavassa” “ativelaṃ namassissaṃ”ti. “Kuto nu tvaṃ āgacchasi, rājagahato āgacchāmī”tiādīsu pana paccuppannasamīpe vattamānavacanaṃ.

Or, when futurity is understood from the words pure or purā, then the present tense is used. Or this is an interchange of tenses, for the ti-endings and so on do indeed frequently occur for other tenses, as in: 'I will conceal among the peaceful' (santesu parigūhāmi); 'After the breaking up of the body, he goes to the next world, to the company of Vāsava' (kāyassa bhedā... gacchati vāsavassa); 'I will worship excessively' (ativelaṃ namassissaṃ). However, in cases like 'Where have you come from?' 'I have come from Rājagaha', the present tense indicates proximity to the present moment.

5,175. Gama vada dānaṃ ghamma vajja dajjā

5.175. For gam, vad, and dā, the substitutes are ghamma, vajja, and dajjā respectively.

Gamādīnaṃ ghammādayo vā honti nta+māna+tyādīsu. Ghammati, ghammanti iccādi.

For the roots gam and so on, ghamma and so on are optional substitutes before the suffixes nta, māna, ti, and so on. For example: ghammati, ghammanti, etc.

Kamme –

In the passive voice –

Upasaggavasā koci, akammopi sakammako;

Yathā+bhibhūyate rāgo, tāpasena mahiddhināti –

By the force of a prefix, some intransitive verb may become transitive; just as 'Passion is overcome by the ascetic of great power'.

Vuttattā akammakato kammani anupubbā bhūdhātuto tyādayo honti.

Because of what has been stated, from the intransitive root bhū, the ti-endings and so on occur in the passive voice in due order.

5,17. Kyo [M 0.0217] bhāvakammesva+parokkhesu māna+nta+tyādīsu

5.17. The suffix ya (kyo) occurs in the impersonal and passive voices, except in the perfect tense, before the suffixes māna, nta, ti, and so on.

Bhāvakammavihitesu parokkhāvajjitesu māna+nta+tyādīsu paresu kyo hoti kriyatthā. Kakāro+nubandhakāriyattho. “Na te kānubandha+nāgamesū”ti paṭisedhā okārābhāvo. Anubhūyati sukhaṃ devadattena.

Before the suffixes māna, nta, ti, and so on, when these are prescribed for the impersonal and passive voices (excluding the perfect tense), the suffix ya (kyo) occurs to denote the action. The letter k is an anubandha for a specific grammatical purpose. Due to the prohibition, 'na te kānubandhanāgamesu', the vowel o does not occur. For example: Anubhūyati sukhaṃ devadattena (Happiness is experienced by Devadatta).

Ettha ca –

And in this connection:

Ākhyātena avuttattā, kattuto tatiyā na tu;

Dutiyā hoti kammassa, vuttattā paṭhamāpi+dha.

Because the agent is not expressed by the finite verb, it takes the third case ending. The object, however, because it is expressed by the verb, here takes the first case ending.

Anubhūyanti sampattiyo tayā. Anubhūyasi tvaṃ devadattena. Anubhūyatha tumhe. Ahaṃ anubhūyāmi, tayā mayaṃ anubhūyāma. Dvitte anubhuyyati+ccādi. Evaṃ paracchakke.

Anubhūyanti sampattiyo tayā (Accomplishments are experienced by you). Anubhūyasi tvaṃ devadattena (You are experienced by Devadatta). Anubhūyatha tumhe (You all are experienced). Ahaṃ anubhūyāmi (I am experienced), tayā mayaṃ anubhūyāma (we are experienced by you). With doubling, the form is anubhuyyati, etc. The same applies in the middle voice.

Bhāve adabbavuttino bhāvassa ekattā ekavacanameva. Tañca paṭhamapurisekavacaneyeva sambhavati, neva+ññaṃ, bahulaṃvidhānā. Bhūyati bhūyate devadattena, sampati bhavanantyattho.

In the impersonal construction (bhāva), because the action does not refer to a substance and is singular by nature, only the singular form of the verb is used. And that occurs only in the third person singular, not otherwise, this being a general rule. For example: Bhūyati or bhūyate devadattena, meaning 'there is a becoming by Devadatta now'.

Pacadhātuto kamme kyo.

From the root pac, in the passive voice, the suffix ya (kyo) is added.

37. Kyassati

37. For kya, ī.

Kriyatthā kyassa īña vā hoti. Ño ādyāvayavattho. Devadattena odano pacīyati paccati, reādese odanā pacīyare pacīyanti, paccare paccanti. Cavaggapubbarūpāni. Tvaṃ pacīyasi paccasi, tumhe pacīyatha paccatha. Ahaṃ pacīyāmi paccāmi, mayaṃ pacīyāma paccāma. Paracchakke devadattena odano pacīyate iccādi.

For the suffix ya (kya), ī (indicated by īña) is an optional substitute. The ñ is an anubandha. For example: Devadattena odano pacīyati, paccati (Rice is cooked by Devadatta). With the substitution of re: odanā pacīyare (or pacīyanti); paccare (or paccanti). The forms show assimilation to the preceding palatal consonant. Tvaṃ pacīyasi, paccasi (You are cooked); tumhe pacīyatha, paccatha (you all are cooked). Ahaṃ pacīyāmi, paccāmi (I am cooked); mayaṃ pacīyāma, paccāma (we are cooked). In the middle voice: Devadattena odano pacīyate, etc.

Gamito [M 0.0218] kamme cchaṅa ca īñaāgame ca kate tena gāmo gacchīyati, gāmā gacchīyanti. Gacchīyasi, gacchīyatha. Gacchīyāmi, gacchīyāma. Evaṃ paracchakke. Gamīyati gammati, gamīyanti gammanti. Gamīyasi gammasi, gamīyatha gammatha, gamīyāmi gammāmi, gamīyāma gammāma paracchakkepi evaṃ. Tathā ghammīyati, ghammīyanti iccādi.

From the root gam, in the passive voice, when the ccha substitute and the ī augment have been applied, the forms are: tena gāmo gacchīyati (the village is gone to by him), gāmā gacchīyanti (villages are gone to). Gacchīyasi (you are gone to), gacchīyatha (you all are gone to). Gacchīyāmi (I am gone to), gacchīyāma (we are gone to). The same applies in the middle voice. Without the ccha substitute: gamīyati, gammati; gamīyanti, gammanti. Gamīyasi, gammasi; gamīyatha, gammatha. Gamīyāmi, gammāmi; gamīyāma, gammāma. The same applies also in the middle voice. Similarly, with the ghamma substitute: ghammīyati, ghammīyanti, etc.

Kriyatthā kattari tyādi, kammasmiñca sakammakā;

Bhāve vā+kammakā kammā+vacanicchāya maññate.

For the meaning of action, in the active voice, etc., and in the passive voice, [the verb is] transitive; or in the impersonal voice, [it is] intransitive, which is understood by the desire not to express the object.

Tathā hi vijjamānassāpi kammāssa avacanicchāyaṃ idaṃ vuccati –

Thus, even when the object exists, due to the desire not to express it, this is said:

Satopi na vivakkhā+ssa, asatopi ca sā bhave;

Taṃ yathā+nudarā kaññā, vañjhāvaddhitako yathā.

Even when it exists, there is no intention to express it; and even when it does not exist, that [intention] may be. This is like a maiden with a slender waist, or like a barren woman's adopted child.

Vivakkhā lokikā esā, asakya+mativattituṃ;

Katha+mesa vipariyāso, loko evā+nayujjate.

This intention to express is worldly, impossible to transgress. How is this a reversal? The world itself is engaged in this way.

(Vattamānapaccayanayo).

(The method of the present tense suffixes).

2. Bhavissati ssati ssanti ssati ssatha ssāmi ssāma ssate ssante ssase ssavhe ssaṃ ssāmhe

2. Bhavissati: ssati, ssanti, ssasi, ssatha, ssāmi, ssāma; ssate, ssante, ssase, ssavhe, ssaṃ, ssāmhe.

Bhavissati=anāraddhe atthe vattamānato kriyatthā ssatyādayo honti.

'Bhavissati': In the sense of that which has not yet begun, the suffixes beginning with `ssati` occur after a root for the meaning of action.

35. A+ī+ssādīnaṃ byañjanassiña

35. The augment `i` for the consonant of [the suffixes] beginning with a, ī, and ssa.

Kriyatthā paresaṃ aādīnaṃ īādīnaṃ ssādīnañca byañjanassi+ña hoti vibhāsā. Vavatthitavibhāsā+yaṃ. Sseti ssādīnaṃ ssatiādīnañcāvayavo gahito, “ūbyañjanassā”ti siddhepi [M 0.0219] tyādīsu etesamevāti niyamattho+ya+mārambho. Lassākāralope o+avādese bhavissati, bhavissanti. Bhavissasi, bhavissatha. Bhavissāmi, bhavissāma. Bhavissate, bhavissante. Bhavissase, bhavissavhe. Bhavissaṃ, bhavissāmhe.

For the meaning of action, for the consonant of the following suffixes beginning with a, ī, and ssa, the augment `i` occurs optionally. This is a restricted option. By `ssa` [in the rule], the component `ssa` of `ssati`, etc., is taken. Although this is established by the rule `ūbyañjanassā`, the present rule is commenced for the purpose of restricting it to only these suffixes among `ti`, etc. With the elision of the `a` of `la` [the verbal ending] and the substitution of `ava` for `o`, [the forms are]: bhavissati, bhavissanti. Bhavissasi, bhavissatha. Bhavissāmi, bhavissāma. Bhavissate, bhavissante. Bhavissase, bhavissavhe. Bhavissaṃ, bhavissāmhe.

Kamme –

In the passive voice:

49. Kyassa sse

49. Of `kya`, when `ssa` [follows].

Kyassa vā lopo hoti sse. Sukhaṃ tayā anubhavissati, anubhavissanti. Anubhavissasi, anubhavissatha. Anubhavissāmi, anubhavissāma. Aññatra anubhūyissati, anubhūyissanti iccādi. Evaṃ paracchakke. Bhāve-bhūyissati bhūyissate.

Of `kya`, there is optional elision when `ssa` follows. For example: Happiness will be experienced by you (`Sukhaṃ tayā anubhavissati`); [other forms are] `anubhavissanti`, `anubhavissasi`, `anubhavissatha`, `anubhavissāmi`, `anubhavissāma`. Otherwise [when `kya` is not elided]: `anubhūyissati`, `anubhūyissanti`, etc. Thus also for the other set of six endings. In the impersonal voice: `bhūyissati`, `bhūyissate`.

Kattari-pacissati, pacissanti iccādi. Kamme-pacissati odano devadattena, pacīyissati, paccissati. Paccissanti odanā pacīyissanti, pacīyissare, paccissare, paccissanti.

In the active voice: `pacissati` (he will cook), `pacissanti` (they will cook), etc. In the passive voice: rice will be cooked by Devadatta (`pacissati odano devadattena`), or `pacīyissati`, or `paccissati`. Rice (plural) will be cooked (`Paccissanti odanā`), or `pacīyissanti`, or `pacīyissare`, or `paccissare`, or `paccissanti`.

Gamito kattari-so gacchissati, te gacchissanti. Tvaṃ gacchissasi, tumhe gacchissatha. Ahaṃ gacchissāmi, mayaṃ gacchissāma. Gacchissate, gacchissante. Gacchissase, gacchissavhe. Gacchissaṃ, gacchissāmhe. Saggaṃ gamissati, gamissanti. Gamissasi, gamissatha. Gamissāmi, gamissāma iccādi. Kamme-gacchiyissati, gacchiyissanti iccādi. Kyalope gamissati, gamissanti iccādi. Tathā ghammissati ghammīyissati, ghammissanti, ghammīyissanti iccādi.

From the root `gam`, in the active voice: he will go (`so gacchissati`), they will go (`te gacchissanti`). You will go (`tvaṃ gacchissasi`), you all will go (`tumhe gacchissatha`). I will go (`ahaṃ gacchissāmi`), we will go (`mayaṃ gacchissāma`). `gacchissate`, `gacchissante`. `gacchissase`, `gacchissavhe`. `gacchissaṃ`, `gacchissāmhe`. He will go to heaven (`saggaṃ gamissati`), `gamissanti`. `gamissasi`, `gamissatha`. `gamissāmi`, `gamissāma`, etc. In the passive voice: `gacchiyissati`, `gacchiyissanti`, etc. With the elision of `kya`: `gamissati`, `gamissanti`, etc. Similarly, `ghammissati`, `ghammīyissati`; `ghammissanti`, `ghammīyissanti`, etc.

3. Nāme garahāvimhayesu

3. When the particle `nāma` [is used] in the sense of blame and astonishment.

Nāmasadde [M 0.0220] nipāte sati garahāyaṃ vimhaye ca gamyamāne ssatyādayo honti. Ime hi nāma kalyāṇadhammā paṭijānissanti. Ettha “jyādīhi knā”ti knāvikaraṇe “ñāssane jā”ti jādeso. Na hi nāma bhikkhave tassa moghapurisassa pāṇesu anuddayā bhavissati. Kathañhi nāma so bhikkhave moghapuriso sabbamattikāmayaṃ kuṭikaṃ karissati. Vimhaye-acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, santena vata bho pabbajitā vihārena viharanti, yatra hi nāma saññī samāno jāgaro pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva dakkhiti, na pana saddaṃ sossati. Acchariyaṃ andho nāma pabbata+mārohissati, badhiro nāma saddaṃ sossati. (Bhavissantipaccayanayo).

When the word `nāma` is a particle, and the sense of blame or astonishment is understood, the suffixes beginning with `ssati` occur. For example: Indeed, these so-called virtuous people will make claims (`paṭijānissanti`). Here, the vikaraṇa `knā` is by the rule `jyādīhi knā`, and the substitution `jā` for `ñā` is by `ñāssane jā`. [Blame:] Indeed, monks, will that foolish man have any compassion for living beings? How indeed, monks, will that foolish man build a hut made entirely of clay? [Astonishment:] Astonishing indeed, sirs, marvelous indeed, sirs, how peacefully the recluses dwell in this dwelling, where one, being conscious and awake, would neither see nor hear the sound of five hundred carts passing close by. Astonishing! A blind man, it seems, will climb a mountain; a deaf man, it seems, will hear a sound. (The section on the future tense suffixes).

4. Bhūte ī uṃ o ttha iṃ mhā ā ū se vhaṃ a mhe

4. In the past tense: ī, uṃ, o, ttha, iṃ, mhā; ā, ū, se, vhaṃ, a, mhe.

Bhūte parisamatte atthe vattamānato kriyatthā īādayo honti. Bhūtānajjatane upari vakkhamānattā ime īādayo bhūtajjatane. “Suvo ahosi ānando”tiādīsu bhūtasāmaññeva bhavanti.

In the sense of a past, completed action, the suffixes beginning with `ī` occur after a root for the meaning of action. Because the non-today past will be explained later, these suffixes beginning with `ī` are for the today past. In examples such as 'Tomorrow, Ānanda was,' they are simply in the general past.

Ahassu+bhayato aḍḍha-rattaṃ vā tadupaḍḍhataṃ;

Antokatvāna viññeyyo, aho ajjatano iti;

Tadañño pana yo kālo, so+najjatanasaññito.

Including half the night on both sides of the day, or a little more, should be known as 'today'. But whatever time is other than that is designated as 'not-today'.

Iti paṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ ī,

Thus, the third person singular ending is `ī`.

15. Ā+ī+ssādīsva+ña vā

15. Before [the suffixes] beginning with ā, ī, and ssa, the augment `a`, optionally.

Āādo [M 0.0221] īādo ssādo ca kriyatthassa vā aña hotīti dhātuto pubbaṃ aña. “Kattari lo”ti lo, ekāra+avādesā ca.

Before [the suffixes] beginning with ā, ī, and ssa, for the meaning of action, the augment `a` optionally occurs. The augment `a` is placed before the root. By `kattari lo`, `lo` [is applied], and also the substitutions of `e` and `ava`.

38. Eyyātha+sse+a+ā+ī+thānaṃ o+a+aṃ+ttha+ttho+vhoka

38. For `eyyātha`, `sse`, `a`, `ā`, `ī`, and `tha`, [the substitutes are] `o`, `a`, `aṃ`, `ttha`, `ttho`, and `vho` respectively.

Eyyāthādīnaṃ oādayo vā honti yathākkamaṃti īssattho, abhavittho, bhavittho, abhavattho, bhavattho. “Ā ī ū mhā ssā ssamhānaṃ vā”ti īssa rassattaṃ. So abhavi bhavi, abhavī bhavī.

For `eyyātha`, etc., `o`, etc., optionally occur respectively. For example, for `ī` there is `ttho`, as in `abhavittho`, `bhavittho`; `abhavattho`, `bhavattho`. By the rule `Ā ī ū mhā ssā ssamhānaṃ vā`, there is optional shortening of `ī`. He was (`so abhavi, bhavi`; `abhavī, bhavī`).

39. Uṃssiṃ+svaṃ+su

39. uṃ, iṃsu, aṃsu.

Tiuṃssa iṃsu+aṃsu vā honti. Abhaviṃsu bhaviṃsu, abhavaṃsu bhavaṃsu, abhavuṃ bhavuṃ.

For `ti` and `uṃ`, `iṃsu` and `aṃsu` optionally occur. Examples: `abhaviṃsu`, `bhaviṃsu`; `abhavaṃsu`, `bhavaṃsu`; `abhavuṃ`, `bhavuṃ`.

42. Ossa a+i+ttha+ttho

42. For `o`: `a`, `i`, `ttha`, `ttho`.

Ossa aādayo vā honti. Abhava bhava, abhavi bhavi, iñāgame abhavittha bhavittha, abhavattha bhavattha, abhavittho bhavittho, abhavattho bhavattho.

For `o`, `a`, etc., optionally occur. Examples: `abhava`, `bhava`; `abhavi`, `bhavi`. With the `i` augment: `abhavittha`, `bhavittha`; `abhavattha`, `bhavattha`; `abhavittho`, `bhavittho`; `abhavattho`, `bhavattho`.

43. Si

43. `si`.

Ossa si vā hoti. Abhavisi bhavisi, abhavasi bhavasi. Abhavo bhavo.

For `o`, `si` optionally occurs. Examples: `abhavisi`, `bhavisi`; `abhavasi`, `bhavasi`; `abhavo`, `bhavo`.

45. Mhātthāna+muña

45. For mhā and ttha, uña.

Esaṃ [M 0.0222] uña vā hoti. Īādisambandhīnameva gahaṇaṃ. Abhavuttha bhavuttha.

For these, uña optionally occurs. Only those connected with ī, etc., are taken. Examples: abhavuttha, bhavuttha.

46. Iṃssa ca siña

46. And for iṃ, siña.

Iṃssa ca siña vā hoti mhātthānañca bahulaṃ. Ikāraññakārā uccāraṇaādyāvayavatthā. Abhavasittha bhavasittha, abhavittha bhavittha, abhavattha bhavattha, abhavisiṃ bhavisiṃ, abhavasiṃ bhavasiṃ, abhaviṃ bhaviṃ. Uñāgame āssa rasso. Abhavumha bhavumha abhavumhā bhavumhā. Siñāgame abhavasimha bhavasimha abhavasimhā bhavasimhā abhavimha bhavimha abhavimhā bhavimhā abhavamha bhavamha abhavamhā bhavamhā. Paracchakke – “eyyāthā”dinā tthe abhavittha bhavittha abhavattha bhavattha. Rasse abhavatha bhavatha, abhavā bhavā, abhavu bhavu. Abhavise bhavise, abhavase bhavase, abhavivhaṃ bhavivhaṃ abhavavhaṃ bhavavhaṃ, assa a+mādese abhavaṃ bhavaṃ abhava bhava, abhavimhe bhavimhe abhavamhe bhavamhe. Kamme sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyittho anvabhūyattho anubhūyattho anvabhūsi anubhūsī anvabhūyī anubhūyī, anvabhūyiṃsu anubhūyiṃsu anvabhūyaṃsu anubhūyaṃsu anvabhūyuṃ anubhūyuṃ iccādi. Bhāve-tena abhūyittho bhūyittho abhūyattho bhūyattho abhūyi bhūyi abhūyī bhūyī. Tena abhūyattha bhūyattha abhūya bhūya abhūyā bhūyā.

And for iṃ, siña optionally occurs, and frequently for mhā and ttha. The letters i and ñ are for the purpose of pronunciation, etc. Examples: abhavasittha, bhavasittha; abhavittha, bhavittha; abhavattha, bhavattha; abhavisiṃ, bhavisiṃ; abhavasiṃ, bhavasiṃ; abhaviṃ, bhaviṃ. When uña is inserted, ā is shortened. Examples: abhavumha, bhavumha; abhavumhā, bhavumhā. When siña is inserted, examples: abhavasimha, bhavasimha; abhavasimhā, bhavasimhā; abhavimha, bhavimha; abhavimhā, bhavimhā; abhavamha, bhavamha; abhavamhā, bhavamhā. In the Parassapada – by 'eyyāthā' etc., for ttha: abhavittha, bhavittha; abhavattha, bhavattha. When shortened: abhavatha, bhavatha; abhavā, bhavā; abhavu, bhavu. Examples: abhavise, bhavise; abhavase, bhavase; abhavivhaṃ, bhavivhaṃ; abhavavhaṃ, bhavavhaṃ. When a is substituted for as: abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ; abhava, bhava; abhavimhe, bhavimhe; abhavamhe, bhavamhe. In the passive voice: 'sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyittho', 'anvabhūyattho', 'anubhūyattho', 'anvabhūsi', 'anubhūsī', 'anvabhūyī', 'anubhūyī'; 'anvabhūyiṃsu', 'anubhūyiṃsu', 'anvabhūyaṃsu', 'anubhūyaṃsu', 'anvabhūyuṃ', 'anubhūyuṃ', etc. In the impersonal voice: 'tena abhūyittho', 'bhūyittho', 'abhūyattho', 'bhūyattho', 'abhūyi', 'bhūyi', 'abhūyī', 'bhūyī'; 'tena abhūyattha', 'bhūyattha', 'abhūya', 'bhūya', 'abhūyā', 'bhūyā'.

So apacittho pacittho iccādi kattusamaṃ. Kamme-apacīyittho pacīyittho apacīyattho pacīyattho. Cavaggapubba- rūpe [M 0.0223] apaccittho paccittho apaccattho paccattho apacīyi pacīyi apacīyī pacīyī apacci pacci apaccī paccī, apacīyiṃsu pacīyiṃsu apaciṃsu paciṃsu apacīyaṃsu pacīyaṃsu apaccaṃsu paccaṃsu apacīyuṃ pacīyuṃ apaccuṃ paccuṃ iccādi kattusamaṃ, pubbarūpova viseso.

He cooked (apacittho, pacittho), etc., is the same as in the active voice. In the passive voice: apacīyittho, pacīyittho; apacīyattho, pacīyattho. In forms with a preceding palatal consonant: apaccittho, paccittho; apaccattho, paccattho; apacīyi, pacīyi; apacīyī, pacīyī; apacci, pacci; apaccī, paccī; apacīyiṃsu, pacīyiṃsu; apaciṃsu, paciṃsu; apacīyaṃsu, pacīyaṃsu; apaccaṃsu, paccaṃsu; apacīyuṃ, pacīyuṃ; apaccuṃ, paccuṃ, etc., is the same as in the active voice; the only difference is the preceding form.

So gāmaṃ agacchittho gacchittho iccādi purimasamaṃ.

He went to the village (agacchittho, gacchittho), etc., is the same as the preceding.

30. Ḍaṃsassa ca ñchaṅa

30. And for ḍaṃs, ñchaṅa.

Ḍaṃsassa ca gamissa ca ñchaṅa vā hoti ā+īādīsu. Agañchittho gañchittho agañchattho gañchattho agañchi gañchi agañchī gañchī iccādi.

For ḍaṃs and for gam, ñchaṅa optionally occurs in suffixes beginning with ā, ī, etc. Examples: agañchittho, gañchittho; agañchattho, gañchattho; agañchi, gañchi; agañchī, gañchī, etc.

29. Gamissā

29. For gam, ā.

Āādo īādo ca gamissa ā hoti vā. So agā agami gami agamittho gamittho agamattho gamattho. Īpaccaye lassākārassa “himimesva+ssā”ti ettha “assā”ti yogavibhāgā dīghe “dīghā īssā”ti īssa siādeso, agamāsi agami gami agamī gamī, agamiṃsu gamiṃsu agamaṃsu gamaṃsu agamuṃ gamuṃ. Ossa aādese ajjhaguṃ. Tvaṃ ajjhagā parassa lopo. Tumhe ajjhaguttha. Ahaṃ ajjhagaṃ, mayaṃ ajjhagamha. Paracchakke – “eyyāthā”dinā tthe so agacchittha gacchittha agañchittha gañchittha agamittha gamittha agama gama agamā gamā. Te agamū gamū, ossa āādese ajjhaguṃ. Tvaṃ agamise gamise. Tumhe agamivhaṃ. “Eyyāthā” dinā a+mādese ahaṃ agamaṃ gamaṃ ajjhagaṃ. Mayaṃ agamimhe gamimhe. Kammeagacchīyi agamīyi, agacchiyuṃ agamiyuṃ iccādi. Tathā aghammī ghammī iccādi.

For the root gam, ā is optionally substituted before suffixes beginning with ā and ī. Examples: so agā, agami, gami; agamittho, gamittho; agamattho, gamattho. When ī is the suffix, for the 'a' of the aorist marker, by splitting the rule 'himimesva+ssā' to get 'assā', and when lengthened by 'dīghā īssā', there is the substitution of si for ī: agamāsi, agami, gami, agamī, gamī; agamiṃsu, gamiṃsu; agamaṃsu, gamaṃsu; agamuṃ, gamuṃ. When a is substituted for o: ajjhaguṃ. You (sg.) ajjhagā, with elision of the following suffix. You (pl.) ajjhaguttha. I ajjhagaṃ, we ajjhagamha. In the Parassapada – by 'eyyāthā' etc., for ttha: so agacchittha, gacchittha; agañchittha, gañchittha; agamittha, gamittha; agama, gama; agamā, gamā. They agamū, gamū; when ā is substituted for o: ajjhaguṃ. You (sg.) agamise, gamise. You (pl.) agamivhaṃ. By 'eyyāthā' etc., with the substitution of a for m: I agamaṃ, gamaṃ, ajjhagaṃ. We agamimhe, gamimhe. In the passive: agacchīyi, agamīyi; agacchiyuṃ, agamiyuṃ, etc. Similarly: aghammī, ghammī, etc.

13. Māyoge ī+āādī

13. In connection with mā, the suffixes beginning with ī, ā, etc.

Māyoge [M 0.0224] sati īādayo āādayo ca vā honti. Sakakālato kālantarepi paccayavidhānattho+yaṃ. Mā bhavaṃ abhavittho iccādi. Vāvidhānāssatyādi+eyyādi+tvādayopi honti, mā bhavaṃ bhavissati, mā bhavaṃ bhaveyya, mā bhavaṃ bhavatu iccādi. (Īādipaccayanayo).

When mā is used, suffixes beginning with ī and suffixes beginning with ā optionally occur. This is for the purpose of prescribing suffixes even for a time different from their own. For example: 'Mā bhavaṃ abhavittho,' etc. Due to this optional rule, future (ssati, etc.), optative (eyya, etc.), and imperative (tu, etc.) suffixes also occur, e.g., 'Mā bhavaṃ bhavissati,' 'Mā bhavaṃ bhaveyya,' 'Mā bhavaṃ bhavatu,' etc. (This is the method for suffixes beginning with ī, etc.).

5. Anajjatane ā ūo ttha a mhā ttha tthuṃ se vhaṃ iṃ mhase

5. In the Anajjatanī (Aorist): ā, ū, o, ttha, a, mhā, ttha, tthuṃ, se, vhaṃ, iṃ, mhase.

Avijjamānajjatane bhūtatthe vattamānato kriyatthā āādayo honti vā. “Eyyāthā”dinā tthe “ā ī ū mhā” iccādinā rasse ca so abhavattha bhavattha abhava bhava abhavā bhavā, te abhavu bhavu abhavū bhavū. O, “ossā”tiādinā aādayo, abhava bhava abhavi bhavi abhavattha bhavattha abhavattho bhavattho, siādese abhavasi bhavasi abhavo bhavo. Tumhe abhavattha bhavattha. Ahaṃ abhavaṃ bhavaṃ abhava bhava, mayaṃ abhavamha bhavamha abhavamhā bhavamhā. So abhavattha bhavattha. Te abhavatthuṃ bhavatthuṃ. Tvaṃ abhavase bhavase. Tumhe abhavavhaṃ bhavavhaṃ. “Issa ca siña”ti siṃ, ahaṃ abhavasiṃ bhavasiṃ abhaviṃ bhaviṃ. Mayaṃ abhavamhase bhavamhase. Kamme-tthe sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyittha, iñāgamābhāve anubhūyattha iccādi. Bhāve-abhūyattha bhūyattha iccādi.

In the past tense not of today (Anajjatanī), for the purpose of the action, suffixes beginning with ā, etc., optionally occur instead of the present tense endings. By 'eyyāthā' etc., for ttha, and by 'ā ī ū mhā' etc., and with shortening: so abhavattha, bhavattha; abhava, bhava; abhavā, bhavā. Te abhavu, bhavu; abhavū, bhavū. For o, by 'ossā' etc., suffixes beginning with a, etc.: abhava, bhava; abhavi, bhavi; abhavattha, bhavattha; abhavattho, bhavattho. With the substitution of si: abhavasi, bhavasi; abhavo, bhavo. You (pl.) abhavattha, bhavattha. I abhavaṃ, bhavaṃ; abhava, bhava. We abhavamha, bhavamha; abhavamhā, bhavamhā. He abhavattha, bhavattha. They abhavatthuṃ, bhavatthuṃ. You (sg.) abhavase, bhavase. You (pl.) abhavavhaṃ, bhavavhaṃ. By 'issa ca siña', siṃ: I abhavasiṃ, bhavasiṃ; abhaviṃ, bhaviṃ. We abhavamhase, bhavamhase. In the passive, for ttha: 'sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyittha' (happiness was experienced by you); in the absence of the iñ-augment, anubhūyattha, etc. In the impersonal: abhūyattha, bhūyattha, etc.

So [M 0.0225] odanaṃ apacattha pacattha iccādi kattusamaṃ. Kamme-apacīyattha pacīyattha apaccattha paccattha apacīya pacīya apacīyā pacīyā apacca pacca apaccā paccā. Apacīyu pacīyu apacīyū pacīyū apaccu paccu apaccū paccū iccādi. “Māyoge ī+āādī”ti māyogepi āādayo, mā bhavaṃ apaccattha iccādi.

He cooked rice (so odanaṃ apacattha, pacattha), etc., is the same as in the active voice. In the passive: apacīyattha, pacīyattha; apaccattha, paccattha; apacīya, pacīya; apacīyā, pacīyā; apacca, pacca; apaccā, paccā; apacīyu, pacīyu; apacīyū, pacīyū; apaccu, paccu; apaccū, paccū, etc. According to 'Māyoge ī+āādī', even when mā is used, suffixes beginning with ā, etc., occur, e.g., 'Mā bhavaṃ apaccattha,' etc.

Tathā agacchattha gacchattha iccādi purimasamaṃ. Tathā agamattha gamattha iccādipi aghammattha ghammattha iccādipi. (Anajjatanapaccayanayo).

Likewise, agacchattha, gacchattha, etc., are the same as the preceding. Likewise, agamattha, gamattha, etc., and also aghammattha, ghammattha, etc. (This is the method for Anajjatanī suffixes).

6. Parokkhe a u e ttha a mha ttha re ttho vho i mhe

6. In the Parokkhā (Perfect): a, u, e, ttha, a, mha, ttha, re, ttho, vho, i, mhe.

Apaccakkhe bhūtānajjatane vattamānato kriyatthā aādayo honti. Akkhānaṃ=indriyānaṃ paraṃ parokkhaṃ. Tasmiṃ. “Aparokkhesū”ti vacanā kya+lādivikaraṇā na honti.

In the unperceived past tense not of today, for the purpose of the action, suffixes beginning with a, etc., occur instead of the present tense endings. Parokkha means beyond the eyes (akkhānaṃ), that is, beyond the senses (indriyānaṃ paraṃ). In that tense, because of the statement 'in the unperceived', the vikaraṇas kya, etc., do not occur.

5,71. Parokkhāyañca

5.71. And in the Parokkhā.

Parokkhāyaṃ paṭhama+mekassaraṃ saddarūpaṃ dve bhavati. “Bhūssa vuka” itiādīsu vuka, bhūva bhūva iti dvitte –

In the Parokkhā, the first sound-form with a single vowel is doubled. By rules such as 'Bhūssa vuka', there is vuka; when doubled, it is bhūva bhūva –

5,75. Lopo+nādibyañjanassa

5.75. Elision of the non-initial consonant.

Dvitte pubbassa ādito+ññassa byañjanassa lopo hoti.

When doubled, of the former part, there is elision of the consonant other than the initial one.

18. Pubbassa a

18. For the former, a.

Aādīsu dvitte pubbassa bhūssa a hoti.

Before suffixes beginning with a, when doubled, the bhū of the former part becomes a.

5,78. Catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā

5.78. For the fourth and second, the third and first.

Dvitte [M 0.0226] pubbesaṃ catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā honti yathākkamaṃti bakāre so babhūva kira, te babhuvu kira. Tvaṃ babhuve kira, iña tumhe babhuvittha kira. Ahaṃ babhuva kira, mayaṃ babhuvimha kira. So babhuvittha kira, te babhuvire kira. Tvaṃ babhuvittho kira, tumhe babhuvivho kira. Ahaṃ babhuvi kira, mayaṃ babhuvimhe kira. Kamme-anupabhuva kira iccādi. Bhāvebabhuva babhuvittha kira.

When doubled, for the fourth and second consonants of the former part, there are the third and first respectively. Thus, with the letter ba: so babhūva kira, te babhuvu kira. Tvaṃ babhuve kira; and, tumhe babhuvittha kira. Ahaṃ babhuva kira, mayaṃ babhuvimha kira. So babhuvittha kira, te babhuvire kira. Tvaṃ babhuvittho kira, tumhe babhuvivho kira. Ahaṃ babhuvi kira, mayaṃ babhuvimhe kira. In the passive: anupabhuva kira, etc. In the impersonal: babhuva, babhuvittha kira.

Papaca, papacu. Papace, iñāgame papacittha. Aññatra “saṃyogādilopo”ti lopo, papacittha. Papaca, papacimha. Papacittha, papacire. Papacittho papacitho, papacivho. Papaci, papacimhe. Evaṃ kamme.

Papaca, papacu. Papace; with the iñ-augment, papacittha. Elsewhere, by the rule 'saṃyogādilopo', there is elision, resulting in papacittha. Papaca, papacimha. Papacittha, papacire. Papacittho, papacitho; papacivho. Papaci, papacimhe. Likewise in the passive.

Aādipaccaye dvibhāve anādibyañjanalope pubbassa “kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā”ti cavaggajakāre “byañjane dīgharassā”ti dīghe ca kate so gāmaṃ jagāma kira, jagamu. Jagame, jagamittha. Jagama, jagamimha. Jagamittha, jagamire. Jagamittho, jagamivho. Jagami, jagamimhe. Evaṃ kamme.

With the a-suffix, upon reduplication, with the elision of the non-initial consonant, and for the preceding [syllable], when a ca-group consonant is made according to 'for the ka-group, a ca-group letter arises,' and when lengthening is done according to 'before a consonant, long or short': so gāmaṃ jagāma kira, jagamu. Jagame, jagamittha. Jagama, jagamimha. Jagamittha, jagamire. Jagamittho, jagamivho. Jagami, jagamimhe. Thus in the passive voice.

Mūḷhavikkhittabyāsattacittena attanāpi kriyā katā abhinibbattikāle+nupaladdhāsamānā phalenā+numīyamānā parokkhāva vatthuto. Tena uttamavisayepi payogasambhavo. (Parokkhāpaccayanayo).

Even actions done by oneself, by one whose mind is confused, scattered, and attached, not being perceived at the moment of arising and being inferred by their result, are in reality obscure. Therefore, the possibility of application arises even in the highest sphere. (The method of Parokkhā suffixes).

7. Yyodo [M 0.0227] vā+tipattiyaṃ ssā ssaṃsu sse ssatha ssaṃ ssamhā ssatha ssiṃsussasessavhessiṃ ssāmhase.

7. In the conditional mood: ssā, ssaṃsu, sse, ssatha, ssaṃ, ssamhā, ssatha, ssiṃsu, ssase, ssavhe, ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

Eyyādo visaye kriyātipattiyaṃ ssādayo honti. Vidhurapaccayopanipātato kāraṇavekallato vā kriyātipatana+manipphatti kriyātipatti. Ete ca ssādayo sāmatthiyā atītānāgatesveva honti, na vattamāne, tatra kriyātipatyasambhavā. Iñāgame ssāssa vā rasse ca sace so paṭhamavaye pabbajjaṃ alabhissa, arahā abhavissa bhavissa abhavissā bhavissā vā, te ca taṃ alabhissaṃsu, arahanto abhavissaṃsu bhavissaṃsu. “Eyyāthā”dinā ssessa vā akāre tvaṃ abhavissa bhavisse. Tumhe abhavissatha. Ahaṃ abhavissaṃ. Rasse mayaṃ abhavissamha bhavissamha abhavissamhā bhavissamhā. Paracchakke-so abhavissatha, abhavissiṃsu. Abhavissase, abhavissavhe. Abhavissiṃ, abhavissāmhase.

In the domain of the optative and so on, in the conditional mood, the suffixes 'ssā' and the like occur. Kriyātipatti is the non-occurrence or non-completion of an action, due to the intervention of an adverse condition or a deficiency of cause. And these suffixes 'ssā' and the like, by their nature, occur only in the past and future, not in the present, because in the present the non-occurrence of an action is impossible. With the i-augment, and with the optional change of 'ssā' to 'ssa', and with shortening: 'If he in his early life had obtained ordination, he would have become an Arahant (abhavissa, bhavissa, abhavissā, or bhavissā).' 'And if they had obtained it, they would have become Arahants (abhavissaṃsu or bhavissaṃsu).' By the rule 'eyyāthā' etc., 'sse' optionally becomes 'a': 'you would have been (abhavissa or bhavisse).' 'You (plural) would have been (abhavissatha).' 'I would have been (abhavissaṃ).' With shortening: 'we would have been (abhavissamha, bhavissamha, abhavissamhā, or bhavissamhā).' In the middle voice: he would have been (abhavissatha), they would have been (abhavissiṃsu). You would have been (abhavissase), you (plural) would have been (abhavissavhe). I would have been (abhavissiṃ), we would have been (abhavissāmhase).

Kamme-tena sukhaṃ anvabhavissa, anvabhavissaṃsu kyalopo. Anvabhūyissa anvabhūyissā iccādi. Bhāve-tena abhūyissa bhūyissa abhūyissā bhūyissā. Abhūyissatha bhūyissatha.

In the passive voice: 'by him, happiness would have been experienced (anvabhavissa)'; 'they would have been experienced (anvabhavissaṃsu)'; with elision of 'kya'. 'Anvabhūyissa,' 'anvabhūyissā,' etc. In the impersonal voice: 'by him, it would have been (abhūyissa, bhūyissa, abhūyissā, bhūyissā).' 'It would have been (abhūyissatha, bhūyissatha).'

Evaṃ taṇḍulādisādhanaṃ alabhissa, odanaṃ apacissa pacissa iccādi. Kamme-tena odano apacissa pacissa apacissā pacissā apacīyissa pacīyissa apacīyissā pacīyissā apaccissa paccissa apaccissā paccissā iccādi.

Thus: 'If one had not obtained the means, such as rice-grains, one would have cooked the rice (apacissa, pacissa, etc.).' In the passive voice: 'by him, the rice would have been cooked' (with the forms apacissa, pacissa, apacissā, pacissā, apacīyissa, pacīyissa, apacīyissā, pacīyissā, apaccissa, paccissa, apaccissā, paccissā, etc.).

So agacchissa gacchissa agacchissā gacchissā iccādi. Cchādesā+bhāve agamissa gamissa agamissā gamissā iccādi. Kamme-agacchissa [M 0.0228] gacchissa agacchīyissa iccādi. Agamissa gamissa agamīyissa iccādi. Tathā aghammissa iccādi. (Kriyātipattipaccayanayo).

He would have gone (agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchissā, gacchissā, etc.). In the absence of the 'cch' substitution: he would have gone (agamissa, gamissa, agamissā, gamissā, etc.). In the passive voice: it would have been gone to (agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchīyissa, etc.; agamissa, gamissa, agamīyissa, etc.). Similarly, aghammissa, etc. (The method of conditional mood suffixes).

8. Hetuphalesve+yya eyyuṃ eyyāsi eyyātha eyyāmi eyyāma etha eraṃ etho eyyāvho eyyaṃ eyyāmhe.

8. In the case of cause and effect, the endings are: eyya, eyyuṃ, eyyāsi, eyyātha, eyyāmi, eyyāma, etha, eraṃ, etho, eyyāvho, eyyaṃ, eyyāmhe.

Hetubhūtāyaṃ phalabhūtāyañca kriyāyaṃ vattamānato kriyatthā eyyādayo honti vā. Lavikaraṇavuddhiādi pubbasamaṃ. Parikappe –

In an action that is a cause or an effect, 'eyya' and the like occur optionally in the sense of action from the present tense. The L-augment, vikaraṇa suffixes, vuddhi strengthening, etc., are as before. In the conditional mood –

75. Eyye+yyāse+yyannaṃ ṭe

75. For 'eyya,' 'eyyāsi,' and 'eyyaṃ,' there is 'ṭe'.

Eyya+eyyāsi+eyya+miccesa+me vā hoti. So dāni kinnu kho bhave, yadi so paṭhamavaye pabbajeyya, arahā bhaveyya.

For 'eyya,' 'eyyāsi,' and 'eyyaṃ,' there is optionally 'e'. Example: 'Now what indeed would he be (bhave)?' 'If he were to go forth in his early life, he would become an Arahant (bhaveyya).'

47. Eyyuṃssuṃ

47. For 'eyyuṃ,' there is 'uṃ' or 'suṃ'.

Eyyu+miccassa ñuṃ vā hoti. Sace saṃkhārā niccā bhavuṃ bhaveyyuṃ, na nirujjheyyuṃ. Yadi tvaṃ bhave bhaveyyāsi. “Eyyāthā” dinā assa okāre tumhe bhaveyyātho bhaveyyātha katha+mahaṃ devo bhaveyyāmi.

For 'eyyuṃ,' there is optionally 'uṃ'. Example: 'If formations were permanent, they would be (bhavuṃ or bhaveyyuṃ), they would not cease (nirujjheyyuṃ).' 'If you were to be (bhave or bhaveyyāsi).' By the rule 'eyyāthā' etc., 'ā' becomes 'o': 'you (plural) would be (bhaveyyātho or bhaveyyātha).' 'How would I become a god (bhaveyyāmi)?'

78. Eyyāmasse+mu ca

78. For 'eyyāma,' there is also 'emu'.

Eyyāmassa emu vā hoti u ca. Kinnu kho mayaṃ bhavemu bhaveyyāmu bhaveyyāma. Paracchakke-bhavetha, bhaveraṃ. Bhavetho, bhaveyyāvho. Bhave bhaveyyaṃ, bhaveyyāmhe. Kamme-sukhaṃ [M 0.0229] tayā anubhuyye anubhuyyeyya, anubhuyyuṃ anubhūyeyyuṃ. Tena tvaṃ anubhūye anubhūyeyyāsi, tumhe anubhūyeyyātho anubhūyeyyātha. Tenā+haṃ anubhūyeyyāmi, mayaṃ anubhūyemu anubhūyeyyāmu anubhūyeyyāma. Paracchakke-anubhūyetha iccādi. Bhāve-bhūye bhūyeyya bhūyetha.

For 'eyyāma,' there are optionally 'emu' and 'eyyāmu'. Example: 'What indeed should we be (bhavemu, bhaveyyāmu, or bhaveyyāma)?' In the middle voice: bhavetha, bhaveraṃ. Bhavetho, bhaveyyāvho. Bhave, bhaveyyaṃ, bhaveyyāmhe. In the passive voice: 'happiness would be experienced by you (anubhuyye or anubhuyyeyya)'; 'they would be experienced (anubhuyyuṃ or anubhūyeyyuṃ).' 'By him you would be experienced (anubhūye or anubhūyeyyāsi)'; 'you (plural) would be experienced (anubhūyeyyātho or anubhūyeyyātha).' 'By him I would be experienced (anubhūyeyyāmi)'; 'we would be experienced (anubhūyemu, anubhūyeyyāmu, or anubhūyeyyāma).' In the middle voice: 'anubhūyetha,' etc. In the impersonal voice: bhūye, bhūyeyya, bhūyetha.

Vidhimhi-so odanaṃ pace paceyya iccādi. Kamme-pacīye pacīyeyya pacce pacceyya iccādi.

In the injunctive sense: 'he should cook the rice (pace or paceyya),' etc. In the passive voice: pacīye, pacīyeyya, pacce, pacceyya, etc.

Anumatiyaṃ-so gāmaṃ gacche gaccheyya iccādi. Aññatra game gameyya iccādi. Tathā ghamme ghammeyya iccādi.

In the permissive sense: 'he may go to the village (gacche or gaccheyya),' etc. In other cases: game, gameyya, etc. Similarly, ghamme, ghammeyya, etc.

Pāto paceyya ce bhuñje, icce+ttha pacanakriyā;

Hetubhūtāti viññeyyā, phalaṃ tva+nubhavakriyā.

If one should cook in the morning and then eat, here the act of cooking should be understood as the cause; the act of partaking is the result.

11. Sattya+rahesve+yyādī

11. In the sense of capability and worthiness, the suffixes 'eyya' and the like occur.

Sattiyaṃ arahate ca kriyatthā eyyādayo honti. Bhavaṃ khalu pattaṃ paceyya, bhavaṃ satto, bhavaṃ araho.

In the sense of capability and worthiness, 'eyya' and the like occur in the sense of action. 'Indeed, the venerable one could cook the food (paceyya)'; 'the venerable one is capable (satto)'; 'the venerable one is worthy (araho).'

12. Sambhāvane vā

12. Optionally, in the sense of possibility.

Sambhāvane gamyamāne dhātunā vuccamāne ca eyyādayo honti vibhāsā. Api bhavaṃ gilitaṃ pāsāṇaṃ paceyya udaragginā, sambhāvemi saddahāmi bhavaṃ paceyya, bhavaṃ pacissati, bhavaṃ apaci.

When possibility is understood and expressed by a verbal root, 'eyya' and the like occur optionally. 'Even if the venerable one were to digest a swallowed stone with his stomach's fire (paceyya)...' 'I consider it possible (sambhāvemi), I believe (saddahāmi) the venerable one could digest it (paceyya), will digest it (pacissati), or has digested it (apaci).'

9. Pañha+patthanā+vidhīsu

9. In the sense of questions, aspirations, and injunctions.

Pañhādīsu kriyatthato eyyādayo honti.

In the sense of questions and the like, 'eyya' and the like occur in the sense of action.

Pañhā [M 0.0230] saṃpucchanaṃ, iṭṭhā-siṃsanaṃ yācanaṃ duve;

Patthanā, bhattiyā vā+tha, na vā byāpāraṇā vidhi.
