A question is an inquiry. Aspiration is of two kinds: wishing for what is desired and requesting. An injunction is a command, whether given with respect or not.

Pañhe-kiṃ so bhattaṃ paceyya, udāhu byañjanaṃ. Patthanāyaṃ-aho vata so paceyya ce. Vidhimhi-bhavaṃ pattaṃ paceyya. (Eyyādipaccayanayo).

In a question: 'Should he cook the rice (paceyya), or the curry?' In aspiration: 'Oh, if only he would cook (paceyya)!' In an injunction: 'The venerable one should cook the food (paceyya).' (The method of 'eyya' and related suffixes).

10. Tu antu hi tha mi ma taṃ antaṃ ssu vho e āmase

10. The suffixes are: tu, antu, hi, tha, mi, ma, taṃ, antaṃ, ssu, vho, e, āmase.

Pañhapatthanāvidhisve+te honti kriyatthato. Āsiṃsanatthe-so sukhī bhavatu, te sukhitā bhavantu.

In the sense of questions, aspirations, and injunctions, these suffixes occur in the sense of action. In the sense of blessing: 'May he be happy (bhavatu)'; 'May they be happy (bhavantu).'

48. Hissa+to lopo

48. Of the suffix 'hi' after 'a', there is elision.

Ato parassa hissa vā lopo hoti. Tvaṃ sukhī bhava bhavāhi, himhi dīgho. “Eyyāthā”dinā vhoka, tumhe sukhitā bhavathavho bhavatha. Ahaṃ sukhī bhavāmi, mayaṃ sukhino bhavāma. Paracchakke-tathā bhavataṃ, bhavantaṃ. Bhavassu, bhavavho. Bhave bhavāmase. Kamme-tayā anubhūyatu, anubhūyantu iccādi. Bhāve-bhūyatu, bhūyataṃ.

Optionally, there is elision of 'hi' after 'a'. Example: 'May you be happy' (bhava or bhavāhi); with 'hi', there is lengthening. By the rule 'eyyāthā' etc., 'vho' [replaces 'tha']: 'May you (plural) be happy' (bhavavho or bhavatha). 'May I be happy' (bhavāmi); 'May we be happy' (bhavāma). In the middle voice: 'May the two of them be' (bhavataṃ); 'May they be' (bhavantaṃ). 'May you be' (bhavassu); 'May you (plural) be' (bhavavho). 'May I be' (bhave); 'May we be' (bhavāmase). In the passive voice: 'May it be experienced by you' (tayā anubhūyatu); 'May they be experienced' (anubhūyantu), etc. In the impersonal voice: 'May it be' (bhūyatu, bhūyataṃ).

Āṇattiyaṃ-devadatto dāni odanaṃ pacatu, pacantu iccādi. Kamme-tena odano paccatu iccādi. Tathā so gāmaṃ gacchatu iccādi. “Ū lasse”ti lasse+kāre gametu, gamentu iccādi. Ghammādese ghammatu, ghammantu iccādi. Kamme-gacchīyatu iccādi. Tathā gamīyatu iccādi.

In the sense of command: 'Let Devadatta now cook the rice,' 'let them cook,' and so on. In the passive: 'Let the rice be cooked by him,' and so on. Likewise: 'Let him go to the village,' and so on. By the rule 'Ū lasse,' for the suffix 'la', 'e' is substituted: 'let him go' (gametu), 'let them go' (gamentu), and so on. In the substitution of 'ghamma': 'let him sweat' (ghammatu), 'let them sweat' (ghamantu), and so on. In the passive: 'let it be gone to' (gacchīyatu), and so on. Likewise: 'let it be gone to' (gamīyatu), and so on.

Vidhimhi-lassa lope lutte vuddhi, idha pabbato hotu.

In the injunctive mood: when the imperative ending 'la' is elided, 'vuddhi' (vowel strengthening) occurs. For example: 'here, let there be a mountain' (idha pabbato hotu).

Nimantane-adhivāsetha [M 0.0231] tumhe bhante bhagavā bhojanaṃ, vasatissa “curādito ṇī”ti ṇimhi “assā ṇānubandhe”ti ā, “yuvaṇṇāna+meo paccaye”ti e ca hoti. Idha nissīdatu bhavaṃ, sadassa “jara+sadāna+mīma vā”ti īma, manubandhattā antasarato īma.

In the sense of invitation: 'Venerable sirs, may you accept the meal for the Blessed One.' For the root 'vas', by the rule 'curādito ṇī', the suffix 'ṇī' is applied; by 'assā ṇānubandhe', 'ā' is applied; and by 'yuvaṇṇānameo paccaye', 'e' is also applied. Here, 'may the revered one be seated' (idha nissīdatu bhavaṃ); for the root 'sad', by the rule 'jarasadānamīma vā', the augment 'īma' is optionally applied; because it has 'm' as an indicatory letter, it is placed after the final vowel.

Ajjhesane-desetu bhante bhagavā dhammaṃ, ettha curādittā purimasamaṃ.

In the sense of entreaty: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One teach the Dhamma.' Here, the formation is similar to the previous case due to it being a 'curādi' group root.

Anumatiyaṃ-puccha vāsava maṃ pañhaṃ, pavisatu bhavaṃ. Ettha pucchato hissa lopo. Evaṃ nisīda.

In the sense of permission: 'Vāsava, ask me a question.' 'May the revered one enter.' Here, for 'pucchati', there is elision of the ending 'hi'. Thus, 'sit down' (nisīda).

Patthanā=yācanā, tatra-dada=dāne, dadāhi me gāmavarāni pañca, dāto lassa ekāre ca ekaṃ me nayanaṃ dehi.

Aspiration is requesting. In that context, for the root 'dada' in the sense of giving: 'Give me five excellent villages.' And for the root 'dā', when the imperative ending 'la' becomes 'e'; also, 'give me one eye' (dehi).

Pattakāle-sampatto te kālo kaṭakaraṇe, kaṭaṃ karotu bhavaṃ. Ettha “tanāditvo”ti o.

At the appropriate time: 'Your time for making the mat has arrived.' 'May the revered one make the mat.' Here, 'o' is applied by the rule 'tanādito'.

Tvādī eyyādayo vatta-mānā sampati,+nāgate;

Bhavissati, parokkhādi-cattāro+tītakālikā.

The endings beginning with 'ti' and 'eyya' are of the present tense, denoting the present and the future. The future tense is for the future; the four tenses beginning with the perfect are of past time.

5,173. Gama yami+sā+sa disānaṃ vā cchaṅa

5.173 For the roots 'gam', 'yam', 'sā', 'sa', and 'dis', 'ccha' is optionally substituted.

Etesaṃ vā cchaṅa hotinta+māna+tyādīsu. So saggaṃ gacchati gameti, gacchanti iccādi. Kamme-gacchīyati gamīyati iccādi. Yama=uparame, parokkhāanajjatanarūpāni sabbattha payoga+manugamma yojetabbāni. Nipubbo, niyacchati niyamati, niyacchanti niyamanti. Saṃpubbo, “ye saṃssā”ti ññattaṃ, saññamati, saññamanti. Kamme-niyacchīyati niyamīyati niyammati, saññamīyati vā. Tathā [M 0.0232] niyacchissati, saññamissati. Niyacchi, saṃyami. Niyacchissa, saṃyamissa. Niyaccheyya, saṃyameyya. Niyacchatu, saññamatu. Isa+siṃsa=icchāyaṃ, so saggaṃ icchati, icchanti iccādi. “Lahussupantassā”ti vuddhimhi esati, esanti iccādi. Kamme-icchīyati, “vā kvacī”ti vuddhimhi esīyati. Pubbarūpe issati issate iccādi. Icchissati esissati iccādi. Icchi esi. Icchissa esissa. Iccheyya eseyya. Icchatu esatu iccādi. Āsa=upavesane, so āsane acchati iccādi. “Byañjane dīgharassā”ti rasso, upapubbo, tathā upāsati. Acchissati upāsissati. Acchi upāsi. Acchissa upāsissa. Accheyya upāseyya. Acchatu upāsatu iccādi. Disa=pekkhane, dicchati dicchanti iccādi sabbaṃ purimasamaṃ. Labha=lābhe, ito paraṃ visesaṭṭhānamevavakkhāma, sabbavāro vuttānusārena gahetabbo. Labhati, labhanti iccādi. Kamme-kyassa pubbarūpādimhi kate labbhati iccādi.

For these roots, 'ccha' optionally occurs before 'anta', 'māna', 'ti' and so on. 'He goes to heaven' (gacchati / gameti), 'they go' (gacchanti), and so on. In the passive: 'gacchīyati', 'gamīyati', and so on. The root 'yam' is in the sense of cessation. The forms of the perfect (parokkhā) and aorist (ajjatanī) should be applied everywhere according to usage. With the prefix 'ni': 'niyacchati', 'niyamati'; 'niyacchanti', 'niyamanti'. With the prefix 'saṃ', by the rule 'ye saṃssā', it is known: 'saññamati', 'saññamanti'. In the passive: 'niyacchīyati', 'niyamīyati', 'niyammati', or 'saññamīyati'. Likewise: 'niyacchissati', 'saññamissati'; 'niyacchi', 'saṃyami'; 'niyacchissa', 'saṃyamissa'; 'niyaccheyya', 'saṃyameyya'; 'niyacchatu', 'saññamatu'. The root 'is' is in the sense of desiring: 'he desires heaven' (icchati), 'they desire' (icchanti), and so on. By 'Lahussupantassā', with 'vuddhi' strengthening: 'esati', 'esanti', and so on. In the passive: 'icchīyati'; by 'vā kvacī', with 'vuddhi' strengthening: 'esīyati'. With assimilation: 'issati', 'issate', and so on. 'Icchissati', 'esissati', and so on. 'Icchi', 'esi'. 'Icchissa', 'esissa'. 'Iccheyya', 'eseyya'. 'Icchatu', 'esatu', and so on. The root 'ās' is in the sense of sitting: 'he sits on a seat' (acchati), and so on. By 'Byañjane dīgharassā', there is shortening; with the prefix 'upa', similarly 'upāsati'. 'Acchissati', 'upāsissati'. 'Acchi', 'upāsi'. 'Acchissa', 'upāsissa'. 'Accheyya', 'upāseyya'. 'Acchatu', 'upāsatu', and so on. The root 'dis' is in the sense of seeing: 'dicchati', 'dicchanti', and so on, all are the same as before. The root 'labh' is in the sense of gain; from here on, we will explain only the special cases; all instances are to be understood according to what has been stated. 'Labhati', 'labhanti', and so on. In the passive, when assimilation of the suffix 'ya' is performed: 'labbhati', and so on.

73. Labhā iṃ+īnaṃ thaṃ thā vā

73. After 'labh', the endings 'iṃ', 'īnaṃ', 'thaṃ', 'thā' are optionally used.

Labhasmā iṃ īnaṃ thaṃ+thā vā honti. So alabhittha labhittha alabhi labhi iṃ paccaye alatthaṃ alabhiṃ iccādi.

After 'labh', 'iṃ', 'īnaṃ', 'thaṃ', and 'thā' optionally occur. For example: 'he obtained' (alabhittha / labhittha), 'he obtained' (alabhi / labhi). With the suffix 'iṃ': 'I obtained' (alatthaṃ / alabhiṃ), and so on.

26. Labha vasa+cchida bhida rudānaṃ cchaṅa

26. For 'labh', 'vas', 'chid', 'bhid', and 'rud', 'ccha' is substituted.

Labhādīnaṃ cchaṅa hoti ssena saha. Lacchati labhissati, lacchanti labhissanti iccādi. Kriyātipattiyaṃ ssābhāgassa cchaṅādese alacchā alabhissa iccādi. Vasa=nivāse, vacchati vasissati. Kamme-bahulādhikārā “assū”ti ukāro[M 0.0233], pubbarūpe vussati vussissati iccādi. Tathā avacchā avasissā. Chida=dvedhākaraṇe, checchati chindissati, “mañca rudhādīnaṃ”ti maṃ lo ca. Lassa lopo ca. Bhida=vidāraṇe, bhecchati bhindissati. Abhecchā abhindissā. Ruda=rodane, rucchati rodissati. Arucchā arodissā iccādi.

For 'labh' and so on, 'ccha' occurs along with 'ssa'. 'He will obtain' (lacchati / labhissati), 'they will obtain' (lacchanti / labhissanti), and so on. In the conditional mood (kriyātipatti), when 'ccha' is substituted for the 'ssa' part: 'he would have obtained' (alacchā / alabhissa), and so on. For 'vas' in the sense of dwelling: 'he will dwell' (vacchati / vasissati). In the passive, by the governing rule of extensive application (bahulādhikāra), 'u' is applied by the rule 'assū'; with assimilation, 'it is dwelt' (vussati), 'it will be dwelt' (vussissati), and so on. Likewise: 'it would have been dwelt' (avacchā / avasissā). For 'chid' in the sense of cutting in two: 'he will cut' (checchati / chindissati); by the rule 'mañca rudhādīnaṃ', the infix 'ṃ' is inserted. For 'bhid' in the sense of breaking: 'he will break' (bhecchati / bhindissati). 'He would have broken' (abhecchā / abhindissā). For 'rud' in the sense of weeping: 'he will weep' (rucchati / rodissati). 'He would have wept' (arucchā / arodissā), and so on.

Aññapaccayepi chidassa “cchaṅa” iti yogavibhāgā cchaṅa, bhūte ūṃ paccaye acchecchuṃ acchindiṃsu. Vuttato aññadhātūnañca, gama=gamane, gacchaṃ gacchissaṃ. Aññapaccayepi vaca=byattavacane iccādi, kamme-bahulādhikārā tyādīsu parabhūtesupi yathāgamaṃ vacādīnañcassa “vacādīnaṃ vassuṭa vā”ti kamme uṭa ca “assū”ti assa u ca, tena dhammo uccati vuccati, vuccanti iccādi, yassa ca pubbarūpaṃ.

Even with other suffixes, 'ccha' is applied to 'chid' by splitting the rule (yogavibhāga). In the past tense, with the suffix 'ūṃ': 'they cut' (acchecchuṃ / acchindiṃsu). And also for other roots than those mentioned: for 'gam' in the sense of going, 'I went' (gacchaṃ), 'I would have gone' (gacchissaṃ). Even with other suffixes, for 'vac' in the sense of clear speech, and so on: in the passive, by the governing rule of extensive application, before 'ti' and so on, even when they follow other elements, according to tradition, for the roots 'vac' and so on, by the rule 'vacādīnaṃ vassuṭa vā', 'uṭa' is optionally applied, and by 'assū', 'a' becomes 'u'; therefore, 'the Dhamma is spoken' (dhammo uccati / vuccati), 'they are spoken' (vuccanti), and so on, for which there is also assimilation.

27. Bhuja muca vaca visānaṃ kkhaṅa

27. For the roots 'bhuj', 'muc', 'vac', and 'vis', 'kkha' is substituted.

Bhujādīnaṃ kkhaṅa hoti ssena saha. Vakkhati vacissati, vakkhanti vacissanti iccādi.

For 'bhuj' and so on, 'kkha' occurs along with 'ssa'. For example: 'he will speak' (vakkhati / vacissati), 'they will speak' (vakkhanti / vacissanti), and so on.

21. Īādo vacassoma

21. Before 'ī' and so on, for 'vac', 'oma' is substituted.

Īādīsu vacassa oma hoti. Makārānubandhattā “mānubandho sarāna+mantā paro”ti paribhāsato sarā paro. Avoci, avocuṃ, avoco iccādi. Anajjatane-avaca avacā vacā iccādi. Kriyātipattiyaṃ-avakkhā avacissā, avakkhiṃsu avacissiṃsu iccādi. Vaceyya iccādi. Kamme-vucceyya iccādi. Tathā vacatu, vuccatu iccādi.

Before 'ī' and so on, 'oma' is substituted for 'vac'. Because it has 'm' as an indicatory letter, according to the meta-rule 'mānubandho sarānamantā paro', it is placed after the vowel. Examples are 'he said' (avoci), 'they said' (avocuṃ), 'you said' (avoco), and so on. In the aorist: 'avaca', 'avacā', 'vacā', and so on. In the conditional: 'avakkhā', 'avacissā'; 'avakkhiṃsu', 'avacissiṃsu', and so on. 'Vaceyya', and so on. In the passive: 'vucceyya', and so on. Likewise, 'vacatu', 'vuccatu', and so on.

Bhuja=pālanajjhohāresu[M 0.0234], “bhujā” dinā kkhavādese bhokkhati bhuñjissati.

The root 'bhuj' is used in the senses of protecting and consuming. By the rule for 'bhuj' and so on, with the substitution 'kkha', the forms are 'he will eat' (bhokkhati) or 'he will eat' (bhuñjissati).

Kusa=akkose, āpubbo, tassa rasso ca, akkosati iccādi ñeyyaṃ, lavikaraṇalopavuddhiyo.

The root 'kus' is in the sense of reviling. With the prefix 'ā', which is shortened, 'akkosati' and so on should be understood, involving elision of the conjugational sign and vowel strengthening (vuddhi).

34. Kusa+ruhehī+ssa chi

34. For 'kus' and 'ruh', 'chi' is optionally substituted for the aorist ending 'ī'.

Kusā ruhā ca parassa īssa chi vā hoti. Pararūpapaṭhamakkharāni, akkocchi akkosi iccādi. Abhipubbo ruha=rohane, abhirucchi abhiruhi iccādi.

After 'kus' and 'ruh', 'chi' is optionally substituted for the following 'ī'. For example: 'he reviled' (akkocchi / akkosi), and so on. With the prefix 'abhi', for the root 'ruh' in the sense of ascending: 'he ascended' (abhirucchi / abhiruhi), and so on.

Vaha=pāpuṇane, vahati, vahanti. Kamme-kye “hassa vipallāso”ti vipariyāso, tena so vuyhati, “assū”ti uttaṃ. Vahissati, vuyhissati. Avahi, avuyhittha, avuhi. Avahissā, vuyhīssā iccādi. Vaheyya, vuyheyya. Vahatu, vuyhatu iccādi.

The root 'vah' is in the sense of carrying. Forms are 'he carries' (vahati), 'they carry' (vahanti). In the passive, with the suffix 'ya', by the rule 'hassa vipallāso', there is metathesis of 'h', and by the rule 'assū', 'a' becomes 'u'; by this, the form is 'it is carried' (vuyhati). Other forms: 'he will carry' (vahissati), 'it will be carried' (vuyhissati); 'he carried' (avahi / avuhi), 'it was carried' (avuyhittha); 'he would carry' (avahissā), 'it would be carried' (vuyhīssā), and so on. Optative: 'he should carry' (vaheyya), 'it should be carried' (vuyheyya). Imperative: 'let him carry' (vahatu), 'let it be carried' (vuyhatu), and so on.

Jara=jīraṇe,

The root 'jar' is in the sense of decaying.

5,174. Jara marāna+mīyaṅa

5.174 For 'jar' and 'mar', 'īya' is substituted.

Jara marānaṃ īyaṅa vā hoti māna+nta+tyādīsu. Jīyati. “Jara sadāna+mīma”ti īmaāgamo lo ca, jīrati. Kamme-jīrīyati jīyīyati. Evaṃ jīyissati jīrissati, jīyīyissati jīrīyissati. Ajīyi ajīri, ajīyīyi ajīrīyi. Ajīyissā ajīrissā, ajīyīyissā ajīrīyissā ajīyissā ajīrīyissā iccādi. Mara=pāṇacāge, īyaṅa, mīyati marati, mīyanti maranti iccādi.

For 'jar' and 'mar', 'īya' optionally occurs before 'māna', 'anta', 'ti', and so on. For example, 'it decays' (jīyati). By the rule 'Jarasadānamīma', the augment 'īma' is applied, resulting in 'jīrati'. In the passive: 'jīrīyati', 'jīyīyati'. Likewise, future: 'jīyissati', 'jīrissati'; 'jīyīyissati', 'jīrīyissati'. Aorist: 'ajīyi', 'ajīri'; 'ajīyīyi', 'ajīrīyi'. Conditional: 'ajīyissā', 'ajīrissā'; 'ajīyīyissā', 'ajīrīyissā', and so on. The root 'mar' is in the sense of giving up life; with 'īya', the forms are 'he dies' (mīyati / marati), 'they die' (mīyanti / maranti), and so on.

Disa=pekkhane,

The root 'dis' is in the sense of seeing.

5,124. Disassa [M 0.0235] passa dassa dasa da dakkhāti

5.124 For 'dis', the substitutions 'passa', 'dassa', 'dasa', 'da', and 'dakkha' occur.

Ete ādesā disassa vā honti. Anekavaṇṇattā sabbādeso. Passati passanti, dakkhati dakkhanti. Kamme-kye pubbarūpo, dissati dissanti, vipassīyati dakkhīyati iccādi.

These substitutions for the root 'dis' occur optionally. Because they consist of more than one letter, they substitute for the entire root. Examples are 'he sees' (passati), 'they see' (passanti); 'he will see' (dakkhati), 'they will see' (dakkhanti). In the passive, with the suffix 'ya', there is assimilation: 'it is seen' (dissati), 'they are seen' (dissanti); 'it is clearly seen' (vipassīyati), 'it will be seen' (dakkhīyati), and so on.

6,69. Dakkha+kha+heti+hohīti lopo

6,69. Elision [of 'ssa'] occurs after 'dakkha', 'kha', 'heti', and 'hohīti'.

Dakkhādīhi ādesehi parassa ssassa lopo vā hoti. Dakkhati dakkhissati. Apassi passi, apassiṃsu passiṃsu apasso passo, apassittha passittha. Apassiṃ passiṃ, apassimha passimha. Tathā adassī dassī, adassiṃsu dassiṃsu iccādi. Anajjatane dasādeso, addasā addasa. Addā adda iccādi. Apassissa dakkhissa iccādi. Passeyya dakkheyya, passatu dakkhatu iccādi.

After substitutions such as 'dakkha', the following 'ssa' is optionally elided. For example, 'dakkhissati' becomes 'dakkhati'. 'Apassi' becomes 'passi'; 'apassiṃsu' becomes 'passiṃsu'; 'apasso' becomes 'passo'; 'apassittha' becomes 'passittha'; 'apassiṃ' becomes 'passiṃ'; 'apassimha' becomes 'passimha'. Similarly, 'adassī' becomes 'dassī'; 'adassiṃsu' becomes 'dassiṃsu', and so on. In the aorist, the substitution 'dasa' occurs, as in 'addasā' and 'addasa'; 'addā' and 'adda', and so on. 'Apassissa' becomes 'dakkhissa', and so on. 'Passeyya' becomes 'dakkheyya'; 'passatu' becomes 'dakkhatu', and so on.

Sada=visaraṇagatyāvasādanādānesu, nipubbo, “jarasadāna+mīma vā”ti īmaāgamo. Nisīdati, nisīdanti iccādi. Bhāve-nisajjati, nisajjate.

The root 'sad' is used in the senses of scattering, going, sinking, and taking. When preceded by the prefix 'ni', according to the rule 'jarasadānam īma vā', the augment 'īma' optionally occurs. Examples are 'nisīdati' (he sits), 'nisīdanti' (they sit), and so on. In the impersonal construction: 'nisajjati', 'nisajjate'.

Yaja=devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadānesu, yajati, yajanti iccādi. Kamme –

The root 'yaj' is used in the senses of worshipping deities, assembling, acting, and giving. Forms include 'yajati' (he worships), 'yajanti' (they worship), and so on. In the passive voice –

5,113. Yajassa yassa ṭi+yīti

5,113. For 'yaj', there are the substitutions 'ya', 'sa', 'ṭi', and 'yī'.

Yajassa yassa ṭi+yī honti kānubandheti bahulādhikārā tyādivisayepi kye pubbarūpe ca ijjati yijjati mayā buddho. So yajissati, tena ijjissate yijjissate. So yajī[M 0.0236], tena ijji yijji. So yajissā, tena ijjissā yijjissā. So yajeyya, tena ijjeyya yijjeyya. So yajatu, tena ijjatu yijjatu iccādi.

For 'yaj', the substitutes 'ya', 'sa', 'ṭi', and 'yī' are given. Due to the indicatory 'k', the governing principle of 'bahulam', in the context of verb endings such as 'ti', and with assimilation when the passive suffix 'ya' follows, the forms 'ijjati' and 'yijjati' are found, as in 'mayā buddho ijjati' (the Buddha is worshipped by me). Thus, 'so yajissati' (he will worship) becomes 'tena ijjissate' or 'yijjissate' (it will be worshipped by him). 'So yajī' (he worshipped) becomes 'tena ijji' or 'yijji' (it was worshipped by him). 'So yajissā' (he would have worshipped) becomes 'tena ijjissā' or 'yijjissā' (it would have been worshipped by him). 'So yajeyya' (he should worship) becomes 'tena ijjeyya' or 'yijjeyya' (it should be worshipped by him). 'So yajatu' (let him worship) becomes 'tena ijjatu' or 'yijjatu' (let it be worshipped by him), and so on.

Vada=vacane, “gamavadā” dinā vadassa vajjādeso vā, lassa “ūlasse”ti kvaci e ca, vajjati vadeti vadati, vajjenti vadenti iccādi. Kamme – “kyassā”ti īña, vajjīyati vajjati vadīyati, vajjīyanti vajjanti vadīyanti. Vadissati, vadissanti. Avadī vadī, avadiṃsu vadiṃsu. Avadissa vadissa. Vajje vajjeyya vade vadeyya, vajjeyyuṃ vadeyyuṃ. Vajjetu vadetu vadatu iccādi yathāgamaṃ ñeyyaṃ.

The root 'vad' is used in the sense of speaking. According to the rule 'gamavadā...', 'vajjā' is the optional substitute for 'vad'. And sometimes, according to 'ūlasse', 'e' is substituted for the 'a' suffix. Examples are: 'vajjati', 'vadeti', 'vadati'; 'vajjenti', 'vadenti', and so on. In the passive voice, according to the rule 'kyassā...', with the 'īya' suffix, the forms are: 'vajjīyati', 'vajjati', 'vadīyati'; 'vajjīyanti', 'vajjanti', 'vadīyanti'. Future: 'vadissati', 'vadissanti'. Aorist: 'avadī', 'vadī'; 'avadiṃsu', 'vadiṃsu'. Conditional: 'avadissa', 'vadissa'. Optative: 'vajje', 'vajjeyya', 'vade', 'vadeyya'; 'vajjeyyuṃ', 'vadeyyuṃ'. Imperative: 'vajjetu', 'vadetu', 'vadatu', and so on, which should be understood according to the grammatical tradition.

Kamu=padavikkhepe, “parokkhāyañcā”ti caggahaṇena kama kama iti dvitte anādibyañjanalope lavikaraṇe “kavaggahā” dinā kassa ce niggahītāgame ca kate caṃkamati kamati iccādi. Cala=kampane, caṃcalati. Jala+dala=dittiyaṃ, dvitte daddallati iccādi. (Savuddhikabhūvādinayo).

The root 'kam' is used in the sense of stepping. By the inclusion of 'ca' in the rule 'parokkhāyañca', when 'kama' is reduplicated ('kama kama'), with the elision of the non-initial consonant of the reduplicative syllable, the application of the 'a' suffix, the change of 'k' to 'c' according to the rule 'kavaggahā...', and the insertion of a niggahīta, the form 'caṃkamati' is made; also 'kamati', and so on. The root 'cal' is used in the sense of trembling, e.g., 'caṃcalati'. The roots 'jal' and 'dal' are used in the sense of shining; when reduplicated, 'daddallati', and so on. (This follows the method of the Savuddhika Bhūvādi group).

Hū+bhū=sattāyaṃ, tyādīsu “kattari lo”ti lo, tassa lope “yuvaṇṇāna+meo paccaye”ti okāro. So hoti, te honti. Hosi, hotha. Homi, homa iccādi. Bhāve-tena hūyati hūyate.

The roots 'hū' and 'bhū' are used in the sense of existence. Before endings such as 'ti', the suffix 'a' is applied in the active voice according to the rule 'kattari a'; upon its elision, 'o' is substituted for the vowel of the root according to the rule 'yuvaṇṇānam eo paccaye'. Examples are: 'so hoti' (he is), 'te honti' (they are); 'hosi' (you are), 'hotha' (you all are); 'homi' (I am), 'homa' (we are), and so on. In the impersonal construction: 'tena hūyati', 'hūyate'.

31. Hūssa he+hehi+hohi ssatyādo

31. For 'hū', [the substitutes are] 'he', 'hehi', and 'hohi' before the future suffix 'ssa', etc.

Hūssa heādayo honti ssaccādo. Hessati hehi ssati hohissati.

For 'hū', 'he' and so on are the substitutes before the future suffix 'ssa', etc. Examples: 'hessati', 'hehissati', 'hohissati'.

69. Dakkha+kha+hehi+hohīhi lopoti

69. Elision [of 'ssa'] occurs after 'dakkha', 'kha', 'hehi', and 'hohīhi'.

Dakkhādīhi [M 0.0237] ādesehi parassa ssassa vā lopo hoti. Hehiti hehissati, hohiti hohissati. Hehinti hehissanti, hohinti hohissanti iccādi. Anajjatane īmhi añāgamo, “paro kvacī”ti īssa lopo, so ahu. Vuddhimhi “dīghā īssa” iti īssa siādeso, suvo ahosi ānando.

After substitutions such as 'dakkha', the following 'ssa' is optionally elided. For example: 'hehissati' becomes 'hehiti'; 'hohissati' becomes 'hohiti'; 'hehissanti' becomes 'hehinti'; 'hohissanti' becomes 'hohinti', and so on. In the aorist, before the 'ī' ending, there is the augment 'a'; according to the rule 'paro kvaci', the 'ī' is elided, e.g., 'so ahu' (he was). With vṛddhi, according to 'dīghā īssa', 'si' is substituted for 'ī', as in 'suvo ahosi ānando'.

41. Hūto resuṃ

41. After 'hū', 'uṃ' [becomes] 'resuṃ'.

Hūto parassa u+miccassa resuṃ vā hoti. Rakārānubandho “rānubandhentasarādissā”ti antasarādissa lopo. Ahesuṃ. Okāravuddhi avādese ahavuṃ. Ossa siādese ahosi.

After 'hū', the following 'uṃ' optionally becomes 'resuṃ'. The indicatory 'r' causes the elision of the final part of the base according to the rule 'rānubandhe...'. For example, 'ahesuṃ'. With vṛddhi of 'o' and its substitution by 'ava', 'ahavuṃ' is formed. With the substitution of 'si' for the 'o' ending, 'ahosi' is formed.

46. Iṃssa ca siña

46. And for 'iṃ', ['siña' is the substitute].

Imiccassa siña hoti mhātthānañca bahulaṃ. Ñākāro ākhyāvayavattho (ukāro) ikāro uccāraṇattho. “Aīssā” dinā iñāgame tumhe ahosittha, ahosi. Parassaralope rasse ca ahuṃ, ahosimha, ahumha, rasso. Bhāve-abhavi, āssatthādeso, abhavittha. Anajjatane āūādipaccaye kate “yuvaṇṇāna+miya ṅuvaṅa sare”ti uvaṅādese ahuvā, ahuvu, ahuvo, ahuvattha. Assa amādese ahuṃ ahuvaṃ, ahumha iccādi. Bhāve-tena ahuyi ahuyittha. Ahavissā, ahavissaṃsu iccādi. Bhāve-ahuyissa, ahuyissatha. Pubbassaralopo, heyya[M 0.0238], heyyuṃ iccādi. Bhāve-hūyeyya, hūyetha. Hotu, hontu iccādi. Bhāve-hūyatu, hūyataṃ. Anupubbe anubhoti iccādi sabbavāresu yojetabbaṃ. Bhāve rūpābhāvā. Kamme-anubhūyati iccādi viseso.

For 'iṃ', 'siña' is the substitute, and frequently also for 'mhā'. The letter 'ñ' indicates a verbal element; the 'i' (or 'u') is for ease of pronunciation. According to 'Aīssā...', with the augment 'i', 'tumhe ahosittha' and 'ahosi' are formed. With elision of the following vowel and shortening, 'ahuṃ', 'ahosimha', and 'ahumha' are formed. In the impersonal: 'abhavi'; with the substitution of 'ttha' for 'āssu', 'abhavittha'. In the aorist, when suffixes like 'ā' and 'ū' are applied, by the rule 'yuvaṇṇānam...', with the 'uvaṅa' substitution, 'ahuvā', 'ahuvu', 'ahuvo', 'ahuvattha' are formed. With the substitution of 'aṃ' for 'assa', 'ahuṃ', 'ahuvaṃ', 'ahumha', etc., are formed. In the impersonal: 'tena ahuyi', 'ahuyittha'. Conditional: 'ahavissā', 'ahavissaṃsu', etc. In the impersonal: 'ahuyissa', 'ahuyissatha'. With elision of the preceding vowel: 'heyya', 'heyyuṃ', etc. In the impersonal: 'hūyeyya', 'hūyetha'. Imperative: 'hotu', 'hontu', etc. In the impersonal: 'hūyatu', 'hūyataṃ'. With the prefix 'anu', 'anubhoti', etc., should be formed in all tenses. As there are no impersonal forms for this, in the passive, 'anubhūyati', etc., are the specific forms.

Si=saye, lassa lopo vuddhi, seti. Ayādese sayati, senti sayanti iccādi. Kamme-atipubbo, kye “dīgho sarassā”ti issa dīghe ca kate tena atisīyati, atisīyanti iccādi. Bhāve-tena sīyati, sīyate. Tathā bhavissatiādīsu.

The root 'sī' is used in the sense of lying down. With elision of the 'a' suffix and vṛddhi, 'seti' is formed. With the substitution of 'aya', 'sayati' is formed; also 'senti', 'sayanti', etc. In the passive, when preceded by 'ati', and when the 'ya' suffix follows, the 'i' is lengthened according to the rule 'dīgho sarassā...', thus forming 'atisīyati', 'atisīyanti', etc. In the impersonal: 'tena sīyati', 'sīyate'. The same applies to the future tense and so on.

Nī=pāpane, dvikammako+yaṃ, ajaṃ gāmaṃ neti nayati, nenti nayanti iccādi. Kamme-nīyate gāmaṃ ajo devadattena iccādi. Tathā sesesupi yojetabbaṃ.

The root 'nī' is used in the sense of leading; this is a verb that takes two objects. For example, 'ajaṃ gāmaṃ neti' or 'nayati' (he leads the goat to the village); 'nenti', 'nayanti', etc. In the passive: 'nīyate gāmaṃ ajo devadattena' (the goat is led to the village by Devadatta), and so on. The same should be applied in the remaining cases.

Ṭhā=gatinivattiyaṃ –

The root 'ṭhā' is used in the sense of cessation of movement –

5,175. Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivā

5,175. For 'ṭhā' and 'pā', ['tiṭṭha' and 'piva' are the substitutes].

Ṭhāpānaṃ tiṭṭhapivāhonti vā nta+māna+tyādīsu. Lassa lope tiṭṭhati, tiṭṭhanti, ṭhāti, ṭhānti.

For 'ṭhā' and 'pā', 'tiṭṭha' and 'piva' are the optional substitutes before endings such as 'nta', 'māna', and 'ti'. With the elision of the 'a' suffix, the forms are 'tiṭṭhati', 'tiṭṭhanti'; and 'ṭhāti', 'ṭhānti'.

5,131. Pādito ṭhāssa vā ṭhaho kvaciti

5,131. After prefixes such as 'pa', 'ṭha' is sometimes the optional substitute for 'ṭhā'.

Pādito parassa ṭhāssa kvaci ṭhaho hoti vā. Saṇṭhahati, saṇṭhahanti. Lasse, adhiṭṭheti, adhiṭṭhenti. Kamme –

After prefixes such as 'pa', the following 'ṭhā' sometimes optionally becomes 'ṭha'. For example: 'saṇṭhahati', 'saṇṭhahanti'. With the 'e' suffix: 'adhiṭṭheti', 'adhiṭṭhenti'. In the passive voice –

5,137. Aññādissā+ssī kye

5,137. For the 'ā' of roots such as 'ñā', 'ī' [is substituted] when the passive suffix 'ya' follows.

Ñādito+ññassa ākārantassa kriyatthassa ī hoti kye. Upaṭhīyati, upaṭhīyanti. Ṭhahādese “kyassā”ti īña[M 0.0239], tena patiṭṭhahīyati, patiṭṭhahīyanti. Bhāve-īmhi ṭhīyati, ṭhīyate. Tathā papubbe patiṭṭhissati patiṭṭhahissati. Īssa simhi aṭṭhāsi, aṭṭhaṃsu, saṇṭhahi, saṇṭhahiṃsu. Patiṭṭhissa patiṭṭhahissa. Tiṭṭhe tiṭṭheyya, saṇṭhe saṇṭheyya, saṇṭheyyuṃ, saṇṭhahe saṇṭhaheyya. Tiṭṭhatu ṭhātu, saṇṭhahatu iccādi.

For roots ending in 'ā' such as 'ñā' which have a verbal meaning, 'ī' is substituted when the passive suffix 'ya' follows. For example: 'upaṭhīyati', 'upaṭhīyanti'. When 'ṭha' is the substitute, according to 'kyassā...', the suffix 'īya' is used, thus: 'patiṭṭhahīyati', 'patiṭṭhahīyanti'. In the impersonal, with 'ī': 'ṭhīyati', 'ṭhīyate'. Similarly, when preceded by 'pa': 'patiṭṭhissati', 'patiṭṭhahissati'. In the aorist: 'aṭṭhāsi', 'aṭṭhaṃsu'; 'saṇṭhahi', 'saṇṭhahiṃsu'. Conditional: 'patiṭṭhissa', 'patiṭṭhahissa'. Optative: 'tiṭṭhe', 'tiṭṭheyya'; 'saṇṭhe', 'saṇṭheyya', 'saṇṭheyyuṃ'; 'saṇṭhahe', 'saṇṭhaheyya'. Imperative: 'tiṭṭhatu', 'ṭhātu'; 'saṇṭhahatu', and so on.

Pā=pāne, pivādese pivati. “Tavaggavaraṇā” do “bayañā”ti yogavibhāgena vassa bakāro, pibati. Kammepīyati, pīyanti iccādi.

The root 'pā' is used in the sense of drinking. With the substitution 'piva', the form is 'pivati'. By splitting the rule ('yogavibhāgena') 'Tavaggavaraṇā...bayañā...', 'v' becomes 'b', resulting in 'pibati'. In the passive: 'pīyati', 'pīyanti', and so on.

Asa=bhuvi,

The root 'as' is used in the sense of being,

52. Tassa thoti

52. For 't', 'th' [is the substitute].

Atthito parassa tassa tho hoti. Pararūpe paṭhamakkharatakāre ca atthi. “Nta+māna+nti+yi+yuṃsvā+dilopo”ti assa lopo, santi.

After the 'at' [of 'as'], the following 't' becomes 'th'. With assimilation to the following form, and the first letter being 't', 'atthi' is formed. According to the rule 'Nta...', there is elision of the 'a' of 'as', resulting in 'santi'.

53. Sihisva+ṭa

53. Sihisvaṭa

Atthissa aṭa hoti sihisu. Ṭo sabbādesattho. Tvaṃ asi. Pararūpādimhi kate idāni tumhe attha.

For the root as, aṭa is the substitute in the context of the endings si and hi. The letter ṭ indicates total substitution. For example, tvaṃ asi. After coalescence with the following form, etc., it is now tumhe attha.

54. Mimānaṃ vā mhimhā ca

54. And for mi and ma, optionally mhi and mhā.

Asasmā paresaṃ mimānaṃ mhimhā vā honti taṃsanniyogena asassa aṭa ca. Amhi.

After the root as, for the following endings mi and ma, mhi and mhā are optionally substituted; and in conjunction with this, aṭa is also substituted for as. For example, amhi.

55. Esu sa

55. In these cases, sa.

Esu [M 0.0240] mimesu asassa so hoti, pararūpabādhanatthaṃ. Asmi, amha asma. Bhavissatipaccaye –

In these cases of the endings mi and ma, sa is substituted for as to prevent coalescence with the following form. Examples: asmi, amha, asma. In the future tense suffix—

5,129. A+ā+ssaādīsu

5.129. In the case of a, ā, ssa, and so on.

Parokkhā a-ādo anajjatana ā-ādo kriyātipattissā-ādo bhavissatissatyādo ca atthissa bhu hoti. Ādesavidhānaṃ asassāpayogatthaṃ, kismiñci paccayavisese, tasmā asitabbantiādi na bhavati. Bhavissati, bhavissanti. Abhavā, abhavu. Kriyātipattiyaṃ bhuādese abhavissa, abhavissaṃsu iccādi. Eyyādimhi –

In the perfect tense, which has affixes beginning with a; in the aorist, with affixes beginning with ā; in the conditional, with affixes beginning with ssa; and in the future, with affixes beginning with ssati; the root bhū is substituted for the root as. The purpose of this substitution rule is to prevent the use of the root as with certain specific suffixes; therefore, forms such as asitanti, etc., do not occur. Examples: bhavissati, bhavissanti; abhavā, abhavu. In the conditional, when bhū is substituted, the forms are abhavissa, abhavissaṃsu, etc. In the optative, etc.—

50. Atthite+yyādicchannaṃ sa+su+sa+satha+saṃ+sāma

50. For the six endings of the optative mood, etc., of the root as, the substitutes are sa, su, sa, satha, saṃ, and sāma.

Asa=bhuvi+ccasmā paresaṃ eyyādicchannaṃ sādayo honti yathākkamaṃ. Pararūpe so assa, te assu. Tvaṃ assa, tumhe assatha. Ahaṃ assaṃ, mayaṃ assāma. Tvādimhi so atu, assa lope santhu, ayādese tvaṃ ahi, tumhe attha. Amhi, amha, sādese asmi asma. Bahulādhikārā ajjatane āsi, āsiṃsu, āsuṃ iccādīpi honti.

After the root as ('to be'), for the following six endings of the optative, etc., sa and the others are substituted respectively. With coalescence: so assa (he would be), te assu (they would be). Tvaṃ assa (you would be), tumhe assatha (you would be). Ahaṃ assaṃ (I would be), mayaṃ assāma (we would be). In the imperative, etc.: so atu; with elision of assa, santhu; with the substitution of aya, tvaṃ ahi, tumhe attha. The forms are amhi, amha; with the substitution of sa, they are asmi, asma. By the authority of the 'variously' rule, in the aorist, forms such as āsi, āsiṃsu, āsuṃ, etc., also occur.

Brū=vacane,

The root brū, in the sense of speaking.

36. Brūto tissīña

36. After brū, for ti, īña.

Brūto parassa tissa īña vā hoti. Vuddhiavādese lassa lope bravīti.

After the root brū, for the following ending ti, īña is optionally substituted. With vuddhi strengthening, the substitution of av, and the elision of la, the form is bravīti.

5,97. Na brūsso

5.97. Not o for brū.

Brūssa [M 0.0241] o na hoti byañjane. Brūti. Uvaṅādese brūvanti.

For the root brū, the substitution to o does not occur before a consonant. For example, brūti. With the substitution of uvaṅ, the form is brūvanti.

20. Tya+ntīnaṃ ṭa+ṭū

20. For ti and anti, ṭa and ṭū.

Āhā paresaṃ ti+antīnaṃ ṭa+ṭū honti. Ṭakārā sabbādesatthā. Atoyeva āhā paresaṃ tiantīnaṃ ṭaṭūvidhānañāpakā tiantīsu brūssa āho. Āha, āhu. Brūsi, brūtha. Brūmi, brūma iccādi. Bravissati. Abravi abravī, abravuṃ. Anajjatane abravā, abravu. Parokkhāyaṃ –

After āha, for the following endings ti and anti, ṭa and ṭū are substituted. The letter ṭ indicates total substitution. For this very reason, the rule prescribing ṭa and ṭū for the following ti and anti after āha indicates that in the context of ti and anti, āha is the substitute for brū. Examples: āha (he said), āhu (they said). Brūsi (you say), brūtha (you say). Brūmi (I say), brūma (we say), etc. Future: bravissati. Aorist: abravi, abravī, abravuṃ. Imperfect: abravā, abravu. In the perfect tense—

16. Aādīsvā+ho brūssa

16. For brū, āha is the substitute before endings beginning with a.

Brūssa āho hoti parokkhāaādīsu. Supine kira so āha, te āhu iccādi. Abravissa. Brave braveyya. Vuddhippaṭisedhe brūtu, bravantu iccādi.

For brū, āha is the substitute before the endings of the perfect tense, which begin with a. For example: supine kira so āha (it is said he spoke in a dream), te āhu (they said), etc. Conditional: abravissa. Optative: brave, braveyya. With the prohibition of vuddhi strengthening: brūtu, bravantu, etc.

Hana=hiṃsāyaṃ, timhi vikaraṇalope so hanati hanti. Te hananti iccādi. Kamme-ye nassa ññe pubbarūpaṃ, tena haññati, haññanti haññare. Tathā hanissati iccādi.

The root han, in the sense of 'to harm'. Before the ending ti, with the elision of the conjugational sign, the forms are hanati and hanti. For example, te hananti (they strike), etc. In the passive voice, before the suffix ya, the n becomes ññ through assimilation, hence: haññati, haññanti, haññare. Likewise, hanissati, etc.

67. Hanā cha+khā

67. After han, cha and khā.

Hanā ssāssa cha+khā vā honti. Paṭihaṃkhāmi paṭihanissāmi. Haṃchema hanissāma. Ahani, ahaniṃsūtiādi sabbattha yojetabbaṃ. Huvādayo

After the root han, for the future suffix ssa, cha and khā are optionally substituted. Examples: paṭihaṃkhāmi or paṭihanissāmi (I will strike back); haṃchema or hanissāma (we will strike). Forms such as ahani, ahaniṃsu, etc., should be applied in all tenses. The hu group of roots.

Hu=havane[M 0.0242]. Tyādīsu lo. “Parokkhāyañcā”ti caggahaṇena hu huti dvittaṃ, “kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā”ti hassa jo, lalopo vuddhi ca, juhoti aggiṃ, aññatra “yavā sare”ti vakāro, juhvati. Juhonti. Juhvanti. Juhosi juhvasi, juhotha juhvatha. Iccādi. Kamme – “dīgho sarassā”ti dīghe hūyati tena aggi iccādi. Juhissati, juhissanti. Ajuhavi ajuhosi, ajuhavuṃ ajuhaviṃsu ajuhavaṃsu ajuhosuṃ. Ajuhissa, ajuhissaṃssu. Juhe juheyya. Juhotu, juhontu iccādi.

The root hu, in the sense of 'offering'. Before ti, etc., there is elision of the conjugational sign. By the inclusion of ca in the rule 'Parokkhāyañca', hu is reduplicated. By the rule 'kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā', the h becomes j; with elision of la and vuddhi strengthening, the form is juhoti aggiṃ (he offers to the fire). Alternatively, by the rule 'yavā sare', a v is inserted, giving juhvati. Other forms: juhonti, juhvanti; juhosi, juhvasi; juhotha, juhvatha, etc. In the passive: by the rule 'dīgho sarassā', the vowel is lengthened, giving hūyati tena aggi (the fire is offered by him), etc. Future: juhissati, juhissanti. Aorist: ajuhavi, ajuhosi; ajuhavuṃ, ajuhaviṃsu, ajuhavaṃsu, ajuhosuṃ. Conditional: ajuhissa, ajuhissaṃsu. Optative: juhe, juheyya. Imperative: juhotu, juhontu, etc.

Hā=cāge, pure viya dvebhāvachādesalope “rasso pubbassā”ti pubbassa āssa rasso. Jahāti iccādi. Kamme – “aññādissā+ssī kye”ti kye āssa ī, hīyati iccādi. Jahissati. Ajahāsi, “dīghā īssa” iti si, pajahi, ajahiṃsu ajahaṃsu, pajahiṃsu pajahuṃ. Kamme-pahīyi pahīyittha. Ssādi+eyyādi+tvādīsupi ñeyyā.

The root hā, in the sense of 'to abandon'. As before, with reduplication, substitution of cha, and elision, by the rule 'rasso pubbassā', the preceding ā is shortened. Thus, jahāti, etc. In the passive, by the rule 'aññādissāssī kye', before the suffix kya, ā becomes ī, thus hīyati, etc. Future: jahissati. Aorist: ajahāsi; by 'dīghā īssa' with si, pajahi; ajahiṃsu or ajahaṃsu; pajahiṃsu or pajahuṃ. Passive aorist: pahīyi, pahīyittha. The forms for the future, optative, and imperative should also be understood.

Dā=dāne, dvibhāvarassattāni, lalopo, dadāti, dadanti iccādi. “Gamavadā” dinā dajjādese dajjati, dajjanti iccādi. Lasse+kāre dānaṃ deti iccādi.

The root dā, in the sense of 'giving'. With reduplication, shortening, and elision of la, the forms are dadāti, dadanti, etc. By the rule 'Gamavadā...', with the substitution of dajja, the forms are dajjati, dajjanti, etc. With the substitution of e for the ending, the form is dānaṃ deti (he gives a gift), etc.

22. Dāssa daṃ vā mimesva+dvitte

22. For dā, daṃ is optionally substituted before the endings mi and ma, when the root is not reduplicated.

Advitte vattamānassa dāssa daṃ hoti vā mimesu. Vaggantaṃ, dammi demi, damma dema. Īkāre dīyati iccādi. Anāgatatthe iñāgame saraṇopādi, dadissati, dadissanti. Dajjissati, dajjissanti. Lavikaraṇe [M 0.0243] dassati, dassanti. Ajjatane-adadi, adadiṃsu, adajji, adajjiṃsu, adāsi, adaṃsu. Anajjatane-adadā, adadu. Kālātipattiyaṃ-adadissa adajjissa, le adassa, dassaṃsu. Eyyādimhi-dade dadeyya dajje dajjeyya. “Ṭā”ti bahulādhikārā dajjādesā parassa eyyassa ṭā, dajjā, dajjuṃ dajjeyyaṃ dadeyyuṃ. Tvādīsu-dadātu, dadantu, dajjatu, dajjantu, lasse+kāre detu, dentu iccādi. Sabbattha kammepi yojanīyaṃ.

For the root dā in the present tense, when not reduplicated, daṃ is optionally substituted before the endings mi and ma. With the class nasal, the forms are dammi, demi; damma, dema. With the suffix ī (passive), dīyati, etc. In the future tense, with the iñ augment like in saraṇa, etc.: dadissati, dadissanti; dajjissati, dajjissanti. With the la conjugational sign: dassati, dassanti. In the aorist: adadi, adadiṃsu; adajji, adajjiṃsu; adāsi, adaṃsu. In the imperfect: adadā, adadu. In the conditional: adadissa, adajjissa; with the la sign, adassa, dassaṃsu. In the optative: dade, dadeyya; dajje, dajjeyya. By the authority of the 'variously' rule regarding ṭā, after the substitute dajja, the following eyya becomes ṭā, giving: dajjā, dajjuṃ, dajjeyyaṃ, dadeyyuṃ. In the imperative: dadātu, dadantu; dajjatu, dajjantu; with the substitution of e for the ending, detu, dentu, etc. This should be applied in the passive voice everywhere as well.

Dhā=dhāraṇe, tyādimhi caggahaṇena dvitte pubbākārassa rassatte lalope “catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā”ti pubbadhakārassa dakāre ca kate dadhāti, dadhanti. Pipubbo, “tadaminā” dinā āssa lopo, “dhāssa ho”ti dvitte parassa dhāssa hakāro, dvāraṃ pidahati, pidahanti. Lasse+kāre nidheti, nidhenti. Kamme-vidhīyati, vidhīyanti iccādi. Dhassati, pidahissati, paridahessati. Adhāsi, pidahi. Adhassa, pidahissa. Dadhe dadheyya, pidahe pidaheyya. Dadātu, pidahatu, nidhetu, nidhentu iccādi. (Juhotyādayo).

The root dhā, in the sense of 'to hold'. Before ti, etc., by the inclusion of ca, with reduplication, shortening of the preceding ā, elision of la, and by the rule 'catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā', the preceding dh becomes d, forming dadhāti, dadhanti. With the prefix pi, by the rule 'tadaminā...', the ā is elided; by 'dhāssa ho', in reduplication the second dhā becomes h, forming dvāraṃ pidahati (he closes the door), pidahanti. With the substitution of e for the ending: nidheti, nidhenti. In the passive: vidhīyati, vidhīyanti, etc. Future: dhassati, pidahissati, paridahessati. Aorist: adhāsi, pidahi. Conditional: adhassa, pidahissa. Optative: dadhe, dadheyya; pidahe, pidaheyya. Imperative: dadātu, pidahatu; nidhetu, nidhentu, etc. (This is the juhoti group).

Bhūvādi ca juhādi ca, huvādidhātavo ci+me;

Savuddhikabhūvādīhi, tidhā bhedaṃ upenti te.

The bhū group and the juhoti group, and the hu group of roots are these; with the bhū group which takes vuddhi, they undergo a threefold division.

(Bhūvādinayo.)

(The method of the bhū group.)

Adhunā [M 0.0244] vikaraṇapabhedapakāsanatthaṃ rudhādīnaṃ aṭṭhagaṇānaṃ kānici rūpāni udāhariyante –

Now, to illustrate the varieties of conjugational signs, some forms of the roots belonging to the eight groups beginning with 'rudh' are cited –

Rudha=āvaraṇe, tyādayo honti. Eva+muparipi sabbagaṇesu.

The root 'rudh' is in the sense of 'to obstruct'. The endings 'ti', etc., are applied. Thus also in all the subsequent groups.

5,19. Mañca rudhādīnaṃ

5,19. And the infix ṃ for the Rudhādi group.

Rudhādiko aparokkhesu kattuvihitamāna+nta+tyādīsu lo hoti mañca+ntasarā paro. Niggahītassa vaggantaṃ, “lahussupantassā”ti saṃyogattā na vuddhi. So maggaṃ rundhati, rundhanti iccādi. Kamme-nipubbo kyo dhassa cavagga+pubbarūpa+tatiyakkharajakārā, tena maggo nirujjhati iccādi. Iñāgame rundhissati, nirujjhissati. Arundhi, arundhiṃsu. Nirujjhittho, nirujjhi, nirujjhiṃsu. Arundhissa, arundhissaṃsu, nirujjhissa, nirujjhissaṃsu. Rundhe rundheyya, nirujjhe nirujjheyya. Rundhatu, rundhantu. Tvaṃ rundha rundhāhi. Nirujjhatu, nirujjhantu iccādi.

For the Rudhādi group, in the active voice endings such as 'ti', the infix 'ṃ' is inserted before the final consonant of the root. For the niggahīta (ṃ), the nasal of the same class as the following consonant is substituted. Due to the resulting consonant cluster, there is no vowel strengthening, according to the rule 'lahussupantassā'. He obstructs the path (rundhati), they obstruct (rundhanti), and so on. In the passive, with the prefix 'ni', the passive sign 'ya' is added; the 'dh' of the root and this 'ya' assimilate to 'jjha'. Hence, 'maggo nirujjhati' (the path is obstructed), and so on. In the future tense: 'rundhissati', 'nirujjhissati'. In the aorist: 'arundhi', 'arundhiṃsu'; 'nirujjhittho', 'nirujjhi', 'nirujjhiṃsu'. In the conditional: 'arundhissa', 'arundhissaṃsu'; 'nirujjhissa', 'nirujjhissaṃsu'. In the optative: 'rundhe', 'rundheyya'; 'nirujjhe', 'nirujjheyya'. In the imperative: 'rundhatu', 'rundhantu'; 'tvaṃ rundha', 'rundhāhi'; 'nirujjhatu', 'nirujjhantu', and so on.

Chida=dvedhākaraṇe, chindati, chindanti. Kamme-chijjati, chijjanti. Bhavissatipaccaye – “labha vasacchidā” dinā cchaṅādese checchati chindissati. Kamme-pubbarūpaṃ, chijjissati, chijjissanti. Achindi chindi, acchejji, acchejjiṃsu. Acchindissā achijjissā. Chinde chindeyya, chijje chijjeyya, chindatu, chindantu, chijjatu, chijjantu iccādi.

Chida: in the sense of dividing in two. 'chindati', 'chindanti'. In the passive: 'chijjati', 'chijjanti'. In the future tense, by the rule beginning with 'labha vasacchidā', with the substitution of 'ccha', the forms are 'checchati' and 'chindissati'. In the passive, with assimilation, 'chijjissati', 'chijjissanti'. Aorist: 'achindi', 'chindi'; 'acchejji', 'acchejjiṃsu'. Conditional: 'acchindissā', 'achijjissā'. Optative: 'chinde', 'chindeyya'; 'chijje', 'chijjeyya'. Imperative: 'chindatu', 'chindantu'; 'chijjatu', 'chijjantu', and so on.

Bhuja=pālanajjhohāresu, bhuñjati, bhuñjanti iccādi. Bhavissatimhi “bhuja+muca+vaca+visānaṃ kkhaṅa”ti dhātvantena saha ssassa [M 0.0245] kkhaṅādese vuddhi, bhokkhati, bhuñjissati, bhokkhanti, bhuñjissanti iccādi.

Bhuja: in the senses of protecting and eating. 'bhuñjati', 'bhuñjanti', and so on. In the future tense, by the rule 'bhuja+muca+vaca+visānaṃ kkhaṅa', 'kkha' is substituted for 'ssa' along with the final consonant of the root, and there is vowel strengthening (vuddhi), resulting in forms like 'bhokkhati', 'bhuñjissati', 'bhokkhanti', 'bhuñjissanti', and so on.

Muca=mocane, muccati, muccanti iccādi. Kamme-muccati, muccanti iccādi. (Rudhādinayo).

Muca: in the sense of releasing. 'muñcati', 'muñcanti', and so on. In the passive: 'muccati', 'muccanti', and so on. (This is the Rudhādi conjugation).

Diva=kīḷā vijigiṃsā vohāra juti thuti gatīsu,

Diva: in the senses of playing, desiring victory, transacting, shining, praising, and moving.

5,21. Divādīhi yaka

5,21. From the Divādi group, the suffix 'ya'.

Divādīhi kattari lavisaye yaka hoti. Kakāro kānubandhakāriyattho, eva+mupari ca. Vassa bakāre pubbarūpaṃ, so jutaṃ dibbati, dibbanti iccādi. Kamme-kye tena dibbati, dibbanti iccādi. Dibbissati, tena dibbissati. Adibbi dibbi. Tena adibbi dibbi. Adibbissa. Tena adibbissa. Dibbe dibbeyya. Tena dibbe dibbeyya. Dibbatu. Tena dibbatu iccādi.

From the Divādi group, in the active voice, in the domain of 'la'-endings, the suffix 'ya' occurs. The letter 'k' indicates the functions of a k-anubandha; this applies hereafter as well. The 'v' of the root becomes 'b'. He plays dice (jutaṃ dibbati), they play (dibbanti), and so on. In the passive, with the suffix 'ya', by him it is played (tena dibbati), they are played (dibbanti), and so on. Future: 'dibbissati'; by him it will be played, 'dibbissati'. Aorist: 'adibbi', 'dibbi'; by him it was played, 'adibbi', 'dibbi'. Conditional: 'adibbissa'; by him it would be played, 'adibbissa'. Optative: 'dibbe', 'dibbeyya'; by him it might be played, 'dibbe', 'dibbeyya'. Imperative: 'dibbatu'; by him let it be played, 'dibbatu', and so on.

Siva=tantusantāne, sibbati, sibbanti iccādi. Pada=gamane, upubbo, cavaggapubbarūpāni, uppajjati, uppajjare uppajjanti iccādi. Kammekye tena paṭipajjate iccādi. Bhāve-uppajjate tayā. Budha=avagamane, jhakārapubbarūpāni yakkharesu. Dhammaṃ bujjhati, bujjhare bujjhanti iccādi. Kamme-mayā dhammo bujjhate iccādi. Yudha=sampahāre, yujjhati+ccādi. Naha=bandhane, “hassa vipallāso”ti ye vipallāso, sannayhati+ccādi. Mana=ñāṇe, ññakāra+pubbarūpāni, maññati+ccādi. Tusa=tuṭṭhimhi, pubbarūpe tussati+ccādi. Sama=upasame, sammati+ccādi.

Siva: in the sense of sewing; 'sibbati', 'sibbanti', and so on. Pada: in the sense of going; with 'ud' preceding, and assimilation to the 'ca'-group, 'uppajjati', 'uppajjare', 'uppajjanti', and so on. In the passive with 'ya', by that, 'paṭipajjate', and so on. In the impersonal voice: 'uppajjate' by you. Budha: in the sense of understanding; with assimilation to 'jjha' with the 'ya' suffix. One understands the Dhamma, they understand, they understand, and so on. In the passive: the Dhamma is understood by me, and so on. Yudha: in the sense of fighting; 'yujjhati', and so on. Naha: in the sense of binding; by the rule 'hassa vipallāso', there is metathesis of 'h' and 'y', 'sannayhati', and so on. Mana: in the sense of knowing; with assimilation to 'ñña', 'maññati', and so on. Tusa: in the sense of satisfaction; with assimilation, 'tussati', and so on. Sama: in the sense of being calm; 'sammati', and so on.

Jana=janane[M 0.0246], “janissā”ti ā hoti kānubandhe bahulādhikārā, so jāyati, jāyanti+ccādi. Kamme-janituṃ payojetīti “payojakabyāpāre ṇāpi ce”ti ṇimhi “aññatrāpī”ti vuddhipaṭisedhe kyamhi “dīgho sarassā”ti dīghe ca kate tena janīyati, janīyanti iccādi. So jāyissati. Tena janissati. So ajāyi, tena ajanīyi. So ajāyissa, tena ajanīyissa. So jāye jāyeyya, tena janīyeyya. So jāyatu, tena janīyatu iccādi. (Divādinayo).

Jana: in the sense of generating or being born. By the rule 'janissā', 'ā' is substituted for the final vowel of the root before a suffix with a 'k'-anubandha, by the governing rule of 'bahula' (variously). Thus, he is born (so jāyati), they are born (jāyanti), and so on. In the passive, when the suffix 'ya' is added, the vowel is lengthened by the rule 'dīgho sarassā'; thus, by him it is produced (tena janīyati), they are produced (janīyanti), and so on. He will be born (so jāyissati); by him it will be produced (tena janissati). He was born (so ajāyi); by him it was produced (tena ajanīyi). He would be born (so ajāyissa); by him it would be produced (tena ajanīyissa). He might be born (so jāye, jāyeyya); by him it might be produced (tena janīyeyya). Let him be born (so jāyatu); by him let it be produced (tena janīyatu), and so on. (This is the Divādi conjugation).

Tuda=byathane,

Tuda: in the sense of afflicting.

5,22. Tudādīhi ko

5,22. From the Tudādi group, the suffix 'a'.

Tudādīhi kattari lavisaye ko hoti. Tudati, tudanti iccādi. Kamme-tudyati tujjati, tudyare tudyanti, tujjare tujjanti+ccādi. Tathā tudissati tujjissati. Atudi, atudiṃsu, atujji. Atudissa atujjissa, tudeyya tujjeyya. Tudatu, tudantu, tujjatu iccādi.

From the Tudādi group, in the active voice, in the domain of 'la'-endings, the suffix 'a' occurs. 'Tudati', 'tudanti', and so on. In the passive: 'tudyati', 'tujjati', 'tudyare', 'tudyanti', 'tujjare', 'tujjanti', and so on. Similarly, in the future: 'tudissati', 'tujjissati'. Aorist: 'atudi', 'atudiṃsu', 'atujji'. Conditional: 'atudissa', 'atujjissa'. Optative: 'tudeyya', 'tujjeyya'. Imperative: 'tudatu', 'tudantu', 'tujjatu', and so on.

Visa=pavesane, papubbo. So gāmaṃ pavisati iccādi. Kamme-pavisīyati iccādi. Pavisissati. Pavisīyissati. Pāvisi, īmhi “bhujamucā” dinā yogavibhāgā kkhaṅa. Pāvisi, pavisi pāvekkhi, pathaviṃ pāvisiṃsu pavisiṃsu. Pāvisīyi. Pāvisissa pavisissa. Pāvisīyissa. Pavise paviseyya, vikaraṇalopo [M 0.0247] pavisīyeyya. Pavisatu, pavisīyatu iccādi. Nudati. Disa=uccāraṇe, uddissati, likhati, tusati iccādi. (Tudādinayo).

Visa: in the sense of entering; with 'pa' preceding. He enters the village, and so on. In the passive: 'pavisīyati', and so on. Future: 'pavisissati'; (passive) 'pavisīyissati'. Aorist: 'pāvisi'. By splitting the rule beginning with 'bhujamucā', the substitution 'kkha' occurs before the 'ī'-aorist ending, forming 'pāvekkhi'. The forms are 'pāvisi', 'pavisi', 'pāvekkhi'; they entered the earth ('pathaviṃ pāvisiṃsu', 'pavisiṃsu'). Passive aorist: 'pāvisīyi'. Conditional: 'pāvisissa', 'pavisissa'; (passive) 'pāvisīyissa'. Optative: 'pavise', 'paviseyya'; (passive) 'pavisīyeyya'. Imperative: 'pavisatu'; (passive) 'pavisīyatu', and so on. 'Nudati'. Disa: in the sense of uttering; 'uddissati', 'likhati', 'tusati', and so on. (This is the Tudādi conjugation).

Ji=jaye,

Ji: in the sense of conquering.

5,23. Jyādīhi knā

5,23. From the Ji-group, the suffix 'knā'.

Jyādīhi kattari lavisaye knā hoti. Na vuddhi. Kilese jināti, jinanti. Tena kileso jīyati, jīyanti, kye dīgho. Jinissati, jinissanti. Ajini jini. Ajīyi, ajīyittha. Ajinissa. Ajīyissa. Jineyya. Jinātu iccādi. Ci=caye, tathā cināti, cinanti iccādi.

From the Ji-group of roots, the affix 'knā' occurs in the active voice in the domain of 'la'-endings. There is no vowel strengthening. He conquers defilements (kilese jināti), they conquer (jinanti). Passive: By him a defilement is conquered (tena kileso jīyati), they are conquered (jīyanti); there is lengthening of the vowel before the passive sign 'ya'. Future: He will conquer (jinissati), they will conquer (jinissanti). Aorist: He conquered (ajini, jini). He was conquered (ajīyi, ajīyittha). Conditional: He would conquer (ajinissa). He would be conquered (ajīyissa). Optative: He might conquer (jineyya). Imperative: Let him conquer (jinātu), etc. Ci: to accumulate; similarly 'cināti', 'cinanti', etc.

Ñā=avabodhane,

Ñā: in the sense of understanding.

5,120. Ñāssa ne jā

5,120. For 'ñā', 'jā' is substituted when 'na' follows.

Ñādhātussa jā hoti nakāre. Vijānāti.

For the root 'ñā', 'jā' is substituted when the letter 'na' follows. Example: 'vijānāti'.

61. Ñāssa sanāssa nāyo timhi

61. 5,121. For 'ñā' and 'sanā', 'nāya' is substituted when 'ti' follows.

Sanāssa ñāssa nāyo vā hoti timhi. Nāyati, vijānāti iccādi. Kamme-viññāyati iccādi. Kye “āsse cā”ti ettha “āsse”ti yogavibhāgā āssa e hoti, yassa dvitte ñeyyati, ñeyyanti iccādi. Vijānissati, vijānissanti. Kamme – “kyassa sse”ti kyalope rasse ca kate ñāssati, ñāssanti, viññāyissati, paññāyissati.

For 'sanā' and 'ñā', 'nāya' is optionally substituted when 'ti' follows. Examples: 'nāyati', 'vijānāti', etc. In the passive: 'viññāyati', etc. When the passive sign 'ya' follows, by splitting the rule 'āsse ca' here as 'āsse', 'ā' becomes 'e', and with doubling of 'y', forms like 'ñeyyati', 'ñeyyanti', etc. are derived. Future: 'vijānissati', 'vijānissanti'. Passive future: By the rule 'kyassa sse', with the elision of 'ya' and shortening of the vowel, forms like 'ñāssati', 'ñāssanti', 'viññāyissati', 'paññāyissati' are derived.

65. Ssassa hi kamme

65. 5,122. For 'ssa', 'hi' is substituted in the passive.

Ñāto parassa ssassa hi vā hoti kamme, paññāyihiti, paññāyihinti. Añāgame samajāni, saṃjāni, saṃjāniṃsu. Samajā- niṃsu[M 0.0248]. Kamme-paññāyi, paññāyiṃsu. Ajānissa. Kamme-aññāyissa.

After 'ñā', 'ssa' optionally becomes 'hi' in the passive. Examples: 'paññāyihiti', 'paññāyihinti'. With the 'a'-augment (in the aorist): 'samajāni', 'saṃjāni', 'saṃjāniṃsu', 'samajāniṃsu'. Passive aorist: 'paññāyi', 'paññāyiṃsu'. Conditional: 'ajānissa'. Passive conditional: 'aññāyissa'.

63. Eyyassi+yāñā vā

63. 5,123. For 'eyya', 'iyā' and 'ñā' are optional substitutes.

Ñāto parassa eyyassa iyā+ñā honti vā. Jāniyā.

After 'ñā', for the following 'eyya', 'iyā' and 'ñā' are optional substitutes. Example: 'jāniyā'.

62. Ñāmhi jaṃ

62. 5,124. When 'ñā' follows, 'ja' is substituted for the root.

Ñādese sanāssa ñāssa jaṃ vā hoti. Jaññā, jāneyya, jāneyyuṃ. Kamme-paññāyeyya, paññāyeyyuṃ. Vijānātu, vijānanthu. Kamme-viññāyatu iccādi.

When 'ñā' is the substitute for 'eyya', 'ja' is optionally substituted for the roots 'sanā' and 'ñā'. Examples: 'jaññā', 'jāneyya', 'jāneyyuṃ'. Passive: 'paññāyeyya', 'paññāyeyyuṃ'. Imperative: 'vijānātu', 'vijānanthu'. Passive imperative: 'viññāyatu', etc.

Mā=māne, “ā ī ssādīnaṃ byañjanassiña” iti iñaiti yogavibhāgā iñāgame pubbasaralopo, mināti, minanti. Kamme-mīyati iccādi. Lū=chedane, “kṇāknāsu rasso”ti dhātussa rasso, lunāti, lunanti. Kamme-lūyati iccādi. Dhu=kampane, dhunāti iccādi. (Jyādinayo).

Mā = in pride. By splitting the rule 'ā ī ssādīnaṃ byañjanassiña' into 'iña iti', there is the augment 'iñ' and elision of the preceding vowel: mināti, minanti. In the passive: mīyati, etc. Lū = in cutting. By 'kṇāknāsu rasso', the root vowel is shortened: lunāti, lunanti. In the passive: lūyati, etc. Dhu = in shaking: dhunāti, etc. (The method for the Jyādi group).

Kī=dabbavinīmaye,

Kī = in exchange of goods,

24. Kyādīhi kṇā

24. From the Kyādi class of roots, the affix kṇā occurs.

Kyādīhi lavisaye kṇā hoti. “Kṇāknāsu rasso”ti rasse kiṇāti, kiṇanti iccādi. Kamme-vikkīyati, vikkīyanti. Vikkiṇissati, vikkiṇissanti. Vikkīyissati, vikkīyissanti. Akiṇi, vikkiṇi, vikkīyi. Akiṇissa, vikkiṇissa. Vikkiṇe vikkiṇeyya.

From the Kyādi class of roots, the affix kṇā occurs in the verbal sphere. By 'kṇāknāsu rasso', with shortening, forms like kiṇāti, kiṇanti, etc., are derived. In the passive: vikkīyati, vikkīyanti. Future: Vikkiṇissati, vikkiṇissanti. Passive future: Vikkīyissati, vikkīyissanti. Aorist: Akiṇi, vikkiṇi, vikkīyi. Conditional: Akiṇissa, vikkiṇissa. Potential: Vikkiṇe, vikkiṇeyya.

Vikkīye[M 0.0249]. Vikkīyeyya. Vikkiṇātu, vikkiṇantu, vikkīyatu, vikkīyantu iccādi. Su=savane, suṇāti, suṇanti iccādi.

Vikkīye, vikkīyeyya. Imperative: Vikkiṇātu, vikkiṇantu, vikkīyatu, vikkīyantu, etc. Su = in hearing: suṇāti, suṇanti, etc.

Saka=sattiyaṃ,

Saka = in power, in ability,

5,121. Sakā+pānaṃ kuka+ku ṇe

5.121. For Saka, the augments āpāna, kuka, and ku occur when ṇe is present.

Saka+āpānaṃ kuka+kuiccete āgamā honti ṇe. Sakkuṇāti, sakkuṇanti. Sakkunāti, sakkunanti.

For Saka, these augments āpāna, kuka, and ku occur when ṇe is present. Examples: Sakkuṇāti, sakkuṇanti. Sakkunāti, sakkunanti.

53. Sse vā

53. Optionally before sse.

Sakasmā kṇāssa kkho vā hoti sse. Sakkhissati, sakkhissanti.

After Saka, kkho optionally occurs for kṇā when sse follows. Examples: Sakkhissati, sakkhissanti.

58. Sakā kṇāssa kha īādo

58. For Saka, kha occurs for kṇā when ī, etc., follow.

Sakasmā kṇāssa kho vā hoti īādīsu. Asakkhi sakkhi, sakkhiṃsu. Asakkhissa, asakkhissaṃsu. Sakkuṇe sakkuṇeyya. Sakkuṇātu, sakkuṇantu.

After Saka, kho optionally occurs for kṇā when ī, etc., are present. Aorist: Asakkhi, sakkhi, sakkhiṃsu. Conditional: Asakkhissa, asakkhissaṃsu. Potential: Sakkuṇe, sakkuṇeyya. Imperative: Sakkuṇātu, sakkuṇantu.

Apa=pāpuṇane, papubbo, “sakā+pānaṃ kuka+ku ṇe”ti kukate sampatti pāpuṇāti, pāpuṇanti iccādi. Kammepāpīyati, pāpīyanti. Pāpuṇissati, pāpuṇissanti. Kamme-pāpīyissati, pāpīyissanti. Pāpuṇi, pāpuṇiṃsu. Kamme-pāpīyi, pāpīyittha. Apāpuṇissa. Kamme-apāpīyissa. Pāpuṇe, pāpuṇeyya. Kamme-pāpīyeyya. Pāpuṇātu, pāpuṇantu. Kamme-pāpīyatu iccādi. (Kyādinayo).

Apa = in reaching, prefixed by pa. By the rule 'sakāpānaṃ kukaku ṇe', when the augment 'kuka' is applied, the result is pāpuṇāti, pāpuṇanti, etc. In the passive: pāpīyati, pāpīyanti. Future: Pāpuṇissati, pāpuṇissanti. Passive future: Pāpīyissati, pāpīyissanti. Aorist: Pāpuṇi, pāpuṇiṃsu. Passive aorist: Pāpīyi, pāpīyittha. Conditional: Apāpuṇissa. Passive conditional: Apāpīyissa. Potential: Pāpuṇe, pāpuṇeyya. Passive potential: Pāpīyeyya. Imperative: Pāpuṇātu, pāpuṇantu. Passive imperative: Pāpīyatu, etc. (The method for the Kyādi group).

Su=savane,

Su = in hearing,

25. Svādīhi kṇo

25. From the Svādi class of roots, the affix kṇo occurs.

Suādīhi [M 0.0250] lavisaye kṇo hoti. Kānubandhattā na vuddhi. Dhammaṃ suṇoti. Parassaralope suṇonti. Kamme-kye dīghe sūyati, sūyanti. Dvitte suyyati suyyanti+ccādi. Iñāgame suṇissati, suṇissanti. Kamme-kyalope vuddhi. Sossati, sossanti iccādi. Asuṇi suṇi, asuṇiṃsu suṇiṃsu.

From the Su-ādi group of roots, the affix kṇo occurs in the verbal sphere. Because 'ka' is an anubandha, there is no vuddhi. Dhammaṃ suṇoti (He hears the Dhamma). With elision of the following vowel: suṇonti. In the passive, when 'ya' follows, there is lengthening: sūyati, sūyanti. With reduplication: suyyati, suyyanti, etc. With the iñ-augment: suṇissati, suṇissanti. In the passive, with the elision of 'kya', vuddhi occurs. Alternative future forms are sossati, sossanti, etc. Aorist: Asuṇi, suṇi; asuṇiṃsu, suṇiṃsu.

60. Tesu suto kṇo+kṇānaṃ roṭa

60. In those forms, for kṇo and kṇā after Su, 'roṭa' is the substitute.

Tesu īādīsu suto paresaṃ kṇo+kṇānaṃ roṭa vā hoti. Rakāro anubandho. Ṭo sabbādesattho. Ussa lope dvittaṃ īssa si ca. Assosi, assosiṃsu. “Iṃssa ca siña”ti yogavibhāgā siña, assosiṃsu, paccassosuṃ. Asuyi, asuyittha. Asuṇissa, tena asuyissa. Suṇe suṇeyya, suṇeyyaṃ. Tena sūye sūyeyya. Suṇātu, suṇantu. Sūyatu, sūyantu iccādi.

In those aorist forms beginning with 'ī', for the following 'kṇo' and 'kṇā' after 'Su', 'roṭa' is optionally the substitute. The letter 'ra' is an anubandha. 'Ṭo' indicates a complete substitution. With the elision of 'u', doubling, and 'si' for 'ī', the forms Assosi, assosiṃsu are derived. By splitting the rule 'Iṃssa ca siña' into 'siña iti', the forms assosiṃsu, paccassosuṃ are derived. Aorist passive: Asuyi, asuyittha. Conditional: Asuṇissa; by that rule, asuyissa. Potential: Suṇe, suṇeyya, suṇeyyaṃ; by that rule, sūye, sūyeyya. Imperative: Suṇātu, suṇantu. Sūyatu, sūyantu, etc.

Gi=sadde, giṇoti. Giṇanti. Tvaṃ giṇosi. Giṇissati, giṇissanti. Agiṇissa. Giṇeyya. Giṇotu iccādi. Vu=saṃvaraṇe, āvuṇoti, āvuṇanti. Āvuṇosi iccādi. Sesesupi yojetabbaṃ. (Svādinayo).

Gi = in sound: giṇoti, giṇanti. Tvaṃ giṇosi. Future: Giṇissati, giṇissanti. Conditional: Agiṇissa. Potential: Giṇeyya. Imperative: Giṇotu, etc. Vu = in covering: āvuṇoti, āvuṇanti. Āvuṇosi, etc. The rest should be similarly applied. (The method for the Svādi group).

Tana=vitthāre,

Tana = in expansion,

26. Tanāditvo

26. From the Tanādi class, the affix 'o' occurs.

Tanādito kattari lavisaye o hoti. Kittiṃ tanoti, tanonti iccādi.

From the Tanādi group, in the active voice and in the verbal sphere, the affix 'o' occurs. For example: kittiṃ tanoti (he spreads fame), tanonti (they spread fame), etc.

76. Ovikaraṇassu paracchakke

76. For the 'o' vikaraṇa, 'u' occurs in the attanopada context.

Ovikaraṇassa [M 0.0251] u hoti paracchakkavisaye. Tanute, tanvante. Tanuse, tanuvhe. Tanve, tanvamhe. Kamme –

For the 'o' vikaraṇa, 'u' occurs in the attanopada context. Examples: tanute (he spreads), tanvante (they spread); tanuse (you spread), tanuvhe (you all spread); tanve (I spread), tanvamhe (we spread). In the passive voice –

5,138. Tanassā vā

5.138. For tan, optionally 'ā'.

Tanassa vā ā hoti kye. Papubbo, patāyati. Pataññati, patāyare patāyanti pataññare pataññanti+ccādi. Tathā vikaraṇalope iñāgame ca tanissati, tanissanti. Patāyissati. Atani, ataniṃsu. Atanissa. Patāyissa. Taneyya, taneyyuṃ. Tanotu, tanontu iccādi.

For tan, optionally 'ā' occurs before 'kya'. With the prefix pa-: patāyati, pataññati; patāyare, patāyanti, pataññare, pataññanti, etc. Similarly, with the elision of the vikaraṇa and the addition of the 'iñ' augment: tanissati, tanissanti; patāyissati. Aorist: atani, ataniṃsu. Conditional: atanissa; patāyissa. Potential: taneyya, taneyyuṃ. Imperative: tanotu, tanontu, etc.

Kara=karaṇe,

Kara = in doing,

5,177. Karassa sossa kubba+kuru+kayirā

5.177. For the 'o' of 'kara', the substitutes are 'kubba', 'kuru', and 'kayirā'.

Karassa sa okārassa kubbādayo vā honti nta+māna+tyādīsu. Kubbati, kubbanti. Karoti, karonti. Karosi, karotha.

For the 'o' of 'kara', the substitutes 'kubba', etc., optionally occur before endings such as 'nta', 'māna', 'ti', etc. Examples: Kubbati, kubbanti. Regular forms: Karoti, karonti; Karosi, karotha.

23. Karassa sossa kuṃ

23. For the 'o' of 'kara', the substitute is 'kuṃ'.

Karassa sa okārassa kuṃ vā hoti mimesu. Kummi karomi. Kumma karoma. Paracchakke kurute kubbate, kubbante iccādi. Kayirati, kayiranti iccādi. Kamme-kyassa dvitte īssa rasso, kariyyati, karīyati vā iccādi. “Tavaggavaraṇā” dinā [M 0.0252] ye rassa yakāre kayyati, kayyanti. Bahulādhakārā kamme kvaci iminā kayirādese tena kayirati, kayiranti iccādi. Bhavissatimhi –

For the root kara with its o vikaraṇa, kuṃ is optionally substituted before the mi and ma endings. Examples: kummi for karomi (I do); kumma for karoma (we do). In the attanopada: kurute, kubbate, kubbante, and so on. Kayirati, kayiranti, and so on. In the passive, when the consonant before ya is doubled, the long ī is shortened, resulting in kariyyati, or optionally karīyati, and so on. By the rule Tavaggavaraṇā, etc., ra is assimilated to the following ya, resulting in kayyati, kayyanti. Due to the governing rule of bahula, in the passive, sometimes by this rule the substitution kayira occurs, resulting in kayirati, kayiranti, and so on. In the future tense –

25. Hāssa cā+haṅa ssena

25. And hā and āhaṅa with ssa.

Karassa sossa hāssa ca āhaṅa vā hoti ssena saha. Kāhati, kāhanti iccādi. Iñāgame kāhiti, kāhinti iccādi. Āhaṅādesābhāvapakkhe karissati, karissanti iccādi. Ajjatane –

For the root kara, the future suffix ssa is optionally changed to hā or āhaṅa. Examples: kāhati (he will do), kāhanti (they will do), and so on. With the i augment: kāhiti, kāhinti, and so on. When this substitution does not occur, the forms are karissati, karissanti, and so on. In the aorist tense –

24. Kā īādīsu

24. Kā before ī and so on.

Karassa sa okārassa kā hoti vā īādīsu.

For the root kara with its o vikaraṇa, kā is optionally substituted before ī and the following endings.

44. Dīghā īssa

44. After a long vowel, for ī.

Dīghato parassa īssa si vā hoti. Akāsi. Īlope akā, akaṃsu. Ossa siādese akāsi. Siñāgame akāsittha. Akāsi, akāsiṃ, akāsimha. Aññatra akarikari, akariṃsu kariṃsu akaṃsu iccādi. Tena akarīyi iccādi. Akarissa iccādi. Kamme-akarīyissa iccādi. Eyyādimhi “kvaci vikaraṇānaṃ”ti ovikaraṇalope karekareyya, kareyyuṃ iccādi. Kubbe kubbeyya iccādi.

For the ī that follows a long vowel, si is an optional substitute. Example: akāsi (he did). With the elision of ī: akā, akaṃsu. With the substitution of si for ī: akāsi. With the si augment: akāsittha. Akāsi (he did), akāsiṃ (I did), akāsimha (we did). Elsewhere: akari, akariṃsu, kariṃsu, akaṃsu, and so on. Hence, akarīyi, and so on. Akarissa, and so on. In the passive: akarīyissa, and so on. In the optative, by the rule kvaci vikaraṇānaṃ, with the elision of the o vikaraṇa: kareyya, kareyyuṃ, and so on. Kubbe, kubbeyya, and so on.

71. Ṭā

71. Ṭā

Kayirā parassa eyyassa ṭā hoti. So kayirā.

After kayirā, the following eyya becomes ā. Example: So kayirā (he should do).

70. Kayire+yyasse+yyumādīnaṃ

70. Of eyya, eyyuṃ, and so on, after kayirā.

Kayirā [M 0.0253] parassa eyyumādīnaṃ eyyassa lopo hoti. Kayiruṃ. Tvaṃ kayirāsi, kayirātha. Kayirāmi, kayirāma.

After kayirā, the eyya of eyyuṃ and the following endings is elided. Examples: kayiruṃ (they should do); tvaṃ kayirāsi (you should do), kayirātha (you all should do); kayirāmi (I should do), kayirāma (we should do).

72. Ethassā

72. For etha, ā.

Kayirā parasse+thassa ā hotītiādissa essa ā hoti. Kayirātha dhīro. Kamme-kariyeyya, kariyeyyu+miccādi. Karotu kurutu vā, kubbantu karontu iccādi. Paracchakke-kurutaṃ, kubbantaṃ. Kurussu karassu iccādi. “Eona+ma vaṇṇe”ti akāro. Kuruvho, kubbe, kubbāmase. Kamme-karīyatu iccādi.

After kayirā, for the following etha, ā is substituted; that is, for the initial e, ā is substituted. Example: kayirātha dhīro (the wise one should do). In the passive: kariyeyya, kariyeyyuṃ, and so on. Imperative: karotu or kurutu; kubbantu, karontu, and so on. In the attanopada: kurutaṃ, kubbantaṃ. Kurussu, karassu, and so on. By the rule E ona ma vaṇṇe, the letter a occurs. Kuruvho, kubbe, kubbāmase. In the passive: karīyatu, and so on.

5,133. Karotissa kho

5.133. For karoti, kho.

Pādito parassa karassa kvaci kha hoti. Abhisaṅkharoti iccādi. Sabbattha yojetabbaṃ. “Tadaminā”dinā khādese abhisaṃkhāsīti viseso. Saka=sattiyaṃ, sakkoti iccādi. Apa=pāpuṇane, papubbo, pappoti iccādi. (Tanādinayo).

For the root kara following a prefix, kha is sometimes substituted. Example: abhisaṅkharoti, and so on. This should be applied in all cases. By the rule Tadaminā, etc., with the substitution of kha, abhisaṃkhāsi is a special form. The root saka is in the sense of 'power', for example, sakkoti, and so on. The root āp is in the sense of 'attaining', preceded by the prefix pa, for example, pappoti, and so on. (End of the Tanādi section).

Cura=theyye,

The root cura in the sense of 'theft'.

1,15. Curādito ṇi

1.15. After the curādi group, ṇi.

Curādīhi kriyatthehi sakatthe ṇi paro hoti. “Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā”ti vikappena lo. Dhanaṃ corayati coreti iccādi. Kamme-corīyati iccādi. Corayissati coressati [M 0.0254] iccādi. Kamme-corīyissati iccādi. Acorayi corayi acoresi coresi iccādi. Acorayissa iccādi. Kamme-acorīyissa iccādi. Coraye corayeyya iccādi. Coretu corentu iccādi.

After the roots of the curādi group, which have the sense of action, the suffix ṇi follows in their own meaning. By the rule Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā, there is optional elision. Examples: dhanaṃ corayati (he steals wealth), coreti (he steals), and so on. In the passive: corīyati, and so on. Future: corayissati, coressati, and so on. In the passive future: corīyissati, and so on. Aorist: acorayi, corayi, acoresi, coresi, and so on. Conditional: acorayissa, and so on. In the passive conditional: acorīyissa, and so on. Optative: coraye, corayeyya, and so on. Imperative: coretu, corentu, and so on.

Cinta=cintāyaṃ, saṃyogattā na vuddhi, cinteti cintayati, cintenti. Kamme-cintīyati, cintīyanti iccādi. Manta=guttabhāsane, manteti mantayati iccādi. Pāla=rakkhaṇe, so dhammaṃ pāleti pālayati. Tena pālīyati+ccādi. (Curādinayo).

The root cint is in the sense of 'thinking'; due to the preceding conjunct consonant, there is no vuddhi strengthening: cinteti (he thinks), cintayati (he thinks), cintenti (they think). In the passive: cintīyati (it is thought), cintīyanti (they are thought), and so on. The root mant is in the sense of 'secret consultation': manteti (he consults), mantayati (he consults), and so on. The root pāl is in the sense of 'protecting': so dhammaṃ pāleti (he protects the Dhamma), pālayati. Hence, the passive pālīyati (it is protected), and so on. (End of the Curādi section).

Bhūvādi ca rudhādi ca, divādi ca tudādayo;

Jyādī kiyādī svādī ca, tanādī ca curādayo.

The Bhūvādi group and the Rudhādi group, the Divādi group and the Tudādi group; the Juhotyādi group, the Kriyādi group, and the Svādi group; the Tanādi group and the Curādi group.

(Vikaraṇavidhānaṃ).

(The Section on Vikaraṇas).

5,1. Tija+mānehi kha+sā khamā+vīmaṃsāsu

5.1. After tij and mān, the suffixes kha and sa occur in the sense of 'patience' and 'investigation' respectively.

Khantiyaṃ tijā, vīmaṃsāyaṃ mānā ca kha+sapaccayā honti yathākkamaṃ. Tija=nisāne, akārassā+payogo. Khe “lahussupantassā”ti patte+kārassa “aññatrāpī”ti paṭisedho. Yakāravajjitabyañjanassa “pararūpa+mayakāre byañjane”ti pararūpañca. “Catutthadutiyā” dinā paṭhamakkharakakāre ca “khachasāna+mekassaro+di dve”ti tikkha tikkha iti dvibhāve “lopo+nādibyañjanassā”tiādito+ññassa byañjanassa lope ca kate titikkhādhātuto tyādipaccaya+lavikaraṇāni. Titikkhati iccādi purimasamaṃ[M 0.0255]. Kamme-titikkhīyati iccādi. Ito paraṃ kammodāharaṇaṃ na karissāma.

From the root tij in the sense of patience, and from mān in the sense of investigation, the suffixes kha and sa occur respectively. The root tij means 'to sharpen'; its a is not used. In the case of the suffix kha, when the strengthening of the vowel i is due by the rule lahussupantassa, it is prohibited by aññatrāpi. For a consonant not followed by ya, assimilation occurs by the rule pararūpaṃ ayakāre byañjane. By the rule Catutthadutiyā, etc., the first letter becomes ka, and by khachasānamekassaro'di dve, there is reduplication as tikkha tikkha, and then by lopo'nādibyañjanassa, etc., the non-initial consonant is elided. From the resulting root titikkha, the ti, etc., endings and the a vikaraṇa are applied. The forms titikkhati, etc., are similar to the previous examples. In the passive: titikkhīyati, etc. Henceforth, we shall not provide examples for the passive voice.

Māna=pūjāyaṃ+timasmā sapaccaya, dvittādimhi kate “mānassa vī parassa ca maṃ”ti pubbamānassa vī ca paramānassa mañca hoti. Vīmaṃsadhātuto tipaccayādimhi kate vīmaṃsati iccādi. Titikkhissati, vīmaṃsissati iccādi. Eva+muparipi ajjatanādīsupi yojetabbaṃ. Payojakattā ṇi, “ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā”ti lavikaraṇaṃ, tejayati tejeti. Tathā curādittā na lavikaraṇaṃ, mānayati māneti.

The root mān is in the sense of 'honoring'; from this, the suffix sa is added. When reduplication and other operations are performed, by the rule mānassa vī parassa ca maṃ, the first māna becomes vī and the second becomes maṃ. From the resulting root vīmaṃsa, when the suffix ti, etc., is applied, the form is vīmaṃsati, and so on. Future forms are titikkhissati, vīmaṃsissati, and so on. In this way, it should also be applied to the aorist and other tenses. In the causative, the suffix ṇi is added, and by the rule Ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā, the a vikaraṇa is optional, resulting in tejayati, tejeti. Likewise, for mān, since it belongs to the curādi group, there is no a vikaraṇa, resulting in mānayati, māneti.

5,2. Kitā tikicchā+saṃsayesu cho

5.2. After the root kit, the suffix cha occurs in the sense of 'healing' and 'doubt'.

Tikicchāyaṃ saṃsaye ca vattamānā kitā cho hoti. Kita=nivāse, chapaccaye pubbeva pararūpādimhi ca kate “kitassā+saṃsaye vā”ti dvitte pubbassa tiādese tikicchadhātuto tyādayo. Tikicchati, tikicchanti+ccādi. Vipubbato kitā chappaccayādimhi kate “kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā”ti dvitte pubbassa kassa co. Vicikicchati, vicikicchanti+ccādi. Payojakattā ketayati+ccādi purimasamaṃ.

From the root kit, when it means 'healing' or 'doubt', the suffix cha occurs. The root kit means 'to dwell'. When the suffix cha is applied and assimilation, etc., has been performed, then by the rule kitassa asaṃsaye vā, in reduplication, the first syllable is substituted by ti. From the resulting root tikiccha, the ti, etc., endings are applied. Thus: tikicchati, tikicchanti, and so on. From the root kit preceded by vi, when the suffix cha, etc., is applied, then by the rule kavaggahānaṃ cavaggajā, in reduplication, the first ka becomes ca. Thus: vicikicchati, vicikicchanti, and so on. In the causative, ketayati, etc., is formed similarly to the previous examples.

5,3. Nindāyaṃ gupa+badhā bassa bho ca

5.3. In the sense of censure, after gup and badh, cha occurs, and ba becomes bha.

Nindāyaṃ gupa+badhehi cho hoti bassa bho ca. Gupa=rakkhane+tīmasmā chappaccaye “aññatrāpī”ti ottābhāve ca pararūpādimhi “kavaggahā” dinā gassa je ca kate “gupissussā”ti dvitte pubbassa ussa i hoti. Tyādi+lavikaraṇādimhi [M 0.0256] jigucchati iccādi. Nindāyaṃ-badha=bandhane+tīmasmā chappaccaye ca imināva bassa bhakāre ca pararūpe paṭhamakkhare bhacchabhacchaiti dvitte anādibyañjanassa lope “catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā”ti dvitte pubbassa bhassa bakāre “khachasesvassī”ti ikāre dīghe ca kate bībhacchadhātuto tyādayo honti. Bībhacchati, bībhacchanti iccādi. Aññatra gopeti+ccādi.

In the sense of censure, after the roots gup and badh, the suffix cha occurs, and ba is substituted by bha. The root gup means 'to protect'. From this, with the suffix cha, and with assimilation, etc., performed, and with ga becoming ja by kavaggahā, etc., then by the rule gupissa ussa i, in reduplication, the u of the first syllable becomes i. With the ti, etc., endings and the a vikaraṇa, the form is jigucchati, and so on. In the sense of censure, from the root badh ('to bind'), with the suffix cha, and by this same rule, ba becomes bha. After assimilation, the first letter is reduplicated as bhaccha-bhaccha. The non-initial consonant is elided. By catutthadutiyānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā, in the reduplicated syllable, the first bha becomes ba. By khachasu issa ī, the vowel i is lengthened. From the resulting root bībhaccha, the ti, etc., endings are applied. Thus: bībhacchati, bībhacchanti, and so on. In other senses: gopeti, and so on.

5,4. Tuṃsmā lopo ci+cchāyaṃ te

5.4. After tuṃ, elision occurs, in the sense of desire, with the suffixes coded by te.

Tumantato icchāya+matthe te kha+sa+chā honti bahulaṃ, tuṃpaccayassa lopo ca hoti, sutattā. Bhuja=pālana+jjhohāresu. Bhojanāyāti viggayha “tuṃ+tāye”ccādinā tuṃpaccaye “lahussupantassā”ti okāre pararūpe ca kate bhottu+micchatīti viggayha iminā khapaccaye tuṃpaccayassa iminā ca lope “nimittābhāve nemittikassāpi ca abhāvo”ti ñāyā pararūpaokārānaṃ abhāve khassa pararūpa+khakārādimhi ca kate bhukkha bhukkha iti dvitte tatiyabakāro hoti, bubhukkhadhātuto tyādayo honti, bubhukkhati, bubhukkhanti iccādi.

After a word ending in the infinitive suffix tuṃ, in the sense of desire, the suffixes kha, sa, and cha (coded as te) frequently occur, and the tuṃ suffix is also elided, as is known from the sutra. The root bhuj is in the senses of 'protecting' and 'eating'. From the analysis bhojanāya ('for the purpose of eating'), the infinitive suffix tuṃ is applied by the rule tuṃ tāye, etc. The vowel is strengthened to o by lahussupantassa, and assimilation is performed. From the analysis bhottuṃ icchati ('he wishes to eat'), by this rule the suffix kha is added, and the tuṃ suffix is elided. According to the maxim 'when the cause is absent, the effect is also absent', the assimilation and the vowel strengthening to o are reversed. When the suffix kha is added and assimilation to the initial kha is performed, there is reduplication as bhukkha bhukkha. The first letter becomes the third of its class, ba. From the resulting root bubhukkha, the ti, etc., endings are applied, yielding bubhukkhati, bubhukkhanti, and so on.

Ji=jaye, jayanāya iti viggayha pure viya tumādimhi kate jetu+micchatīti viggayha sappaccaye jisa jisa iti dvitte anādibyañjanalope dvitte parassa jissa “jiharānaṃ giṃ”ti giṃ. Jigiṃsadhātuto tyādīsu jigiṃsati, jigiṃsanti iccādi.

'Ji' in the sense of 'to conquer'. Taking 'for conquering' as the analysis, as before when `tum` etc. have been applied, and taking 'desires to conquer' as the analysis, with the suffix `sa`, in the reduplication `jisa jisa`, with the elision of the non-initial consonant, in the reduplication, for the latter `jisa`, `giṃ` is substituted by the rule `jiharānaṃ giṃ`. From the root `jigiṃsa`, with the `ti` etc. endings, `jigiṃsati`, `jigiṃsanti`, etc., are formed.

Ghasa=adane[M 0.0257], ghasitu+micchati chappaccayādimhi pure viya kate ghassa “kavaggahā”dinā jhe jhassa “catutthadutiyā” dinā jakāre “khachasesvassī”ti ikāre ca kate jighacchadhātuto tyādayo honti. Jighacchati, jighacchanti+ccādi.

'Ghas' in the sense of 'to eat'. In the sense 'desires to eat', when the suffix `cha` etc. has been applied as before, for `gha`, `jha` is substituted by `kavaggahā` etc.; for `jha`, `ja` is substituted by `catutthadutiyā` etc.; and `i` is substituted by `khachasesvassī`. From the root `jighaccha`, the forms with `ti` etc. endings arise. Thus, `jighacchati`, `jighacchanti`, etc.

5,5. Īyo kammā

5.5. The suffix `īya` [occurs] after an object.

Icchākammato icchāya+matthe īyapaccayo hoti. Putta+micchatīti īyapaccaye īyādivuttittā “ekatthatāyaṃ”ti vibhattilopo. Puttīyati, puttīyanti+ccādi.

From a noun that is the object of desiring, in the sense of desire, the suffix `īya` occurs. Taking 'desires a son' as the analysis, when the suffix `īya` is applied, the case ending is elided due to the formation of a derivative with `īya` etc. and by the rule `ekatthatāyaṃ`. Thus, `puttīyati`, `puttīyanti`, etc.

5,6. Upamānā+cāre

5.6. From a standard of comparison, in the sense of conduct.

Kammato upamānā ācāratthe īyo hoti. Putta+mivā+carati puttīyati sissaṃ, puttīyanti+ccādi.

From an object used as a standard of comparison, in the sense of conduct, the suffix `īya` occurs. For example, 'behaves like a son' becomes `puttīyati sissaṃ` (he treats the disciple as a son); `puttīyanti`, etc.

5,7. Ādhārāti

5.7. From a locus.

Īyo hoti. Kuṭiya+mivā+carati kuṭīyati pāsāde. Pāsādevā+carati pāsādīyati kuṭiyaṃ, pāsādīyanti+ccādi.

The suffix `īya` occurs. For example, 'behaves as if in a hut' becomes `kuṭīyati pāsāde` (he behaves in a mansion as if it were a hut); 'behaves as if in a mansion' becomes `pāsādīyati kuṭiyaṃ` (he behaves in a hut as if it were a mansion); `pāsādīyanti`, etc.

5,8. Kattutā+yo

5.8. From an agent, `āyo`.

Kattuto+pamānā ācāratthe āyo hoti. Pabbato ivā+carati sīlādiguṇayogatoti pabbatāyati yogī, pabbatāyadhātuto tyādayo.

From an agent used as a standard of comparison, in the sense of conduct, the suffix `āyo` occurs.
