For example, 'behaves like a mountain' (because of being endowed with virtues such as morality) becomes `pabbatāyati yogī` (the yogi is like a mountain). From the root `pabbatāya`, the `ti` etc. endings are applied.

5,9. Cyatthe

5.9. In the sense of `cvi` (becoming).

Kattuto [M 0.0258] abhūtatabbhāve āyo hoti bahulaṃ. Bhusoti paṭhamantato abhuso bhuso bhavatīti bhusāyati, bhusāyanti iccādi. “Vicchābhikkhaññesu dve”ti ābhikkhaññatthe dvitte apaṭapaṭā paṭapaṭā bhavatīti āye paṭapaṭāyati, paṭapaṭāyanti+ccādi. Alohito lohito bhavati lohitāyati.

From a noun, in the sense of 'becoming what one was not', the suffix `āyo` frequently occurs. For example, from the nominative `bhuso`, in the sense 'what was not much becomes much', `bhusāyati`, `bhusāyanti`, etc. are formed. By `Vicchābhikkhaññesu dve`, in the sense of repetition, with doubling, in the sense 'what was not crackling becomes crackling', with `āyo`, `paṭapaṭāyati`, `paṭapaṭāyanti`, etc. are formed. 'What was not red becomes red', `lohitāyati`.

5,10. Saddādīni karoti

5.10. Makes sounds, etc.

Saddādīhi dutiyantehi karotīti asmiṃ atthe āyo hoti. Saddaṃ karoti saddāyati. Evaṃ verāyati, kalahāyati, dhūpāyati+ccādi.

From `sadda`, etc., ending in the accusative case, in the sense of 'makes', the suffix `āyo` occurs. For example, `saddaṃ karoti` (makes a sound) becomes `saddāyati`. Similarly, `verāyati` (acts with enmity), `kalahāyati` (quarrels), `dhūpāyati` (makes smoke), etc.

5,11. Namotva+sso

5.11. After `namo`, `assa`.

Namoiccasmā karotīti asmiṃ atthe asso hoti. Namo karotīti asmiṃ atthe assapaccaye tyādayo honti, tathāgataṃ namassati, namassanti iccādi.

From the indeclinable `namo`, in the sense of 'makes', the suffix `assa` occurs. In the sense of 'makes homage', when the suffix `assa` is applied, the `ti` etc. endings are applied. For example, `tathāgataṃ namassati` (he pays homage to the Tathāgata), `namassanti`, etc.

5,12. Dhātvatthe nāmasmi

5.12. From a noun, in the sense of a verbal root.

Nāmasmā dhātvatthe bahula+mi hoti. Hatthinā atikkamatīti ipaccaye lavikaraṇa+ekāra+ayādesesu katesu atihatthayati. Evaṃ vīṇāya upagāyati upavīṇāyati, vinayaṃ daḷhaṃ karoti daḷhayati, visuddhā hoti ratti visuddhāyati, kusalaṃ pucchati kusalāyati+ccādi.

From a noun, in the sense of a verbal root, the suffix `i` frequently occurs. For example, in the sense ‘hatthinā atikkamati’ (he bypasses with an elephant), when the `i` suffix, the conjugational sign, the substitution of `e`, and the substitution of `aya` are applied, it becomes ‘atihatthayati’. Similarly, ‘vīṇāya upagāyati’ (he sings along with a lute) becomes ‘upavīṇāyati’; ‘vinayaṃ daḷhaṃ karoti’ (he makes the discipline firm) becomes ‘daḷhayati’; ‘visuddhā hoti ratti’ (the night becomes pure) becomes ‘visuddhāyati’; ‘kusalaṃ pucchati’ (he asks about what is skillful) becomes ‘kusalāyati’, and so on.

5,13. Saccādīhā+pi

5.13. From `sacca` etc., `āpi`.

Saccādīhi [M 0.0259] dhātvatthe āpi hoti. Sacca+mācikkhatīti āpimhi tyādipaccaye “ṇi+ṇāpyā+dīhi vā”ti lavikaraṇa+e+ayādesā. Saccāpayati, saccāpeti iccādi. Attha+mācikkhati atthāpayati. Evaṃ vedāpayati. Sukkhaṃ karotīti sukkhāpayati sukkhāpeti iccādi.

From `sacca` etc., in the sense of a verbal root, the suffix `āpi` occurs. In the analysis ‘saccaṃ ācikkhati’ (he declares the truth), when the suffix `āpi` is applied, followed by the `ti` etc. endings, by the rule `ṇiṇāpyādīhi vā`, the conjugational sign, `e`, and `aya` substitutions occur. Thus, `saccāpayati`, `saccāpeti`, etc. Similarly, ‘atthaṃ ācikkhati’ (he explains the meaning) becomes ‘atthāpayati’. Thus also, `vedāpayati`. ‘Sukkhaṃ karoti’ (he makes dry) becomes `sukkhāpayati`, `sukkhāpeti`, etc.

5,16. Payojakabyāpāre ṇāpi ca

5.16. And `ṇāpi` in the function of the instigator.

Kattāraṃ yo payojeti, tassa byāpāre kriyatthā ṇi+ṇāpī honti bahulaṃ.

In the function of one who employs an agent, the suffixes `ṇi` and `ṇāpi` frequently occur to denote that action.

Ṇipaccayo uvaṇṇantā, āto ṇāpeva hoti+ha;

Dve dve+ko hoti vā sese, bahulaṃtyanuvuttiyā.

The suffix `ṇi` occurs after roots ending in `u` vowels, and `ṇāpi` indeed occurs after roots ending in `ā`. In the remaining cases, both are optional, due to the continuation of the word `bahulaṃ` (frequently).

Akammakāpi honteva, ṇi+ṇāpyantā sakammakā;

Sakammakā dvikammā+ssu, dvikammā ca tikammakā.

Intransitive verbs ending in `ṇi` and `ṇāpi` indeed become transitive. Transitive verbs become ditransitive, and ditransitive verbs become tritransitive.

Tasmā kattari kamme ca, ṇi+ṇāpīnaṃ tu sambhavo;

Na bhāve suddhakattā tu, kammaṃ hoti payojake.

Therefore, `ṇi` and `ṇāpi` can occur in the active and passive voices, but not in the impersonal voice, because the verbs become transitive. In the causative, the original agent becomes the object.

Nayādīnaṃ padhānañca, apadhānaṃ duhādinaṃ;

Suddhakattā ṇi+ṇāpīsu, kamma+makkhyāta gocaraṃ.

In causatives with `ṇi` and `ṇāpi`, the original agent becomes the object expressed by the verb, as does the principal object of roots like `nī`, and the secondary object of roots like `duh`.

Bhavituṃ payojayatīti atthe iminā ṇippaccayo. Ṇakāro ṇānubandhakāriyattho. “Yuvaṇṇāna+me+o paccaye”ti okāre “āyā+vā ṇānubandhe”ti ṇānubandhe āvādeso. Tyādimhi “ṇi+ṇāpyā+pīhi vā”ti lavikaraṇe ekāre “eona+mayavā sare”ti ayādeso. So samādhiṃ bhāvayati bhāveti[M 0.0260], bhāvayanti bhāventi+ccādi. Kamme-tena samādhi bhāvīyati+ccādi. Ettha “dīgho sarassā”ti kye ikārassa dīgho. Bhāvayissati bhāvessati, bhāvayissanti bhāvessanti+ccādi. Ajjatane īssa simhi abhāvesi bhāvesi, abhāvayi bhāvayi, abhāvayiṃsu bhāvayiṃsu. Parassaralope abhāvesuṃ bhāvesuṃ, abhāvayaṃsu bhāvayaṃsu, abhāvayuṃ bhāvayuṃ iccādi. Kamme-abhāvīyi bhāvīyi iccādi. Abhāvissa abhāvayissa, abhāvissaṃsu abhāvayissaṃsu. Kamme-abhāvayissaṃ iccādi. Bhāve bhāveyya iccādi. Kamme-bhāvīyeyya iccādi. Bhāvayatu bhāvetu iccādi. Kamme-bhāvīyatu iccādi.

In the sense of ‘causes to be’, by this rule the suffix `ṇi` is applied. The letter `ṇ` is for the purpose of operations related to the indicatory `ṇ`. By the rule `Yuvaṇṇānaṃ e o paccaye`, `o` is substituted. When there is an indicatory `ṇ`, by the rule `āyāvā ṇānubandhe`, `āv` is substituted. When `ti` etc. follow, by the rule `ṇiṇāpyāpīhi vā`, with the conjugational sign, `e` is formed, and by `eonaṃ ayavā sare`, `aya` is substituted. He cultivates concentration: `bhāvayati` or `bhāveti`; they cultivate: `bhāvayanti` or `bhāventi`, etc. In the passive: by him, concentration is cultivated, `bhāvīyati`, etc. Here, by the rule `dīgho sarassa`, the `i` before the `ya` suffix is lengthened. He will cultivate: `bhāvayissati` or `bhāvessati`; they will cultivate: `bhāvayissanti` or `bhāvessanti`, etc. In the aorist, with the `ī` and `si` endings: `abhāvesi` or `bhāvesi`, `abhāvayi` or `bhāvayi`, `abhāvayiṃsu` or `bhāvayiṃsu`. With elision of the final vowel: `abhāvesuṃ` or `bhāvesuṃ`, `abhāvayaṃsu` or `bhāvayaṃsu`, `abhāvayuṃ` or `bhāvayuṃ`, etc. In the passive: `abhāvīyi` or `bhāvīyi`, etc. Conditional: `abhāvissa` or `abhāvayissa`, `abhāvissaṃsu` or `abhāvayissaṃsu`. In the passive: `abhāvayissaṃ`, etc. Optative: `bhāveyya`, etc. In the passive: `bhāvīyeyya`, etc. Imperative: `bhāvayatu` or `bhāvetu`, etc. In the passive: `bhāvīyatu`, etc.

Pacituṃ payojetīti atthe ṇi+ṇāpī honti. So devadattena odanaṃ pācayati pāceti iccādi, tathā pācāpayati pācāpeti+ccādi. Kamme-so tena devadattena odano pācīyati pācāpīyati+ccādi, bhavissatyādīsupi yojetabbaṃ.

In the sense of ‘causing to cook’, the suffixes `ṇi` and `ṇāpi` occur. For example, `so devadattena odanaṃ pācayati pāceti` (he causes Devadatta to cook rice), etc.; similarly, `pācāpayati pācāpeti`, etc. In the passive: `tena devadattena odano pācīyati pācāpīyati` (by him, rice is caused to be cooked by Devadatta), etc.; this should also be applied in the future tense, etc.

Gantuṃ payojetīti atthe so taṃ purisaṃ gāmaṃ gamayati gameti gacchāpayati gacchāpeti+ccādi. Kamme-tena so gāmaṃ gamīyati gacchāpīyati+ccādi.

In the sense of ‘causing to go’, `so taṃ purisaṃ gāmaṃ gamayati gameti gacchāpayati gacchāpeti`, etc. (he causes that man to go to the village). In the passive: `tena so gāmaṃ gamīyati gacchāpīyati`, etc. (by him, that man is caused to go to the village).

Guha=saṃvaraṇe, guhituṃ payojetīti ṇimhi “guhissa sare”ti dīgho. Gūhayati, gūhayanti iccādi.

`Guh` in the sense of 'to conceal'. In the sense of ‘causing to conceal’, when the suffix `ṇi` is present, by the rule `guhissa sare`, the vowel is lengthened. Thus, `gūhayati` (he causes to conceal), `gūhayanti` (they cause to conceal), etc.

Disa+dusa=appītiyaṃ, dusituṃ payojetīti ṇimhi “ṇimhi dīgho dusassā”ti dīghe dūsayati+ccādi.

The roots ‘disa’ and ‘dusa’ are used in the sense of displeasure. In the sense of ‘causing to displease,’ when the suffix ‘ṇi’ is present, by the rule ‘when ‘ṇi’ is present, the vowel of ‘dusa’ is lengthened,’ with lengthening, the form is ‘dūsayati’, and so on.

Tathā icchantaṃ payojayati icchāpayati icchāpeti, esayati eseti. Niyacchantaṃ payojayati niyamayati niyameti. Tathā āsayati [M 0.0261] āseti, acchāpayati acchāpeti. Lābhayati lābheti, evaṃ vāsayati vāseti, vāsāpayati vāsāpeti. Vāhayati vāheti, vāhāpayati vāhāpeti+ccādi. Evaṃ jīrayati, mārayati, dassayati iccādi. Hū=sattāyaṃ, pahontaṃ payojayati pahāvayati pahāveti iccādi. Sāyayati sāyāpayati sāyāpeti. Nāyāpayati nāyāpeti. Patiṭṭhāpayati patiṭṭhāpeti. Rasse patiṭṭhapeti. Hantuṃ payojayatīti ṇi+ṇāpī, “hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe”ti ghātādese ghātayati ghāteti. Tathā juhāvayati juhāveti, jahāpayati jahāpeti. Hāpayati hāpeti. Dāpayati dāpeti. Vidhāpayati vidhāpeti, pidahāpayati pidahāpeti. (Bhūvādinayo).

Similarly, one causes another to wish, forming ‘icchāpayati’ or ‘icchāpeti’; ‘esayati’ or ‘eseti’. One causes another to restrain, forming ‘niyamayati’ or ‘niyameti’. Likewise, ‘āsayati’ or ‘āseti’; ‘acchāpayati’ or ‘acchāpeti’. ‘Lābhayati’ or ‘lābheti’; similarly, ‘vāsayati’ or ‘vāseti’; ‘vāsāpayati’ or ‘vāsāpeti’. ‘Vāhayati’ or ‘vāheti’; ‘vāhāpayati’ or ‘vāhāpeti’, and so on. Thus, ‘jīrayati’, ‘mārayati’, ‘dassayati’, etc. The root ‘hū’ is used in the sense of existence; one causes another to be able, forming ‘pahāvayati’ or ‘pahāveti’, and so on. ‘Sāyayati’, ‘sāyāpayati’, or ‘sāyāpeti’. ‘Nāyāpayati’ or ‘nāyāpeti’. ‘Patiṭṭhāpayati’ or ‘patiṭṭhāpeti’. With a short vowel, ‘patiṭṭhapeti’. In the sense of ‘causing to kill’, the suffixes ‘ṇi’ and ‘ṇāpi’ are used; by the rule ‘for ‘han’, ‘ghāta’ is substituted when a suffix with an indicatory ‘ṇ’ follows,’ with the substitution of ‘ghāta’, the forms are ‘ghātayati’ or ‘ghāteti’. Similarly, ‘juhāvayati’ or ‘juhāveti’; ‘jahāpayati’ or ‘jahāpeti’. ‘Hāpayati’ or ‘hāpeti’. ‘Dāpayati’ or ‘dāpeti’. ‘Vidhāpayati’ or ‘vidhāpeti’; ‘pidahāpayati’ or ‘pidahāpeti’. (This is the method of the Bhūādi group).

Idāni rudhādiaṭṭhagaṇā dassīyante-rodhayati rodheti. Devayati deveti. Todayati todeti. Jayāpayati jayāpeti. Vikkayati vikkayāpeti. Sāvayati sāveti. Vitānayati vitāneti. Corāpayati corāpeti iccādi.

Now, the eight groups of roots beginning with ‘rudh’ are shown: ‘rodhayati’, ‘rodheti’; ‘devayati’, ‘deveti’; ‘todayati’, ‘todeti’; ‘jayāpayati’, ‘jayāpeti’; ‘vikkayati’, ‘vikkayāpeti’; ‘sāvayati’, ‘sāveti’; ‘vitānayati’, ‘vitāneti’; ‘corāpayati’, ‘corāpeti’, etc.

Khādīhi paccayantehi, api honti ṇi+ṇāpayo;

Ṇi+ṇāpinā+nakānānaṃ, dassanañcettha sādhanaṃ.

From roots of the ‘khādi’ group and others that end in a suffix, the causative suffixes ‘ṇi’ and ‘ṇāpi’ also occur. The existence here of forms with ‘ṇi’, ‘ṇāpi’, and ‘ṇaka’ is the proof.

Titikkhantaṃ payojayati titikkheti titikkhāpeti, tikicchayati tikiccheti tikicchāpayati tikicchāpeti. Evaṃ bubhukkheti bubhukkhāpeti. Pabbatāyayati. Puttīyayati iccādi. (Khādipaccayanayo).

One causes another to endure, forming ‘titikkheti’ or ‘titikkhāpeti’; one causes another to cure, forming ‘tikicchayati’, ‘tikiccheti’, ‘tikicchāpayati’, or ‘tikicchāpeti’. Similarly, one causes another to be hungry, forming ‘bubhukkheti’ or ‘bubhukkhāpeti’. One causes another to act like a mountain, forming ‘pabbatāyayati’. One causes another to be treated as a son, forming ‘puttīyayati’, and so on. (This is the method of suffixes for the Khādi group).

Iti payogasiddhiyaṃ tyādikaṇḍo chaṭṭho.

Thus ends the sixth chapter, the Tyādi section, in the Payogasiddhi.

7. Khādikaṇḍa

7. The Khādi Chapter

Atha [M 0.0262] dhātūhiyeva bhāva+kamma+kattu+karaṇādisādhanasahitaṃ khādividhānaṃ ārabhīyate –

Now, the exposition of the rules for the `khādi` group is begun, from the roots themselves, together with the means of derivation for state, object, agent, instrument, and so forth.

“Tijamānehi khasā khamāvīmaṃsāsu” iccādīhi paccayavidhānañca pararūpadvittādikāriyañca tyādikaṇḍe vuttanayeneva ñātabbaṃ. Titikkhanaṃ titikkhā, “itthiya+maṇaktikayakayā ca” iti suttena apaccayo ca “itthiya+matvā”ti āpaccayo ca hoti. Tathā vīmaṃsanaṃ vīmaṃsā. “Kitā tikicchāsaṃsayesu cho”ti chappaccayādimhi kate tikicchanaṃ tikicchā, vicikicchanaṃ vicikicchā. Gupa=gopane, badha=bandhaneti imehi dhātūhi “nindāyaṃ gupa+badhā bassa bho ca” iti chapaccayādimhi ca dvitte parabakārassa iminā bhakāre ca kate apaccayādi hoti. Jigucchanaṃ jigucchā, bībhacchanaṃ bībhacchā. “Tuṃsmā lopo ci+cchāyaṃ te” iti icchāya+matthe kha+sa+chappaccayā honti. Bhuja=pālanajjhohāresu, bubhukkhanaṃ bubhukkhā. Ji=jaye, jigiṃsanaṃ, jigiṃsā. Ghasa=adane, jighacchanaṃ jighacchā.

By rules such as 'Tijamānehi khasā khamāvīmaṃsāsu,' the prescription of suffixes and operations such as assimilation and reduplication should be understood in the same way as explained in the Tyādi chapter. Endurance is 'titikkhā'; according to the sutta 'itthiya+maṇaktikayakayā ca,' the suffix 'a' and the suffix 'ā' occur, as in 'itthiya+matvā.' Similarly, investigation is 'vīmaṃsā.' When the suffix 'cha' etc. is applied by the rule 'kitā tikicchāsaṃsayesu cho,' treatment is 'tikicchā,' and doubt is 'vicikicchā.' From the roots 'gup' (in the sense of protecting) and 'badh' (in the sense of binding), by the rule 'nindāyaṃ gupa+badhā bassa bho ca,' when the suffix 'cha' etc. is applied, and there is reduplication, and the following 'b' is changed to 'bh' by this rule, the suffix 'a' etc. occurs. Disgust is 'jigucchā,' and loathing is 'bībhacchā.' By the rule 'tuṃsmā lopo ci+cchāyaṃ te,' in the sense of desire, the suffixes 'kha,' 'sa,' and 'cha' occur. From 'bhuja' (in the senses of protecting and consuming), hunger is 'bubhukkhā.' From 'ji' (in the sense of conquering), the desire to conquer is 'jigiṃsā.' From 'ghasa' (in the sense of eating), hunger is 'jighacchā.'

27. Bhāvakammesu tabbānīyā

27. The suffixes -tabba and -anīya in the impersonal and passive senses.

Tabbaanīyā kriyatthā pare bhāvakammesu bhavanti, bahulaṃvidhānā kattukaraṇādīsupi. Bhū=sattāyaṃ, “yuvaṇṇāna+me opaccaye”ti okāre “ūbyañjanassā”ti ūāgamo, ññakāro ādyāvayavattho. Ossa “eona+ mayavā [M 0.0263] sare”ti avādeso, bhūyateti bhavitabbaṃ bhavatā bhavanīyaṃ. Bhāvasse+kattā ekavacanameva, tañca napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ.

The suffixes -tabba and -anīya occur after a root in the impersonal and passive senses, and by the principle of varied application, also in the agentive, instrumental, and other senses. From `bhū` (in the sense of existence): by 'yuvaṇṇāna+me opaccaye,' 'o' is formed; by 'ūbyañjanassā,' there is the augment 'ū'; the 'ññakāra' is for the purpose of the initial member. For 'o,' by 'eona+ mayavā sare,' there is the substitution 'av.' From 'bhūyate' (it is), the forms are 'bhavitabbaṃ' (it should be) by you (`bhavatā`), and 'bhavanīyaṃ'. The agent of the impersonal construction is always singular, and the form itself is of the neuter gender.

Tabbādyabhihito bhāvo,

Dabbamiva pakāsatīti-bahuvacanañca hoti.

The state expressed by -tabba and so forth appears like a substance; thus, it also takes the plural.

Kamme-abhipubbo, abhibhūyate abhibhūyittha abhibhūyissateti abhibhavitabbo kodho paṇḍitena, abhibhavitabbā taṇhā, abhibhavitabbaṃ dukkhaṃ. Evaṃ abhibhavanīyo abhibhavanīyā abhibhavanīyaṃ, kamme abhidheyyasseva liṅgavacanāni.

In the passive, with the prefix 'abhi-': from 'abhibhūyate' (is overpowered), 'abhibhūyittha' (was overpowered), 'abhibhūyissati' (will be overpowered), the forms are derived. Thus, 'abhibhavitabbo kodho paṇḍitena' (anger should be overpowered by the wise), 'abhibhavitabbā taṇhā' (craving should be overpowered), 'abhibhavitabbaṃ dukkhaṃ' (suffering should be overpowered). Similarly, 'abhibhavanīyo' (masculine), 'abhibhavanīyā' (feminine), 'abhibhavanīyaṃ' (neuter). In the passive, the gender and number are determined by the object expressed.

Visessaliṅgātabbādī, tatthā+do pañca bhāvajā;

Napuṃsake siyuṃ bhāve, kto cā+no akattari.

The suffixes `-tabba` and so forth take the gender of the noun they qualify. Therein, the first five arise from the impersonal sense. In the impersonal sense, they are in the neuter gender; and the suffixes `-ta` and `-ana` are used in a non-agentive sense.

Bhāvasmiṃ ghaṇa pume evaṃ, iyuvaṇṇā gahādijo;

Apaccayopi vā+saṃkhyā, tu+māditvantakā siyuṃ.

In the impersonal sense, the suffix 'ghaṇa' is thus masculine; those ending in 'i', 'yu', and 'u' are like the 'gahādi' group. Also the suffix 'a' may be used; or, as indeclinables, those ending in 'tuṃ', 'ti', and '-tva' may occur.

Ito paraṃ upasaggapubbatā ca kālattayassa vākyagahaṇañca vuttanayena ñātabbaṃ, tasmā anurūpavākyameva dassayissāma –

Henceforth, the use of prefixes and the inclusion of sentences in the three tenses should be understood according to the method already stated. Therefore, we will present only an appropriate example sentence.

Āsa=upavesane, āsane āsitabbaṃ tayā āsanīyaṃ. Kamme-upāsīyatīti upāsitabbo guru upāsanīyo. Sī=saye, e+ayādesā, sayanaṃ sayitabbaṃ sayanīyaṃ tayā. Atisīyatīti atisayitabbo kaṭo te atisayanīyo. Pada=gamane, “padādīnaṃ kvacī”ti yuka, kakāro kānubandhakāriyattho, ukāro uccāraṇattho, dassajo pubbarūpañca, uppajjanaṃ uppajjitabbaṃ uppajjanīyaṃ. Paṭipajjīyatīti paṭipajjitabbo maggo paṭipajjanīyo. Budha=ñāṇe, bujjhateti bujjhitabbo [M 0.0264] dhammo bujjhanīyo. Su=savane, sūyateti sotabbo dhammo, ññimhi nāgame “tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā”ti ṇe ca kate “na te kānubandha+nāgamesū”ti okārābhāvo. Suṇitabbo, savanīyo. Kara=karaṇe –

From `āsa` (in the sense of sitting): `āsane āsitabbaṃ tayā` (there should be sitting on the seat by you), `āsanīyaṃ` (it is fit for sitting). In the passive: from `upāsīyati` (is served), `upāsitabbo guru` (the teacher is to be served), `upāsanīyo` (worthy of service). From `sī` (in the sense of lying down), with the substitution of `e` and then `ay`: `sayanaṃ` (lying down), `sayitabbaṃ tayā` (there should be lying down by you), `sayanīyaṃ` (it is fit for lying). From `atisīyati` (is surpassed), `atisayitabbo kaṭo te` (the mat is to be surpassed by you), `atisayanīyo` (it is worthy of surpassing). From `pada` (in the sense of going): by the rule 'padādīnaṃ kvacī,' the suffix `yuka` is applied; the `ka` is for the purpose of the `ka`-anubandha operation, the `u` is for pronunciation, and there is assimilation to the preceding form of `d` and `j`. `Uppajjanaṃ` (arising), `uppajjitabbaṃ` (it should be arisen), `uppajjanīyaṃ` (it is fit for arising). From `paṭipajjīyati` (is proceeded upon), `paṭipajjitabbo maggo` (the path is to be proceeded upon), `paṭipajjanīyo` (worthy of proceeding). From `budha` (in the sense of knowing): from `bujjhati` (knows), `bujjhitabbo dhammo` (the Dhamma is to be known), `bujjhanīyo` (worthy of knowing). From `su` (in the sense of hearing): from `sūyati` (is heard), `sotabbo dhammo` (the Dhamma is to be heard). When the augment `nā` is present, and `ṇ` is made by the rule 'tathanarānaṃ ṭaṭhaṇalā', and there is an absence of 'o' by the rule 'na te kānubandha+nāgamesū', the forms are `suṇitabbo` and `savanīyo`. From `kara` (in the sense of doing):

95. Pararūpa+mayakāre byañjane

95. Assimilation to the following form when a consonant other than 'ya' follows.

Kriyatthāna+mantabyañjanassa pararūpaṃ hoti yakārato aññasmiṃ byañjane. Karīyatīti kattabbo dhammo, kattabbā pūjā, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ.

The final consonant of a verbal stem undergoes assimilation to the following form when followed by a consonant other than 'ya'. From 'karīyati' (is done), the forms are 'kattabbo dhammo' (the Dhamma is to be done), 'kattabbā pūjā' (worship is to be done), 'kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ' (a wholesome deed is to be done).

119. Tuṃ+tuna+tabbesu vā

119. Optionally, when 'tuṃ', 'tuna', or 'tabba' follow.

Tumādīsu karassā hoti vā. Kātabbaṃ hitaṃ.

When the suffixes 'tuṃ' and so forth follow, the vowel of 'kar' optionally becomes 'ā'. For example, 'kātabbaṃ hitaṃ' (what is beneficial should be done).

171. Rā nassa ṇo

171. After 'r', 'n' becomes 'ṇ'.

Rantato kriyatthā paccayanakārassa ṇa hoti. Karaṇīyo.

After a stem ending in 'r', the 'n' of a verbal suffix becomes 'ṇ'. For example, 'karaṇīyo' (to be done).

Bhara=bharaṇe, bharīyatīti bharitabbo bharaṇīyo. Gaha=upādāne “maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ”ti antasarā paromaṃ vā hoti. Makāro+nubandho. “Ṇo niggahītassā”ti niggahītassa ṇo, saṃgayhatīti saṃgaṇhitabbo saṃgaṇhanīyo, “tathanarā”dinā ṇakāre gahaṇīyo. Rama=kīḷāyaṃ, ramīyatīti ramaṇīyo vihāro. Āpa=pāpuṇane, “sakāpānaṃ kukakū ṇe”ti ettha ‘sakāpānaṃ kuka+kū’ti yogavibhāgā ku, ūāgame nāgamassa ṇe ca kate pāpīyatīti pāpuṇitabbo. Pararūpe pattabbo, pāpuṇanīyo, pāpanīyo.

From `bhara` (in the sense of bearing): from 'bharīyati' (is borne), 'bharitabbo' (to be borne), 'bharaṇīyo' (fit to be borne). From `gaha` (in the sense of grasping): by the rule 'maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ,' the infix 'maṃ' optionally comes after the final vowel. The 'm' is an anubandha. By 'ṇo niggahītassā,' the niggahīta becomes 'ṇ'. From 'saṃgayhati' (is grasped), 'saṃgaṇhitabbo' (to be grasped), 'saṃgaṇhanīyo' (fit to be grasped). By the rule 'tathanarādinā,' with 'ṇ', the form is 'gahaṇīyo' (fit to be grasped). From `rama` (in the sense of delighting): from 'ramīyati' (is delighted in), 'ramaṇīyo vihāro' (a delightful monastery). From `āpa` (in the sense of reaching): in the rule 'sakāpānaṃ kukakū ṇe,' by splitting the rule as 'sakāpānaṃ kuka+kū,' the suffix 'ku' is applied; with the augment 'ū', and with 'ṇ' for the augment 'nā', from 'pāpīyati' (is reached), the form is 'pāpuṇitabbo' (to be reached). With assimilation to the following form, 'pattabbo' (to be reached); also 'pāpuṇanīyo' (fit to be reached), 'pāpanīyo' (fit to be reached).

96. Manānaṃ niggahītaṃ

96. For 'm' and 'n', the niggahīta.

Makāra+nakārantānaṃ [M 0.0265] kriyatthānaṃ niggahītaṃ hotya+yakāre byañjane. Vaggantaṃ, gamiyatīti gantabbo. Gamitabbaṃ gamanīyaṃ. Khana=khaṇa=avadāraṇe, niggahītaṃ vaggantattañca, khaññateti khantabbaṃ āvāṭaṃ khanitabbaṃ khananīyaṃ. Hana=hiṃsāyaṃ, haññateti hantabbaṃ hanitabbaṃ hananīyaṃ. Mana=ñāṇe, maññateti mantabbo manitabbo. “Padādīnaṃ kvacī”ti yuka, cavaggādimhi kate maññitabbaṃ maññanīyaṃ.

For verbal stems ending in 'm' and 'n', the final consonant becomes a niggahīta when a consonant other than 'y' follows, or it becomes the corresponding class-nasal. From 'gamiyatīti' (it is gone), 'gantabbo' (to be gone), 'gamitabbaṃ', 'gamanīyaṃ'. From the root 'khana' or 'khaṇa' (in the sense of digging), with the application of niggahīta and the class-nasal rule, from 'khaññateti' (it is dug), 'khantabbaṃ'. The pit is to be dug: 'āvāṭaṃ khanitabbaṃ', 'khananīyaṃ'. From the root 'hana' (in the sense of harming), from 'haññateti' (it is harmed), 'hantabbaṃ', 'hanitabbaṃ', 'hananīyaṃ'. From the root 'mana' (in the sense of knowing), from 'maññateti' (it is known/thought), 'mantabbo', 'manitabbo'. By the rule 'padādīnaṃ kvacī,' with the suffix 'yuka,' when a palatal initial is formed, the forms are 'maññitabbaṃ' and 'maññanīyaṃ'.

Pūja=pūjāyaṃ, “curādito ṇī”ti ṇimhi ñukārassa guruttā okārāvutti “yuvaṇṇāna+meo paccaye”ti ekāre pūjetabbo ūmhi ayādese pūjayitabbo pūjanīyo bhagavā.

Pūja: in the sense of worship. By the rule 'curādito ṇī', when the suffix ṇī is applied, due to the heaviness of the syllable ñu, there is an insertion of o; then by the rule 'yuvaṇṇānam eo paccaye', with the vowel e, [the form is] pūjetabbo. When ū is present, with the substitution of aya, [the forms are] pūjayitabbo [and] pūjanīyo, [meaning] the Blessed One is to be worshipped.

Kattari-yā=pāpuṇane, nīyatīti niyyāniyo maggo, gacchantīti gamanīyā bhogā. Karaṇe-naha=soceyye, nahāyantya+nenāti nahānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ. Sampadāne-dā=dāne, saṃ+papubbo, sammā padīyate assāti sampadāniyo brāhmaṇo.

In the agentive sense: from the root yā, in the sense of reaching. 'It is led out by this,' thus niyyāniyo maggo, the path that leads out. 'They go,' thus gamanīyā bhogā, movable possessions. In the instrumental sense: from the root naha, in the sense of purifying. 'They bathe with this,' thus nahānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ, bathing powder. In the dative sense: from the root dā, in the sense of giving, preceded by saṃ and pa. 'To whom it is well given,' thus sampadāniyo brāhmaṇo, a brahmin worthy of offerings.

28. Ghyaṇa

28. Ghyaṇa

Bhāvakammesu kriyatthā paro ghyaṇa hoti bahulaṃ. Ūmhi kattabbaṃ kāriyaṃ. Hara=haraṇe, harīyatīti hāriyaṃ. Bhara=bharaṇe, bharitabbaṃ bhāriyaṃ. Labha=lābhe, “vaggalasehi te”ti pubbarūpabhakāre “catutthadutiyā” dinā tatiyakkhare ca kate labhitabbaṃ labbhaṃ.

In the sense of state or passive, the suffix ghyaṇa frequently occurs after verbal roots. When ū is present, `kattabbaṃ` is equivalent to `kāriyaṃ` (to be done). From the root hara, in the sense of taking: 'it is taken,' thus `hāriyaṃ` (to be taken). From the root bhara, in the sense of bearing: `bharitabbaṃ` is equivalent to `bhāriyaṃ` (to be borne). From the root labha, in the sense of gaining: by the rule 'vaggalasehi te', with the preceding form having `bha`, and by the rule beginning 'catutthadutiyā...', the third letter of the class being formed, `labhitabbaṃ` becomes `labbhaṃ` (to be gained).

Vaca=byattavacane,

Vaca: in the sense of clear speech.

98. Kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe

98. Kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe

Ghānubandhe [M 0.0266] cakāra+jakārantānaṃ kriyatthānaṃ ka+gā honti yathākkamaṃ.

When a suffix with an indicatory gha follows, for verbal roots ending in the letters c and j, they become k and g respectively.

84. Assā ṇānubandhe

84. Assā ṇānubandhe

Ṇakārānubandhe paccaye pare upantassa akārassa ā hoti. Vacanaṃ vuccateti vākyaṃ. Bhaja=sevāyaṃ, bhajanīyaṃ bhāgyaṃ, jassa gakāro. Ci=caye, cayanaṃ cīyatīti vā ceyyaṃ. Yassa dvittaṃ.

When a suffix with an indicatory ṇ follows, the 'a' of the penultimate syllable becomes 'ā'. 'A word is spoken,' thus `vākyaṃ` (a sentence/utterance). From the root bhaja, in the sense of serving: `bhajanīyaṃ` is equivalent to `bhāgyaṃ` (share/fortune); 'j' becomes 'g'. From the root ci, in the sense of gathering: `cayanaṃ` (gathering), or 'it is gathered' (`cīyatīti`), thus `ceyyaṃ` (to be gathered). There is doubling of 'y'.

5,122. Nito cissa cho

5.122. Nito cissa cho

Nito parassa cissa cho hotītiādicakārassa cho. Vinicchayatīti viniccheyyaṃ, nāgame vinicchinitabbaṃ. E+ayādesesu vinicchetabbaṃ vinicchanīyaṃ. Nī=pāpane, nīyatīti neyyo neyyā neyyaṃ, netabbaṃ.

By the rule 'after ni, the following c becomes ch', the c of `ādi` becomes ch. 'He decides' (`vinicchayatīti`), thus `viniccheyyaṃ` (to be decided). With the n-augment, `vinicchinitabbaṃ` (to be decided). With the substitutions of e and aya, `vinicchetabbaṃ` and `vinicchanīyaṃ` [are formed]. From the root nī, in the sense of leading: 'it is led' (`nīyatīti`), thus `neyyo`, `neyyā`, `neyyaṃ`, [equivalent to] `netabbaṃ`.

29. Āsse+ca

29. Āsse ca

Ākārantato kriyatthā ghyaṇa hoti bhāvakammesu āssa e ca. Dā=dāne, dātabbaṃ deyyaṃ. Pā=pāne, pīyatīti peyyaṃ. Mā=māne, mīyatīti meyyaṃ. Ñā=avabodhane, ñāyatīti ñeyyaṃ ñātabbaṃ, ūmhi nāgamo “ñāssa ne+jā”ti ñāssa jādese jānitabbaṃ, vijāniyaṃ. Khā=pakathane, saṃkhātabbaṃ saṃkheyyaṃ.

After verbal roots ending in 'ā', the suffix ghyaṇa occurs in the sense of state or passive, and 'ā' becomes 'e'. From the root dā, in the sense of giving: `dātabbaṃ` is equivalent to `deyyaṃ` (to be given). From the root pā, in the sense of drinking: 'it is drunk' (`pīyatīti`), thus `peyyaṃ` (to be drunk). From the root mā, in the sense of measuring: 'it is measured' (`mīyatīti`), thus `meyyaṃ` (to be measured). From the root ñā, in the sense of understanding: 'it is known' (`ñāyatīti`), thus `ñeyyaṃ`, [equivalent to] `ñātabbaṃ` (to be known). When ū is present, there is no augment. By the rule 'ñāssa ne jā', with the substitution of `jā` for `ñā`, [the forms are] `jānitabbaṃ` and `vijāniyaṃ`. From the root khā, in the sense of declaring: `saṃkhātabbaṃ` is equivalent to `saṃkheyyaṃ` (to be declared/counted).

30. Vadādīhi yo

30. Vadādīhi yo

Vadādīhi [M 0.0267] kriyatthehi yo hoti bahulaṃ bhāvakammesu. Vada=vacane, vadanaṃ vajjatīti vā vajjaṃ. Mada=ummāde, madanaṃ majjate anenāti vā majjaṃ. Gamanaṃ gammateti vā gammaṃ. Gada=vacane, gajjate gadanīyaṃ vāti gajjaṃ. Pada=gamane, pajjanīyaṃ pajjaṃ gāthā. Ada+khāda=bhakkhane, khajjatīti khajjaṃ khādanīyaṃ. Dama=damane, dammateti dammo damanīyo.

From verbal roots such as vada, the suffix 'ya' frequently occurs in the sense of state or passive. From the root vada, in the sense of speaking: `vadanaṃ` (speaking), or 'it is spoken' (`vajjatīti`), thus `vajjaṃ` (to be spoken/fault). From the root mada, in the sense of intoxication: `madanaṃ` (intoxicating), or 'one is intoxicated by this' (`majjate anenāti`), thus `majjaṃ` (intoxicant). `Gamanaṃ` (going), or 'it is gone to' (`gammateti`), thus `gammaṃ` (accessible). From the root gada, in the sense of speaking: 'it is spoken' (`gajjate`), or `gadanīyaṃ` (to be spoken), thus `gajjaṃ` (to be spoken). From the root pada, in the sense of going: `pajjanīyaṃ` (to be gone on), `pajjaṃ` (a path/verse), as in `gāthā` (a verse). From the roots ada and khāda, in the sense of eating: 'it is eaten' (`khajjatīti`), thus `khajjaṃ`, `khādanīyaṃ` (to be eaten/edible). From the root dama, in the sense of taming: 'it is tamed' (`dammateti`), thus `dammo`, `damanīyo` (to be tamed).

Bhujā+nneti gaṇasuttena anne vattabbe yapaccayo.

By the class-rule (gaṇasutta) beginning 'bhujānam ne', the suffix ya is to be stated for other roots.

83. Lahussupantassati

83. Lahussupantassa

Lahubhūtassa upantassa iyuvaṇṇassa eo honti yathākkamaṃ. Yassa pubbarūpe bhuñjitabboti bhojjo odano, bhojjā yāgu.

Of a light penultimate vowel, i and u become e and o respectively. With assimilation to the preceding consonant, `bhuñjitabbo` (to be eaten) becomes `bhojjo odano` (edible rice), [and] `bhojjā yāgu` (edible gruel).

31. Kicca ghacca bhacca bhabba leyyā

31. Kicca, ghacca, bhacca, bhabba, leyyā

Ete saddā yapaccayantā nipaccante. Kara=karaṇe, iminā nipātanā ye kicādese ca kate pubbarūpaṃ, kattabbaṃ kiccaṃ. Hana=hiṃsāyaṃ, ghaccādesādimhi kate hananaṃ haññateti vā ghaccaṃ. Bhara=bharaṇe, bhaccādesādimhi kate bharaṇīyo bhacco. Bhū=sattāyaṃ, yamhi okāre iminā avādese bhavatīti bhabbo. Liha=assādane, yamhi iminā hassa yakāre lehitabbaṃ leyyaṃ, ekāravuddhi.

These words, ending with the 'ya' suffix, are irregularly formed. From the root kara, in the sense of doing: by this irregular formation, with the substitution of `kicca` for `ya` and assimilation, `kattabbaṃ` becomes `kiccaṃ` (what should be done). From the root hana, in the sense of harming: with the substitution of `ghacca` etc., `hananaṃ` (harming), or 'it is harmed' (`haññateti`), becomes `ghaccaṃ` (what should be killed). From the root bhara, in the sense of bearing: with the substitution of `bhacca` etc., `bharaṇīyo` (to be supported) becomes `bhacco` (a servant). From the root bhū, in the sense of being: when `ya` is present, by this [irregular formation], with the substitution of `ava` for `o`, 'it becomes' (`bhavatīti`) leads to `bhabbo` (capable/fitting). From the root liha, in the sense of tasting: when `ya` is present, by this [irregular formation], with `y` for `h`, `lehitabbaṃ` becomes `leyyaṃ` (to be licked), with vṛddhi to `e`.

32. Guhādīhi yaka

32. Guhādīhi yaka

Guhādīhi [M 0.0268] kriyatthehi bhāvakammesu yaka hoti. Guha=saṃvaraṇe, “lahussupantassā”ti sampattassa okārassa “na te kānubandhanāgamesū”ti paṭisedho. “Hassa vipallāso”ti vipallāse guhanaṃ guhitabbaṃ guyhaṃ. Duha=papūraṇe, dohanaṃ duyhatīti vā duyhaṃ. Sāsa=anusiṭṭhiyaṃ –

From verbal roots such as guha, the suffix yaka occurs in the sense of state or passive. From the root guha, in the sense of concealing: the substitution of 'o' which would be obtained by the rule 'lahussupantassā' is prohibited by the rule 'na te kānubandhanāgamesu'. By the rule 'Hassa vipallāso' (interchange of 'h'), with this interchange, `guhanaṃ` (concealing) or `guhitabbaṃ` (to be concealed) becomes `guyhaṃ` (secret). From the root duha, in the sense of milking: `dohanaṃ` (milking), or 'it is milked' (`duyhatīti`), becomes `duyhaṃ` (to be milked). From the root sāsa, in the sense of instructing –

117. Sāsassa sisa vā

117. Sāsassa sisa vā

Sāsassa sisa vā hoti kānubandhe. Pubbarūpaṃ, sāsīyatīti sisso.

Of `sāsa`, `sisa` optionally occurs when a suffix with an indicatory `ka` follows. With assimilation, 'he is instructed' (`sāsīyatīti`) becomes `sisso` (pupil).

Siddhā eve+te tabbādayo pesā+tisagga+ppattakālesu gamyamānesupi, sāmaññena vidhānato. Pesanaṃ – “kattabba+midaṃ bhavatā”ti āṇāpanaṃ ajjhesanañca. Atisaggo nāma “ki+midaṃ mayā kattabbaṃ”ti puṭṭhassa “pāṇo na hantabbo”tiādinā paṭipattidassanamukhena kattabbassa anuññā. Pattakālo nāma sampattasamayo. Yo kiccakaraṇasamayaṃ upaparikkhitvā karoti, tassa samayārocanaṃ, na tattha ajjhesana+matthi. Bhotā khalu kaṭo kattabbo karaṇīyo kāriyo kicco” evaṃ tvayā kaṭo kattabbo, bhoto hi patto kālo kaṭakaraṇe.

These suffixes beginning with `tabba` are indeed established by general rule even when the senses of command (pesana), permission (atisagga), and opportune time (pattakāla) are understood. Command is commanding and requesting, as in 'This is to be done by you.' Permission is the name for the allowance of what is to be done, shown by way of proper conduct, such as 'A living being is not to be killed,' to one who has asked 'What is to be done by me?'. Opportune time is the name for the arrived time. For one who acts after having examined the time for doing a task, it is the announcing of the time; there is no requesting in that case. 'Indeed, the mat is to be made by you, sir (bhotā khalu kaṭo kattabbo), is to be done (karaṇīyo), is to be made (kāriyo), is a duty (kicco).' Thus, the mat is to be made by you, for the time has arrived for you, sir, to make the mat.

Evaṃ uddhamuhuttepi vattamānato pesādīsu siddhā eva. Tathā arahe kattari sattivisiṭṭhe ca patīyamāne, āvassakā+dhamīṇatāvisiṭṭhe ca bhāvādo siddhā. Uddhaṃ muhuttato-bhotā kaṭo kattabbo. Bhotā rajjaṃ kātabbaṃ, bhavaṃ araho. Bhotā [M 0.0269] bhāro vahitabbo, bhavaṃ sakko. Bhotā avassaṃ kaṭo kattabbo. Bhotā nikkho dātabbo.

Thus, they are established in the sense of command, etc., even when referring to a future moment. Likewise, they are established in the agentive sense when 'worthy' or 'endowed with ability' is understood; and in the sense of state, etc., when 'necessity' or 'being indebted' is understood. From a future moment: 'The mat is to be made by you, sir.' 'The kingdom is to be ruled by you, sir; you are worthy.' 'The burden is to be carried by you, sir; you are able.' 'The mat must necessarily be made by you, sir.' 'The gold coin is to be given by you, sir (as a debt).'

33. Kattari ltu+ṇkā

33. Kattari ltu ṇkā

Kattari kārake kriyatthā ltu+ṇkā honti. Kara=karaṇe, pararūpe “ltu+pitādīna+mā simhī”ti ā silopo ca. Karotīti kattā. Evaṃ bharatīti bhattā. Haratīti hattā. Bhidatīti bhettā, ekāro, ūmhi bheditā. Chindatīti chettā. Bhojanassa dātā bhojanadātā. Sandhātīti sandhātā. Vacatīti vattā. Okārapararūpesu bhuñjatīti bhottā. “Padādīnaṃ kvacī”ti yukāgamo, bujjhatīti bujjhitā. Jānātīti ñātā. Chindatīti chetā. Suṇātīti sotā. “Ū+lasse”ti ūssa ekāre gaṇhātīti gahetā. Bhavatīti bhavitā. Saratīti saritā. “Manānaṃ niggahītaṃ”ti massa niggahīte vaggante ca gacchatīti gantā. Nakārantānampi niggahītaṃ, khanatīti khantā. Sanatīti santā. Maññatīti mantā. Pāletīti pālayitā pāletā, ettha curādittā ṇi.

After verbal roots, the suffixes tu and ṇka occur in the agentive case. From the root kara, in the sense of doing: with assimilation, by the rule 'ltu pitādīnam ā simhī', there is elision of `ā` and `si`. 'He does' (`karoti`), thus `kattā` (doer). Similarly, 'he supports' (`bharati`), thus `bhattā` (supporter). 'He carries' (`harati`), thus `hattā` (carrier). 'He breaks' (`bhidati`), thus `bhettā` (breaker), with `e`; when `ū` is present, `bheditā`. 'He cuts' (`chindati`), thus `chettā` (cutter). 'Giver of food' (`bhojanassa dātā`), thus `bhojanadātā`. 'He joins' (`sandhāti`), thus `sandhātā` (joiner). 'He speaks' (`vacati`), thus `vattā` (speaker). With assimilation involving `o`, 'he eats' (`bhuñjati`), thus `bhottā` (eater). By the rule 'padādīnaṃ kvaci', there is sometimes the `i` augment; 'he understands' (`bujjhati`), thus `bujjhitā`. 'He knows' (`jānāti`), thus `ñātā` (knower). 'He cuts' (`chindati`), thus `chettā`. 'He hears' (`suṇāti`), thus `sotā` (hearer). By the rule 'ūlasse', with `e` for `ū`, 'he takes' (`gaṇhāti`), thus `gahetā` (taker). 'He is' (`bhavati`), thus `bhavitā` (one who will be). 'He remembers' (`sarati`), thus `saritā` (one who remembers). By the rule 'manānaṃ niggahītaṃ', with `m` becoming niggahīta and then a nasal of the class, 'he goes' (`gacchati`), thus `gantā` (goer). For roots ending in `n` also, it becomes niggahīta; 'he digs' (`khanati`), thus `khantā` (digger). 'He is peaceful' (`sanati`), thus `santā`. 'He thinks' (`maññati`), thus `mantā` (thinker). 'He protects' (`pāleti`), thus `pālayitā` or `pāletā`; here, because it belongs to the `curādi` class, the suffix is `ṇi`.

Ṇiṇāpīsu-bhāvayatīti bhāvayitā bhāvetā. Evaṃ sārayitā sāretā, dāpayitā dāpetā, hāpayitā hāpetā, nirodhayitā nirodhetā, bodhayitā bodhetā, ñāpayitā ñāpetā, sāvayitā sāvetā, gāhayitā gāhetā, kārayitā kāretā, kārāpayitā kārāpetā iccādi.

With the suffixes ṇi and ṇāpi: 'he causes to be' (`bhāvayati`), thus `bhāvayitā` or `bhāvetā`. Similarly, `sārayitā` or `sāretā`, `dāpayitā` or `dāpetā`, `hāpayitā` or `hāpetā`, `nirodhayitā` or `nirodhetā`, `bodhayitā` or `bodhetā`, `ñāpayitā` or `ñāpetā`, `sāvayitā` or `sāvetā`, `gāhayitā` or `gāhetā`, `kārayitā` or `kāretā`, `kārāpayitā` or `kārāpetā`, and so on.

Ṇkapaccaye-ṇakāro [M 0.0270] vuddhyattho. Rathaṃ karotīti rathakārako, “assā ṇānubandhe”ti ā amādisamāso ca. Annaṃ dadātīti annadāyako. “Adhātussa kā+syādito ghe+ssī”ti ghe pare assa iādeso, annadāyikā, annadāyakaṃ kulaṃ. “Āssā+ṇāpimhi yuka” itiṇāpito+ññatra yuka. Lokaṃ netīti lokanāyako, ekāre “āyā+vā ṇānubandhe”ti āyādeso. Evaṃ vinetīti vināyako.

With the suffix ṇka, the letter ṇ is for the purpose of vṛddhi. 'He makes a chariot' (`rathaṃ karoti`), thus `rathakārako` (chariot-maker); the `ā` is by the rule 'assā ṇānubandhe', and it is an amādi-compound. 'He gives food' (`annaṃ dadāti`), thus `annadāyako` (food-giver). By the rule 'adhātussa kā syādito ghe ssī', when `ghi` follows, the final `a` is substituted by `i`; hence `annadāyikā` (feminine), `annadāyakaṃ kulaṃ` (neuter). By the rule 'āssā ṇāpimhi yuka', the `yuk` augment occurs elsewhere than after `ṇāpi`. 'He leads the world' (`lokaṃ neti`), thus `lokanāyako` (world-leader); when `e` is present, there is the substitution of `āya` by the rule 'āyā vā ṇānubandhe'. Similarly, 'he trains' (`vineti`), thus `vināyako` (guide).

Akammupapade-karotīti kārako, evaṃ dāyako nāyako, okāre āvādese suṇātīti sāvako. Pure viya ikāre sāvikā. Lunātīti lāvako. Pu=pavane, punātīti pāvako. Bhavatīti bhāvako, upāsatīti upāsako. Gaṇhātīti gāhako pāvako, yājako. Vadha=hiṃsāyaṃ, vadhetīti vadhako, “aññatrāpī”ti vuddhipaṭisedho. “Hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe”ti ghātādeso, hanatīti ghātako. “Maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ”ti maṃ, rundhako, guruttā na vuddhi. Tathā bhuñjatīti bhuñjako. Āyassa rasse kiṇātīti kayako. Pāletīti pālako. Pūjetīti pūjako.

When not preceded by an object in a compound: from 'karoti' comes 'kārako' (doer); similarly, 'dāyako' (giver), 'nāyako' (leader). With the substitution of 'āv' for 'o', from 'suṇāti' comes 'sāvako' (listener). As before, with 'ikā' in the feminine, 'sāvikā' (female listener). From 'lunāti' comes 'lāvako' (reaper). 'Pu' is in the sense of 'purifying'; from 'punāti' comes 'pāvako' (purifier). From 'bhavati' comes 'bhāvako' (one who develops). From 'upāsati' comes 'upāsako' (lay follower). From 'gaṇhāti' comes 'gāhako' (taker); also 'pāvako' (purifier), 'yājako' (sacrificer). 'Vadha' is in the sense of 'killing'; from 'vadheti' comes 'vadhako' (killer), with the prohibition of vṛddhi by the rule 'aññatrāpi'. By the rule 'hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe', 'ghāta' is the substitute for 'hana'; hence, from 'hanati' comes 'ghātako' (slayer). By the rule 'maṃ vā rudhādīnaṃ', 'maṃ' is inserted; thus, 'rundhako' (obstructer), with no vṛddhi due to the heavy syllable. Similarly, from 'bhuñjati' comes 'bhuñjako' (eater). With the shortening of 'āya', from 'kiṇāti' comes 'kayako' (buyer). From 'pāleti' comes 'pālako' (protector). From 'pūjeti' comes 'pūjako' (worshiper).

Khādīsu-titikkhatīti titikkhako. Vīmaṃsatīti vīmaṃsako iccādi. Panudatīti panūdako, “byañjane”ccādinā dīgho. “Bhītvā+nako”ti ettha ‘ānako’ti yogavibhāgā ānako, āssa rasse nakārāgame ca “ñāssa ne jā”ti jādeso, jānanako. Ṇāpimhi –

In the group of roots beginning with 'khād': from 'titikkhati' comes 'titikkhako' (one who is patient). From 'vīmaṃsati' comes 'vīmaṃsako' (investigator), and so on. From 'panudati' comes 'panūdako' (remover); the vowel is lengthened by the rule beginning with 'byañjane'. In the case of 'Bhītvā+nako', here, by splitting the rule, the suffix is 'ānako'; with the shortening of 'ā', the augment 'na', and the substitution of 'jā' by the rule 'ñāssa ne jā', the form is 'jānanako'. In the case of the causative (ṇāpi) –

Aṇa-iti [M 0.0271] daṇḍakadhātu, āṇāpetīti āṇāpako. Tathā saññāpako, patiṭṭhāpako. Saṃ+pa pubbo āpa=pāpuṇane, nibbānaṃ sampāpetīti nibbānasampāpako. Kārāpako, kārāpikā iccādi.

The root 'aṇa' is a daṇḍaka-dhātu; from 'āṇāpeti' comes 'āṇāpako' (one who commands). Similarly, 'saññāpako' (one who makes known), 'patiṭṭhāpako' (one who establishes). From the root 'āpa', in the sense of 'reaching', when preceded by 'saṃ' and 'pa'; from 'nibbānaṃ sampāpeti' (he causes to attain Nibbāna) comes 'nibbānasampāpako' (one who leads to the attainment of Nibbāna). 'Kārāpako' (one who causes to do), 'kārāpikā' (a female who causes to do), and so on.

Bahulaṃvidhānā kammepi-pādehi harīyatīti pādahārako. Cupa=mandagamane, gale cuppatīti galacopako.

By the principle of varied application, also in the sense of the object: from 'pādehi harīyati' (he is carried by the feet) comes 'pādahārako' (one who is carried by the feet). 'Cupa' is in the sense of 'slow movement'; from 'gale cuppati' (he moves slowly in the throat) comes 'galacopako' (one who moves slowly in the throat).

Siddhova ltu arahādīsu “bhavaṃ khalu kaññāya pariggahāraho”ti (pariggahitā). Sīlatthe-upādānasīloti upādātā. Sādhu gacchatīti gantā. Muṇḍanadhammā muṇḍanācārāti muṇḍayitāro, ettha “dhātvatthe nāmasmī”ti imhi ūāgame e+ayādese muṇḍayitusaddamhi āraṅādese ca kate yossa ṭo.

The suffix 'tu' is also established in the senses of 'worthy' and so on. For example: 'bhavaṃ khalu kaññāya pariggahāraho' (Indeed, sir, you are worthy of accepting the maiden), which means 'pariggahetā' (one who accepts). In the sense of habit: 'upādānasīlo' (one whose habit is to grasp) becomes 'upādātā' (one who grasps). From 'sādhu gacchati' (he goes well) comes 'gantā' (one who goes). 'Muṇḍanadhammā muṇḍanācārā' (those whose nature and practice is to shave) becomes 'muṇḍayitāro' (shavers); here, by the rule 'dhātvatthe nāmasmī', with the augment 'ū', the substitution of 'aya' for 'e', and in the word 'muṇḍayitu', when the substitution 'āraṅ' is made, 'ya' becomes 'ṭa'.

34. Āvī

34. Āvī

Kriyatthā āvī hoti bahulaṃ kattari. “Disassa passa+dassa=dasa+da+dakkhā”ti dassādeso, bhayaṃ passatīti bhayadassāvī. Nīmhi bhayadassāvinī. Bhayadassāvi cittaṃ. Appavisayatāñāpanatthaṃ bhinnayogakaraṇaṃ. Sāmaññavihitattā sīlādīsu ca hoteva.

The suffix 'āvī' occurs frequently in the agentive sense from a root denoting an action. By the rule beginning 'Disassa passa...', the substitute is 'dassā'; from 'bhayaṃ passati' (he sees fear) comes 'bhayadassāvī' (one who sees fear). In the feminine, with the 'nī' suffix, it is 'bhayadassāvinī'. In the neuter, 'bhayadassāvi cittaṃ' (a mind that sees fear). The formulation of a separate rule is for the purpose of indicating a limited scope. As it is generally prescribed, it also occurs in the senses of habit and so on.

35. Āsiṃsāya+mako

35. Āsiṃsāyaṃ ako

Āsiṃsāyaṃ gammamānāyaṃ kriyatthā ako hoti kattari. Jīva=pāṇadhāraṇe, jīvatūti jīvako. Nanda=samiddhiyaṃ, nandatūti nandako. Bhavatūti bhavako.

When a wish is implied, the suffix 'ako' occurs in the agentive sense from a root denoting an action. From the root 'jīva', in the sense of sustaining life: from 'jīvatu' (may he live) comes 'jīvako'. From the root 'nanda', in the sense of prosperity: from 'nandatu' (may he prosper) comes 'nandako'. From 'bhavatu' (may he be) comes 'bhavako'.

36. Karā ṇano

36. Karā ṇano

Karato [M 0.0272] kattari ṇa no hoti. Karotīti kāraṇaṃ. Kattarīti kiṃ, karoti anenāti karaṇaṃ.

After the root 'kara', the suffix 'ṇa' does not occur in the agentive sense. The form is 'kāraṇaṃ' (cause). Why is 'in the agentive sense' stated? Because of 'karoti anena iti karaṇaṃ' (that by which one does is an instrument).

37. Hāto vīhi+kālesu

37. Hāto vīhi-kālesu

Hāto vīhismiṃ kāle ca ṇano hoti. “Āssā”tyādinā yuka, jahanti udakaṃti hāyanā vīhayo. Jahāti bhāve padattheti hāyano saṃvaccharo. Vīhikālesūti kiṃ, jahātīti hātā.

After the root 'hā', the suffix 'ṇa' occurs when the meaning is 'rice' or 'time'. By the rule beginning with 'Āssā', the suffix is 'yuka'; from 'jahanti udakaṃ' (they abandon water) comes 'hāyanā vīhayo' (a type of rice). In the sense of the verbal noun, from 'jahāti' (it passes) comes 'hāyano saṃvaccharo' (a year). Why is 'in the sense of rice and time' stated? Because otherwise, from 'jahāti' (he abandons) comes 'hātā' (one who abandons).

38. Vidā kū

38. Vidā kū

Vidasmā kū hoti kattari. Kakāro “kūto”ti visesanattho. Vidatīti vidū, lokavidū.

After the root 'vid', the suffix 'kū' occurs in the agentive sense. The letter 'ka' is for the purpose of specification, as in the rule 'kūto'. From 'vidati' (he knows) comes 'vidū' (one who knows); for example, 'lokavidū' (knower of the world).

39. Vito ñāto

39. Vito ñāto

Vipubbā ñāicca+smā kū hoti kattari. Vijānātīti viññū.

After the root 'ñā' preceded by 'vi', the suffix 'kū' occurs in the agentive sense. From 'vijānāti' (he understands) comes 'viññū' (one who understands).

40. Kammā

40. Kammā

Kammato parā ñāicca+smā kū hoti kattari. Sabbaṃ jānātīti sabbaññū. Evaṃ mattaññū, dhammaññū, atthaññū kālaññū, kataññū iccādi. (Bhikkhūti pana “bharādi” ṇvādisuttena siddhaṃ).

After a word denoting an object, the suffix 'kū' occurs from the root 'ñā' in the agentive sense. From 'sabbaṃ jānāti' (he knows all) comes 'sabbaññū' (the all-knower). Similarly, 'mattaññū' (knower of measure), 'dhammaññū' (knower of the Dhamma), 'atthaññū' (knower of the meaning), 'kālaññū' (knower of time), 'kataññū' (one who is grateful), and so on. (The word 'bhikkhu', however, is formed by the rule for the 'ṇvā' etc. suffixes, beginning with 'bharādi').

41. Kvacaṇa

41. Kvaci aṇa

Kammato parā kriyatthā kvaci aṇa hoti kattari. Kumbhaṃ karotīti kumbhakāro, amādisamāso. Itthiyaṃ kumbhakārī. Evaṃ kammakāro, māsākāro, kaṭṭhakāro, rathakāro suvaṇṇakāro[M 0.0273], suttakāro, vuttikāro, ṭīkākāro. Saraṃ lunātīti saralāvoti o+avādesā. Mante ajjhāyatīti manthajjhāyo, i=ajjhenagatīsu, adhipubbo, e+ayādesā, adhino issa yakāra+cavaggādayo ca.

After a word denoting an object, the suffix 'aṇa' sometimes occurs in the agentive sense from a root denoting an action. From 'kumbhaṃ karoti' (he makes a pot) comes 'kumbhakāro' (potter); this is an 'amādi' compound. In the feminine, 'kumbhakārī'. Similarly, 'kammakāro' (worker), 'māsākāro' (calendar-maker), 'kaṭṭhakāro' (carpenter), 'rathakāro' (chariot-maker), 'suvaṇṇakāro' (goldsmith), 'suttakāro' (author of a text), 'vuttikāro' (author of a commentary), 'ṭīkākāro' (author of a sub-commentary). From 'saraṃ lunāti' (he cuts reeds) comes 'saralāvo', with the substitution of 'av' for 'o'. From 'mante ajjhāyati' (he recites mantras) comes 'manthajjhāyo'; the root is 'i' in the sense of 'going for study', preceded by 'adhi'; there is a substitution of 'ay' for 'e', and also the rules for 'adhino issa yakāra' and 'cavaggādayo'.

Bahulādhikārā iha na hoti “ādiccaṃ passati, himavantaṃ suṇoti, gāmaṃ gacchati”. Kvacīti kiṃ, kammakaro, ettha apaccayo.

Due to the governing principle of 'bahula' (varied application), the suffix does not occur in cases such as 'ādiccaṃ passati' (he sees the sun), 'himavantaṃ suṇoti' (he hears of the Himalayas), 'gāmaṃ gacchati' (he goes to the village). Why is 'sometimes' stated? In 'kammakaro' (worker), the suffix is 'a'.

42. Gamā rū

42. Gamā rū

Kammato parā gamā rū hoti kattari. Rānubandhattā amabhāgalopo. Vedaṃ gacchatīti vedagū, evaṃ pāragū.

After a word denoting an object, the suffix 'rū' occurs from the root 'gam' in the agentive sense. Due to the indicatory letter 'r', the 'am' portion of the root is elided. From 'vedaṃ gacchati' (he goes to the Veda) comes 'vedagū' (one who has mastered the Veda); similarly, 'pāragū' (one who has gone to the far shore).

Sāmaññavidhānato sīlādīsupi hoti. Bhavapāraṃ gacchati sīlenāti bhavapāragū. Antagamanasīlo antagū, evaṃ addhagū.

By general prescription, it also occurs in the senses of habit and so on. From 'bhavapāraṃ gacchati sīlena' (he goes to the far shore of existence by his nature) comes 'bhavapāragū'. 'Antagamanasīlo' (one whose habit is to go to the end) is 'antagū' (one who has reached the end); similarly, 'addhagū' (a traveller).

43. Samāna+ñña+bhavanta+yāditū+pamānā disā kamme rī+rikkha+kā

43. Samāna-añña-bhavanta-yādi-tūpamānā disā kamme rī-rikkha-kā

Samānādīhi yādīhi co+pamānehi parā disā kammakārake rī+rikkha+kā honti. “Syādi syādine+katthaṃ”ti samāse “rānubandhe+ntasarādissā”ti disassa isabhāgalope “rīrikkhakesū”ti samānassa sādese ca samāno viya dissatīti sadī, sadikkho. Ke – “na te kānubandhanāgamesū”ti ettābhāvo, sadiso.

After the root 'dis', when preceded by 'samāna' etc., 'yādi' etc., and words of comparison, the suffixes 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'kā' occur in the objective sense. In a compound, by the rule 'rānubandhe...', the 'isa' portion of 'disa' is elided; and by the rule for 'rī-rikkha-kesu', 'sā' is substituted for 'samāna'. Thus, from 'samāno viya dissati' (he appears like an equal) come 'sadī' and 'sadikkho'. With the suffix 'ka', by the rule 'na te kānubandhanāgamesu', there is no 'e'-vowel, hence 'sadiso'.

125. Samānā ro rī+rikkha+kesu

125. Samānā ro rī-rikkha-kesu

Samānasaddato [M 0.0274] parassa disassa ra hoti vā rī+rikkha+kesūti pakkhe dassa rādese sarī, sarikkho, sariso.

After the word 'samāna', 'ra' is optionally substituted for the following root 'disa' before the suffixes 'rī', 'rikkha', and 'ka'. In the case where the substitution occurs, with 'ra' replacing 'disa', the forms are 'sarī', 'sarikkho', and 'sariso'.

3,86. Sabbādīna+mā

3.86. Sabbādīnamā

Rī+rikkha+kesu sabbādīna+mā hoti. Añño viya dissatīti aññādī, aññādikkho, aññādiso.

In the context of the suffixes `rī`, `rikkha`, and `kesu`, for `sabba` and other pronouns, `mā` occurs. 'One who appears like another' (`añño viya dissati`) is `aññādī`, `aññādikkho`, `aññādiso`.

3,87. Nta+ki+mi+mānaṃ ṭā+kī+ṭī

3,87. Nta+ki+mi+mānaṃ ṭā+kī+ṭī

Rī+rikkha+kesu nta+kiṃ+imasaddānaṃ ṭā+kī+ṭī honti yathākkamaṃ. Ṭakārā sabbādesatthā. Bhavādī bhavādikkho bhavādiso, kīdī kīdikkho kīdiso, ayamiva dissatīti īdī īdikkho īdiso. Ākāre yādī yādikkho yādiso, tyādī tyādikkho tyādiso iccādi.

In the context of `rī`, `rikkha`, and `kesu`, for the words `nta`, `kiṃ`, and `ima`, there are the substitutions `ṭā`, `kī`, and `ṭī` respectively. The letter `ṭa` indicates a complete substitution. Examples: `bhavādī`, `bhavādikkho`, `bhavādiso`; `kīdī`, `kīdikkho`, `kīdiso`; 'one who appears like this' (`ayamiva dissati`) becomes `īdī`, `īdikkho`, `īdiso`. With the vowel `ā`: `yādī`, `yādikkho`, `yādiso`; `tyādī`, `tyādikkho`, `tyādiso`, and so on.

3,88. Tumhāmhānaṃ tāme+kasmiṃ

3,88. Tumhāmhānaṃ tāme+kasmiṃ

Rī+rikkha+kesu tumhāmhānaṃ tāmā honte+kasmiṃ yathākkamaṃ. Tvaṃ viya dissati, ayaṃ viya dissatīti tādī mādī iccādi. Ekasminti kiṃ, tumhādiso amhādiso.

In the context of `rī`, `rikkha`, and `kesu`, `tā` and `mā` occur for `tumha` and `amha` respectively, in the singular. 'One who appears like you' (`tvaṃ viya dissati`), 'one who appears like this' (`ayaṃ viya dissati`) become `tādī`, `mādī`, and so on. Why is 'in the singular' stated? For cases like `tumhādiso` (like you) and `amhādiso` (like us).

3,89. Taṃ+ma+maññatra

3,89. Taṃ+ma+maññatra

Rīrikkhakantato+ññasmiṃ uttarapade tumhāmhāna+mekasmiṃ taṃ+maṃ honti yathākkamaṃ. Tvaṃ dīpo esaṃ, ahaṃ dīpo esaṃti aññapadatthe taṃdīpā maṃdīpā. Tvaṃ saraṇa+mesaṃ, ahaṃ saraṇa+ mesanti [M 0.0275] taṃsaraṇā maṃsaraṇā. Tayā yogo tayyogo, mayā yogo mayyogoti amādisamāse niggahītalopo.

When a subsequent word other than one ending in `rī`, `rikkha`, or `ka` follows, `taṃ` and `maṃ` are substituted for `tumha` and `amha` respectively, in the singular. 'You are a light to them' (`tvaṃ dīpo esaṃ`), 'I am a light to them' (`ahaṃ dīpo esaṃ`)—in the sense of a relative compound, these become `taṃdīpā`, `maṃdīpā`. 'You are a refuge to them' (`tvaṃ saraṇaṃ esaṃ`), 'I am a refuge to them' (`ahaṃ saraṇaṃ esaṃ`)—these become `taṃsaraṇā`, `maṃsaraṇā`. 'Union with you' (`tayā yogo`) becomes `tayyogo`; 'union with me' (`mayā yogo`) becomes `mayyogo`. In compounds such as `amādi`, there is elision of the niggahīta.

3,90. Ve+tasse+ṭa

3,90. Ve+tasse+ṭa

Rī+rikkha+kesu etassa eṭa vā hoti. Edī etādī, edikkho etādikkho, ediso etādiso.

In the context of `rī`, `rikkha`, and `kesu`, for `etassa` (this), `eṭa` occurs optionally. `Edī`, `etādī`; `edikkho`, `etādikkho`; `ediso`, `etādiso`.

44. Bhāvakārake sva+ghaṇa gha kā

44. Bhāvakārake sva+ghaṇa gha kā

Bhāve kārake ca kriyatthā a ghaṇa gha kā honti bahulaṃ.

From roots indicating action, the suffixes `a`, `ghaṇa`, `gha`, and `kā` occur frequently in the sense of state (bhāva) and agent (kāraka).

Apaccayo-paggaṇhanaṃ paggaho, evaṃ niggaho, dhammaṃ dhāretīti dhammadharo, evaṃ vinayadharo. Tathā taṃ karotīti takkaro, dvittaṃ. Evaṃ hitakaro, divasakaro, dinakaro, divākaro, nisākaro, dhanuṃ gaṇhīti dhanuggaho. Evaṃ kavacaggaho. Dada=dāne, sabbakāmaṃ dadātīti sabbakāmadado, sabbadado. Āto “parokkhāyañcā”ti caggahaṇena dvitte “rasso pubbassā”ti rasse ca annaṃ dadātīti annadado, evaṃ dhanado. Saṃpubbo dhā=dhāraṇe, sabbaṃ sandhahatīti sabbasandho. Nī=pāpane, vipubbo, vinesi vineti vinessati etena etthāti vā vinayo, e+ayādesā. Nayanaṃ nayo. Si=sevāyaṃ, nipubbo, nissīyatīti nissayo. Si=saye, anusayi anuseti anusessatīti anusayo. I=gatimhi, patipubbo, paṭicca etasmā phala+metīti paccayo. Saṃ+upubbo, dāgame samudayo[M 0.0276]. Ci=caye, vinicchayate+nena vinicchayanaṃ vā vinicchayo, “nito cissa cho”ti cissa cho. Uccayanaṃ uccayo, saṃcayo. Khi=khaye, khayanaṃ khayo. Ji=jaye, vijayanaṃ vijayo, jayo. Kī=dabbavinīmaye, vikkayanaṃ vikkayo, kayo. Lī=silesane, allīyanti etthāti ālayo, layo. (Ivaṇṇantā).

The suffix `a`: `paggaṇhanaṃ` becomes `paggaho`; similarly, `niggaho`. 'One who upholds the Dhamma' (`dhammaṃ dhāreti`) is `dhammadharo`; similarly, `vinayadharo`. Likewise, 'one who does that' (`taṃ karoti`) is `takkaro`, with doubling. Similarly: `hitakaro`, `divasakaro`, `dinakaro`, `divākaro`, `nisākaro`. 'One who takes a bow' (`dhanuṃ gaṇhāti`) is `dhanuggaho`; similarly, `kavacaggaho`. The root `dada` is in the sense of giving: 'one who gives all desires' (`sabbakāmaṃ dadāti`) is `sabbakāmadado`, `sabbadado`. From a root ending in `ā`, by the inclusion of `ca` in the rule `parokkhāyañca`, there is doubling, and by `rasso pubbassā`, there is shortening: 'one who gives food' (`annaṃ dadāti`) is `annadado`; similarly, `dhanado`. The root `dhā` with the prefix `saṃ` is in the sense of holding: 'one who connects all' (`sabbaṃ sandhahati`) is `sabbasandho`. The root `nī` is in the sense of leading, with the prefix `vi`: 'one led, leads, or will lead by this or herein' becomes `vinayo`, with the substitution of `aya` for `e`. `Nayanaṃ` is `nayo`. The root `si` is in the sense of resorting, with the prefix `ni`: 'it is relied upon' (`nissīyati`) is `nissayo`. The root `si` is in the sense of lying down: 'one lay, lies, or will lie down' becomes `anusayo`. The root `i` is in the sense of going, with the prefix `paṭi`: 'dependent on this, a result comes' (`paṭicca etasmā phalaṃ eti`) is `paccayo`. With the prefixes `saṃ` and `u`, and the augment `d`, `samudayo` is formed. The root `ci` is in the sense of accumulating: 'it is decided by this' or `vinicchayanaṃ` becomes `vinicchayo`; by the rule `nito cissa cho`, `ch` is substituted for `c`. `Uccayanaṃ` is `uccayo`; `saṃcayo`. The root `khi` is in the sense of wasting away: `khayanaṃ` is `khayo`. The root `ji` is in the sense of conquering: `vijayanaṃ` is `vijayo`; `jayo`. The root `kī` is in the sense of exchange of goods: `vikkayanaṃ` is `vikkayo`; `kayo`. The root `lī` is in the sense of clinging: 'they cling to this' (`allīyanti ettha`) is `ālayo`; `layo`. (Words ending in the vowel `i`).

Āsuṇantīti assavā, āssa rasso. Paṭissavanaṃ paṭissavo. Su=passavane, ābhavaggā savantīti āsavā. Ru=saddo ravatīti ravo. Bhavatīti bhavo. Pabhavati etasmāti pabhavo. Lū=chedane, lavanaṃ lavo. (Uvaṇṇantā).

'They listen' (`āsuṇanti`), hence `assavā`; the `ā` is shortened. `Paṭissavanaṃ` is `paṭissavo`. The root `su` is in the sense of flowing: 'they flow up to the highest point of existence' (`ābhavaggā savanti`), hence `āsavā`. The root `ru` is in the sense of sound: 'it sounds' (`ravati`), hence `ravo`. 'It becomes' (`bhavati`), hence `bhavo`. 'It originates from this' (`pabhavati etasmā`), hence `pabhavo`. The root `lū` is in the sense of cutting: `lavanaṃ` is `lavo`. (Words ending in the vowel `u`).

Cara=caraṇe, saṃcaraṇaṃ saṃcaro. Dara=vidāraṇe, ādaranaṃ ādaro. Āgacchati āgamanaṃti vā āgamo. Sappa=gamane, sappatīti sappo. Dibbatīti devo. Pakkamanaṃ pakkamatīti vā pakkamo, evaṃ vikkamo. Cara=caraṇe, vanaṃ caratīti vanacaro. Kāmo avacarati etthāti kāmāvacaro loko, kāmāvacarā paññā, kāmāvacaraṃ cittaṃ. Gāvo caranti etthāti gocaro. Pādena pivatīti pādapo. Evaṃ kacchapo. Sirasmiṃ ruhatīti siroruho, manādittā o. Guhāyaṃ sayatīti guhāsayaṃ cittaṃ, evaṃ kucchisayā vātā. Pabbate tiṭṭhatīti pabbataṭṭho puriso, pabbataṭṭhā nadī, pabbataṭṭhaṃ bhasmaṃ. Evaṃ thalaṭṭhaṃ jalaṭṭhaṃ.

The root `cara` is in the sense of walking: `saṃcaraṇaṃ` is `saṃcaro`. The root `dara` is in the sense of splitting: `ādaranaṃ` is `ādaro`. `Āgacchati` or `āgamanaṃ`, hence `āgamo`. The root `sappa` is in the sense of going: 'it creeps' (`sappati`), hence `sappo`. 'It shines' (`dibbati`), hence `devo`. `Pakkamanaṃ` or 'it departs' (`pakkamati`), hence `pakkamo`; similarly, `vikkamo`. The root `cara` is in the sense of walking: 'one who wanders in the forest' (`vanaṃ carati`), hence `vanacaro`. 'Desire moves about herein' (`kāmo avacarati ettha`), hence `kāmāvacaro loko` (the world of the sense-desire realm), `kāmāvacarā paññā` (wisdom pertaining to the sense-desire realm), `kāmāvacaraṃ cittaṃ` (mind pertaining to the sense-desire realm). 'Cows graze here' (`gāvo caranti ettha`), hence `gocaro` (pasture). 'It drinks with its foot' (`pādena pivati`), hence `pādapo` (tree); similarly, `kacchapo` (tortoise). 'It grows on the head' (`sirasmiṃ ruhati`), hence `siroruho` (hair); the `o` is due to the `manādi` group. 'It lies in a cave' (`guhāyaṃ sayati`), hence `guhāsayaṃ cittaṃ` (mind dwelling in a cave); similarly, `kucchisayā vātā` (winds dwelling in the belly). 'One who stands on a mountain' (`pabbate tiṭṭhati`), hence `pabbataṭṭho puriso` (a man standing on a mountain), `pabbataṭṭhā nadī` (a river on a mountain), `pabbataṭṭhaṃ bhasmaṃ` (ashes on a mountain). Similarly, `thalaṭṭhaṃ` (standing on land), `jalaṭṭhaṃ` (standing in water).

Kicchatthe dumhi akicchatthe su+īsaṃ+sukha upapadesu-dukkhena karīyati karaṇaṃ vā dukkaraṃ. Evaṃ dussayo, dukkhena bharīyatīti dubbharo mahiccho. Evaṃ durakkhaṃ cittaṃ, duddaso dhammo, duranubodho dhammo. Īsaṃ sayatīti īsaṃsayo, evaṃ [M 0.0277] sukhasayo. Īsaṃ karīyatīti īsakkaraṃ kammaṃ. Sukhena karīyatīti sukaraṃ pāpaṃ bālena. Evaṃ subharo appiccho, sudassaṃ paravajjaṃ, subodha+miccādi. Sabbattha pādiamādisamāsā.

When `du` is a pre-verb in the sense of difficulty, and when `su`, `īsaṃ`, and `sukha` are pre-verbs in the sense of ease: 'it is done with difficulty', or 'a difficult doing', hence `dukkaraṃ`. Similarly, `dussayo`; 'it is borne with difficulty', hence `dubbharo` (for one with great craving). Similarly, `durakkhaṃ cittaṃ` (a mind hard to guard), `duddaso dhammo` (the Dhamma hard to see), `duranubodho dhammo` (the Dhamma hard to understand). 'One lies down slightly', hence `īsaṃsayo`; similarly, `sukhasayo`. 'It is done slightly', hence `īsakkaraṃ kammaṃ` (an action done slightly). 'It is done easily', hence `sukaraṃ pāpaṃ bālena` (evil is easily done by a fool). Similarly, `subharo` (for one with few wishes), `sudassaṃ paravajjaṃ` (the fault of others is easy to see), `subodhaṃ`, and so on. In all cases, these are compounds of the `pādi` type.

Ghaṇa-bhavatīti bhāvo, o+āvādesā. Aya=iti daṇḍakadhātu, ayati itoti āyo, āharatīti āhāro. Upahanatīti upaghāto, “hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe”ti ghātādeso. Rañjatīti rāgo, “kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe”ti jassa go. Rañjanti anenāti rāgo. “Assā ṇānubandhe”ti ā, pajjate+nenāti pādo. Tuda=byathane, patujjate+nenāti patodo. Jarīyati anenāti jāro, evaṃ dāro. Bhajīyatīti bhāgo. Evaṃ bhāro. Labbhatīti lābho. Vi+opubbo, voharīyatīti vohāro. Diyyatīti dāyo, yuka. Vihaññati etasmāti vighāto. Viharanti etthāti vihāro. Āramanti etasminti ārāmo. Pacanaṃ vā pāko, cassa ko. Cajanaṃ cāgo. Yajanaṃ yāgo. Rajanaṃ rāgo.

The suffix `ghaṇa`: 'it becomes' (`bhavati`), hence `bhāvo`, with the substitution of `āv` for `o`. The root `aya` is a `daṇḍaka` root: 'it goes' (`ayati`), hence `āyo`; 'it brings' (`āharati`), hence `āhāro`. 'It strikes at' (`upahanati`), hence `upaghāto`; by the rule `hanassa ghāto ṇānubandhe`, `ghāta` is substituted. 'It is colored' (`rañjati`), hence `rāgo`; by the rule `kagā cajānaṃ ghānubandhe`, `g` is substituted for `j`. 'One is colored by this' (`rañjanti anena`), hence `rāgo`. By the rule `assā ṇānubandhe`, there is lengthening to `ā`: 'one goes by this' (`pajjate anena`), hence `pādo`. The root `tuda` is in the sense of afflicting: 'one is goaded by this' (`patujjate anena`), hence `patodo`. 'One is worn out by this' (`jarīyati anena`), hence `jāro`; similarly, `dāro`. 'It is divided' (`bhajīyati`), hence `bhāgo`. Similarly, `bhāro`. 'It is obtained' (`labbhati`), hence `lābho`. With the prefixes `vi` and `ava`: 'it is used' (`voharīyati`), hence `vohāro`. 'It is given' (`dīyati`), hence `dāyo`, with the augment `yuk`. 'One is struck down by this' (`vihaññati etasmā`), hence `vighāto`. 'They dwell here' (`viharanti ettha`), hence `vihāro`. 'They delight in this' (`āramanti etasmiṃ`), hence `ārāmo`. `Pacanaṃ` becomes `pāko`, with `k` substituted for `c`. `Cajanaṃ` is `cāgo`. `Yajanaṃ` is `yāgo`. `Rajanaṃ` is `rāgo`.

127. Ana+ghaṇasvā+parīhi ḷo

127. Ana+ghaṇasvā+parīhi ḷo

Ā+parīhi parassa dahassa ḷo hota+na+ghaṇasu. Paridahanaṃ pariḷāho. Evaṃ dāho. Bhañjanaṃ saṅgo. Evaṃ saṅgo. Saṃkharanaṃ saṃkhāro, “karotissa kho”ti kassa kho. Evaṃ parikkhāro. “Purasmā”ti karassa kho, purekkhāro, ettaṃ tadaminādipāṭhā. Evaṃ upakāro, gāho.

After `ā` and `pari`, for the following root `dah`, `ḷ` is substituted when the suffixes `aṇa` and `ghaṇa` follow. `Paridahanaṃ` (burning) is `pariḷāho`. Similarly, `dāho`. `Bhañjanaṃ` is `saṅgo`. Similarly, `saṅgo`. `Saṃkharanaṃ` is `saṃkhāro`; by the rule `karotissa kho`, `kh` is substituted for `k`. Similarly, `parikkhāro`. By the rule `purasmā`, `kh` is substituted for `kara`, hence `purekkhāro`; this is from the list of readings beginning with `tada`, `amina`. Similarly, `upakāro`, `gāho`.

Gha-vacatīti [M 0.0278] vako. Sica=paggharaṇe, secanaṃ seko. Evaṃ soko, eovuddhiyo. Yuñjanaṃ yogo.

The suffix `gha`: 'it speaks' (`vacati`), hence `vako`. The root `sica` is in the sense of sprinkling: `secanaṃ` is `seko`. Similarly, `soko`; these involve `vuddhi` of `e` and `o`. `Yuñjanaṃ` is `yogo`.

Ka-pī=tappane, pīnetīti pīyo, kānubandhattā na vuddhi, “yuvaṇṇāna+miyaṅuvaṅa sare”ti iyaṅa. Khipa=peraṇe, khipatīti khipo. Bhuñjantya+nenāti bhujo. Yudha=sampahāre āyujjhanti anenāti āyudhaṃ.

The suffix `ka`: The root `pī` is in the sense of satisfying: 'it satisfies' (`pīneti`), hence `pīyo`; due to the `anubandha` `k`, there is no `vuddhi` (strengthening); the `iyaṅ` substitution occurs by the rule `yuvaṇṇānaṃ iyaṅuvaṅa sare`. The root `khipa` is in the sense of throwing: 'it throws' (`khipati`), hence `khipo`. 'One eats with this' (`bhuñjanti anena`), hence `bhujo`. The root `yudha` is in the sense of fighting: 'they fight with this' (`āyujjhanti anena`), hence `āyudhaṃ`.

45. Dādhātvi

45. Dādhātvi

Dādhāto bahula+mi hoti bhāvakārakesu. Dā=dāne, ādiyatītiādi. Evaṃ upādi. Dhā=dhāraṇe, udakaṃ dadhātīti udadhi, “saññāya+mudo+dakassā”ti udakassa udādeso. Jalaṃ dhiyate asminti jaladhi. Vālāni dhīyanti asminti vāladhi. Sandhīyati sandhātīti vā sandhi. Dhīyatīti dhi. Vidhīyati vidhāti vidhānaṃ vā vidhi. Sammā samaṃ vā cittaṃ ādadhātīti samādhi.

From the roots `dā` and `dhā`, the suffix `i` occurs frequently in the sense of state and agent. The root `dā` is in the sense of giving: 'one takes' (`ādiyati`), hence `ādi`. Similarly, `upādi`. The root `dhā` is in the sense of holding: 'it holds water' (`udakaṃ dadhāti`), hence `udadhi`; by the rule `saññāyaṃ udo dakassa`, `uda` is substituted for `udaka`. 'Water is held in this' (`jalaṃ dhīyate asmiṃ`), hence `jaladhi`. 'Hairs are held in this' (`vālāni dhīyanti asmiṃ`), hence `vāladhi`. 'It is joined' (`sandhīyati`) or 'it joins' (`sandhāti`), hence `sandhi`. 'It is held' (`dhīyati`), hence `dhi`. 'It is arranged' (`vidhīyati`), 'it arranges' (`vidhāti`), or 'an arrangement' (`vidhānaṃ`), hence `vidhi`. 'It properly or evenly places the mind' (`sammā samaṃ vā cittaṃ ādadhāti`), hence `samādhi`.

46. Vamādīhya+thu

46. Vamādīhya+thu

Vamādīhi bhāvakārakesva+thu hoti. Vama=uggiraṇe, vamanaṃ vamīyatīti vā vamathu. Vepa+kampa=calane, vepanaṃ vepathu.

After `vama` and other roots, the suffix `athu` occurs in the sense of state and agent. The root `vama` is in the sense of vomiting: `vamanaṃ` (vomiting) or `vamīyati` (is vomited), hence `vamathu`. The roots `vepa` and `kampa` are in the sense of shaking: `vepanaṃ` (shaking), hence `vepathu`.

47. Kvi

47. Kvi

Kriyatthā kvi hoti bahulaṃ bhāvakārakesu. Kakāro kānubandhakāriyattho.

The suffix `kvi` occurs frequently from roots, in the sense of state and agent. The letter `k` is for the purpose of the grammatical operations associated with the `anubandha` `k`.

159. Kvissa

159. Kvissa

Kriyatthā [M 0.0279] parassa kvissa lopo hoti. Sambhavatīti sambhū. Evaṃ vibhavatīti vibhū, abhibhū, sayambhū. Tathā dhu=kampane, sandhunātīti sandhu. Vibhātīti vibhā. Pabhātīti pabhā. Saṃgamma bhāsanti etthāti sabhā, “kvimhi lopo+ntabyañjanassā”ti antabyañjanassa lopo. Bhujena gacchatīti bhujago. Evaṃ urago. Turaṃ=sīghaṃ gacchatīti turaṅgo. Khena gacchatīti khago. Vihāyase gacchatīti vihago, tadaminādipāṭhā vihādeso. Na gacchatīti nago. Evaṃ ago, “nago vā+ppāṇinī”ti vikappena nañasamāse ṭādesanisedho. Jana=janane, kammato jātoti kammajo, amādisamāso, kammajo vipāko, kammajā paṭisandhi, kammajaṃ rūpaṃ. Evaṃ cittajaṃ, utujaṃ, āhārajaṃ. Attajo putto, vārimhi jāto vārijo. Evaṃ thalajo. Paṅkajaṃ. Jalajaṃ. Aṇḍajaṃ. Sarasijaṃ, upapadasamāse bahulaṃvidhānā vibhatyalope “manādīhī”tiādinā siādeso. Dvikkhattuṃ jāto dvijo, “tadaminā” dinā kkhattuṃlopo. Pacchā jāto anujo. Sañjānātīti saññā. Pajānātīti paññā. Evaṃ patiṭṭhātīti patiṭṭhā. Jhā=cintāyaṃ, parasampattiṃ abhijjhāyatīti abhijjhā. Hitesitaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā jhāyatīti upajjhā. So eva upajjhāyo, “sakatthe”ti yo. Sammā jhāyanti etthāti saṃjhā. Kvidantā dhātvatthaṃ na jahanti, liṅgatthaṃ paṭipādayanti.

The elision of the 'kvi' suffix occurs for another root in the sense of action. That which comes into being is 'sambhū'. Similarly, that which becomes powerful is 'vibhū', that which overcomes is 'abhibhū', and that which is self-existent is 'sayambhū'. Likewise, the root 'dhu' is in the sense of shaking; 'sandhunāti' (shakes thoroughly), hence 'sandhu'. That which shines is 'vibhā'. That which shines forth is 'pabhā'. That in which they speak together is 'sabhā'; by the rule ‘kvimhi lopo+ntabyañjanassā’, there is elision of the final consonant. That which goes by its arm is 'bhujago'. Similarly, 'urago'. That which goes quickly is 'turaṅgo'. That which goes in the sky is 'khago'. That which goes in the sky is 'vihago'; by the reading 'tadaminādipāṭhā', there is the substitution 'vihā'. That which does not go is 'nago'. Similarly, 'ago'. By the rule ‘nago vā+ppāṇinī’, there is optionally a prohibition of the substitution of 'ṭa' in a 'nañ-samāsa'. The root 'jana' is in the sense of producing; 'kammato jāto' (born from kamma), hence 'kammajo'. This is an 'amādi-samāsa'. 'Kammajo vipāko' (result born of kamma), 'kammajā paṭisandhi' (rebirth-linking born of kamma), 'kammajaṃ rūpaṃ' (material form born of kamma). Similarly, 'cittajaṃ' (mind-born), 'utujaṃ' (season-born), 'āhārajaṃ' (food-born). 'Attajo putto' (son born of oneself). 'Vārimhi jāto' (born in water), hence 'vārijo'. Similarly, 'thalajo' (land-born), 'paṅkajaṃ' (mud-born), 'jalajaṃ' (water-born), 'aṇḍajaṃ' (egg-born), 'sarasijaṃ' (lake-born). In an 'upapada-samāsa', due to the principle of frequent application, when the case ending is elided, by the rule ‘manādīhī’ and so on, there is the substitution of 'si'. One who is born twice is 'dvijo'; by the rule ‘tadaminā’ and so on, there is elision of 'kkhattuṃ'. One who is born later is 'anujo'. That which perceives is 'saññā'. That which understands is 'paññā'. Similarly, that which is established is 'patiṭṭhā'. The root 'jhā' is in the sense of contemplating; 'parasampattiṃ abhijjhāyati' (contemplates another's prosperity with longing), hence 'abhijjhā' (covetousness). One who contemplates, having established what is beneficial, is 'upajjhā'. That very one is 'upajjhāyo'; by the rule ‘sakatthe’, the suffix 'yo' is used in its own sense. That in which they contemplate properly is 'saṃjhā'. Words ending in 'kvi' do not abandon the meaning of the root but convey the meaning of gender.

48. Ano

48. Ano

Kriyatthā [M 0.0280] bhāvakārakesu ano hoti. Nanda=samiddhiyaṃ, bhāve-nandiyate nandanaṃ. Kamme-anandīyittha nandīyati nandīyissati nanditabbanti vā nandanaṃ vanaṃ. Gahanaṃ gahanīyaṃ vā gahaṇaṃ, “tathanarā” dinā nassa ṇo. Gaṇhanaṃ, niggahītassa no. Caritabbaṃ caraṇaṃ. Bhuyate bhavanaṃ. Huyate havanaṃ. Rundhitabbaṃ rundhanaṃ rodhanaṃ vā. Bhuñjitabbaṃ bhuñjanaṃ bhojanaṃ vā. Bujjhitabbaṃ bujjhanaṃ, “padādīnaṃ kvacī”ti yuka. Bodhanaṃ vā. Suti suyyati vā savanaṃ. Pāpīyatīti pāpuṇanaṃ, “sakāpānaṃ kuka+kū”ti yogavibhāgā kuāgame nāgame ca tassa ṇo ca. Pālīyatīti pālanaṃ iccādi.

The suffix 'ano' occurs in the senses of action, state, and agent. The root 'nanda' is in the sense of prosperity; in the sense of state, 'nandiyate' (is delighted), hence 'nandanaṃ'. In the sense of object, 'anandīyittha' (was delighted), 'nandīyati' (is delighted), 'nandīyissati' (will be delighted), or 'nanditabbaṃ' (should be delighted), hence 'nandanaṃ vanaṃ' (a pleasure grove). The act of seizing is 'gahanaṃ', or what should be seized is 'gahaṇaṃ'; by the rule ‘tathanarā’ and so on, 'na' becomes 'ṇa'. The form is 'gaṇhanaṃ'; for 'niggahīta', there is no (retroflexion). What should be practiced is 'caraṇaṃ'. The act of becoming is 'bhavanaṃ'. The act of offering is 'havanaṃ'. What should be obstructed is 'rundhanaṃ' or 'rodhanaṃ'. What should be eaten is 'bhuñjanaṃ' or 'bhojanaṃ'. What should be understood is 'bujjhanaṃ'; by the rule ‘padādīnaṃ kvacī’, the suffix 'yu' occurs. Or 'bodhanaṃ'. The act of hearing or that which is heard is 'savanaṃ'. That which is reached is 'pāpuṇanaṃ'; by the rule ‘sakāpānaṃ kuka+kū’, due to a division of the rule, the augments 'ku' and 'na' occur, and its 'na' also becomes 'ṇa'. That which is protected is 'pālanaṃ', and so on.

Kattari-rajaṃ haratīti rajoharaṇaṃ toyaṃ. Vijānātīti viññāṇaṃ. Ghā=gandhopādāne, ghāyatīti ghānaṃ. Jhā=cintāyaṃ, jhāyatīti jhānaṃ. Karoti anenāti kāraṇaṃ, dīgho. Viākarīyanti etenāti byākaraṇaṃ. Pūrati+nenāti pūraṇaṃ. Dīyate+nenāti dānaṃ. Pamīyate+nenāti pamāṇaṃ. Vuccate+nenāti vacanaṃ. Panudati panujjate+nenāti vā panudanaṃ. Sūda=pagaraṇe, sūdati sujjate+nenāti vā sūdano. Suṇāti suyate+neneti vā savanaṃ. Luyati luyate+neneti vā lavanaṃ. Evaṃ nayanaṃ. Punāti puyate+neneti vā pavano. Sametīti samaṇo samanaṃ vā. Tathā bhāveti bhāvīyati etāyāti vā bhāvanaṃ. Evaṃ pācanaṃ pācāpanaṃ iccādi. “Ana+saṇasvā parīhi ḷo”ti ḷo, āḷāhanaṃ.

In the sense of agent: 'rajaṃ harati' (removes dust), hence 'rajoharaṇaṃ toyaṃ' (dust-removing water). That which discerns is 'viññāṇaṃ'. The root 'ghā' is in the sense of taking in scents; 'ghāyati' (smells), hence 'ghānaṃ'. The root 'jhā' is in the sense of contemplating; 'jhāyati' (meditates), hence 'jhānaṃ'. That by which one acts is 'kāraṇaṃ' (cause); the vowel is lengthened. That by which things are explained is 'byākaraṇaṃ'. That by which one fills is 'pūraṇaṃ'. That by which one gives is 'dānaṃ'. That by which one measures is 'pamāṇaṃ'. That by which one speaks is 'vacanaṃ'. That by which one repels or is repelled is 'panudanaṃ'. The root 'sūda' is in the sense of preparing; that by which one prepares or is prepared is 'sūdano'. That by which one hears or is heard is 'savanaṃ'. That by which one cuts or is cut is 'lavanaṃ'. Similarly, 'nayanaṃ'. That by which one purifies or is purified is 'pavano'. One who is calm is 'samaṇo', or the act of calming is 'samanaṃ'. Likewise, that by which one develops or is developed is 'bhāvanaṃ'. Similarly, 'pācanaṃ', 'pācāpanaṃ', and so on. By the rule ‘Ana+saṇasvā parīhi ḷo’, the suffix 'ḷa' occurs, as in 'āḷāhanaṃ'.

Adhikaraṇe-tiṭṭhati asinti ṭhānaṃ. Evaṃ sayanaṃ, senaṃ vā āsanaṃ. Adhikarīyati etthāti adhikaraṇaṃ.

In the sense of location: That in which one stands is 'ṭhānaṃ' (place). Similarly, 'sayanaṃ' (bed), 'senaṃ' (lying down), or 'āsanaṃ' (seat). That in which something is established is 'adhikaraṇaṃ' (locus).

Sampadānāpādānesu-sammā [M 0.0281] padīyate yassa taṃ sampadānaṃ. Apecca etasmā ādadātīti apādānaṃ. Bahulādhikārā calanādīhipi sīlasādhudhammesupi ano, calati sīlenāti calano evaṃ jalano, kodhano, kopano. Maṇḍa=bhusane, maṇḍeti sīlenāti maṇḍano. Evaṃ bhūsano. “Aññātrapī”ti okāranisedho.

In the senses of dative and ablative: That to which something is properly given is 'sampadānaṃ'. That from which one takes away is 'apādānaṃ'. Due to the extensive scope of the rule, the suffix 'ano' also occurs with 'calana' and other words, even in the sense of habit or nature: 'calati sīlenāti calano' (one who acts by habit is 'calano'). Similarly, 'jalano' (burning), 'kodhano' (angry), 'kopano' (prone to anger). The root 'maṇḍa' is in the sense of adorning; 'maṇḍeti sīlenāti maṇḍano' (one who adorns by habit is 'maṇḍano'). Similarly, 'bhūsano' (adorner). By the rule ‘Aññātrapī’, there is a prohibition of the 'o' sound.

49. Itthiya+ma+ṇa+kti+ka+yaka+yā ca

49. And in the feminine gender, the suffixes 'ma', 'ṇa', 'kti', 'ka', 'yaka', and 'yā'.

Itthiliṅge bhāve kārake ca kriyatthā aādayo honti ano ca bahulaṃ.

In the feminine gender, in the senses of state, agent, and action, the suffixes 'a' and others occur, and also 'ano' frequently.

A-jara=vayohāniyaṃ, jirati jiraṇaṃ vā jarā. “Itthiya+ma+tvā”ti āpaccayo. Paṭisambhijjatīti paṭisambhidā. Paṭipajjati etāyāti paṭipadā. Evaṃ sampadā, āpadā. Upādīyatīti upādā. Ikkha+cakkha=dassane, upaikkhatīti upekkhā. “Yuvaṇṇāna+meo luttā”ti ekāro. Cintanaṃ cintā. Sikkha=vijjopādāne, sikkhanaṃ sikkhīyantīti vā sikkhā. Evaṃ bhikkhā. Icchanaṃ icchā. “Gamayami”ccādinā cchaṅādeso. Puccha=pucchane, pucchanaṃ pucchā. Midha+medha=saṅgame, apaṭhitadhātu, medhanaṃ medhā. Evaṃ gudha=pariveṭhane, godhanaṃ godhā. Titikkhanaṃ titikkhā. Evaṃ vīmaṃsā, jigucchā, pipāsā, puttiyā. Īhanaṃ īhā.

The suffix 'a': The root 'jara' is in the sense of the decline of life; 'jirati' (it decays) or 'jiraṇaṃ' (the act of decaying), hence 'jarā'. By the rule ‘Itthiyamato ā’, the suffix 'ā' is applied. That which is analyzed is 'paṭisambhidā' (discrimination). One proceeds by means of it—this is 'paṭipadā' (the path). Likewise, 'sampadā' (accomplishment), 'āpadā' (adversity). That which is clung to is 'upādā' (grasping). The roots 'ikkha' and 'cakkha' are in the sense of seeing; 'upaikkhati' (one observes closely), hence 'upekkhā' (equanimity). By the rule ‘Yuvaṇṇānaṃ eo luttānaṃ’, there is the letter 'e'. The act of thinking is 'cintā' (thought). The root 'sikkha' is in the sense of acquiring knowledge; the act of learning or that by which one learns is 'sikkhā' (training). Likewise, 'bhikkhā' (alms). The act of desiring is 'icchā' (desire). By the rule ‘Gamayami’ and so on, there is the substitution 'ccha'. The root 'puccha' is in the sense of asking; the act of asking is 'pucchā' (a question). The roots 'midha' and 'medha' are in the sense of conflict, an unlisted root; the act of contending is 'medhā' (intelligence). Likewise, the root 'gudha' is in the sense of surrounding; the act of surrounding is 'godhā' (a lizard). The act of enduring is 'titikkhā' (endurance). Likewise, 'vīmaṃsā' (investigation), 'jigucchā' (disgust), 'pipāsā' (thirst), 'puttiyā'. The act of striving is 'īhā' (effort).

Ṇa-karaṇaṃ kārā, “assā ṇānubandhe”ti ā hoti, eva+muparipi. Haraṇaṃ hārā muttāvali. Taraṇaṃ tārā, dharaṇaṃ dhārā. Araṇaṃ ārā.

The suffix 'ṇa': The act of doing is 'kārā'; by the rule ‘assā ṇānubandhe’, 'ā' occurs, and likewise in the preceding cases. From 'haraṇaṃ' (carrying) comes 'hārā' (a necklace, a string of pearls). From 'taraṇaṃ' (crossing) comes 'tārā' (a star); from 'dharaṇaṃ' (bearing) comes 'dhārā' (a stream). From 'araṇaṃ' (not fighting) comes 'ārā' (an awl).

Yathākathañci saddamhi, ruḷhiyā atthanicchayo.

In any word whatsoever, the determination of meaning is by convention.

Kti-sambhuvanaṃ [M 0.0282] sambhuti. “Na te”ccādinā na vuddhi. Savanaṃ suti. Nayanaṃ nayati etāyāti vā nīti. Maññatīti mati, “gamādirānaṃ lopontabyañjanassā”ti gamādittā nalopo. Gamanaṃ gantabbāti vā gati. Upahananaṃ upahati. Ramanti etāya ramanaṃ vā rati. Tananaṃ tati. Niyamanaṃ niyati. Bhuñjanaṃ bhutti. Yuñjanaṃ yutti, pararūpaṃ. Evaṃ samāpajjanaṃ samāpajjateti samāpatti. Sampatti. Yaja=devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadānesu, yajanaṃ iṭṭhi, “yajassa yassa ṭiyī”ti ṭiādeso, “pucchādito”ti tassa ṭho, pararūpapaṭhamakkharā ca. Sāsanaṃ siṭṭhi, “sāsassa sisa vā”ti sisa, sānantarassa tassa ṭho”ti ṭhādeso. Bhedanaṃ bhijjateti vā bhitti. Bhaja=sevāyaṃ, bhajanaṃ bhatti. Tana=vitthāre, tanotīti tanti, nassa niggahītādi.

The suffix 'kti': The act of originating is 'sambhuti' (arising). By the rule ‘Na te’ and so on, there is no vowel gradation. The act of hearing is 'suti'. The act of leading, or that by which one leads, is 'nīti' (method). 'Maññati' (one thinks), hence 'mati' (thought); by the rule ‘gamādirānaṃ lopontabyañjanassā’, because it belongs to the 'gam' group, the final 'n' is elided. The act of going, or what is to be gone to, is 'gati' (a course). The act of injuring is 'upahati'. They delight by means of it, or the act of delighting, is 'rati' (delight). The act of stretching is 'tati' (extension). The act of restraining is 'niyati' (restraint). The act of consuming is 'bhutti'.
